# Design envelope

This page lists the engine's limits: every hard boundary, where it starts, what you see when you reach it and the
package or tool that takes you past it. The reference tables are [Scale](#scale), [Rendering](#rendering),
[Geometry](#geometry), [Entities](#entities), [Copies of a model](#copies-of-a-model) and [Platform](#platform)
(tested hardware and browsers are in Platform). The paragraphs just above Scale say how to read their "Starts at"
column. The dated notes between here and those tables, and the sections after Platform, are the change record: each
notes one change's size or behaviour and its evidence. Every number has a row in
[whitepaper/claims.md](whitepaper/claims.md).

- Vortex forcing (ATMO-05, 2026-11-26). The storm has prescribed motion and intensity. The atmosphere uses
  a radial pressure profile with a height envelope. It represents no storm formation, terrain interaction,
  or evolving supercell. Bodies use configured drag area and a pressure lever. Their load field records
  threshold crossings for structural consumers. Water sees spatial atmospheric pressure and wind stress.
  The existing neutral ramp reaches the short-fetch laboratory ceiling of 0.0026 at about 27.6 m/s.
  The physics wind keeps its full speed. WeatherRegions keeps its 60 m/s styling range. The standalone
  GPU Flood retains its scalar preview settings. The scalar and native wet-grid samplers agree in the
  mixed natural vortex fixtures. Each native helper owns disjoint wet-grid rows.
  The optional physical entry is 10,204 B gzip with a 10,511 B ceiling. Each lazy native variant is
  6,443 B raw or 2,502 B gzip. Core and stage receive zero bytes.
  Independent observations and the coupled renderer proof appear in [the ATMO-05 comparison](#atmo-05-accepted-storm-forcing-and-observations).

- Seismic waves (EARTH-08, 2026-11-26). One plane-strain section resolves in-plane P and SV, with
  a level, traction-free top. Pick cell spacing for the shortest wavelength in the scene. The world
  chooses a dyadic rate that keeps the elastic Courant number at or below 0.95. The damped outer strip
  approximates an open side and bottom, and oblique waves can return a weak reflection. Cyclic stress
  screening uses configured soil resistance, with no pore-water pressure evolution. A building receiver
  is one horizontal mode. One, two or four native participants advance the staggered stencil with
  a join between velocity and stress and ordered traction-free surface handling. The solver retains an
  88-byte trial bank per section cell including its coefficient copies, plus the surface and site trials.
  The optional solver is 8,300 B gzip with an 8,556 B ceiling. Each lazy SIMD asset is 4,031 B raw,
  1,895 B gzip and 1,629 B Brotli. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.
  [Measured limits](#earth-08-elastic-site-response-at-mashiki).

- Outdoor sound (SOUND-01). The solver uses a local midpoint sound-speed gradient, one weakly refracted direct
  trajectory or one dominant edge and one coherent horizontal-plane reflection. Both specular legs must reach
  the reflecting point without passing through the terrain. The model omits ground impedance, multiple-edge and
  reflected diffraction, atmospheric ducts and shadow strength, turbulence scattering and phase-resolved audio.
  ISO 9613-1 gives ±10% absorption accuracy for its ordinary weather range. In Rasmussen’s berm experiment,
  5 of 16 spectral readings are inside the figure-reading intervals after the reflection visibility fix. The
  remaining residual reaches 6.97 dB. The figures supply readout ranges and no full experimental uncertainty.
  Playback uses two shelves and a centre gain for the eight-band path. Its configured delay is above 0 through
  180 s, default 30 s. Sound tracing stages up to two sets of configured intervals per link in private scratch.
  The 1/2/4-participant path uses native f64 SIMD for each octave pair. Multiple participants require Node or a
  cross-origin-isolated browser worker. Terrain and field sampling remain on the caller. A finer bed can increase
  sampling work. The optional plain and shared Wasm assets are each 4,374 B raw and 2,078 B gzip.
  The optional Physics and Audio entries are 8,601 B and 1,389 B gzip.

- Webcam face to morph targets (`@margoengine/input/face`, 2026-11-26): no detector shipped; the app supplies one.
  Landmarks alone give 15 of the 52 ARKit shapes (blinks, wide eyes, jaw, smiles, frowns, pucker, brows); the others
  need the detector's blendshape scores. Landmark weights are distance ratios against a neutral face, so they read
  best after `calibrate` on the person; the head rotation from landmarks has no translation.

- Webcam hands and body to a skeleton (`@margoengine/input/body`, 2026-11-26): no detector shipped; the app supplies
  one. Each bone follows one landmark direction, so twist about a bone is kept only where a side direction gives it
  (hips, chest, hands); upper arms and legs take the shortest turn. Joint limits are cones about the rest rotation
  relative to the parent, not hinge axes; the root is rotated, never moved; one pose and one hand per side are read.

- Webcam landmarks (`@margoengine/input/landmarks`, 2026-11-26): no detector shipped; the app supplies one. Margo
  bundles no trained weights and never downloads a model; frames come from the app's own detector (MediaPipe Tasks
  results plug in through `fromMediaPipe`). A stream keeps only the newest `buffer` frames (default 1) for a slow reader.

- Shadow map viewer (`@margoengine/shadows/viewer`, 2026-11-25) shows one layer at a time, nearest texel, no
  filtering, so a map larger than the viewer drops texels; it draws over the frame at order 1000 without depth or
  blending. Virtual shadow map pages (`@margoengine/shadows/virtual`) and the colour (tint) maps of coloured shadows are
  not covered: only depth arrays of `Shadows` and `LocalShadows` (and any depth texture passed by hand).

- Light probe and positional audio helpers (`@margoengine/lines/scene-helpers`, 2026-11-25): `LightProbeHelper` reads
  only L1 (12 floats) or L2 (27 floats) SH and samples its source at 408 directions per `update()` (a function source
  is called that many times a frame); colours are clamped to 0..1 after `exposure`, so a probe brighter than the scale
  saturates. `PositionalAudioHelper` does not draw `maxDistance` at or above Web Audio's 10,000 default, and it draws
  the cones only, not the `coneOuterGain` falloff between them.

- BVH, octree and raycaster helpers (`@margoengine/lines/tree-helpers`, 2026-11-25) draw box edges, 24 points a box, in
  one `Line`: a tree level with many thousands of nodes is that many boxes, so keep `depth` low on a deep tree (`maxDepth`
  says how deep it goes). They read the node bounds when built and on `setDepth`; they do not follow a `refit` or an
  edited tree until `setDepth` is called again. Depth is a whole number from 0 to 64.

- Infinite grid (`@margoengine/lines/infinite-grid`, 2026-11-25) is a plane at one height `y`, drawn as a quad of
  the fade distance's half-width centred under the camera (or the origin), so nothing draws past `fadeDistance`;
  lines under two pixels apart fade out instead of aliasing. It is a transparent overlay: it writes no depth, so
  geometry lying exactly on its plane z-fights with it (raise `y` a little). WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility
  layer; the small WebGL2 preview throws `unsupported`.

- Horse fore fetlock (2026-11-23). The walking pose yields into stance and folds the fetlock locally in swing.
  A compound lower link holds the forehoof path and maintains segment lengths. The walking knee flexion uses
  eased angular velocity. This is a sagittal joint model with terrain slope handled by the live
  hoof solver. The optional entries measure 15,641 B for `horses`, 11,716 B for `horses/model` and 12,035 B for
  `horses/crowd`. [Joint measurements and implementation](../packages/horses/README.md#the-model-model).

- Horse tail motion (2026-11-23). The stride drives a passive sway. A live tail action of strength from 0 to 1
  plays a sweep and rebound for less than 0.94 s across three dock and five hair joints. Baked gait loops include
  the passive sway. Live swishes are timed events. The approximation uses joint rotations for the tail.
  This change measures 15,343 B for `horses`, 11,440 B for `horses/model` and 11,735 B for `horses/crowd`.
  [Motion setup and sources](../packages/horses/README.md#the-model-model).

- Horse terrain contact (2026-11-23). The live horse can plant four reachable world points on a continuous
  height field, with slope-specific hoof angles and a 0.18 s horizontal release. Fitted chains keep their lengths
  and bend sides, and lateral splay is capped at 0.35 radians. The height field uses one elevation per XZ
  and assumes a reachable route. Baked clips and crowd gaits follow their authored plane.
  With the foreleg update, the optional entries are 15,326 B for `horses`, 11,419 B for `horses/model`,
  and 11,765 B for `horses/crowd`.
  [Terrain setup and evidence](../packages/horses/README.md).

- Horse gait transitions (2026-11-23). The runtime matches incoming four-hoof positions and supporting movement,
  then retires the previous cadence over the configured fade (0.3 s by default). The built-in horse has 37 joints,
  including five flexible tail hair joints. Authored skins provide their own joint mapping and remain caller-owned.
  The gait solver uses planar leg anatomy and can shorten the stride to fit a tighter limb while preserving speed.
  This gait-transition pass measured 13,856 B for `horses`, 11,539 B for `horses/crowd`, and 10,673 B for `horses/model`
  before the live terrain contact change.
  [Horse setup and evidence](../packages/horses/README.md).

- Human palm contacts (2026-11-23). The palm must be within the default 0.003 model units and 5 degrees to close.
  One contact solves a contiguous arm and one mapped hand. The grip approximates a cylinder with a diameter
  above 0 and below 1 m, evaluating the approach and six closing poses of each measured digit proxy. Exact skin clearance needs
  the deformed mesh. The anatomical wrist defaults to 1.12 rad flexion, 1.0 rad extension and 0.46 rad sideways
  deviation. The optional forearm
  limit takes perpendicular nonzero flex and roll axes with signed ranges within ±π. See
  [palm calibration](../packages/rigging/README.md#human-palm-and-cylindrical-grips).

- Character limb collision (2026-11-23). The optional rigging contact entry checks caller-configured capsules
  against body volumes and bounds upper limb directions relative to the animated skeleton. An intersecting arm
  triggers a bounded search of eleven alternate bend directions. The sweep checks straight proxy endpoint paths
  and direction limits carried by the shortest arc of the body axis. The default contact margin is 0.0001 model
  units and the work budget is 128 checks (range 1–4,096). Curved joint paths and opposed body axes need an
  intermediate sample. Budget exhaustion and unresolved opposed axes report a blocked path. Direction limits
  require direction data in both snapshots. The contact entry measures 13,167 B gzip.
  [Setup and examples](../packages/rigging/README.md#character-self-collision-during-contact).

- Explicit hinged reach (2026-11-23). `rigging/contact` can solve the last two links using a single authored bend
  plane. It requires an off-axis pole and a perpendicular hinge at the penultimate joint. A blocked path reports a
  failed contact. Angular and spatial margins still apply. The default palm pad clears the thumb web and is bounded
  between 56% and 88% of the wrist-to-middle-knuckle span. Exact mesh clearance requires the deformed asset.

- Swimming and dense rigs (2026-11-23). The CPU rig builder accepts 1–65,536 joints. The swimming entry accepts
  at least four spine segments, 0.001–1,000 m head-to-tail length, and at most 65,536 joints including the fins.
  Nonuniform stations must differ by at least one hundred-millionth of the length. It samples deterministic
  kinematic poses, leaving path integration and water forces to the caller. Existing rendering and skin buffer
  limits still apply. The contact solver takes 2–256 ordered joints, with positive uniform ancestor scales.
  Distances and angles are measured after blending. Standalone joint limits can cover up to 65,536 joints in
  the pose. See [rigging](../packages/rigging/README.md).
- Coral colonies (2026-11-23). The optional CPU generator builds a connected surface at 48–128 samples along
  its longest axis. Colonies scale by a 0.01–30 m diameter. Finer structure beyond the sampled detail requires
  a normal map or a close-up asset. See [procedural coral](../packages/procedural/README.md#coral-colonies-margoengineproceduralcoral).

- Animated flow paths (2026-11-22) use an authored polyline of 2 to 3,999,992 finite float32 points with positive local length. Endpoint fades use fractions of local arc length, adding at most eight points to fit the Lines renderer's 4,000,000-point limit. A visible path has one dash layer and an optional guide. The browser tests read back forward travel, exact seek replay, zero gain and occlusion on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer. The optional `@margoengine/lines/flow` entry adds 5,640 B min+gzip. See [Lines](../packages/lines/README.md#animated-flow-paths) and [the clean-room record](clean-room.md#animated-flow-paths-in-lines-2026-11-22).

- Zero scale (KB-GLTFA B1, 2026-11-19): a mesh, a glTF node (TRS or a matrix with zero columns) and an animation key
  may scale an axis to 0, as glTF 2.0 section 3.5.3 allows. The mesh is flattened: its normals turn by the cofactor
  matrix, a determinant of 0 counts as not mirrored, and a normal the flattened matrix maps to exactly zero (or that
  underflows float32, below about 1e-19 per axis) shades as world +Y, so a sphere at (1, 0, 1) is lit like a +Y face
  and one at (0, 0, 0) draws nothing. Its world sphere radius is the largest axis scale times the local one (0 when
  all are 0). What stays refused, each with its own error because it needs a true inverse: a glTF matrix whose nonzero
  columns are dependent or not orthogonal, `@margoengine/bvh` CPU raycasts (a flattened mesh has no CPU ray hits; GPU
  picking hits it), skinned-mesh and VAT/instanced-skin model roots, bone bind poses, physics and controls parents,
  `@margoengine/scene` reparenting under a flattened parent, and 3MF export (MargoError `'unsupported'`: a 3MF item is a
  solid to print and a flattened one has no volume; glTF, USDZ, OBJ, STL and PLY write it, glTF a zero-column node
  matrix as TRS, packages/exporters/tests/zero-scale.test.js). Evidence:
  packages/core/tests/zero-scale.browser.mjs (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer), packages/gltf/test/audit-gltfa.test.js,
  tests/modern-zero-determinant-normals.test.js.
- River water and the world's edge (KB-BIOMES-RIVERSTEP1, KB-BIOMES-WORLDEDGE1, 2026-11-17): still river water fills a carved channel to three quarters of its depth (at most 1.5 m; 1.5 m over open ground), found 6 m across and 24 m to each bank, never rising downstream and averaged over 9 half cells; it still sits on the 512-cell coupled grid (8 m cells on a 4 km world), so its own waterline is that coarse and the terrain's banks draw the edge. Past the fine clipmap rings the water passes the rings' error (`@margoengine/water/banks`, at most 2 m) and ends where the view's own 2 m heights rise through it, so a creek stays one line of water wherever the view's heightmap holds it; the `riverbed` ground material is still painted under the water (one `heightAt` per texel inside a river's corridor), and past the world's 16 m overview heights (the horizon ring) the creek is that paint only. `horizon` far ground reaches 3 world sizes past each edge (at most 48 km) on texels of up to 32 m and a 64th of the world (a power of two of the world's texels, coarser only to keep 2,049 corners a side; 128 m on 8 km drew peaks as straight-sided cones, KB-BIOMES-HORIZONCONE1), about 3.2 million corners and 2 to 5 s of CPU for an 8 km world and 800,000 for a 4 km one, with no plants and no shadows. Sizes (quality gate bundle measure): `@margoengine/biomes/view` 11,774 to 13,431 B gzip (horizon on by default for land-locked views, so a lazy split would load it anyway and await before the first frame), `@margoengine/biomes/rivers` 2,264 to 2,817 B. Tests: packages/biomes/tests/view.test.js (RIVERSTEP1), tests/horizon.test.js.
- Water captures (KB-WATER-CAPTURECAM1, 2026-11-28): a Water capture (SSR, SceneTargets) draws from the unjittered camera with frame values of its own; a capture that runs before the very first frame's surface draw holds no water.
- Frame budgets and film frames (KB-FILM-CLOCK1, 2026-11-17): the live per-frame budgets in milliseconds (terrain `PlanetTerrain` `budget`, biomes `BiomeView` `budget`, gltf `loadGLTFProgressive` `frameBudget`) make a slower machine do less work a frame, so a frame drawn while work is still arriving differs between machines. Each has a work-count twin that replaces it (`maxBuilds`, `maxSteps`, `maxJobs`) and a `clock` option (also `SceneFade`'s third argument); a film uses the counts. The live defaults are unchanged.
- Film frames on every run (GAP-FILM-READY, KB-FILM-GPUSHARE1, 2026-11-17, LIM-661): a 90-frame rain shot (Bruneton
  sky with clouds, AgX, shadows, Weather rain, 1280x720) read with headless `readPixels` is byte for byte the same in
  every fresh browser from frame 0, alone and beside a second process running a GPU compute load, on WebGPU and the
  WebGL2 layer (RTX A6000; 240 frames, 2 alone and 3 shared runs, also equal). A WebGPU page canvas read in the task
  of the render gives the same bytes; read after an `await` it lags by a varying number of frames. On the WebGL2 layer
  a page canvas shows nothing in the task of a scene's first compute submit (KB-COMPAT-FIRSTTASK1, fixed 2026-11-17: `requestDevice` loads the compute part first). Not
  measured: other scenes, other GPUs, Node with Dawn. Evidence: packages/sky/test/rain-frames-check.mjs.
- KB-SUNSHADOW-OFFSET1 (2026-11-16): directional hard shadows use the same receiver-plane filter, `normalBias` 0.25
  and `slopeBias` as point and spot lights, per cascade, and leave out texels whose surface lies behind the receiver's
  plane. A hard edge at 58 degrees sits 0.98 cm out with 2.42 cm texels (5.82 cm before); the same acne limits as
  point and spot below. A thin occluder meeting a receiver lit at about 80 degrees still lets a strip of about 2.4
  texels of depth through at the contact (the Cornell box's red wall under its ceiling, about 4 px). The directional
  Cornell record moved from absolute 567,377 to 478,366 ("Batch 160 job 8" below). Evidence:
  scripts/clustered-shadow-gpu-check.js, native WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.
- KB-LOCALSHADOW-OFFSET1 (2026-11-16): `LocalShadows` point and spot hard shadows compare each texel with the
  receiver's tangent plane, with `normalBias` 0.25 texels and `slopeBias` 0 by default. A floor lit at 49 to 85 degrees
  with true normals, and at 49 to 66 degrees with shading normals tilted 10 degrees, has no acne. Normals tilted 10
  degrees at 80 to 85 degrees fall to about 0.51 at the defaults; `slopeBias: 2` clears them, at the cost of casters
  within about 2 `slopeBias` sin(angle) texels of the receiver. Directional cascades kept the flat compare and 1.5
  texels until KB-SUNSHADOW-OFFSET1 above. Evidence: scripts/clustered-shadow-gpu-check.js, native WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.
  The point Cornell record moved from absolute 730,273 to 597,154 ("Batch 160 job 8" below).
- Batch 170 stats: accepted difference in drawing against stats.js 0.17.0. Margo redraws a 120-sample frame-time
  line and four text rows each 150 ms (7,617 canvas commands in 10 s at 60 Hz); stats.js scrolls a bar graph with
  one image copy per frame (6,090 commands). Command counts are not costs. Both do nothing while idle.
  The change key adds 50 B gzip to the stats root entry (4,934 to 4,984 B, quality baseline updated with the reason).
  [Counts](whitepaper/batch-170-stats.md). Timing pending the quiet rerun.

- SSAO/GTAO view depth (2026-11-11, KB1900): one more `r32float` target, 4 B a pixel (3.7 MB at 1920 x 1080), written
  once a frame by the extractor; the occlusion and blur passes read depth from it at full precision, so an orthographic
  picture does not move with the eye and depth past 65,504 units keeps its occlusion. The G-buffer's own depth stays
  half float. Perspective pictures move by at most 5 display levels from the precision change. Timing pending the
  quiet rerun.

- Tonemap dithering, vignette colour and .3dl (2026-11-15): optional tonemap root gzip 13,030 to 13,434 B (+404 B),
  ceiling 13,421 to 13,838 B; scenery/scenes, which loads Tonemap, ceiling 20,190 to 21,059 B. New entry
  @margoengine/tonemap/3dl 2,240 B min+gzip (ceiling 2,496 B); it shares the Grade bake with export-cube through one
  chunk. The dither and vignette code sits in the effects variant every vignette or grain user already loads, and the
  options are a few validation lines; a split would add an entry and a dynamic import for about 400 B. The effects
  uniform grows from 96 to 128 B (vignette colour and blend; centre, roundness and the dither step).
- Tonemap `dither` adds one code value of the target at most (1/255 on 8-bit, 1/1023 on `rgb10a2unorm`) and nothing on
  float targets; the noise is white (not blue or high-pass shaped), so it is visible as faint fine grain on a still
  frame, and it changes every frame. `.3dl` import reads integer files only, from 2 to 65 samples per axis; an input
  line that is not a uniform grid from 0 (a shaper) is rejected, and the grid vertices are read as evenly spaced over
  0..1 (Flame's 0 64 ... 1023 places the first steps 0.006% of a step off). Without a Lustre header or `outputBits`
  the output depth is guessed as the smallest of 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 bits that holds the largest value and the largest
  input code. `export3dl` clamps to 0..1 and rounds to the output depth (12 bits by default).

- Tonemap white balance (2026-11-15): optional tonemap root gzip 12,684 to 13,030 B (+346 B), ceiling 12,976 to
  13,421 B. White balance is a von Kries adaptation in the Bradford cone space applied as a 3x3 matrix (two 3x3
  constant matrices and the shader's matrix uniform), so it holds from 1667 to 25000 K where the per-channel gain went
  negative below 1903.4 K. The code sits in the effects variant every white-balance user loads; a split would add an
  entry and a dynamic import for under 400 B. The effects uniform grows from 64 to 96 B.

- Batch 164 SSAO/GTAO: 4x removes one early colour resolve; 1x is unchanged.
  The 40 B/pixel reduction counts logical rgba16float resolve source reads and
  destination writes, not physical bandwidth. No shader, quality, target-size,
  rival-speed or sampling reduction is claimed. Timing pending the quiet rerun.
  Native and ANGLE Vulkan pass exact pixels. Default ANGLE D3D11 varies in
  unchanged control frames too (59 channels, at most two display levels after
  resize); this fixture is not certified byte-stable there.

- Batch 165 job 1: optional tonemap root gzip 12,490 to 12,598 B (+108 B), ceiling 12,561 to 12,976 B. Cube parsing retains one row token array, removes the complete line/comment arrays and the redundant RGBA validation pass, with byte-identical samples. Its synchronous root API is preserved; a split would retain that implementation or change the API. Input caps and GPU grading are unchanged. [Work counts and reproduction](whitepaper/batch-165-workcounts.md); timing pending the quiet rerun.

- Security fix sec-sinks (2026-11-10): sciviz PDF export and SVG provenance read SVG with the strict shared XML reader instead of DOMParser (no DTD internal subset, no undefined entities, nesting at most 512); SVG provenance now splices its record into the source text, so the rest of the file is kept byte for byte instead of being reserialized. Annotation, chart axis, dendrogram and MathML overlays are built with createElementNS, setAttribute and text nodes. MathML strings escape an apostrophe as `&apos;` (same parsed text). Sizes min+gzip, ceiling before to measured after: sciviz/pdf 5,700 to 8,100 B and sciviz/provenance 27,770 to 30,369 B (the reader); sciviz/math 5,002 to 5,145, sciviz/format 8,085 to 8,159, sciviz/annotate 7,680 to 7,740 B (escaped markup and DOM builder). The reader is its own chunk, loaded only by pdf and provenance. Core + stage unchanged.
- Batch 179 job 4 size: sciviz/provenance 0 to 24,854 B gzip, ceiling 25,600 B. The entry includes exact portable numeric/GPU argument decoding and its shared colour data, bounded runnable history, compressed PNG/SVG records and build versions. Splitting would duplicate lifecycle handling or require applications to assemble the export/trace feature. Core + stage stays 24,209 B; no speed claim.

- Batch 179 provenance: opt-in /provenance factories or withProvenance() add PNG/SVG records and trace() to an instance. Version 1 records contain the full portable spec, typed-array/source and numeric-JSON hashes, timestamp, exact build-resolved Margo runtime dependency versions, adapter information and browser identity. Browser privacy can leave adapter fields empty; no driver identity is guessed. Compressed PNG iTXt parsing checks every CRC and bounds the input and inflated text to 256 MiB by default. The record SHA-256 detects content changes and is not an authorship signature. Trace defaults to 10000 retained successful calls and a conservative 256 MiB argument budget; exceeding a bound releases history and makes trace() reject, without interrupting figure rendering. Final portable state preserves camera/time, pipeline, selection, callbacks represented as frames and external data writes; application codecs/operator registries remain explicit replay inputs. Returned ESM needs the normal package resolver, bundler or import map. There is no global prototype patch and no core/stage change.



- Batch 163 points frame reuse retains a 144-byte snapshot per PointsPlugin plus a typed view and flag. It removes unchanged camera uploads only; point culling, sorting, quads and draw counts remain as before. Timing pending the quiet rerun; historical slower rows are not reclassified. See [work-count proof](whitepaper/bp-163-workcounts.md).


### Core and stage stress check (check:core-stress) limits

- CPU only, on a fake WebGPU device and frame queue (`tests/support/core-stress.js`): it proves lifecycle order, not
  GPU timing or a browser's real event order. Seeds are fixed: 1,000 a family in `npm run check:core-stress`, 40 and 30
  in the core and stage package tests.
- Passes only stop and start the loop: `dispose()` inside a frame-graph pass is audit row B10, still open. Rows B5, B7
  to B9 and B12 to B19 of the audit and the WebGL2 compatibility renderer are not driven. Stage feature entries are
  covered only through `attachPlugin`.

### Owner/lifetime check (check:owners) limits

- Only packages with a `test(s)/owner-lifetime.fixture.js` are checked; every other selected package is printed as
  pending (30 of 107 on 2026-11-15; bvh, geometry, navmesh and mesh-edit gained fixtures on 2026-11-21, machinery too; kit-react, kit-viz, kit-web and game are excluded as re-export bundles; voxel-edit, voxel-pathtracer, voxel-net and sciviz gained fixtures the same day, the sciviz one covering the layer families listed under owners-b11 in docs/architecture/operational-playbook.md, not every layer; armies, creative and horses gained fixtures after them). Core, math, splines, kinematics-constraints, brep and the physics
  packages (on hold) are excluded with reasons in `scripts/support/owner-lifetime-registry.mjs`; the pure ones are
  read by `tests/owner-exclusions.test.js`, which fails when one gains anything with a lifetime.
- inspector, scene, compute and netcode (2026-11-21) have fixtures although none is a plain engine plugin: each entry's object hangs
  off an engine plugin registration made by `ownedByEngine` (tests/support/owner-shell.js), so every case checks that the
  object releases its listeners, timers, DOM, device patches and context arrays. inspector's panels and tools run in the browser
  leaves only (they need the page's document); its `/gl` entry is WebGL2-only and is covered by test/gl-browser.mjs. scene's
  `extendMeshes` is a permanent, idempotent prototype patch with nothing to release. compute's fixture queues work and reads
  nothing back (the package's browser suites check values), and compute's `/autotune`, `/subgroups`, `/decomp`, `/onnx`,
  `/quant`, `/nn-extra`, `/stream` and `/sparse` solvers hold nothing beyond the arrays of the context. netcode's pure
  entries (interpolation, extrapolation, smoothing, hitboxes, interest, generate) hold nothing; `serve`, `RoomNode.run` and
  `GameServer.run` are real-time loops of another instance that re-arm an abort listener while a case is being made, which
  the observer would count as that case's (covered by transports.test.js and presence.test.js); `PeerMesh` needs a second peer.
- armies, creative and horses (2026-11-21): armies' and horses' entries are async factories (`PersonCrowd.attach`, `addArmy`, `addHorse`,
  `addHorseCrowd`) called from the owner's scene; the baked person is CPU data made once. game is an install profile of generated
  re-exports and is excluded (`tests/owner-exclusions.test.js` fails if it gains anything but `export ... from`). creative's
  `Planet` decodes its maps with `createImageBitmap`, so it is an entry in the browser leaves only; standalone `PostProcessing`
  (`new`, `attach` and in a `PostStack`) is per view since KB-CREATIVE-POSTVIEW1 was fixed (2026-11-25) and is an owner-lifetime entry; creative's `/grass-settings` and shaders hold nothing. creative's CPU leaf gives `navigator.gpu` a
  `getPreferredCanvasFormat` (`bgra8unorm`) in creative's fixture when the runtime has none.
- The CPU model runs the real core scene router and frame graph on the fake GPU of `tests/support/optional-gpu.js`,
  completed in `tests/support/owner-lifetime-node.js` (pipeline layouts, error scopes, texture writes and layer counts,
  limits, the `GPUShaderStage` and `GPUTextureUsage` globals, a canvas context and core's standard lit shader lines). Fixtures never
  shim a device, so the GPU leaf runs the same fixtures with real resources on a real device, native and WebGL2. Glyphs
  are not rasterised in the CPU model.
- Not covered yet: stage feature entries (they take a Stage, not the engine the harness gives; the Stage itself is), `LabelRenderer`
  and `LabelGL` (DOM), `TransmissionLayers` and the `BatchedMesh`, `Fur` and node-material entries of materials, SSR and
  SSGI (a clear-colour buffer stays in the shared per-device cache, docs/known-bugs.md), and SceneFade, which disposes
  itself on device restore by design, so the attached device-loss case cannot hold for it.
- An asynchronous disposal (a promise from `dispose`, a plugin's `dispose` or `Symbol.asyncDispose`) is awaited for
  5,000 ms at most; one that takes longer fails its entry. ecs `ParallelSchedule` runs in the CPU leaf only, with a
  stand-in worker: `SharedArrayBuffer` needs a cross-origin isolated page, and the browser owner page is not one.
- transitions `LiveTransitions` (with `LiveTransitions.custom` and `createLivePresetTransition`) registers in a
  composite scene it creates and owns, which the harness's peer-engine check (the active scene's plugins) does not see;
  its scene disposal is covered by `packages/transitions/test/live.test.js`. `createMaskTransition` needs an
  `ImageData` or `ImageBitmap`, which the CPU model does not have.
- ifc's `parseIFC` runs on a recording web-ifc API and `parseIFCInWorker` on a recording `Worker`: the real web-ifc
  Wasm is the app's peer and its worker needs the app's served web-ifc script, which `packages/ifc/tests/worker.test.js`
  runs in process.
- xr runs on a recording XR system (`navigator.xr`) in both runtimes, since no runtime gives a page a headset, and its
  entries are the XR plugin, an inline session and `XRModels`. The immersive helpers (layers, pointer, locomotion,
  hands, hit test, AR, performance) need an immersive session with `XRGPUBinding` layers and are covered by their own
  tests on recording sessions. XR draws on a device of its own; the CPU model, which has no WebGPU, hands out an inert one.
- cad's B-rep formats (STEP, IGES, JT) need the kernel's Wasm in its worker and are left to
  `packages/cad/test/cad-brep-worker.test.js`; `parseCADAsync` is an entry only where the runtime has workers (the browser
  leaf), and `addCAD` is covered by the stage fixture.
- `TAAUpscale` draws one full-canvas view and throws on the harness's two views by design; its scene detach is
  covered by `packages/taa/test/scene-owner.test.js`.
- A fixture marked `warmUp` (`OIT.addMesh`, loaders `loadOBJ` and `createOBJMesh`, exporters `exportModel`: materials' 1x1 default textures, made once per device on first use and
  kept for the device's life) is attached, drawn and disposed once on each device before the measured attach and again
  after a device loss, so that fixed set counts against no owner. A set that a package's `onDeviceRestored` makes
  eagerly under the owner would still be charged to it; a leak or growth per attach still fails.
- `LayerCompositor` (pixel) runs with a hidden layer: a visible layer draws under the target's default viewport with a
  scissor narrower than the view's (the camera rectangle), pixel-correct but not the exact view viewport and scissor
  the harness requires of each draw.
- mixer's graphs are checked on a recording Web Audio context (`packages/mixer/tests/owner-lifetime.fixture.js`) in both
  leaves: a real context does not expose its nodes' connections, so the browser leaf does not run real audio nodes.
- road is gated, not excluded: `roadGraph` returns a caller-owned compute `CsrMatrix` (GPU buffers). Its fixture is the
  caller: it opens a compute context on the engine's device (a dependency, ended at cleanup), builds the graph, routes over it
  and disposes the matrix and the results; skipping any of those disposals fails the leaf. The context's own
  `dispose()` would free them too, so it is kept out of the owner's release on purpose.
- The biomes scene fix (KB-OWN-BIOMES1) raised two optional entries: `@margoengine/biomes/far` 3,745 to 3,764 B gzip
  and `@margoengine/biomes/objects` 4,246 to 4,278 B, for capturing the scene before their imports; a split would only
  move the same capture into another entry.
- exporters `capture`, `encodeWEBM` and `encodeTexture` are not entries: they need a 2D canvas or VideoEncoder,
  which the CPU leaf does not have, and check:owners has no browser-only entry; capture is synchronous and restores the
  canvas in a `finally`, covered by its own tests.
- The biomes device restore fix (KB-OWN-BIOMES3, density maps made for the device drawing now) took
  `@margoengine/biomes/far` from 3,775 to 3,846 B and `@margoengine/biomes/objects` from 4,288 to 4,322 B (the quality
  gate's bundle measure; ceilings 4,020 and 4,534 B unchanged). The biomes fixture runs one leaf per entry: its four
  entries in one leaf passed natively but ran past the leaf's 180 s limit on the WebGL2 layer of a busy RTX A6000.
- `HTML` and `Inspector` are pending: they build DOM the CPU model does not have, and check:owners has no browser-only
  entry.
- blender's entries are the .margo files without images (parseMargo, loadMargo, parseMargoNodes, loadMargoNodes,
  parseAnimatedMargo, parseMargoCurves, parseMargoComponents): the files with images need an image decoder the CPU leaf
  lacks, and their scene capture is covered by `packages/blender/tests/async-scene.test.js` and
  `packages/blender/tests/lightmap-scene.browser.mjs`; `margoLive` needs an EventSource and a local Blender.
- The tiles fixture streams each renderer's root tile in before the first frame: a tile model is a plugin of its
  renderer's engine, so one arriving while the harness compares the peer engine's plugins would read as a cross-engine
  registration. `ionAsset` and `hostedTileset` need a network service and are not entries.
- Work after an async factory settles (a stream that keeps loading) runs with no owner and is checked only through
  the plugin hooks it runs in.

## Batch 163 light-helper circle retention

A light helper retains 528 bytes of Float64 circle samples and two three-number coordinate arrays only after it draws a circle. This removes repeated geometry preparation work; it changes no precision, edge count or raster work. Timing pending the quiet rerun. [Proof](whitepaper/bp-163-workcounts.md#job-2-live-light-helper-circles).

## K2 rendering and test limits

K2 native glass scope: automatic per-surface snapshots apply to graph-managed Engine scenes. A caller-owned already-open external render pass (`createRenderer`) gets the same linear sum on a display-encoded target when its `draw` call lends `options.snapshot` (KB2281, 2026-11-11): one caller pass end, one colour copy into a context-sized snapshot texture and one reopened pass per glass surface, the cost the graph path pays too. `@margoengine/xr` lends the hook in its eye passes when a drawn model has glass (KB2281-xr): the eye's 4x samples are then stored rather than discarded, plus one resolve-only pass and one reopened eye pass per glass surface; scenes without glass are unchanged. Without the hook it keeps the native tint/add blend, exact only on `rgba16float` (measured: 197, 221, 239 against the linear 143, 154, 165 of 255 over a 128 grey). The native path keeps its existing tone mapping and sightline tint; there is no new HDR-equivalence or refraction claim.

K2 native glass measured gzip before/after: gltf/pbr 78058/79666 B, model 58923/60402 B, progressive 86739/88346 B, worker 78581/80160 B. Core plus stage remains 24209 B. Three optional ceilings grow in the generated sizes baseline; model remains within its existing ceiling. The synchronous draw adapter, shared lifecycle and scene-copy shader stay together; splitting them would introduce a package cycle or an async gap during model draws. No speed claim.


K2 React packed tests: component lifecycle tests continue to import the installed tarball. Tests of contributor browser scripts use MARGOENGINE_TEST_REPOSITORY to locate the actual repository scripts, while keeping the tests themselves in the packed consumer. The consumer installs the root-pinned @playwright/test dev dependency for its typed browser fixture. No runtime package dependency, public export or GPU shader changes.

K2 React lifecycle: portal worlds retain their committed resource through StrictMode replay and release after real unmount; decal parenting follows the live mesh ref and live parent registry. The packed suite exercises React 18.3.1, while workspace CPU/browser checks use the installed React 19 version. Private shader fixtures are bundled test support, not a new public gltf/pbr API or shipped source file.

K2 grass harness: prototype counters are installed after adapter resolution and once per active device prototype. This is test-only instrumentation; package entries and scene rendering are unchanged. Native and full WebGL2 compatibility retain the same more-than-five-frame assertion and 30000 ms page budget.

## Batch 187: existing lightmap parity entries and opaque visibility

Batch 54 already supplies indexed mesh baking on UV1 (the second UV set), progressive WebGPU compute with a live
texture and AbortSignal, per-texel path bounces in ./global, and dominant-direction maps in ./directional. No duplicate
entries were added. The opaque visibility correction changes ./global from 7,770 to 7,781 gzip bytes (minified entry,
bare imports external); its existing 8,007-byte ceiling holds. Existing mesh/gpu/directional entries measure
3,128/7,722/4,215 bytes by the same method. Core and stage sources are unchanged.

Opaque quad backs now block area-light shadow segments and diffuse paths in both quad and path modes. Their back
sides supply no emission or reflected light. This matches the existing direct point/spot/directional baker's two-sided
shadow visibility. Alpha omission and glass transport retain their explicit visibility rules. Surface transport still
uses the stored texel's front normal and diffuse radiance; it does not add two-sided emission or a new material model.
The historical Cornell loss was a bounce-count mismatch in the reference (KB2604h, fixed 2026-11-11); this change makes no accuracy-parity claim.

Progressive splat cancellation rejects pending consumers and requests async
iterator return without waiting indefinitely for producer IO or cleanup. The
producer owns external work; its return implementation must release that work.
Aborting between buffered batches prevents further decoded records. See
docs/splats-progressive.md for exact cancellation regressions and sources.

Batch 175 job 1: sciviz/omezarr opens OME-NGFF 0.4/Zarr2 and 0.5/Zarr3 multiscales with named spatial/time/channel axes, composed dataset/group scale and translation, one bricked source per stored level, and a dyadic renderer adapter. Reads retain source coordinates; stored LOD samples use nearest-neighbour physical-coordinate sampling, not a claim that arbitrary stored pyramids equal on-the-fly box averaging. Supply volume.bounds and a known range when attaching its source to brickedVolume. Each level also exposes its existing ZarrArray for typed exact-region reads. Rendering is float32; 64-bit integer Zarr reads use the existing Float64 representation and are exact only through 2^53. Arrays are 2D through 5D; renderer volumes need three nondegenerate dimensions. Unknown nonsingleton axes require selection before use. Channel and image default to zero; frame comes from BrickRequest. No IO or GPU allocations occur on import.

HTTP/S3 stores support absolute and suffix Range reads, credential headers, a base URL query (signed or SAS token) kept on every object request, missing-key-only 404 handling and lifetime/request cancellation. Defaults: maxBytes and maxDecodedBytes 67,108,864 bytes each, channel 0, image 0, 16 cached Zarr shard indexes and no cached payloads. A server ignoring Range may return at most maxBytes. Shard indexes use bytes (either endian) plus optional CRC32C; inner shapes must divide shard shape. Standard one-level sharding is supported; nested sharding and codecs outside the documented pipeline reject. Blosc1 supports memcpy, BloscLZ, LZ4/LZ4HC, zlib and zstd, byte and bit shuffle; extended Blosc2 filter pipelines and legacy Snappy reject. Zstd dictionary frames retain the existing decoder's explicit unsupported result. LZ4 includes numcodecs length-prefixed blocks and N5 Java streams with 28-bit seeded xxHash checksums. N5 fixed-size scalar blocks support raw, gzip (a zlib stream when the compression attributes set useZlib: true, any other non-boolean useZlib rejects at open), bzip2, XZ, LZ4, Blosc and zstd; variable-length/object blocks are not scalar-volume arrays. Precomputed supports raw, grayscale/RGB JPEG and compressed_segmentation, unsharded and identity-hashed sharded scales; other image/segmentation encodings and Murmur-hashed shards reject explicitly. These limits concern codec/storage variants, not silent missing-data fallbacks.

Scale evidence uses work and bytes, with no timed benchmark: a 10^12-sample synthetic array opens with zero chunk reads and a one-sample ROI reads exactly one 8-byte chunk. The three real regions each return 32,768 float32 samples (131,072 bytes), rendered as nine resident bricks in 105,040 GPU bytes on native WebGPU and the full WebGL2 layer. The original full dimensions are IDR 2048x2048x1937, N5 12000x1600x6368 and FlyEM 34427x39725x41394. This proves bounded selected-region work, not full-dataset residency or a measured speed comparison. Independent lossless IDR/N5 values match all samples exactly; existing JPEG/Pillow IDCT rounding differs by at most 1 on the recorded FlyEM sample. No lossless precision or JPEG bit-exactness claim is made for that lossy source.
API lock Day 0 (2026-11-10): core/stage are locked by package, including future entries. Other reported packages
warn in watch pending Day 1 promotion. The declaration-text gate does not prove runtime semantics or general subtype
compatibility. Only additions, trailing optional parameters and optional relaxations are recognized as compatible;
other declaration edits conservatively break. Approval binds entry, symbol, change and an eight-character SHA-1 of
the old block (review identity, not a security hash). Coverage requires resolved reports per non-alias exports entry.
See [API lock](conventions.md#api-lock) for policy, sources and regression evidence.

Batch 190 job 2: `@margoengine/oit/precise` adds PreciseOIT, 3777 B min+gzip (new from 0 B, ceiling 4033 B). Four R32F sums plus R16F revealage cost 18 bytes per pixel at 1x, 72 at 4x; five simultaneous colour attachments are required. Native WebGPU needs Engine.create's `features: ['float32-blendable']`; full WebGL2 needs EXT_float_blend and renderable R32F targets (4x R32F renderbuffers for MSAA). Missing capabilities reject before buffer allocation. No float32 filtering is required. The weighted approximation, depthScale default (camera-target distance), order default 8, material texture budget and sorted handling of transmission/custom blending/depth overrides are unchanged. No `blending` option is exposed by this entry. Float32 sums have the finite f32 range, so total weighted radiance must stay below roughly 3.4e38; the final HDR target still sets the output range. Core and stage remain 24209 B combined gzip.

Batch 190 job 1: `@margoengine/oit/peel` adds PeelOIT, 3037 B min+gzip (new from 0 B, ceiling 3293 B). It captures ten nearest distinct depths by default, adjustable with a positive safe integer `layers`; more layers cost one geometry redraw and one resolve draw each. Storage is `12 * layers + 8` bytes per pixel, 128 B/pixel at the default, independent of scene MSAA. Exact order holds at distinct raster depths; coplanar fragments share one layer and the last submitted wins. The peels test only their own depth buffer, not the opaque one (opaque depth is applied when the layers resolve), so transparent fragments hidden behind opaque surfaces still take layers: `layers` must cover them too (audit 2026-11-15). Transparent coverage is single sample even over a 4x opaque target; post FXAA works. This matches the documented rival antialiasing restriction. RGBA16F captured radiance still has a 65504 maximum. Full WebGL2 compatibility requires renderable floating targets; no fragment storage or float32 blending. Refraction, transmission/custom blending, depth overrides and particles remain on their existing paths; addEffect explicitly refuses this model-only pass. Core and stage remain unchanged at 24209 B combined gzip.

Batch 204 job 2: optional exporters/textures is 10015 B gzip (new from 0 B),
ceiling 10316 B. Resize accepts at most 16384 per side and 16777216 pixels for
input, output and horizontal intermediate (Float64 RGBA, at most 512 MiB).
WebP/AVIF/JPEG encoding requires the requested platform canvas encoder;
unsupported or silently substituted formats reject with a coded error naming
the missing MIME. Chromium 157 encoded WebP but lacked AVIF encoding in both
backend checks. PNG works without canvas for RGBA input. Native encode timeout
is 30 seconds; native quality and low-alpha canvas rounding are platform-defined.
AVIF byte input currently needs caller-decoded RGBA. AVIF uses the published
draft glTF extension contract, with optional PNG/JPEG fallback; no ratification
or portable AVIF encoder claim. Details and defaults: exporter-textures.md.

Batch 256 migration: `@margoengine/netcode/migrate` exports HostMigration and its
typed options/state. Give each peer the same schema, initial state, frame and
host (default lowest id), and reliable full-mesh Connection links. It owns and
closes these links, forwards other message kinds to earlier handlers, and uses
wire prefix 112 for migration. Up to 64 peers; checkpoint default 1 MiB, maximum
16 MiB. Initial frame defaults to 0, operation/recovery/wait timeout to 10 seconds.
Frames, sequences and authority epochs are unsigned 32-bit; create a new session
before overflow. `confirm(state, frame, { signal })` serially prepares and commits
on every connected peer and resolves only after all stored acknowledgements.
`confirmed` is a detached locally committed copy; await confirm before treating
it as globally confirmed. Exactly two committed checkpoints are retained.
Host disconnect selects the lowest surviving id, restores the newest common
checkpoint and completes a survivor acknowledgement barrier before isHost becomes
true. `handoff(target, { signal })` moves authority without leaving. Only isHost
may simulate/publish authority work; use waitForHost to resume after migration.
Abort/timeout of a publishing operation retires that session and closes its links
rather than reusing an uncertain checkpoint. Cancelling waitForHost only cancels
that wait. Trusted peers and a connected surviving full mesh are required; arbitrary
network partitions, malicious voters, durable restart and adding peers to a live
session require external membership/fencing or a fresh session. No consensus or
partition-safety claim is made. The public role-switch behavior of Photon Realtime
is covered, with explicit checkpoint replication/restoration supplied here.
New migration entry gzip is 8,351 B (previously absent), ceiling 8,607 B. Complete
checkpoint validation, two-phase replication, handoff and recovery remain in one
optional entry. Splitting them would expose protocol internals and duplicate
session lifecycle wiring. Core and stage remain 23,950 B combined gzip.

Batch 256 Rust generation: `@margoengine/netcode/generate-rust` exports
generateRust(schema.json or compiledSchema, { source? }). Output is standalone
Rust 2021 requiring Rust 1.82 or newer, with no crate dependencies. Each schema
type becomes Msg<Name>, each field f_<name>, maps BTreeMap<u32, T>, enums u32
wire indices and optionals Option<Box<T>>. Native methods encode, decode,
encode_delta, decode_delta and same use the runtime codec's wire contract and
normalized SCHEMA_HASH. f32 fields use native f32; quantized values use f64.
Encoding and decoding return margo_wire::Result, validate limits and reject
trailing bytes, invalid UTF-8, non-finite floats and malformed map/mask data.
Nesting above 256 codec calls returns an error to bound untrusted recursion.
This is a generator and native protocol codec, not a new engine Wasm bundle.
New entry gzip is 9,827 B (previously absent), ceiling 10,122 B. Schema validation,
complete codec emission and native data conversion stay together; a split would
force generator consumers to assemble a second template entry without saving
runtime application bytes. Core and stage remain unchanged.

Batch 256 presence: `@margoengine/netcode/presence` exposes RoomPresence,
PresenceStore, MemoryPresence, StorePresence, openSqlitePresence and RoomNode.
Run each node's `run({ signal })` promise and handle its rejection; `close()` or
`await using` withdraws it after in-flight heartbeat/service tasks have stopped.
Lease defaults to 10 seconds, heartbeat to 1 second (strictly shorter than lease),
IPC timeout to 5 seconds and poll interval to 20 ms. List snapshots are eventually
consistent; `sync()` refreshes them immediately. Remote reserve always executes
on the room owner and returns its endpoint and one-time join credential. Failed
or uncertain RPCs are never replayed. A cancellation after the owner claims a
request may leave its reserved seat until normal reservation expiry. Private
and full rooms remain routable by id but are hidden from public list results.
The shared-store adapter requires atomic take and expiry-aware reads. The supplied
SQLite WAL adapter uses Node's lazy built-in sqlite module and a local file shared
by processes on one host; network filesystems and multi-host SQLite are unsupported.
Implement the public store/presence contract for a network database. The control
plane is trusted server code; applications authenticate matchmaking endpoints.
Presence entry gzip is 6,219 B (new entry, previously absent), ceiling 6,475 B.
The optional entry retains the complete shared-store adapter and native SQLite
path; splitting would add another public adapter entry without reducing room
control-plane work. Core and stage stay unchanged at 23,950 B combined gzip.

Batch 256 lobby: `@margoengine/netcode/lobby` provides `LobbyRoom` and `RoomLobby`.
List results contain room id/name, detached scalar metadata, connected clients,
reserved/reconnecting seats and capacity. Name and metadata filters are exact;
locked, full and private rooms are omitted. Reservations default to 15 seconds,
accept 1..2147483647 integer milliseconds, and hold capacity through async auth.
Join with `RoomsClient.joinById(roomId, { seatToken }, joinOptions)`. Join options
come from the server reservation, and the token is consumed once after successful
authentication. Cancellation/expiry/disposal free holds. Applications expose the
lobby over their own authenticated HTTP API and protect tokens with TLS; holding
a token grants its reserved join identity. Ordinary Room subclasses can be listed
but require LobbyRoom to reserve. Entry gzip is 4,183 B (new entry, previously
absent); its size ceiling is 4,439 B. Keeping the capacity-safe reservation and
listing together avoids a second room wrapper. Core and stage are unchanged.

Compatibility compute pipeline binding counts obey `device.limits` on every
compute route. Explicit layouts count all compute-visible entries across groups,
even unused entries; external textures consume four sampled-texture slots, one
sampler and one uniform. Overflow is a validation error and async creation
rejects with `GPUPipelineError`. The complete shader readback leaf, including
validation and recovery, passes on native WebGPU and full compat. Lower-tier and
other package gaps remain separately listed. Batch 273 failure 18 entry gzip:
root 105,454 B, device 105,996 B, XR 105,896 B, tiers 105,955 B. Core + stage
remain 23,950 B; no ceiling was increased.

Verify's shadow archive store retains its 5 GiB cap and per-write oldest-first
eviction. Windows reads fresh enumeration metadata through its system .NET
runtime rather than individually statting every ordinary archive; a helper
invocation is bounded at 60 seconds. Links/directories and non-Windows platforms
retain Node stat behavior. Every insertion still inventories the full directory,
so enumeration/transfer work scales with archive count. No metadata is retained
between evictions. This changes tooling work, not engine size.

GPU commands run at once (Scott, 2026-11-16), however many other jobs use the GPU. `scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs` starts its command at once and keeps one limit: `--max=<min>` (default 10) ends the command's whole process tree and exits 124 with `TIMEOUT after N min`. Heavy load can make a GPU driver reset or a browser lose its device (the restore paths cover that). Proof: `tests/run-with-timeout.test.js`.

`savePrefilteredEnvironment` saves the lighting as it was when called (one submitted snapshot, so a reblend during
the save does not reach the file) and rejects with code `state` while `environment.refreshPending`; the readback holds
a second copy of every mip in mapped buffers until it resolves. The one-submit save took the
`@margoengine/environment/prefiltered` entry from 3,949 B to 4,007 B min+gzip (ceiling raised with it, KB-A3d).

Batch 234 independent caustics continuation: the optional entry is 8961 B
min+gzip (8122 B at the initial checkpoint), ceiling 8378 -> 9230 B. The extra

Core plus stage remains current main's 23950 B, below 25000 B; this job changes

Current acceptance and retained history: [caustics record](water-caustics.md).

Historical initial caustics checkpoint: `@margoengine/water/caustics` measures 8122 B
min+gzip (8378 B ceiling), absent before this optional entry. Its three RGB
flux-vector maps cost `24 * resolution ** 2 * layers` bytes: 18 MiB at the
256-square/12-slice defaults, plus captures and stack targets. Sides 32..2048,
2..32 horizontal height slices, camera-centred map width 0.1..100000 m and

now pass; the following record preserves the earlier checkpoint status. [Research and current evidence](water-caustics.md).

Batch 213 job 1: optional `rigging/vrm0` is 6,543 B min+gzip (previously absent;

## Owned Zstd destination limits

The internal shared reader's optional destination is exclusive caller storage
until the promise settles. Its capacity adds a limit to `maxOutputSize`; it
never grows or substitutes the buffer. Returned bytes are a prefix view.
Input/output ranges must not overlap. Do not resize, detach, transfer or grow
its Wasm memory while borrowed. On rejection its contents are unspecified.
The existing 256MiB output and128MiB window defaults, dictionary refusal,
checksum verification, concatenated/skippable frames and cancellation remain.
This does not replace the shipped Basis transcoder or close its RSS losses.


## Batch 134 corpus, upload and memory limits

[Current combined-Wasm evidence](whitepaper/results/batch-134-corpus-uploads-memory.json)
contains 51 real primary seeds / 17,908 historical-target calls, plus 32,784
new scalar ABI calls and 628 authored-container calls. Complete missing-target
and public integration fuzz proof remains open. The same 1,296 scalar images
round-trip 131,581,656 compressed bytes on real RTX A6000 WebGPU. This is
compressed-byte transport; no sampled-pixel, full mip-chain texture or public
loader acceptance. Native WebGPU exposes no ETC2/EAC support on this adapter;
993 such images remain unproven rather than passed.

Fresh old/new processes retain all outputs on all 173 accepted scalar pairs.
Maximum Wasm high water is 17,170,432 old / 10,747,904 new bytes, with no
per-pair Wasm loss. Maximum process RSS is 112,460 old / 113,708 new KiB;
25 per-pair RSS losses remain open. RSS includes runtime/input/output and
allocator behavior; it is not just Wasm pages or peak-live allocations. The
JS adapter materializes a full Zstd level then copies it into Wasm, adding

## Batch 171 tracer numerical limits and size attribution

The CPU streamline step is a maximum arc step, adaptively shortened. Local error estimate is the RK4
step-doubling norm / 15, bounded by 1e-6 times current arc step; it is not a guaranteed global error bound.
Unresolved stages/turns halve; progress stops at max(1e-6 min(step, grid spacing), 32 epsilon
max(abs(position components), step)), as well as minSpeed/masks/boundaries/maxSteps. No critical-point
location, global separatrix preservation or closed-orbit classification is claimed. True cycles are retained.
/tubes remains 2,533 B gzip, /grids 23,735 B, LIC 23,461 B, flow 8,665 B. The tracer repair changes
/maths 5,389 -> 5,703 B (ceiling 5,638 -> 5,959) and root 50,303 -> 50,599 B (within 51,813).

lookup/data, proven by an isolated local-history substitution with the identical measurement method.

Owned Chromium runs under a browser host process (`scripts/support/browser-host.mjs`,
2026-11-10): the suite ends the browser through the host, is acknowledged as soon
as every process has been ended (on Windows the listed children's kill runs in Windows
PowerShell, whose start takes 0.6 to about 4 s and is bounded at 10 s, KB-HOST-KILLLATE1),
and waits for the kernel's teardown of the
ended processes only up to 2,000 ms, then moves on. The host waits up to 120 s more
and records any survivor in `test-results/browser-host-survivors.log`. A following GPU job can
therefore start while the kernel is still freeing the ended browser's GPU
allocations (measured 65 ms to 1.2 s beside the batches, 8.7 s beside verify). The
30,000 ms shutdown budget and 5,000 ms process-list bound are unchanged.

Sciviz `/flow` supplies fixed-step RK4 pathlines/streaklines and GPU particles/trails on regular 2D/3D grids
with linear temporal interpolation. Adaptive error control and extrapolation are not supplied. The default
10,000-step budget accepts 1 to 1,000,000; at most 4,096 frames. CPU input copies plus
output/final-copy/scratch are capped at 128 MiB, excluding caller input and module overhead. Copy/integration
chunks are 16,384 samples/128 steps. The feature-local Wasm is 7,916 bytes, capped below 16,000 raw and 8,000 gzip
by CPU tests. It loads lazily per call; root/fallback do not load it. Samples are float32 and arithmetic/output
float64. Streaklines reuse one instance/field copy for 1..4096 ordered releases, returning observation-time
endpoints and NaN gaps for invalid/unfinished releases. GPU transport is forward only; each RK stage uses
float32 normalised coordinates/velocities, with four stages and an accepted-endpoint validity check. The
analytic GPU/CPU test bound is 0.0002 distance units on its stated fields, not a general error guarantee.
GPU layer creation copies fields; its 1..1000000 particles and 2..256 history samples (defaults 1024/32)
must fit 128 MiB of GPU buffers and device binding/buffer limits. CPU copies are additional. Bounds/widths
must survive float32; normalised velocities and step-times-velocity are at most float32 max/16 for arithmetic
headroom. Lifetime defaults to 10 time units, expires at step endpoints and fixed-seed respawn defaults true.
Width defaults 2 CSS pixels (positive, at most 64), opacity 0.8, sRGB colour #7ddcff. Heads are squares;
history fades quadratically and never bridges respawn generations. Uniform/random/rake/region seed layouts
are deterministic for a given seed/partition on one backend; cross-device bit identity is unclaimed.
Actual device replacement replays accepted partitions, bounded by maxSteps; advance/draw do no position
readback. Explicit readPositions has a 30000 ms default timeout. WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility pass
numeric/pixel/lifecycle tests; native WebGL2 flow remains pending with batch 181. NOAA daily means do not
establish observed tracks or forecast accuracy. The official Moving wind example preserves these limitations.
The `/flow` JavaScript entry is 8,665 B gzip (raised optional ceiling 8,854 B);
the previous CPU-only size was 2,130 B (ceiling 2,386 B). Root was 36,916 B, driver 4,476 B (retired since), Wasm 7,916 raw /
3,585 gzip B; their ceilings are unchanged by flow. Keeping one coherent flow entry avoids an artificial loader
between transport, seed semantics and owned replay state.
No core/stage implementation change is part of this feature.

Voxel streaming memory admission (2026-11-09): `VoxelStreamer.memoryBudget` limits loaded chunk typed-array
bytes, not total process memory. Both ready and loading jobs reserve the loaded chunks' mean size; a finished
stored or generated chunk joins only when its actual `byteLength` fits after LRU eviction outside the load range.
A chunk that cannot fit remains pending, including one larger than the entire budget. Initial unknown-size loads,
pending results, workers, stores and failed saves are outside this budget. Edits, externally added chunks and
budget reductions can leave the protected load range over budget; further admission stops. Deterministic stored,
variable-size and packed-worker regressions are in `packages/voxel/tests/streamer.test.js`.

Sciviz CPU extraction foundation (2026-11-10): `@margoengine/sciviz/fallback` exports `marchingCubes`, not a
WebGL2 figure adapter yet. The JavaScript entry is 2,002 bytes gzip against a new 2,258-byte ceiling; it loads one

The same derived case table produces normalized positions and unnormalized outward gradients, eight float32
words per vertex, 96 bytes per triangle. Default `maxTriangles` is floor(128 MiB / 96); field, cases, tables and
vertices together are capped at 2 GiB, excluding the returned copy and allocator overhead. Dimensions are at
least two per axis; the input length must match; the level must be finite in float32. Both passes yield every
16,384 cells for cancellation. NaN samples follow the GPU's comparison/interpolation behaviour. All 256 cases,
non-cubic row tails, chunk boundaries and the real MRI are checked in `packages/sciviz/tests/fallback.test.js`.

KB1405, native sciviz WebGL2 driver retired (2026-11-11, Scott's yes): `@margoengine/sciviz/webgl2` and
`attachWebGL2` are removed, with the root's type-only driver seam. The driver drew CPU-backed surfaces, bars,
histograms and heatmaps on the small preview renderer and refused axes, points, lines, volumes, slices and isosurfaces,
so it was a partial copy of the figure and about 45 optional entries would still have refused it. Every figure
now draws through `createFallbackFigure` on the complete layer, which the evidence above matches to native WebGPU.
A device class that only the native driver served does not exist: its shaders needed `highp` fragment precision like the
layer's tiers, and `/tiers` covers half-float and LDR targets. Sizes: the 4,476 B entry and its 4,667 B ceiling are
gone; the sciviz root measured 63,709 B min+gzip (bare imports external, rolldown) before and 63,559 B after; the
CPU extractor entry stays 2,223 B; core + stage stays 24,812 B under 25,000 B. WebGPU steady-frame work counts do not
change (the removed branches ran only on the preview backend). The regression tests are the new
`createFallbackFigure` cases in `fallback-browser.mjs` and the isolation cases in `backend-isolation.test.js`.

Sciviz restoration (2026-11-10): CPU-backed layers rebuild on a replacement device; `Figure.ready()` waits for
isosurface reconstruction. Pending old-device extractions reject with code `state`. Caller-owned GPU arrays
cannot survive device loss without a CPU copy: their layers hide and must be recreated on the replacement
device. CPU isosurfaces retain 4 bytes per voxel; meshes retain positions, normals and values (28 bytes per
corner), graphs retain 12 bytes per node for positions plus 4 bytes per node value and 8 bytes per edge, and map
tiles retain 4 bytes per decoded pixel for restoration. Bricked volumes reread their source.
3D axis labels use 8 CSS pixels of clearance; crowded tick labels are omitted, with data ticks and grid lines
unchanged. Active bricked frame aborts cancel source signals and late publication; standalone `ready` aborts
cancel only the wait. Regression coverage: `packages/sciviz/tests/restoration-browser.mjs`,
`entries-browser.js`, `updates.test.js` and `demos-browser.mjs` (head/stars at 390 x 844 and 1440 x 900).

Sciviz volume and isosurface grids require integer dimensions of at least two samples per axis; single slices
belong in a 2D `Figure.heatmap`. Axis errors are reported separately from mismatched sample counts.
Overlapping isosurface extractions and bricked frame requests run in request order. An isosurface extraction
holds the displayed and pending vertex buffers (96 bytes per triangle in each); an aborted or failed extraction
keeps the displayed surface. `Figure.replace(old, next)` rebuilds a trace and briefly holds both layers rather
than updating its buffers in place. Await the replacement builder and call `replace` immediately, with no render
or wait between them. Serialize asynchronous changes with `Figure.timeline`; a disposed timeline does not
cancel user callback work. These guarantees are covered by the sciviz unit and browser suites; no speed claim.

2026-11-26: core bug fix KB-CLEAR-CAPTURE1, a background clears a capture's linear target (a post effect's float capture) with the colour decoded from sRGB, took core from 22,225 B to 22,262 B and core + stage from 24,846 B to 24,892 B; 2026-11-14: core bug fix, the frame delta stays one number object, so onFrame callbacks and render no longer allocate a number each frame, took core from 22,217 B to 22,219 B and left core + stage at 24,839 B;
