ATMO-09's Col de Porte diagnostic holds out three later snow-skin temperatures in each of two weather episodes.
In the end-labelled default run, hourly temperature RMSE is 4.87 K at night and 1.01 K by day. The last nighttime
mean is 6.84 K warm and exceeds even the study's rough radiometric sensitivity. The emissivity and time-label
sensitivities retain the nighttime warm bias. Independent turbulent flux, melt and multi-site validation remain open.
The optional surface-energy entry is 7,459 B min+gzip. Each Wasm variant is 7,688 B raw and 2,934 B gzip.
The standalone helper is 654 B gzip.

### React page

What a minimal React page downloads, and why it is larger than core + stage (23,924 B gzip). The cube page of the
bundler matrix (`Canvas`, `Mesh`, `BoxGeometry`, `PbrMaterial`, `useFrame`, and `OrbitControls` from
`@margoengine/react/controls`), built by Vite 8.3.4, React 19.3 and `@margoengine/react` installed alone with
`@margoengine/controls` (2026-10-27), measured from the build's source maps (minified bytes per package; gzip is each
package's own gzip size, scaled so the parts add up to the chunk's). Core lights every scene by default
(a sun and an ambient term), so this is also the minimal lit page.

| Part | Minified B | Gzip B | Needed for a lit scene? |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `react-dom` (client) | 206,925 | 62,263 | Yes: the app's own UI runtime, not Margo's |
| `react` + `scheduler` | 11,635 | 4,430 | Yes: the app's own |
| `@margoengine/core` (engine, renderer, Wasm kernel, camera, shaders, geometry) | 49,485 | 19,056 | Yes |
| `@margoengine/react` (components, internal, assets, the shadows hook) | 14,241 | 5,488 | Yes: `Canvas`, `Mesh` and the hooks |
| `@margoengine/stage` | 2,771 | 1,405 | Not to draw (core draws and lights the cube); `Canvas` wraps its engine in the stage it hands to `onCreated` and `<Stage>` |
| Vite runtime (preload helper, module preload polyfill), app code and `@margoengine/math` (170 B) | 3,135 | 1,609 | The build's own |
| **Entry, requested before the page runs** | **288,234** | **94,251** | Budget 100,000 B gzip |
| `@margoengine/controls/orbit` + its view helpers + profiles, when `OrbitControls` mounts | 17,999 | 6,951 | Yes, for orbiting |
| **Everything the page fetches** | **306,233** | **101,202** | |

React and React DOM are 66% of the page; Margo's part (core, stage, bindings) is 25,949 B gzip (27,028 B before the
stage feature entries and the React subpaths of 2026-10-27, which took 3,089 B of minified loaders out of the stage). Nothing optional is in
the entry: `PbrMaterial` is core's material and pulls in no other package.

- **Fixed (2026-10-26):** `OrbitControls`, `MapControls` and `CadControls` loaded the `@margoengine/controls` index,
  so mounting them fetched TransformControls, DragControls, the gizmo and the `@margoengine/bvh` raycaster as one
  112,655 B (39,072 B gzip) chunk. They now load `@margoengine/controls/orbit` and `/profiles`, `ArcballControls`
  loads `/arcball` and `TransformControls` loads `/transform`: the mount costs 6,951 B gzip, and a Vite build emits
  107,027 B gzip in all instead of 135,875 B.
- **Emitted, never fetched:** the arcball chunk (3,192 B gzip). Nothing else: since 2026-10-27 neither `Canvas` nor
  the stage reaches an optional package, so there are no stand-in stubs either.
- **A textured model** (`<Gltf src="BoxTextured.glb">` from `@margoengine/react/gltf`, with `@margoengine/gltf/pbr`
  installed): the entry grows by
  1,750 B gzip (the `Model` binding), and mounting it fetches gltf/pbr (175,257 B, 56,074 B gzip: glTF parsing, the
  PBR material and shader, compression hooks) plus the model. The Draco and Basis Wasm are emitted for files that use
  them; this one does not, and the page does not request them.
- **Through `margoengine/react`:** a page emits no Draco or Basis file. `Model`, `Fbx`, `Animation` and the `materials`
  components reach those decoders, so they are separate entries (`margoengine/react/gltf`, `/fbx`, `/animation`,
  `/materials`); Vite copies a `new URL` file when it reads a module, before tree-shaking.
- **Through a kit or `materials`, `animation`, `fbx`:** no Draco or Basis file either. Only the root of `@margoengine/gltf/pbr`
  names the decoders; packages that draw models use `@margoengine/gltf/pbr-model`, and `loadGLTF` is imported from
  `margoengine/gltf/pbr`, not from `margoengine/game`, `/web` or `/viz`.
- Still on the controls index: `PointerLock` (from `@margoengine/react/controls`), because `@margoengine/controls` has no
  pointer-lock entry; a page that does not use it never emits it.

## External video materials (2026-11-08)

`@margoengine/video/material` adds a caller-owned `HTMLVideoElement` or `VideoFrame` to a `Material.features` list. No JS-side frame upload occurs. The browser/driver may still copy or convert internally; platform zero-copy and throughput are unmeasured. A frame is imported per draw, one sampler per device; there are no mipmaps or repeat wrapping. UV0 (default) and UV1 are supported; `flipY` defaults to true, matching Texture's image orientation (first row at v=1); false puts it at v=0. Sources must be ready/open and origin-clean. WebGL2 returns `MargoError` code `unsupported` with a help link. Core's compact material has no feature slot. Custom WGSL must retain the standard surface/base-colour hook. The existing material's own maps, lighting and other features keep their own costs. External textures consume four sampled-texture slots, one implicit sampler and one uniform slot, in addition to the explicit filtering sampler; a fully mapped material can exceed a device's default limits. Alpha affects colour rendering; auxiliary caster/picking passes retain the material's existing alpha inputs. Generated colour frames and a canvas MediaStream on the RTX A6000/Edge prove imports across tasks, no material-path frame uploads and sRGB byte accuracy within 2 of 255 at 1x and 4x MSAA. Real movie files, other adapters, browser-internal copies, speed and custom shader combinations are unmeasured. Run `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node packages/video/test/material-check.mjs` after a package build.

## Page canvas recording (2026-11-08)

`@margoengine/video/record` records origin-clean page canvases with MediaRecorder, on WebGPU, WebGL2 or 2D. Container support and codecs are the browser's choice: default WebM, optional MP4, otherwise coded unsupported with a help link. The caller supplies optional live audio tracks, cloned so originals remain owned by the caller. No audio mixing is performed. All compressed chunks stay in memory until stop. Real-time capture can drop frames or shorten media on a busy/background page; no exact duration/frame count or A/V synchronization bound is claimed. Stop waits for the final chunk; abort, disposal and errors release owned tracks and discard the result. No Node/OffscreenCanvas API or alternate codec fallback is included. The real RTX A6000/Edge check decodes WebM (VP8/Opus) and MP4 (H.264/Opus) from both backends: generated colour and a tone are stand-ins. Other browsers, players, codecs, microphone permission paths and long recordings are unmeasured. Entry 1,140 B gzip; budget 1,396 B. No speed claim. See LIM-571. WebKit (Playwright WebKit 27.2 on the Apple M6, 2026-11-10): a WebM recorded there plays back about 10 levels too bright in WebKit's own `<video>` ((61, 113, 164) for #336699) although its VP8 frames hold the right BT.601 limited-range code (Y 95, Cb 159, Cr 100, read raw through WebCodecs and by ffmpeg). Margo does not switch such a caller to MP4: the WebM is correct and asked for; a caller who will play the file back in Safari can pass `format: 'mp4'`, whose H.264 draws (50, 101, 151) there. `packages/video/test/record-check.mjs` accepts that colour only as the named WebKit defect and only with those encoded values (docs/known-bugs.md).

## 360 and stereo video (2026-11-08)

`@margoengine/video/360` uses UV0 of `sphereGeometry`, an unlit back-sided material and a camera at its centre. Image centre -Z, right +X, top +Y. Mono (default) spans the whole source; stereo-left-right holds one complete panorama per half, selected explicitly for a screen material (eye left by default). Stereo sources need at least two pixels across, enforced before binding. Sampling clamps half a texel inside each eye; no mips or repeat wrapping. WebGL2 receives coded unsupported with a help link. One video feature per material; playback and source lifetime remain caller-owned. XR reuses native `XRLayers.video` with an equirectangular sphere, automatic compositor eye choice and radius 0 at infinity; it requires the draft WebXR Layers API and XRMediaBinding. Missing XR support propagates the existing XR error. Generated colour panoramas prove six screen directions and both eyes on RTX A6000/Edge; an integrated stand-in session/binding proves XR delegation and layer lifecycle. No headset, real movie, other browser/GPU or speed evidence. Entry 1,694 B gzip, budget 1,881 B. LIM-573.

## Own 2D certified geometry and solver evidence (2026-11-08)

The optional Rust kernel's exact rectangle SAT path requires a current canonical axis rectangle in pair-local
coordinates, finite vertex squared norms at most 2^120 and B-normal squared norms at most 4. The preferred-face
distance certificate additionally requires a coordinate-magnitude bound M in [1,2^20], positive finite A-face
separation and its finite radius/speculation/result checks. These restrict eligibility for an optimization;
all other inputs retain the full prior collision path. [Proof](architecture/physics2d-manifold-proof.md) and
[entry 101](whitepaper/perf-history.md) record the precise guards and unchanged native/Wasm hashes.

The two-point block solver remains production behavior. Earlier per-point alternatives did not meet all contracts
and establish a browser gain. All original accuracy bars remain unchanged. The subsequent sustained-support fix
establishes the required centered 1:1000 contact stack and deliberately re-pins the mixed scene; see the
[support contract](#own-2d-sustained-contact-support). Owned-2D CCD remains separate T-11 / 127.y work, distinct
from existing 1000:1 joint-chain and 3D CCD evidence.
After browser diagnostics: Edge 3.66/1.69/14.52 ms and Firefox 3.50/1.52/11.20 ms for Margo/Box2D/Rapier; separate
loaded sessions cannot prove before/after speed. The Box2D goal remains open and quiet reruns are required.

### Own 2D input validation

The raw Rust kernel under `packages/physics2d/kernel` exposes checked `Result<_, PhysicsError>` body/shape/chain
creation, world stepping and handle operations, bounds queries, scalar/coherent/four-pair and smooth-chain collision.
The public Rust `solver::solve` entry also checks current inputs and derived outputs; its direct-call substep
must be positive and representable. `World::step` retains its validated nonpositive-step no-op policy.
Use `?` to propagate a refusal, or read `PhysicsError::code()` and `help()`; the latter points to this section.
The Rapier-backed TypeScript facade is a separate API. Pure math and mass-property utilities are not all checked
entry points; in particular, `mass::mass_of` retains its direct `MassData` return.

| Code | Refusal |
| --- | --- |
| `PHYSICS2D_NOT_FINITE` | A required finite input or current-state value is NaN or infinite |
| `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_CORE` | An invalid active core count or radius would make collision data unsafe to index or use |
| `PHYSICS2D_DEGENERATE` | A requested shape/chain has insufficient usable geometry |
| `PHYSICS2D_ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` | Derived arithmetic cannot represent a required finite value, including positive mass/inertia lost to underflow or an overflowing reciprocal |
| `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_HANDLE` | A body, shape, contact or joint relationship refers outside the current valid objects |
| `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_PARAMETER` | A checked parameter violates its domain, such as negative density, friction or restitution |

Body definitions, collision poses and speculative cutoffs require finite used values. Shape material values are
finite and nonnegative. There is no geometry-independent minimum positive density: shape and aggregate mass,
inertia, moments, centres, extents and required reciprocals must remain representable in their actual arithmetic.
This includes the reciprocal of a positive inverse mass/inertia: a finite first reciprocal can round to a value
whose inverse overflows. Both the rounded centre and reconstructed origin are checked before publication.
Derived contact normal/tangent metrics and their required inverses must also be finite: two individually valid
inverse masses can overflow when added. Such a contact returns `PHYSICS2D_ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` before solving.
Computed contact-point relative velocity, normal approach and anchor base are also checked; finite body velocity
alone does not imply a representable `v + w cross r` at a very large contact arm.
Nonzero finite rotation pairs use scale-safe normalization when their squared length overflows or underflows;
ordinary normalization bits are retained. Exact zero pairs in a body definition retain the documented identity
conversion. A directly mutated zero stored body rotation is `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_PARAMETER`; a nonfinite or zero
rotation derived during integration returns the arithmetic error rather than becoming identity or zero silently.
An infinite density and a unit box at `f32::from_bits(1)` are refused before publishing a shape or NaN centre.
Genuine zero density or zero-area geometry keeps its zero-mass behavior; a positive mass/inertia rounded to zero
cannot take that fallback. A dynamic body with no mass retains the existing 1 kg, no-turn fallback.

Body/shape creation and an entire `create_chain` call are transactional for validation/arithmetic failures:
no partial body, shape list, mass state or chain proxies are published, and refused IDs remain available.
`World::step` preflights current public mutable data and relationships before simulation work: body state and
shape lists, current core counts/used vertices/normals/radii, materials/chain ghosts, contact handles/counts/used
values and joint handles/state. A stale broad-phase shape ID is checked before callback indexing. A linear
visitation check over shape references refuses duplicate, missing and foreign-body references.
Used cached normal impulses must be nonnegative. Friction retains the ordinary product/sqrt result when that
product is finite and uses a scale-safe geometric mean when it overflows. Invalid derived scalar or SIMD clamp
bounds propagate to the step's coded arithmetic-error check, rather than asserting inside Rust's clamp.
These checks use current data. Explicit documented sentinels, such as a joint motor's
positive-infinite maximum force for an unlimited motor, remain supported. A later simulation arithmetic error
is returned to the caller; the whole step is not a rollback transaction.

At `47f81f909`, the reproduced collision panic requires both a NaN pose and NaN cutoff: a missing closest-distance
candidate leaves a zero hit mask, whose trailing-zero index escapes the candidate rows. The literal NaN-pose
review call with a finite cutoff returned an empty manifold here. The fix rejects nonfinite public inputs and
checks missing face/distance candidates internally, including the four-pair path; it does not treat invalid
input as an ordinary empty contact. Native regressions cover both forms, overflow, current-array mutations,
creation rollback and valid retained-reference results. Each existing Wasm `check(i)` also exercises invalid
input refusal before comparing the same three production hashes. No hash was re-pinned and no speed result is
claimed. [Reproduce](whitepaper/reproduce.md#own-2d-input-validation) lists the commands and baseline failures.

Input validation closes the input/publication and absent-candidate error class. The separately derived support
correction below establishes the required centered contact bar. Owned-2D CCD is separate T-11 / 127.y work.

## Frame-accurate video decoding (2026-11-08)

Optional `@margoengine/video/codecs` fully buffers nonfragmented, self-contained, unencrypted AVC avc1 MP4. It reads the first video track, one sample description, stsz/stsc/stco/co64/stts/ctts/stss and a rate-1 media edit optionally after an empty edit, including 64-bit headers and edit versions 0/1. Movie times have microsecond precision; colliding timestamps are refused. Each request decodes from sync through the GOP, flushing reordering, selecting the requested timestamp and closing other frames. Requests are exclusive and abortable; caller closes returned frames. Edits expose only frames whose PTS starts inside the media edit; empty lead-in clamps to the first visible frame. No audio, streaming, playback scheduler, arbitrary edits, fragmented MP4, WebM, other codecs, rotation/display transforms or external media references. Large files/long GOPs can need substantial memory/CPU. WebCodecs/AVC support is browser-specific and checked; renderer independent, including beside WebGL2 (the external material remains WebGPU-only). Unit stand-ins prove reordered sample tables, edit boundary regression and ownership. Generated AVC MP4 is decoded/rendered on RTX A6000/Edge. The outside CC0 MDN flower clip adds 150 real AVC High frames with B-frame reordering: every edited timestamp matches FFprobe and all 150 copied decoded-frame byte arrays match the independently demuxed WebCodecs reference exactly. This shares the browser decoder and is not cross-decoder accuracy proof. Edit bounds use exact native ticks, with one microsecond rounding after edits; source decode timestamps must also remain unique. Other browsers/GPUs and speed unmeasured. Entry 3,458 B gzip, unchanged budget 3,593 B. LIM-575.

## Video alpha and chroma key (2026-11-08)

Optional `@margoengine/video/alpha` reuses the external material feature. Stacked colour is top/left, raw grayscale red-channel alpha bottom/right; equal pixel halves require an even packed dimension of at least 2. Both rectangles clamp at half-texel bounds. Colour must be straight, not premultiplied. RGB keying uses sRGB Euclidean distance, threshold 0.15 and softness 0.1 by default, green key [0,1,0]. Threshold is 0..sqrt(3), softness positive through sqrt(3), with distinct float32 edges; feature parameters are fixed on creation. No despill, lighting adaptation or colour/hair recovery. One external video feature per material, UV0/flipY true defaults; caller owns playback and source lifetime. Alpha multiplies source/material alpha before colour-pass alphaTest/blending; enable transparent for soft edges. Existing direct sRGB output-space blending is preserved. Shadow/picking coverage retains its existing material inputs, without external alpha. WebGL2 refuses with code/help link. Real RTX A6000/Edge checks generated masks at 0/64/128/255 for both layouts, fractional keying and cutout; these are stand-ins, not real movies. ## Own 2D collision filtering, sensors and events (2026-11-24)

The own 2D kernel (`packages/physics2d/kernel`) filters pairs by collision groups (memberships in the high 16 bits, the filter in the low 16; each shape's filter must hold a membership of the other), by active collision types (`ACTIVE_*` bits, a pair needs both shapes to allow its body kinds; the default is dynamic with anything, and a pair with no dynamic body is kept only when one shape is a sensor) and by solver groups (a pair whose solver groups do not meet reports contact but pushes nothing). A sensor reports an overlap and pushes nothing. Events are listed in shape id order for the last step: a pair starts when its closest point is nearer than `TOUCH_ON` (0.5 linear slop) and stops beyond `TOUCH_OFF` (1.5 linear slop), or when its pair leaves the broad phase. Contact force events carry the normal impulse of each substep's biased pass, summed over the step and divided by its length, so an impact inside the step is counted; the relax pass's small corrections are not. Accepted difference: events fire for either shape asking, as Rapier does. Tests: `packages/physics2d/kernel/tests/events.rs`.

## Own 2D scene queries (2026-11-24)

`packages/physics2d/kernel/src/query.rs` answers rays (`ray_cast`, `ray_cast_all`, with `solid` choosing a hit at 0 or the exit for a ray that starts inside), points, shapes placed in the world (`shape_overlap`) and shapes slid along a unit direction (`shape_cast`, `shape_cast_all`; a shape already overlapping is met at 0). Every query culls with the broad phase's fat boxes and then tests the exact shape at its body's pose; `World::set_transform` refits a moved body's boxes at once, so a query right after a teleport sees it. Filters: collision groups, kind flags (sensors, fixed, kinematic, dynamic), an excluded shape and an excluded body. Direction vectors must be unit length within 1e-3 and finite (`PHYSICS2D_INVALID_PARAMETER`, `PHYSICS2D_NOT_FINITE`). A shape cast is conservative advancement on the convex distance function and stops within 0.1 linear slop of touching, in at most 64 iterations per candidate shape; a candidate that has not converged by then is not reported. Tests: `packages/physics2d/kernel/tests/queries.rs`, including 400 random rays checked against marching.

## Own 2D removal (2026-11-24)

`World::remove_shape`, `remove_body` and `remove_joint` take things out between steps. A removed shape leaves the broad phase and its contacts at once; a pair that was touching reports a stop on the next step, and the bodies it touched wake. A removed body takes its shapes and joints. Body and shape slots are reused by the next one created (a joint's id is never reused, and other joints keep theirs), so a world that adds and removes bullets every step stays the size of its busiest moment. A refused creation leaves no slot behind. Tests: `packages/physics2d/kernel/tests/lifecycle.rs`.

## Own 2D body controls (2026-11-24)

The kernel's `World` sets velocities (`set_velocity`), applies impulses at the centre or at a world point (`apply_impulse`, `apply_torque_impulse`), keeps a force and torque acting every step until `reset_forces` (`add_force`), sets damping, gravity scale, sleep permission, continuous collision and dominance (`set_body_params`), locks or frees turning (`set_fixed_rotation`) and drives a kinematic body to a position (`set_next_kinematic`: the step gives it the speed that reaches the target in exactly one step, so what it pushes feels the motion, then places it on the target). In a contact between bodies of different dominance the higher one acts with infinite mass, as in Rapier's user guide. Accepted limit: the sustained-contact certificates (`solver/path_support.rs`) read gravity and the bodies' own masses alone, so a world with any applied force, torque or non-zero dominance solves without them. Tests: `packages/physics2d/kernel/tests/bodies.rs`.

## Own 2D continuous collision (2026-11-24)

A body with `ccd` set (`BodyDef::ccd`, `set_body_params`) that travels more than twice the speculative margin (0.04 m) in a step is swept after the solve against the shapes of static and kinematic bodies (sensors, filtered pairs and joint-excluded pairs left out) and set back to its earliest time of impact, with its velocity kept (`packages/physics2d/kernel/src/ccd.rs`, conservative advancement, Mirtich 1996). Accepted limits: a dynamic body it meets is swept too (both move through the step, the search bounds their travel together) and is put back to the same time as the ccd body, soft CCD (`softCcd`) widens a body's contact margin to the reach given, so the solver stops a fast body at what it would hit one step ahead with no sweep (the broad phase boxes grow by the same reach; contacts of such a body are not batched in lanes), a kinematic target is tested at its end pose, a pair that already touches when the step begins is swept too, but stopped only where its gap closes by more than four times the linear slop (0.02 m) past the gap it began with, so a body resting on or sliding along a face is left to the contact solver and a long thin body that hits a wall at high speed and spin no longer swings through it after the hit (a 2 m by 0.1 m bar at 150 m/s and 8, -8 or 20 rad/s stays in front of a 0.1 m wall for 60 steps; KB-PHYSICS2D-CCD-SPIN1), and a search that has not converged in 32 iterations stops at the safe time reached. Tests: `packages/physics2d/kernel/tests/ccd.rs`.

## Physics2D on the own 2D kernel (2026-11-24)

`@margoengine/physics2d` no longer uses Rapier 2D: `Physics2D.load()` compiles `dist/physics2d.wasm` (the committed blueprint `packages/physics2d/src/physics2d-kernel.wasm`, 407 kB raw), and the Rapier objects (`Body2D.raw`, `Joint2D.raw`, `Physics2D.world`, `Physics2DOptions.rapier`, `RapierModule2D`) are gone; the breaks are recorded in `api/breaks.json`. Accepted differences from the Rapier build, each with its cause: friction defaults to 0.5 and restitution to 0 as before, but the contact solver is the kernel's soft step, so resting poses differ from Rapier's by a fraction of the linear slop (5 mm); a collider's `mass` option sets its density from the shape's area (the kernel has no mass override), which is the same mass for a solid shape and none for an edge; `setEnabled(false)` makes a collider meet nothing and drops it from queries but its mass still counts (Rapier removes it from the body's mass too); `overlapShape` and `castShape` take a box, circle, capsule, segment or a convex polygon of at most 8 points (Rapier also took concave polygons as compounds); a polyline whose last point repeats its first is a closed chain; the character controller is TypeScript over the kernel's shape cast, so its exact corner cases (slope entry, stepping onto a ledge a hair wider than `minWidth`) follow the algorithm in `packages/physics2d/src/character.ts` and not Rapier's; `pushDynamic` applies the character's mass times the speed into the body as an impulse. Tests: `packages/physics2d/tests/physics2d.test.js` and `kernel-features.test.js`.


Since 2026-11-26 a pair's friction and restitution combine by Rapier's rules (C2-12), the average by default: before,
the kernel took the square root of the product of the frictions and the larger restitution. A scene whose bodies bounce
off a floor of restitution 0 now bounces at half its restitution unless it sets `Max` (as in Rapier); frictions that
differ meet at their mean. Snapshots written before (version 13 and earlier) read with the average.
## Own 2D shapes beyond the first six (2026-11-24)

`Vehicle2D` (`@margoengine/physics2d/vehicle`, 2026-11-26) is Rapier's ray cast vehicle seen from the side. Accepted differences from Rapier's 3D controller: no steering and no sideways grip (the axle points out of the screen); its wheel pushes are held on the chassis as forces over each step, beside the body's own forces, so they act in every substep (an impulse before the step would make the chassis's velocity read 3/8 of g dt high at rest with 4 substeps) and `resetForces` on the chassis clears them until the next step; one ray per wheel, so a wheel can drop into a gap narrower than itself. Rapier 2D 0.21.0 has no vehicle controller to compare against. Tests: `packages/physics2d/tests/vehicle.test.js`.

`triangle`, `trimesh`, `heightfield`, `halfspace`, `compound`, `voxels`, `borderRadius` and one-sided polylines are options of `Physics2D` colliders (`packages/physics2d/src/shapes.ts`). Accepted differences from Rapier: `borderRadius` grows the shape outward as Rapier's round shapes do, so a box of `width` 20 with radius 6 is 32 wide; a `trimesh` is one convex piece per triangle, so a body sliding over its seams can catch there unless it is made with `fixInternalEdges` (2026-11-26, `kernel/src/seams.rs`), which joins the triangles: shared edges are found by exact vertex positions, so an edge that meets another only in part (a T-junction) is outline, not a seam; removing one triangle's kernel shape alone would leave its neighbours' seams as they were (the facade removes a mesh whole), and a new outline on one (`set_shape_core`) drops its seams. Rapier's `ORIENTED` has nothing to add in 2D (the triangles are solid, so a point inside the mesh is always found) and its `DEFORMABLE` has no call in Rapier's JavaScript API that moves the vertices afterwards; a `halfspace` is a polygon 200,000 world units across and deep, not infinite; `voxels` collide as merged outlines with no thickness, as tile maps do, so a very fast body needs `ccd: true`, and answer every scene query (point, ray, overlap, cast, projection) from the filled cells themselves (`kernel/src/voxel.rs`, a lookup and a grid walk; a voxels collider cannot be rotated, and its query-only shape adds no mass and touches nothing); a `heightfield` is a chain with smooth joins, solid on the up side. A one-sided polyline is solid on the side its right-hand normals point to (left to right is up on screen) and a body that is already behind it stays behind; ray queries still meet it from both sides. A `mass` on a compound or mesh is spread over its pieces by area. Tests: `packages/physics2d/tests/shapes-more.test.js` and `kernel/tests/chain.rs`.

## Own 2D snapshots, debug lines and added mass (2026-11-24)

`World::snapshot` writes the whole world as bytes (bodies, shapes, joints with their warm start, contacts with theirs, the broad phase's fat boxes, free slots and the step counter) and `World::from_snapshot` makes a world that steps bit for bit as the original would, from any step (`kernel/tests/snapshot.rs`, and through the facade `physics2d/tests/kernel-features.test.js`); a truncated, altered or foreign snapshot is refused with `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_PARAMETER` or `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_HANDLE`. `Physics2D.restore` accepts a snapshot only while the bodies, colliders and joints are the ones it was taken with; moving, waking and changing them is fine, adding or removing one is a `state` error (restore first). The events of the last step are not part of a snapshot. `World::debug_lines` and `Physics2D.debugRender` give outlines (a circle is 24 segments, a rounded corner 6, so a drawn circle is within 0.9 percent of the true radius), joints (anchor to anchor), contact points with normals and the broad phase's fat boxes as coloured segments, for eyes only. `additionalMass` adds kilograms to the shapes' mass and scales the inertia by the same ratio; Rapier's additional mass properties take an inertia of their own, which Margo does not. The Wasm is 407 kB raw with these.

## Own 2D generic joints, locked axes and the PID controller (2026-11-24)

`JointKind::Generic` holds any mix of three locks of a plane joint (the x axis and the y axis of body A's frame, and the turn between the frames), each frame turned by its own angle; x and y together are a pinned point, one alone a pin-slot, and the locks solve exactly along paths like every other joint (`kernel/tests/generic_joint.rs`). `type: 'slot'` is the pin-slot along an axis. `lockTranslation` (a body option and a method) holds a body's origin on an axis with such a joint to a fixed body no one sees; it holds the position the body has when it is locked, `teleport` moves the lock with the body, and unlike Rapier's velocity lock a body pushed by a contact it cannot absorb on the locked axis is held by the joint's stiffness, not by an infinite mass, so a very hard push shows as a small give (the joint spring, `joint_hertz`). `multibody: true` on a joint is accepted and does nothing: chains and trees solve exactly already; use `addArticulation` for joint-space control. `PidController2D` sums `kp` times the error, `ki` times its integral and `kd` times the velocity error, for the position and the angle, and changes the velocity by that times the step; Rapier's PID controller returns a correction of its own form, and the gains do not carry over one for one.

## Own 2D physics hooks (2026-11-24)

`Physics2D.hooks` takes `filterPair(colliderA, colliderB)` (false removes the pair: no contact, no events), `filterIntersection(colliderA, colliderB)` (the same for a pair with a sensor in it, as Rapier splits its contact pair and intersection pair filters: a sensor pair asks only `hooks.filterIntersection`, a solid pair only `hooks.filterPair`; before 2026-11-24 `filterPair` was asked of sensor pairs too, so a collider that vetoed its sensor pairs through `filterPair` sets `filterIntersection` now; `collider.setActiveHooks` and `collider.activeHooks` change and read what a collider asks) and `modifyContact(change)` (set `solverActive`, `friction`, `restitution` or `oneWay` for this step's touching contact). The kernel calls them through two Wasm imports (`env.hook_filter`, `env.hook_contact`) and only for pairs where one collider set `hooks.filterPair` or `hooks.modifyContact`; a hook runs inside the step, so it must be quick, must not change the world and must not call into it. `filterPair` is asked every step for every such pair its broad phase finds (Rapier asks when the pair is created and the contact is first computed); `modifyContact` for every touching contact of an awake pair. A contact whose `oneWay` direction has no positive part along its normal (from collider A to collider B, in world axes, so the platform collider being A or B decides the direction to give) or whose `solverActive` is false still reports events and pushes nothing, as solver groups do. `change.tangentVelocity` makes a conveyor: friction drives collider B's surface to that speed relative to collider A along `change.tangent`. It is carried in a side array of target speeds indexed by constraint, written only when a hook set one, so the 128-byte `Constraint` is unchanged (the layout test still pins it) and a world with no conveyor reads nothing from it; the four-lane blocks hold one more lane of speeds, subtracted from the friction rows' relative speed, and a scene with every speed 0 steps bit for bit as one without hooks (`kernel/tests/conveyor.rs`). The sustained-contact certificates are off while a conveyor speed is set. A world restored from a snapshot keeps its hooks. Tests: `packages/physics2d/tests/kernel-features.test.js`.

## Own 2D point projection, box queries, contact pairs and body setters (2026-11-24)

`projectPoint` returns the nearest accepted collider with the closest point on its outline (the query point itself and distance 0 when it is inside; a chain, a segment and a voxel outline have no inside) and walks the kernel's sorted list, so a `predicate` may reject any number of nearer colliders; it tests every shape, which is linear in their number. `intersectionsWithBox` tests the exact bounds of the colliders the broad phase offers. `contactPairs(collider)` lists the contacts as the last step left them, including a pair whose boxes overlap but whose shapes are apart (`touching` false) or whose solver is off; its points are in world units and its `impulse` is the last substep's. Body setters (`linearDamping`, `angularDamping`, `gravityScale`, `canSleep`, `ccd`, `dominance`, `setType`) take effect at once and wake the body; `setType('fixed')` stops it and `setType('dynamic')` weighs it from its colliders. `CharacterMoveResult2D.hits` lists the colliders a move hit with the surface normal out of each and the contact point. Tests: `kernel/tests/queries.rs`, `tests/kernel-features.test.js`.

## Own 2D articulations (2026-11-24)

`Physics2D.addArticulation(root, links)` joins bodies into a tree of revolute and prismatic joints hanging from `root` and returns an `Articulation2D` with the joint space made explicit: `positions()` and `velocities()` (the child's turn less its parent's, or the slide along the unit axis), `driveTo`, `setMotor` and `setLimits` per joint, `forwardKinematics`, `pointAt`, `jacobian` (central differences of the exact forward kinematics), `solveIK` (damped least squares, Wampler 1986, Nakamura and Hanafusa 1986: steps cut to 0.3 rad, positions kept inside the limits) and `setPositions`.

How it is solved, and how that differs from Rapier's multibody joints and from Featherstone's articulated-body algorithm (Rigid Body Dynamics Algorithms, Springer 2008): Margo keeps the bodies as ordinary bodies of the world and holds them together with the kernel's joints in maximal coordinates, solved exactly. A chain is one block-tridiagonal elimination; a tree with a branch is solved by sparse block elimination over the tree (Baraff, "Linear-Time Dynamics using Lagrange Multipliers", SIGGRAPH 1996: leaves first, each body's child joints reduced into the joint above, then back substitution from the root; `kernel/src/joint/tree.rs`, linear in the number of joints for a bounded number of joints a body). Joints that form a ring keep block Gauss-Seidel, as meshes do. The reason for maximal coordinates is that contacts of any link, sensors, groups, hooks and sleeping all stay in the one solver, where reduced coordinates would need a second contact path through generalised Jacobians.

Measured: a one-rod pendulum within 1 percent of the physical pendulum's period; a double pendulum within 3 percent of its energy over four seconds; a 20-link chain under a 3000:1 end within 1 percent of its length; a 12-body humanoid-shaped tree hanging by the head with a 1000:1 torso keeps every joint within 0.07 mm over twenty seconds, and the same tree solved by Gauss-Seidel flies apart (hundreds of metres; `kernel/tests/joint_trees.rs`); a chain solved as a tree matches the chain sweep within 2 mm after four seconds with a 500:1 end. Against Rapier 2D 0.21 as an oracle (`tests/oracle-rapier.test.js`): its impulse-joint chain agrees with ours within 0.05 rad over a second (a three-link arm), its impulse joints leave the humanoid's joints open by 1.8 m where ours stay within 0.07 mm, and its multibody joints turn a rod released level 0.495 rad in 0.3 s where the closed form (angular acceleration 3 g / 2 L) and its own impulse joint give 0.652, so the oracle for the arm is its impulse joints. Tests: `packages/physics2d/tests/articulation.test.js`.

## Own 2D sustained contact support

The recovery cap applies to the combined elastic residual, `max(beta*s+C*lambda,-P)`, rather than penetration
bias alone. For positive recovery speed P, stationary positive support retains the original spring root
`beta*s+C*lambda=0`: the cap imposes no finite force ceiling on feasible, representable loads. This is not an
unbounded floating-point magnitude or arbitrary-geometry stability guarantee. P=0 retains disabled recovery
and may have nonunique overpenetrated stationary states; the coupled correction declines it.

The coupled equilibrium correction is limited to a certified dynamic contact path with one static terminal.
It retains physical masses and the original compliance. Branches, cycles, multiple anchors, joints,
kinematic/sleeping terminals, nonzero restitution, original separating motion, open rows, unsupported gravity
wrenches or uncertified ranks use general capped dynamics. Current geometry, unilateral/friction feasibility,
finite arithmetic, casts, rotations and residuals are certified before an atomic component commit. Recovery
displacement uses the existing P*h substep budget. Sleep observes actual substep pose rate as well as final
relaxed speed, with unchanged thresholds/time and island propagation.

All 29 native physical bars pass, including the unchanged 1:100 and required 1:1000 centered contact predicates,
100-row pile sag, slope creep, bounce, friction, joints and sleep. The 1:1000 result is 0.518550681 m sag versus
0.518550736 m closed form, zero final displacement from the one-second sample, asleep at 0.8833334 s. The
unchanged regression fails on verified main 47f81f909: 1.186208290 m sag and 92.105 mm creep. The mixed-scene pin changes
intentionally from `9acb68471fbe6ba0` to `92db6847c4e919d4`; pyramid/joint-grid pins are unchanged. It changes again,
to `749b88a3c4d673fc`, when a pair's friction and restitution combine by Rapier's rules with the average by default
(2026-11-26, C2-12); its mixed shapes differ in friction and restitution, the pyramid's and joint grid's do not.
The same two stack predicates run inside Wasm `check(0)`; native scalar/SIMD and shipped Wasm SIMD agree on
the stack metrics. Wasm always selects SIMD even when its stored `contact_lanes` setting is false.

The preserved geometry-dependent point spring has a negative local bending direction in the sagged 1:1000
column under small lateral perturbations, independently differentiated and checked with Margo's own manifolds.
Centered axial acceptance does not establish arbitrary lateral stability. No artificial angular stiffness or
mass threshold was fitted to hide it. See the [support derivation](architecture/physics2d-support-proof.md),
[bending analysis and executable probe](architecture/physics2d-support-bending.md), and
[reproduction commands](whitepaper/reproduce.md#own-2d-sustained-support).

The normal solver's finite-predicate reduction relies on actual private caller dataflow, not arbitrary
independent helper arguments. It preserves the same accepted/exceptional lane masks, raw-row and used-soft
domain checks, cap membership, post-motion finiteness and coded errors. The
[IEEE proof and compiler inventory](architecture/physics2d-finite-certificates.md) state those restrictions;
static predicate counts do not establish dynamic instruction counts or a browser speed gain.

The frame planner is linear in bodies, contacts and joints. Its flat graph/path/gap buffers retain capacity
bounded by historical maximum body/contact counts, rather than per-body or per-component capacity maxima.
Current graph contents, eligibility and weights rebuild each frame. General branching graphs skip the extra
substep path work; accepted components still use local allocations and two banded factorizations each substep.
Retaining scratch memory trades its lifetime for fewer allocation calls; this is not an allocation-free world
or a Box2D speed-parity claim. CCD remains outside this correction.

Optional `@margoengine/lighting2d/cookie` projects 2D textures (cookies / gobos) onto light footprints to shape lights with window patterns and flashlights. Supports scale, offset, rotation, wrapping modes (zero, clamp, repeat, mirror) and blend modes (multiply, alpha, color). WebGPU only; WebGL2 rejects with coded error and help link. Real RTX A6000 check passes with 0 wrong pixels against the CPU reference form. LIM-593.

## Mixer offline mix (`mixer/pcm`, GAP-FILM-MIX)

`mixPCM` holds the whole mix in memory (one Float32Array per bus and channel, 4 bytes a sample) and does not resample:
decode every source at the mix's rate (8 to 768 kHz). 1 to 32 channels; `pan` only in two-channel mixes. Ducking is
keyed by sample peak, not loudness. The limiter measures true peak with the ITU-R BS.1770-5 four-phase interpolator,
so it holds that estimate (not an ideal reconstruction) at or under the ceiling; where the gain moves inside the
interpolator's 12 taps, which a look-ahead near 0 makes likely, the last excess is removed by lowering the whole
signal. One measured run on the workstation (2026-11-25, Node, one thread): one minute of stereo with a ducked bus took
1.0 s limited and 0.6 s with `limiter: false`. An abort is read between clips and ducks, not inside a loop.

## Mixer loudness (batch 111)

Optional mixer/loudness analyses finite Float32 PCM, mono/stereo or Web Audio 5.1 order
L/R/C/LFE/SL/SR. LFE is excluded from loudness, surrounds weight 1.41, others 1. All channels
contribute to true peak. Rates: 32/44.1/48/88.2/96/176.4/192 kHz. Published 48 kHz K filters
are bilinearly re-expressed at the other rates; tests preserve 1 kHz calibration within 0.1 LU.
Ungated M/S windows are 400 ms/3 s every 10 ms. Integrated blocks overlap 75%, with absolute
-70 LUFS and relative -10 LU gates. Incomplete windows are discarded; unavailable/silent
measurements are -Infinity. Histories/energy memory scales with duration. No file decoding,
live worklet metering, LRA, UI or full EBU certification. Generated standard tone/offset tests
are stand-ins, not the downloaded corpus or authentic programmes. Real Edge rendered calibration
and normalisation pass beside WebGPU/WebGL2; other browsers and speed are unmeasured.
Normalisation copies PCM, defaults -23 LUFS/-1 dBTP, target above -70 through 0 and peak cap
-96..0 dBTP. It applies constant gain, not compression/clipping; cap and changed absolute-gate
membership may prevent the requested loudness, and the after report exposes the actual outcome.
A programme with no qualifying complete 400 ms block raises coded state with help link.
Peak cap/measurement uses the finite four-phase FIR model, not all DACs/codecs. LIM-596.
Loudness entry: 2,106 B gzip, budget 2,362 B.
Mixer root entry: 7,408 B gzip, budget 7,664 B. At the original loudness landing, core plus stage measured 23,837 B gzip.
Mixer gain/mute/solo/duck scheduling now validates finite nonnegative audio times/durations and float32 parameter/gain bounds before mutating state or cancelling automation. Invalid releases remain active; undefined release/gate durations retain 0.4/0.01 second defaults. Regression: mixer.test.js.

Lights masked or on mismatched layers are clipped in the shader or culled before draw submission. WebGPU only; WebGL2 rejects with coded error and help link. Real RTX A6000 check passes with 0 wrong pixels against the CPU reference form. LIM-597.

## 2D global illumination (batch 55)

Optional `@margoengine/lighting2d/gi` evaluates 1..8 spatial cascades, 1..32 base directions, angular ratio 1..8,
interval ratio >1, base distance >0, 0..4 finite diffuse bounce orders, albedo 0..1, intensity >=0. Defaults are
4/4/4/4/16/1/.5/1 respectively. World probe spacing doubles from one unit; centres are on the .5 lattice.
The far interval ends at baseDistance * intervalRatio ** (cascades - 1), which must fit float32.
Radiance/transmittance merges trace each of four child connectors before interpolation (RASTI appendix A).
Two-sided surface patches are at most baseDistance long; diffuse gathers use 32 normalized cosine samples and
midpoint-constant patch radiance. Surface gathers offset origins by .001 world units and ignore ray/edge
intersections at distances <= .0001 to avoid self-intersection. Small sources and spatial detail below those samples can be missed. The analytic
radius-six circular-source test over eleven distances 8..60 is within 5% of asin(radius/distance)/pi on CPU and RTX A6000;
this is a measured fixture bound, not an arbitrary-scene accuracy guarantee. No speed claim.
Patch count is capped at 65,536. The CPU hierarchy has an 8,000,000 sample-evaluation ceiling per query/grid.
GPU scene/cascade buffers must each fit maxStorageBufferBindingSize and 1D dispatch groups must fit
maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension; excessive combinations throw a coded RangeError instead of truncating work.
Cascade memory is 16 bytes per spatial/angular sample; two surface fields use 64 bytes per patch, plus 32 bytes
geometry per patch, 32 per emitter, 96 per direct light, masks and aligned per-dispatch uniforms.
CPU/GPU options, finite bounce orders, exact opaque visibility/energy fixtures and lifecycle are tested. Native WebGL2
rejects with coded unsupported/help. HDR needs a floating target; an unorm target clamps at presentation. LIM-599.

Optional `@margoengine/lighting2d/height` casts perspective and directional height shadows and self-shadows based on vertical extrusion and elevation for top-down games. Ray-interval clipping along height spans projects shadows on the ground and lower receivers, and self-shadows flat +z-facing receivers at one elevation per pass. The CPU helper additionally accepts a normal; the GPU height pass has no normal-map input. WebGPU only; WebGL2 rejects with coded error and help link. Real RTX A6000 check passes with 0 wrong pixels against the CPU reference form. LIM-600.

## Emissive sprites and bloom hookup (batch 55)

Optional `@margoengine/lighting2d/emissive` adds glowing emissive sprites with distance falloff and bloom threshold extraction. The pass owns separate `rgba16float` emission and local extraction textures and replaces its target each frame.
The local threshold is `max(sprite.bloomThreshold, pass.bloomThreshold)`, default 0.8 for both; intensity/strength defaults
are 1. An unattached image effect factory (`connectBloom(() => new Bloom(options))`) is recreated after device restoration
and dispatched with the actual `encodeImage` API. The local analytic glow is not a blur; spatial convolution comes from Bloom. WebGPU only; WebGL2 rejects with coded error and help link. Real RTX A6000 check passes with 0 wrong pixels against the CPU reference form. LIM-601.

## Batch 168 lightmap reference

The modified Cornell box has 15 parallelograms and 881 irradiance texels. Against a complete Cycles
128-sample diffuse bake at one indirect bounce on both sides (Cycles `diffuse_bounces` 1, Margo `bounces` 1,
path mode, 32 paths and 16 area samples a texel), physical lightmap MAE is 0.024863 (relative 0.087125), max

Default weighted OIT loses to exact ordered transparency on five overlapping unlit coverage panes:

## Batch 168 sky radiance reference

The default Preetham sky does not match Mitsuba 3.9.1 sunsky (Hosek-Wilkie): zenith-Y-normalized RGB
MAE 1.439228 over 297 directions, max 70.681783. Per-case relative MAE is 0.199319 to 0.765628.
Sun elevations 10/45/75 degrees, turbidity 2/3/6, ground albedo 0, sun disk off. This is a sampled
angular-radiance comparison, not hemisphere integration or absolute physical-unit equivalence.

Accepted difference (KB3148c, 2026-11-11): the gap is the model. Margo's default is the 1999 Preetham fit, the
same model as three.js `Sky` and Babylon's `SkyMaterial`; Mitsuba sunsky is the 2012 Hosek-Wilkie fit, which its
authors and Zotti et al. 2007 show corrects Preetham's horizon brightening and high-turbidity behaviour. The paper
Preetham model alone, without Margo's tuning, measures MAE 1.436382 on the same 297 directions; Margo's daylight-locus
floor moves the grid by MAE 0.012108 (relative 1.74 % at most, `packages/sky/test/sunsky-reference.test.js`), and its
clamps do not act on this grid. Hosek-Wilkie's coefficients are published only inside the authors' source code, so
Margo cannot ship that model clean room without fitting its own coefficients; for a physically based sky use
`model: 'bruneton'` or `HillaireSky`. Sources: A. J. Preetham, P. Shirley and B. Smits, "A Practical Analytic Model for Daylight", SIGGRAPH 1999, https://doi.org/10.1145/311535.311545; L. Hosek and A. Wilkie, "An Analytic Model for Full Spectral Sky-Dome Radiance", ACM TOG 31(4) 2012, https://cgg.mff.cuni.cz/projects/SkylightModelling/HosekWilkie_SkylightModel_SIGGRAPH2012_Preprint.pdf; G. Zotti, A. Wilkie and W. Purgathofer, "A Critical Review of the Preetham Skylight Model", WSCG 2007, https://www.cg.tuwien.ac.at/research/publications/2007/zotti-2007-wscg/zotti-2007-wscg-paper.pdf.

## Mars magnitude tables (2026-11-15)

`planetPositions` in `@margoengine/sky/astro` gives Mars' V magnitude by Mallama and Hilton 2018, Eq. 6:
5 log10(r delta) - 1.601 + 0.02267 alpha - 0.0001302 alpha^2 + L(effective sub-longitude) + L(Ls). The two L tables
(36 entries each, 10 degree steps) are printed only in Mallama, "The magnitude and albedo of Mars", Icarus 192 (2007),
which is closed access, so they were recovered from public reference values:

- Source: JPL Horizons, whose manual names Mallama and Hilton 2018 for planet magnitudes. Observer tables from the
  official API (`https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api`, COMMAND 499, CENTER 500@399, QUANTITIES
  9,14,15,19,20,24,44: APmag, sub-Earth and sub-solar longitude, r, delta, S-T-O, App_Lon_Sun), fetched 2026-11-15:
  14,800 fitting dates (1990-01-01 to 2040-01-01, every 1777 minutes) and 3,986 held-out dates (1985-01-01 05:17 to
  2045-01-01, every 7919 minutes). No personal data was sent.
- Fit: APmag minus the published distance and phase terms, least squares for the 72 entries. Each table is read by
  Stirling's formula to fourth differences (the paper's choice, Explanatory Supplement 3rd ed. 14.2.4), which is the
  quartic through the five entries around the argument. Horizons' data choose the reading: centred on the entry below
  the argument leaves 0.00030 rms (Horizons prints three decimals, whose rounding alone is 0.00029), centred on the
  nearest entry 0.0044, the other five-entry windows 0.0039 to 0.0084; the effective sub-longitude is the mean of the
  sub-Earth and sub-solar west longitudes (0.00030 rms), not either one alone (0.0111 and 0.0110) and not the
  longitude of the 3D midpoint of the two points (up to 0.003 off where their latitudes differ by 14 degrees).
- Identifiability: over the 50 years the sub-longitude turns about 351 degrees a day and Ls about 0.52, so the two
  angles fill their plane independently; the design's condition number is 2.3 apart from one null direction, a
  constant moved from one table to the other. Every fitted entry lands within 0.00004 of a whole thousandth, so the
  tables are thousandths; the constant is the one that makes the eight values Mallama 2017 (arXiv:1609.05048,
  Tables A-4.4 and A-4.6, V) prints at 0, 100, 200 and 300 degrees match, and all eight do.
- Residual: with Horizons' own geometry the rounded tables leave 0.00030 rms and 0.00062 at most on the fitting dates,
  0.00030 and 0.00062 on the held-out dates. Through `planetPositions` (Standish's elements, the IAU 2009 Mars pole
  and prime meridian of Archinal et al. 2011) Mars is within 0.0029 of Horizons on all 18,786 dates (0.00048 rms on
  the held-out ones): the rest is Standish's r and delta near opposition, up to 0.0025 magnitude by themselves.
  Meeus 41, used until this change, was up to 0.17 off on the same dates.
- Limits: geocentric Mars stays below a phase angle of 48 degrees, inside Eq. 6's 50; global dust storms (about 0.12
  magnitude dimmer, not predictable) are not modelled, as in the paper. Regression: `packages/sky/test/astro.test.js`
  (13 held-out Horizons dates within 0.003).

## Audio Doppler (batch 110)

Optional audio/doppler: 1,090 B gzip; audio root unchanged at 7,508 B; core plus stage unchanged at 23,837 B. Defaults: speedOfSound 343 m/s, authored playbackRate from the sound. Positive finite sound speed; nonnegative finite rate at most float32 maximum / 39. Estimates world displacement per audio-clock second; first/coincident/backward-clock samples neutral, repeated times retain history. Reset after teleports and motion during suspension. Owns playback rate while attached, restores authored rate on disposal; use controller.playbackRate for authored changes, never Audio.sync concurrently. Buffers only; other source kinds produce unsupported with a help link. One controller per sound. Listener pose/source ordering and teardown are covered.

Classical instantaneous stationary-medium approximation with each radial Mach number clamped to -0.95..0.95, ratio bounded 1/39..39. Not supersonic acoustics, wind, retarded-time positions, travel delay or pitch-only time stretching. Existing listener smoothing applies. Real browser renders beside all three rendering routes measure generated 1 kHz source approach at 1111.111 Hz, recession at 909.091 Hz, listener approach at 1100 Hz and co-motion/rest at 1000 Hz, each within 0.1 Hz with zero GPU validation errors. LIM-603, generated stand-ins only; real recordings, listening quality, other browsers and performance unmeasured.


## Batch 168 contact-shadow reference

Screen-space `ContactShadows` (`@margoengine/post/contact-shadows`, 2026-11-16) counts a hit only when the ray is behind
the depth by more than 1.5 pixel spans of depth (the start pixel's depth change to its flatter neighbour on each axis), so
a lit slope does not shadow itself: 0 of 76,800 pixels of a bare floor under a 7 degree light darken, on WebGPU and the
WebGL2 layer (packages/post/test/contact-shadows-browser.mjs). The trade-off: a contact closer than that bias (under a
pixel's depth change, so sub-pixel on screen) is not drawn, and the effect reads four more depth texels a pixel.

Default ContactShadows is a height-faded, fixed-Gaussian local contact cue. Under a radius-0.5 sphere,
against ray-traced uniform-hemisphere visibility, exposed-ground darkness MAE is 0.048174, RMSE 0.074416,
max 0.288788 (15,472 pixels, 4096 rays each; reference quadrature max error 0.001734). Defaults are retained:
size 4, height 1, blur 0.06, opacity 0.6, resolution 256. No physical lighting or area-light parity is claimed.
Accepted difference (KB3193, 2026-11-11): the default darkens the ground under a caster by how near its underside
is, a footprint cue by design (one pass, cacheable with `static`); a sphere's footprint lies under the sphere, so
the exposed ground stays nearly white (mean darkness 0.000177 against 0.048351). Sky occlusion beside a caster is
staging/accumulate-ambient: AmbientShadows with `ambient: 1` (all-sky visibility, 1024 cosine directions, opacity 1) on the same scene, pixels and reference measures MAE 0.001561, RMSE 0.001948, max 0.007994, mean darkness 0.048200 against 0.048351, on WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer (`packages/studio/test/sky-occlusion-browser.mjs`).


The independent Cycles OIT reference (1024 samples, seed 168) gives Margo MAE 1.632960 versus Babylon
0.132651. Exact primary-ray transport versus Cycles MAE is 0.094812; maximum miss 125 includes path
noise and silhouette sampling. This validates the ordering loss without treating stochastic reference
pixels as a zero-error raster oracle. No additional speed claim. See whitepaper/results/batch-168-oit-cycles.json.

## Audio event containers (batch 110)

Optional audio/events: 5,491 B gzip with shared audio implementation; audio root 7,638 B and core plus stage 23,837 B. Defaults: mode random (no immediate repeated index), voices 4 per buffer, volume [1,1], pitch [0,0] cents, cooldown 0 seconds, random Math.random, voiceOptions pool defaults, play position origin. Nonempty decoded positive-duration buffers; finite ordered volume endpoints 0..1 and pitch -4800..4800 cents. Cooldown finite and nonnegative; draws finite in [0,1). Pitch changes duration. No loading or timers. Total preallocated voices = buffer count times voices; stealing is per buffer, not a global cap. Snapshot ranges, not caller arrays. Recordings, listening quality, other browsers, random-generator statistical quality and performance remain unmeasured.

## Adaptive music (batch 110)

Optional audio/music: 1,572 B gzip (bare mixer peer external); core plus stage 23,837 B. Reuses optional mixer peer buses and fades. Defaults bpm 120, beatsPerBar 4, loopBeats 4, leadTime 0.05 s, exponential fade 0.02 s (about 98% settled). Positive finite tempo, positive integer bar/loop beats, finite grid/seconds and float32 linear gains. Buffers must cover the loop; trailing samples unused. All stems start at one origin and run continuously, including silent layers; each loop is its own one-shot source started at origin + k * loop on the audio clock (scheduled ahead: a whole OfflineAudioContext render at start, otherwise max(1 s, 2 loops), refilled each listener frame and loop end), so browsers that round start or loop points to whole frames (Firefox) stay within a frame of the grid without accumulating. Caller authors aligned/seamless loops and headroom. Fixed tempo, no analysis, stretching, section sequencing or streaming.

States are copied stem-name/dB maps, omitted stems silent. Requests validate before mutation; exact beat/bar boundaries eligible after both requested time and now+leadTime. New requests replace automation at/after their boundary; earlier transitions survive. No frame work/timers. Suspension freezes the audio clock; stop cuts sources, restart clears pending automation and resets phase. Listener teardown disposes owned buses/sources, preserving buffers. LIM-607: Node scheduling/lifecycle stand-ins and real browser sample-reference PCM for aligned generated 600/900 Hz loops and beat/bar state changes on all three routes, error below 5e-8 and zero GPU errors. ### Pixel batch 102 review limits (2026-11-08)

Flat CRT mapping uses the same integer centre-coordinate quotient as PixelScale nearest; all-off includes exact source boundaries with no excluded samples. Curved CRT reference comparisons exclude points within 0.001 texel of an edge, where float32 and float64 can choose different texels. Scale/CRT scissor clipping applies to canvas views; an explicit output texture still covers its own fitted rectangle. Palette cycling uses the represented finite product `rate * seconds` modulo the run length; multiplication can already round away fractional steps at large magnitudes, and overflow is rejected with coded `state` and a help link. Tests cover native WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer on one RTX A6000/Edge only; other hardware, physical CRT fidelity and performance remain unmeasured.

## Ambisonic beds (batch 110)

Optional audio/ambisonics: 1,919 B gzip; audio root 7,638 B and core plus stage 23,837 B. First-order four-channel ACN/SN3D W,Y,Z,X buffers only, positive finite duration, explicit convention assumption. Default format ambix; other conventions/channel counts produce linked unsupported. No FuMa/N3D/A-format conversion, higher/mixed orders, appended stereo, CAF adaptor or Opus metadata parser. Loading delegates to existing listener.load with AbortSignal and browser codec support; four-channel 24-bit PCM WAV with 44.1-to-48 kHz resampling is tested.

Default loop true, volume 1 within 0..1, smoothing listener.smoothing (default 0.02 s finite nonnegative time constant). Eight gain paths, one source, splitter and stereo merger per bed. Identity ACN front/left/up maps engine -Z/-X/+Y. Normalized copied world quaternion rotates field; listener forward/up define the inverse head orientation, translation ignored. Collinear directions retain the last independent decoder orientation (initially -Z forward, +Y up). Camera following copies camera.up, including roll and exact poles. Two virtual cardioids at +/-30 degrees output 0.5*(W+direction dot XYZ) times volume. This is stereo ambience, not HRTF/binaural localization or arbitrary loudspeaker decoding. Gain interpolation blends matrices rather than remaining a rigid rotation during fades. Author seamless loops and headroom. Start at/after now; stop/restart resets phase. Listener teardown/dispose cuts sources and frees decoder nodes, preserving buffers.

LIM-610: Node full yaw/elevation/roll basis and lifecycle checks, and real browser PCM on all three routes for generated independent-channel tones/loops and a licensed external rain-stimulus excerpt, each within 1e-6 of float64 channel matrices with zero GPU errors. First four channels of the CC BY 4.0 external 64-channel file are interpreted as ACN/SN3D; this proves file decoding and matrix routing, not a microphone chain or verified acoustic capture. XR apps feed headset world forward/up through existing listener.setPose; physical headset tracking, subjective localization, other browsers/devices and performance unmeasured.

### Scatter interaction numeric limits (batch 77 audit)

LIM-604 retains its field-size, resolution and 4,096-interactor limits. Every position has three finite f32
components; radius, bend, size and resolution/size must fit positive normal f32 (at least 2^-126), so permitted
subnormal flushing cannot zero a divisor. Strength is a number in [0,1]. A rejected update keeps the last successful
interactors. Shifts beyond the field's side discard its old pushes without signed 32-bit wrapping. Floating-point
world precision still applies; the field reads XZ and does not simulate a physical explosion. The optional interact
entry measures 7,463 minified bytes / 3,318 B gzip with bare peers external. The budget rises from 3,206 to 3,574 B
(the measured entry plus the established 256 B headroom) for input validation, atomic updates, a bounded shift and
overflow-safe distance maths. Those extra checks and ALU preserve finite extreme inputs; no speed is measured.
Core plus stage remains 23,837 B gzip.


## Batch 160 outside material pictures

The metallic-roughness test covers the entire 123-primitive Khronos textureless sphere model with a
fixed camera/sun, no IBL and 4x MSAA, at 512 x 512 on the RTX A6000 only. The full-frame RGB byte MAE
ceiling is exactly the measured 0.6997248331705729 on WebGPU and 0.7010663350423177 on the WebGL2
compatibility layer (lowered 2026-11-12 by KB3240, the dielectric diffuse weight of the glTF metal/dielectric
mix; 1.7865498860677083 and 1.7865447998046875 before); max channel error is 254. Foreground errors and integer sum budgets are recorded in
whitepaper/results/batch-160-metallic-roughness.json. Native WebGL2 rejects PBR explicitly.
Like for like (the viewer transfer, one sample) the MAE is 0.009241739908854166: an accepted difference, see
"Sample Viewer like for like" below. This is not proof of physically accurate materials or other devices. Frozen
reference PNGs remain outside the repository; CI unit tests validate the comparison contract and record,
while the GPU reproduction requires those outside files. No speed or bundle-size change is claimed.

### Sample Viewer like for like (accepted differences, 2026-11-15, KB3267)

Two display choices carry nearly all of the clearcoat and metallic-roughness loss against the Khronos glTF Sample
Viewer, and both are deliberate:

- Output transfer. The viewer's downloaded PNG measures as a pure power curve, pow(x, 1/2.2): an analytic model of
  Margo's BRDF with that curve matches it within about 0.2 levels on 16 probe spheres (black box, no viewer source
  read). Margo writes the exact sRGB transfer of IEC 61966-2-1 (the linear toe below 0.0031308, then
  1.055 x^(1/2.4) - 0.055), the curve glTF 2.0 uses for its colour textures, CSS Color 4 defines for `srgb` and a
  WebGPU `-srgb` canvas format encodes. The power curve is up to 8.5 levels brighter in deep shadow (at an sRGB byte
  of 7) and up to 1.5 levels darker in the mid tones.
- Antialiasing. The viewer's PNG has one sample per pixel (an emissive probe shows only the levels 0 and 179 to
  182); Margo resolves 4x MSAA, so every silhouette pixel differs.

What Margo does extra: the exact standard curve, so dark tones decode back to the linear values that were lit, and
antialiased edges. Trade-off: the frozen all-pixel figures against the viewer stay higher than a matched renderer
would score; no setting is changed to chase them. glTF 2.0 leaves the display transform to the viewer.

Like-for-like row: `node scripts/reference-rendering/run.mjs --case=<family> --like-for-like` (native
WebGPU) rewrites only the final sRGB encode of Margo's WGSL to pow(x, 1/2.2)
(scripts/reference-rendering/viewer-transfer.mjs) and creates the engine with `exactSize`, one sample per pixel.
It is gated by the case's `likeForLike` row, the first measurement, pinned by tests/reference-rendering.test.js
(RTX A6000, Edge 157, 512 x 512, all pixels; the anisotropy and iridescence rows were measured 2026-11-15 with the same option, the sheen row on
2026-11-15 after KB3297c and re-pinned the same day after KB3297d):

| case | main (exact sRGB, 4x MSAA) | like for like (pow 1/2.2, 1 sample) | share left |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| clearcoat | MAE 1.6820462544759114, absolute 1,322,815 | MAE 0.05530420939127604, absolute 43,493, max 94 | 3.3 % |
| metallic-roughness | MAE 0.6997248331705729, absolute 550,286 | MAE 0.009241739908854166, absolute 7,268, max 254 | 1.3 % |
| anisotropy | MAE 1.0324020385742188, absolute 811,914 | MAE 0.20022964477539062, absolute 157,467, max 254 | 19.4 % |
| iridescence | MAE 0.7803204854329427, absolute 613,669 | MAE 0.34775416056315106, absolute 273,485, max 97 | 44.6 % |
| sheen | MAE 1.3442039489746094, absolute 1,057,125 | MAE 0.27827199300130206, absolute 218,842, max 103 | 20.7 % |

Neither the anisotropy nor the iridescence residual is in the material formulas: over flat areas (no reference neighbour step above 30 summed levels)
anisotropy differs by 22,227 and iridescence by 18,828 in all, under 0.03 levels a channel over the frame. Iridescence:
1,745 pixels lit in both pictures with more than 30 summed levels of error hold 254,007 of the 273,485 (92.9 %), all
on the 2048 x 2048 BLEND guides texture (alpha-0 white with opaque black lines), where Margo's alpha-weighted area
mips keep the lines black and the viewer greys them (65098f33fe, "Batch 160 budgets re-recorded" above). Anisotropy:
135,240 (86 %) sits on reference-edge pixels, mostly the near-mirror arcs of the smoothest rows, where one sample per
pixel catches or misses a highlight thinner than a pixel; Margo's perceptual roughness floor 0.045 (Filament) widens
them. Floors of 0.02 and 0.005 give 143,094 and 168,648, so no floor reproduces the viewer and the floor stays.
Both are accepted differences; no formula or setting changed.

Sheen: before KB3297c main measured like for like MAE 0.3409881591796875 (absolute 268,164, max 188). One residual is
a choice of the viewer and stays an accepted difference: its base darkening measures as 1 - sheenColor
sRGB_encode(E), its albedo lookup read through an sRGB encode, where KHR_materials_sheen and Enterprise PBR keep E in
linear light (a model with that encode matches the viewer's spheres within 0.2 to 0.4 levels for roughness 0.3 and
up). Margo keeps the spec's linear E, so it darkens the base under a sheen less than the viewer. Attribution
(2026-11-26, `node scripts/reference-rendering/sheen-attribution.mjs`, black box): the sheen lobe matches the viewer
byte for byte and the whole residual is this base darkening. With the viewer's lookup modelled as
sRGB_encode(E(n, max(r, 0.25))) the like-for-like absolute falls from 218,842 to 23,113 (0.029 MAE), the rest being
one-sample edges and text (11,305) and the spheres (11,808). The encode holds the roughness 0.33 to 1 rows (141,533,
64.7 %); the roughness 0 row (66,004, 30.2 %) needs the lookup floor as well, where the spec's E is 0 and the lobe
is black in both pictures. Accepted difference (Scott, 2026-11-26, "Yes, accept it"): cause, the viewer's albedo
lookup, read through the sRGB encode and at a sheen roughness of at least about 0.25. What Margo does extra: the spec's
linear E (the cosine-weighted integral of the sheen BRDF, KHR_materials_sheen and Enterprise PBR) with no floor, so the
base under a sheen loses only the light the sheen lobe reflects, and nothing at roughness 0, where the lobe is black.
Trade-off: the like-for-like sheen row stays at 218,842 (MAE 0.27827199300130206) against 23,113 for a renderer with
the viewer's lookup; no setting is changed to chase it. Before KB3297d the
maximum, 205, sat on two silhouette pixels where gltf/pbr's sheen roughness floor of 0.03 drew a bright rim the
viewer does not; with no floor and n.h taken from the clamped cosines the maximum is 103, the square 3,061,310 to
2,944,566, and the absolute rises from 217,478 to 218,842. That rise belongs to this accepted difference: the rise is the Sample Viewer's encoded albedo-table ring (KB3297c), which the old floor hid: the floor's albedo (E(0.05, 0.03) = 0.71) had darkened the base on the ring inside the roughness 0 rims as the viewer's sRGB-encoded lookup darkens it everywhere at roughness 0.
The rims of the roughness 0 spheres move 467 summed levels closer to the viewer and that ring 1,831 further. The
pinned row was re-recorded once for it (Scott, 2026-11-15; docs/known-bugs.md, KB3297d).

The metallic-roughness maximum of 254 sits on 1,536 changed pixels, nearly all on silhouettes where the two
rasterizers cover a pixel differently. Nothing is left to fix in either BRDF at this resolution. Sources:
IEC 61966-2-1:1999, "Multimedia systems and equipment, Colour measurement and management, Part 2-1: Default RGB
colour space, sRGB" (not read, paywalled; constants checked against CSS Color 4); W3C, "CSS Color Module Level 4",
section "Predefined colour spaces: sRGB", https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/; W3C, "WebGPU", texture formats
`rgba8unorm-srgb` and `bgra8unorm-srgb`, https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/; Khronos, "glTF 2.0 Specification", section
3.9 (materials: sRGB colour textures, linear lighting), https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html;
K. Akeley, "Reality Engine Graphics", SIGGRAPH 1993, https://doi.org/10.1145/166117.166131 (multisample
antialiasing).

## React Native target dropped (LIM-615)

React Native is not supported; batch 117 job 6 is dropped. Margo targets the web, including mobile browsers.
The planned native path is the Rust engine. A React Native target would require a native WebGPU surface and
Android/iOS toolchains and devices to prove rendering, loading and lifecycle behavior; this repository provides
no such proof. Checked 2026-11-09: Hermes's current [language feature documentation](https://github.com/meta/hermes/blob/static_h/doc/Features.md)
and [next stable release notes](https://github.com/meta/hermes/blob/static_h/doc/blog/2026-06-05-new-hermes-stable-release.md)
do not document supported WebAssembly execution. The Hermes author's [WebAssembly preview](https://tmikov.blogspot.com/2026/02/webassembly-comes-to-hermes_01829874520.html)
describes experimental execution, not production readiness. This is not a claim that Hermes cannot run Wasm;
neither the preview nor compiling Hermes itself to Wasm establishes Margo phone compatibility.

## Wasm Content Security Policy

A policy that restricts scripts must permit Wasm compilation with `script-src 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` for each Wasm-backed path, including core engine creation and stages. Worker response policies need the permission too. [CSP requirements](csp.md) list the exact header and entries. Blocked initialization reports MargoError code `failed` with a help link; unrelated binary, SIMD and fetch errors retain their identity.

### Lighting2d direct-pass storage and lifetime ceilings

- Rect, circle and polygon masks (including inversion) and layer filtering run on root, soft, cookie and height.
  Circle centres default to world `(0,0)`. Polygon vertices cost 16 bytes each and must fit `maxStorageBufferBindingSize`.
- Height occluders cost 48 bytes each; emissive sprites cost 64 bytes each. Both lists grow to the device storage binding
  limit; the former 64-item truncation is removed. Oversized lists throw before drawing.
- Height light uniforms cost `max(256, minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment)` bytes each, capped by `maxBufferSize`.
  Soft samples are integers 1..64. Cameras require finite values and positive zoom. Mutated lights/sprites are validated.
- Height directional shadow rays are capped at 10,000 world units; elevation for shadow projection clamps to
  `[0.01, PI/2 - 0.01]` radians. Circle footprints are analytic here; ordinary direct shadows use 24-sided circle edges.
- Emissive owns three full-resolution `rgba16float` textures, 24 bytes/pixel, plus caller output and any optional Bloom
  intermediates. HDR values may overflow half precision above 65,504; an unorm presentation clips above 1.
- Native WebGL2 is unsupported by every lighting2d entry. Tests assert the coded rejection rather than a rendered route.

not geodesic spacing. Finite coordinates within +/-1,000,000; radius 0.000001..1,000,000; maximum 65,536 triangles,

cover a domain or return the point limit. No spectral, maximal-covering or frame-time promise. Output is float64;
conversion to float32 can reduce separation. Signals precede synchronous sampling; workers enable in-flight aborts.

## Caustic path guiding (batch 99, LIM-622)

`@margoengine/voxel-pathtracer/guiding` adds a pure diffuse continuation proposal toward the existing deflector
table: up to eight static orthogonal pure smooth non-dispersive glass instances and eight mirrors. Visible box
faces are sampled by world area; interior origins use enclosing faces, excluding any face containing the origin.
The PDF converts to solid angle and sums all overlapping bounds. Actual voxel traversal and Fresnel transport
remain unchanged. `guideStrength` is finite `0..0.95`, default `0.5`; zero uses the original kernel exactly,
and empty guide tables retain the baseline random stream. No learning, photons or persistent GPU allocation.

Roulette removes accumulated cosine/mixture factors from its survival heuristic so small importance weights
are not immediately discarded. The heuristic scale is bounded `1e-20..1e20`, with actual survival `0.05..1`
after bounce three and actual throughput divided by that survival. Ordinary bounce caps still truncate paths.
Bounds can contain empty geometry or point below the surface, producing zero-contribution proposals. Other
BSDFs, unsupported deflectors and geometry beyond the table retain ordinary path sampling. A geometry prior
can increase variance when its objects contribute little. No general convergence or wall-time gain is claimed.

`tests/guiding-browser.mjs` keeps a fixed 2x squared-RGB-error bar on a generated small-glass caustic at 64 samples
against a 16,384-sample guided reference, with separate independent original-tracer energy comparisons and an
analytic unit furnace. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility run the shader; native WebGL2 refuses with code
`unsupported` and a registered help link. Native device restoration and disposal are exercised.

Entry size with bare peers external: guiding 2,535 B gzip; new budget 2,791 B includes the standard 256 B headroom.
Root 80,431 B, studio 1,047 B, resampled 1,934 B and core plus stage 23,837 B remain unchanged. No existing size,
accuracy or time gate was relaxed.

## Multiple-scattering tracer sky (batch 99, LIM-626)

The new optional `@margoengine/voxel-pathtracer/sky` imports the optional sky peer's existing `/hillaire` entry.
`traceSkyEnvironment` calls `bakeHillaireEnvironment`, returning a linear RGBA Float32 map plus a separate attenuated
sun. Bake defaults are 256x128, noon, altitude zero, sun illuminance 20, Earth, multiple scattering and stylized
night enabled. Width is 1..2048, height 1..1024 and storage must fit the device's buffers. Altitude is at most
100000000 metres, sun illuminance at most 1000000, coefficients/albedo at most 1, radii/heights at most 100000 km.
The existing 256x64 transmittance and 32x32 multiple LUTs feed a 64-step ray march per texel. Higher scattering orders
are isotropic, geometry spherical and the observer position fixed by altitude. Re-bake when settings change; this
environment adds no local atmospheric attenuation or aerial perspective. Night reuses the stylized gradient,
procedural stars and moon, time zero without twinkle; unresolved stars retain mean integrated light. It does not
include astronomical catalogues, Milky Way, spectral airglow or spectral transport. Numeric night magnitudes other
than normalized moon direction are at most 1000000. A plain WebGL2 context is refused with coded help; a WebGL2
compatibility device executes the same model. Native and compatibility values, analytic vacuum/ground, traced
lighting, cancellation, resource disposal and real native device restoration are recorded in
`docs/whitepaper/results/batch-99-sky-20261109.json`. No speed or reference-renderer equality claim.
