bake 10822 B; tracer root 80431 B and core plus stage 23837 B unchanged. Entry budgets use the standard
max(256 B, 3%) headroom; the strict core/stage limit remains 25000 B.

The environment bake requires Float32-distinct planet/atmosphere radii and vertical scattering optical depth
at most 6 in every channel (Rayleigh plus scattering Mie, integrated from ground to top). This keeps a
representable escape probability in the geometric-series LUT. Minimum observer clearance is 1 metre or
2 to 4 Float32 radius steps, whichever is larger. Night moonSize must be at least 0.000001 radians; narrower
discs are outside the bake domain. Both equirectangular dimensions determine the night filtering footprint.

## Space colonisation trees (LIM-631)

Optional procedural/trees generates a branching skeleton, not a surface mesh. Default root [0,0,0],
seed 1, 512 attraction points in an ellipsoid above the root, segmentLength 0.2, influenceRadius 3,
killRadius 0.3, maxNodes 2048 and maxIterations 128. Custom XYZ Float64Array attraction points can
extend below a supplied root for roots; an empty cloud returns only the root. Custom point/root coordinates are finite
within +/-1,000,000. Count is bounded to 8192, nodes to 16384, iterations to 512 and the product of
attractors, node capacity and iteration capacity to 134,217,728. SegmentLength 0.0001..10000,
influenceRadius 0.0001..1,000,000, killRadius at least half the segment length and at most the influence
radius. A node never grows a second child at the position of one it already has, so points that stay nearer a
parent than its new child (less than half a segment along the growth direction) stall rather than stack copies.
A cap or lack of reachable attraction can stop growth with points remaining; inspect stopped
and remainingAttractions. No guarantee all attraction points are reached, no collision avoidance,
species, biological validity, tubes/leaves, or artistic-quality claim. Output arrays are owned.
Loading is abortable; generation checks abort before synchronous work, with a worker needed for
interruption in flight. One feature-local Rust/Wasm asset; CPU generation on either rendering backend
survives device/context loss. All proof inputs are STAND-IN. No elapsed-time or SIMD speed claim.
Entry JavaScript 1,540 B gzip, new ceiling 1,796 B; trees.wasm 39,113 B raw / 16,393 B gzip.
Fixed seed 19 with influenceRadius 1.5: 218,405 complete distance tests versus 821,423 exhaustive,
identical 674-node skeleton. The count excludes grid lookup and bounding-box operations. Core plus
stage remains 23,837 B gzip below its unchanged strict 25,000 B ceiling.
Shared loading failures now have code failed, help and original cause; caller abort reasons and specific CSP/HTTP faults are preserved. Current Poisson JS 1,335 B and dungeon JS 1,277 B remain within their unchanged ceilings of 1,525 B and 1,479 B; all Wasm assets are unchanged.

### Accumulated planar shadows (batch 56, job 2)

The optional staging/accumulate entry averages equal-weight binary visibility from points on a
horizontal disk. The Y-up receiver is finite; geometry outside its footprint or height is clipped.
Light height above the plane must exceed the casting height after float32 rounding. Receiver sizes
are 1e-6..1e6, world/light coordinate magnitudes at most 1e6, radius 0..1e6, frames integer 1..1024;
blur must be 0 and static false. One sample per rendered frame, then held history; camera changes
do not invalidate world-space shadows. In-place pose/vertex changes need invalidate(); constantly
changing geometry cannot converge. Opacity/displacement/clipping GPU changes conservatively reset.

No inverse-square or cosine weighting, HDR light sampling, indirect light, general receiver surface,
or photographic-product quality claim. Raster resolution and hardware subpixel snapping bound thin
detail. The exact GPU oracle is the Windows Direct3D eight-bit raster grid; other hardware can differ
at subpixel boundaries. WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are tested; native WebGL2 refuses with
linked unsupported. Generated geometry is a stand-in. Entry 9,314 B gzip (ceiling 9,593 B); inherited
root 8,129 B (unchanged ceiling 8,259 B); core plus stage 23,837 B below 25,000 B. No speed claim.

## Sharp SDF models (LIM-632)

Optional procedural/sdf uses a feature-local Rust/Wasm uniform-grid dual contourer.
Default is an axis-aligned box of half size .75 in bounds [-1.5,1.5]^3, 24 cells
per axis. Resolution is 4..64; at most 63 sphere/box/binary CSG nodes; coordinates
within +/-10000, sizes .0001..10000, bounds extent .0001..10000 per axis. All sampled
boundary values must be positive or generation throws, never silently clips.
Analytical primitive gradients, 40 root bisections, mass-point QEF pseudoinverse
with absolute 1e-10 eigenvalue cutoff, 27 active constraint sets. Returns owned
Float64 vertices and analytic unit gradient normals with outward Uint32 triangles; no UVs or materials.
Min/max CSG fields need not be exact distances. No sampled fields, arbitrary
callbacks, rotated primitives, adaptive octrees, topology repair or exact CAD.
Subcell components, multiple edge crossings, tangencies and disconnected patches
inside one cell can be missed or nonmanifold; touching CSG can produce degenerate
triangles, and so can a surface through a grid point (known-bugs, open). Each dual
quad splits along the diagonal that keeps both triangles facing along its edge;
at a sharp seam a QEF vertex can still sit across the crease and fold a triangle
(8 of 200,920 triangles in 300 random two-sphere unions). CPU generation is synchronous with pre-abort; worker required in flight.
The independent asset is lazy; output survives real WebGPU/WebGL2 loss and disposal.
Khronos Box (Cesium, CC-BY-4.0) is the external corner/plane/volume/topology reference;
other sphere, CSG, scale and hostile controls are generated stand-ins. No visual,
production-scene, elapsed-time or SIMD claim. Cached edge roots have four cell uses
per solve, a deterministic reduction in root work with identical Hermite data.
Analytic bounds default to tree enclosure plus 10% per-axis margin (at least
0.0001). Explicit bounds retain boundary rejection; automatic bounds outside
coordinate/extent limits give linked failed and request explicit bounds. Updated
entry/asset sizes are recorded with the test-page validation evidence below. Core plus stage is unchanged at 23,837 B gzip, strictly below 25,000 B.

### Batch 76 review corrections (LIM-625, LIM-627, LIM-629)

Root, custom and mask sampling addresses the full capture, using absolute fragment pixels for offset viewports and scissors. Reveal coordinates and custom UVs refer to the full target, not just its viewport. Exact generated spatial-color comparisons cover all four built-in kinds, custom and mask at idle/0/0.5/1, 1x/4x MSAA, and preservation outside a stacked scissor. Evidence: packages/transitions/test/viewport-browser.js. These stand-ins do not establish artistic quality or cross-device behavior.

Custom WGSL must be trusted. Validation checks compilation and the reachable resource interface, not execution work or time; accepted loops can stall a GPU or cause device timeout. The costly-loop regression compiles and disposes without dispatch. User code shares the wrapper module and can read before/after captures and settings (progress, kind index, displacement, zero). Only group 0 bindings 0..2 are exposed: one settings uniform and two read-only textures. Reachable extra texture/sampler/uniform/storage bindings reject before attachment; unused declarations can compile without any extra resources. The interface exposes no host JavaScript, DOM, network, files or other engine buffers. This is no guarantee against browser/driver defects. AbortSignal cancels compilation waiting/attachment only, never attached rendering or GPU execution. Real-compiler boundary regressions are in gpu-browser.js; custom.test.js proves abort after attachment does not detach or stop frames.

Frozen-frame and live output requires a valid normalized or float color render attachment. Supported formats: r8unorm, rg8unorm, rgba8unorm, rgba8unorm-srgb, bgra8unorm, bgra8unorm-srgb, r16float, rg16float, rgba16float, rgb10a2unorm; feature-dependent r8snorm, rg8snorm, rgba8snorm, r16unorm, r16snorm, rg16unorm, rg16snorm, rgba16unorm, rgba16snorm, rg11b10ufloat require enabled WebGPU format capabilities. r32float/rg32float/rgba32float require 1x engine sampling because the 4x path needs resolve support. Output texture shape/usage limits still apply. Live captures remain RGBA8; float output does not recover HDR source data. Integer/depth rejection, unchanged source updates/progress, and baseline normalized/float acceptance are tested in live.test.js and live-browser.js. Capture-side validation shared by built-in/custom/mask is tested in transitions.test.js. See the [WebGPU capability table](https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#plain-color-formats) for device feature requirements.

## Tileable GPU texture baking (LIM-639)

The optional procedural/textures entry compiles one WebGPU compute pipeline and
bakes RGBA8 linear RGB, alpha 1. Native WebGL2 uses a lazy fragment pass on the
source engine canvas, returning an owned WebGLTexture and its gl context; native
WebGPU returns an owned GPUTexture. Neither handle crosses devices/contexts. Five
stylized patterns: periodic value noise, bricks, tiles, longitudinal wood-like
bands and rust-like threshold patches. No photographic, anatomical, corrosion or
PBR material accuracy is asserted. Four fixed noise periods 4,8,16,32, weights
8,4,2,1, quintic interpolation. Every preset shares a caller-set two-colour palette.
Defaults: bricks, 256 square, seed1, repeats[4,8], detail .2, grout .08, stagger .5,
color[.55,.2,.08], secondary[.15,.12,.1], offset[0,0]. Dimensions16..2048 and device
limit; repeats integer1..64, even brick rows; seed uint32; detail/stagger0..1;
grout0...45; RGB0..1; phase +/-1024 reduced modulo1. Repeat affects brick/tile cells
and wood bands, not fixed noise/rust octaves. No mipmaps or analytic antialiasing;
undersampled mortar/noise can alias. Use repeat-addressed sampling. Neighbouring
pixel centres across a repeat boundary are different samples of a periodic field.
Bakes are async and abortable; incomplete resources are released on failure, abort,
disposal or loss. A replacement device requires a new baker. Outputs are owned;
baker disposal destroys retained outputs. No CPU pixel loop or Wasm is involved.
44,415 GPU channel checks match an independent generated oracle within one RGBA8
quantization step. Integer phase translations are byte exact; one-texel shifts
cross both texture edges. Real WebGPU loss, in-flight abort/disposal and replacement
are tested. Native WebGL2 pixel/state/abort/disposal/loss/restoration tests use
the same one-channel-step tolerance. Mortar on an exact floating-point threshold
can differ across rasterizers. Numerical and lifecycle controls are stand-ins. External reference is
limited to a calibrated row-offset measurement from Lefebvre/Poulin 2000 Fig.1(d),
39/88 pitch with two source pixels of uncertainty, plus GPU raster quantization.
Original PDF/JPEG downloaded for measurement, never redistributed. No external
colour reconstruction, wood/rust realism, cross-device bytes or speed claim.
The WebGL2 shader chunk is lazy; no Wasm or external image asset is required.
Updated entry sizes are recorded with the test-page validation evidence below.
Core plus stage remains 23,837 B gzip, strictly below 25,000 B.

### Spectral transport and chromatic lens (batch 99 job 8, LIM-641)

Optional voxel-pathtracer/spectral traces one RGB path, then importance-samples one hero wavelength
in 380-780 nm only at the first dispersive glass interface or active chromatic camera lens.
Earlier contributions stay RGB, and a path without dispersion has no spectral colour noise. It scales dielectric
transmission by the squared incident/transmitted index ratio, retaining separate light-PDF Jacobians.
RGB coefficients remain RGB; the CIE weights do not reconstruct reflectance or emission spectra.
Captures with wavelength set are monochromatic with unit RGB weight; Albedo, normal and depth use hero samples; instance/palette IDs remain centre-ray values. Transparent alpha averages geometric coverage uniformly over wavelengths, or uses the fixed capture wavelength.

Lens settings are immutable at attachment: lensAbbe 0 or 5-200 (default 0), focalLength 1e-6-1e6 world
units (default 0.05). Only camera projection with nonzero aperture uses longitudinal chromatic power.
There is no lateral colour, physical lens stack, diffraction, lens transmission or measured optical
fidelity. Slope correction permits virtual/infinite wavelength focus without singular division.
One sample uses one traversal; no equal-cost convergence or speed claim. The spectralTransport factory
combines this entry with the other optional tracing features through /compose. Root glass and sampling limitations still apply.

Generated stand-in analytic transport and disk-edge tests run on native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility;
plain WebGL2 gives linked unsupported. The spectral transport repair measured 1083 B gzip (previously 1541 B);
its composition factory brings the current entry to 1215 B (unchanged ceiling 1797 B), with inherited root 81091 B gzip. Core plus stage stays 23924 B gzip, under 25,000 B.

## Rectangular building grammar (LIM-642)

productions for an oriented rectangle. It is not a general CGA grammar interpreter.

rows, so each edge meets exactly one opposite edge (no T junction, no pinholes);
each planar face shares its vertices, so welding by position gives a closed
2-manifold solid. GPU-independent lazy

### LIM-650: textured rectangle area lights

Optional `@margoengine/clustered/area-texture` (`AreaLightTextures`): an RGBA8 image on each `AreaLights` rectangle,
sRGB by default, alpha premultiplied. Enforced: at most 16 distinct images, 1,024 texels a side, 4,194,304 texels in all
with their level chains (`RangeError`); one entry per area light (64). The image is stored as half-float linear RGB in a
storage buffer (binding 153), so it adds no sampled texture or sampler. By method: the scalar LTC integral of each lobe
is multiplied by the image filtered over what that lobe sees: the lookup point is where the transformed rectangle's
vector form factor meets its plane, the level is the one whose texel spans the clamped cosine's half-peak footprint
(diameter 1.287 h over the square root of the area, both in the lobe's space), read trilinearly from a box-filtered
chain. It is an approximation: a one-colour image is exact (within half-float rounding, 2^-11), but a detailed image
under a wide lobe is the filtered mean around one point, not the exact integral of the image under the lobe; the
vector form factor ignores the horizon clip; level-0 texels are bilinear with clamped edges, and the chain is
isotropic, so a lobe stretched along one axis of the light reads one blur for both. Built from the LTC paper's integral
and the cosine footprint; the paper's own textured-light section could not be read (docs/clean-room.md, C19).
Proved on stand-ins: the CPU mirror (`packages/clustered/test/area-texture.test.js`) and a real-WebGPU frame check
(`scripts/clustered-light-images-gpu-check.js`: one-colour image against the plain light within 2/255, a split image
lights each side of the floor). No reference against a path tracer yet. Sizes: `npm run quality -- --gate=sizes`.

### LIM-654: light linking and layers

Optional `@margoengine/clustered/layers` (`LightLayers`): a 32-bit layer mask on each clustered point or spot light
(`setLayers`, default 1, layer 0) and on each receiver added through `LightLayers.add` (default 1); a light shades a
receiver when the masks share a bit. Enforced: masks are integers from 0 to 2^32 - 1 and at most 1,024 light masks, one
per clustered light (`RangeError`); a receiver once (`TypeError`). The light masks live in a storage buffer (binding
154); the receiver's mask is a constant in its own shader, so a receiver's layers cost no per-object data, and a change
of a receiver's layers recompiles its shader. By design: core meshes are on layer 0 only (core has no per-mesh slot for
a mask), and area and directional lights are not layered. With every mask 1 the hook is off and the shaders and GPU work
are unchanged. Proved on stand-ins: the CPU mirror (`packages/clustered/test/layers.test.js`: the mask truth table, the
shader rewrite, binding 154 only while needed) and the real-WebGPU `scripts/clustered-light-images-gpu-check.js` (a
layer-1 light leaves a layer-0 floor black, a layer-0 light leaves a layer-1 floor black, a floor on both layers matches
the unlayered light within 2/255). Sizes: `npm run quality -- --gate=sizes`.

bounces; the full row is pinned exactly at the measured value, no slack, and KB4000's measured-path work must come in under
it. No speed or equivalence claim. Re-recorded 2026-11-27 (KB-VOL-TINT-DISPLAY1, the manager's ruling): volume files draw
through the pass, whose Beer-Lambert is exact on one slab (1 level, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer) where the tint was 22 levels
bright. Viewer 1,450,312 -> 1,279,373 (compat 1,279,301), Cycles full 13,834,286 -> 13,883,255 (+48,969; compat 13,883,197),
direct 1,744,201 -> 1,969,228 (+225,027; compat 1,969,232): the tint's lead on the Cycles rows was its own brightness error
standing in for the internal reflection the thickness model lacks (accepted difference above). AMD RDNA 2 receipt
re-measured: 1,277,305 / 13,885,109 / 1,972,680 native, 1,222,662 / 13,913,810 / 2,018,141 compatibility.

## Optional packages on the small preview

The full compatibility device accepts inferred module-private WGSL variable types.
Temporal DOF now has a full-layer route:
half colour/CoC writes, then half-image tile maxima, followed by the existing
gather and join. Its existing MSAA depth approximation and finite sampling limits
still apply. Research and regression paths are in
`docs/whitepaper/compat-continuation-research.md`. Core plus stage is 23,924 B gzip
after the upstream transform-reference diagnostic; these optional repairs do not
change core or stage source.

The small `/preview` engine has backend `webgl2` and no GPU device; the full WebGL2 compatibility layer exposes backend `webgpu`. GPU-only renderers refuse during setup with linked `unsupported`, allowing awaited `autoEngine` setup to escalate through `loadCompat`. Mesh/geometry LOD, screen UI, HTML, stats and picking via `/pick` retain their preview routes. Imposter levels and LOD fading require a complete tier. The texture baker runs under the full layer; current main also provides a native fragment baker on the small preview. Selection and gltf/pbr already refused; their reported silent blank was not reproduced. See `packages/webgl2-compat/test/package-tiers-browser.mjs` for pixel and escalation evidence and `scripts/check-preview-contract.mjs` for the merge gate. Core and stage source are unchanged.

Explicit install() retains an available native WebGPU adapter with a linked MargoError state warning, unless force is true. The full layer needs backend webgpu (or auto), while backend webgl2 requires a preview fallback. The added Gemini GPU attachments refuse preview and escalate; Lighting2D and LayerCompositor use the full device. The current procedural native fragment baker is a real preview route. No new hardware or performance claim is made.

React `<Svg>` on the small preview draws each fill and stroke as a lit, opaque core mesh in its SVG colour, because the preview has no unlit or transparent material: SVG opacity is not applied there, and document order is kept by a +z step per part (1/1000 of the drawing's extent, the whole stack within 5% of it), so the drawing reads correctly from +z. Evidence: `packages/react/scripts/test-shapes-browser.mjs` (svg webgl2).

Canvas recording with audio remains subject to user activation. Its README example initializes a Record button and creates/resumes audio from the click; it does not await permission during module setup. This changes the example, with no new recording, timing or cross-browser capability claim.

### Height-aware grass interaction (batch 77 jobs 3 and 4)

Interactor radius is a sphere in world units, tested at each push-field cell's
bilinearly sampled heightmap height plus the scatter centre Y. Airborne spheres
that miss the surface add no push. The field still stores horizontal vectors,
interpolated at roots, over a camera-centred square; overhangs and multiple
surfaces at one XZ are outside this heightfield representation. Ground sampling
adds four textureLoad reads per field cell; each interactor upload is 32 bytes.
An explosion is a one-frame stamp; existing pushes recover with the usual rate.
The terrain chunks README example holds 16 chunks with 1,024 clumps each and
7/3/1-blade LOD meshes. It makes no huge-area or frame-rate claim.

## Optional RT alpha limits

`bvh/alpha-triangles` preserves original face TEXCOORD_0/material provenance;
`shadows/rt-alpha` snapshots those data into one storage buffer. Five fragment
storage buffers are required, versus four for ordinary RT. WebGL2 and lower
WebGPU tiers use the existing map fallback. Storage costs 16 + 32*faces +
64*masks bytes plus each mask's alpha pixels padded to four bytes, with masks
deduplicated by identity. CPU images must be below 256 MiB and within the device's
buffer limits; each dimension is an integer 1..1,048,576. UV/transform values must
be finite float32; factor/cutoff are 0..1. Four times each masked face's absolute
affine UV bound must fit float32, including the offset, to prevent intermediate
overflow. Repack after UV/material/topology edits.
Core geometry is opaque; model skin/morph positions are bind pose. Unsupported
images/UV sets are reported by modelAlphaMasks.skipped and retain its opaque
policy. The real-GPU traversal/fragment and public Shadows.attach pixel proofs
pass for default/quarter-turn masks, restoration and fallback. RT far ends at
the configured distance; the map fallback instead uses the map's full reach.
Measured gzip entries: bvh root 23,362 / 23,398 B ceiling, bvh/gpu
5,582 / 5,738 B, bvh/alpha 16,513 / 16,873 B, shadows/rt 6,409 / 6,486 B.
New alpha-triangles is 1,125 B (1,381 B ceiling); rt-alpha is 8,739 B
(8,816 B ceiling). No existing ceiling rises. Core plus stage remains 23,924 B.

packages/webgl2-compat/test/tier-packages-browser.mjs). The shared tier check took
`@margoengine/taa/upscale` from 7,384 to 7,624 B gzip and the root from 14,686 to
14,927 B.

TAAUpscale with a 4x capture on the WebGL2 layer (`@margoengine/taa/upscale`, 2026-11-11,
KB5580a) reads each depth texel as the nearest of the texel and its four neighbours.
WebGL2 shaders cannot read single samples (GLSL ES 3.00 has no multisample sampler), so
the layer's resolved depth is one sample where native WebGPU keeps the nearest of the
four. The neighbourhood is wider than a pixel's own coverage, so silhouettes reject
history over one more low-resolution texel than natively. Measured in
packages/taa/test/upscale-browser.mjs: 31.96 dB on the layer against 31.76 natively
and 30.90 before. Native reads are unchanged.

The Orrery on the WebGL2 layer (`examples/orrery`, Scott accepted 2026-11-15) differs
from native WebGPU on 3.54% of pixels (d > 2, mean 0.454, `npm run visual:compat`,
RTX A6000, Edge 157, 2026-11-16) through the PostStack's 1x depth: native keeps the
nearest of the 4 samples (`depthCopy` in packages/shared/msaa.js), the layer sample 0.
Native does better on silhouettes: a partly covered pixel keeps its object's depth for
DOF, contact shadows, SSAO and TAAUpscale. The native resolve is not changed for the
layer. With TAAUpscale's jitter phase held (native noise 0.00%): 3.11% as shipped,
3.51% with DOF's layer widening off, 2.26% with DOF off; a probe build whose native depth
copy keeps sample 0 gives 1.24%, and 0.00% with the widening or DOF off, so DOF adds no
difference of its own. Free running, two native captures differ on 0.23% to 0.36%
(max d up to 241) because TAAUpscale cycles through 8 jitter phases with the camera
still. Method and reproduction: docs/known-bugs.md (the Orrery entry) and
[webgl2-compat-demos.md](webgl2-compat-demos.md#accepted-difference-per-sample-reads-of-multisampled-textures).

### Batch 56 review: finite studio directions
### Batch 56 review fixes: dominant HDR ground shadow

The optional staging/ground receiver approximates one distant light from the
luminance-weighted first radiance SH moment. It follows environment rotation;
multiple-light visibility, physical HDR light size, full radiometry, product
self-shadow and photographic floor reconstruction are outside this approximation.
It retains contact receiver dimensions, texture limits and spatial Gaussian blur.
At moment length <= 1e-6 * abs(luminance L0), intensity zero, or receiver-normal
cosine <= 1e-6, it draws no directional shadow. Very low lights need a wide
receiver; the configured rectangle clips long shadows. No CPU geometry loop,
new Wasm, core feature or speed claim is added. Native WebGL2 preview refuses;
WebGPU and the compatibility backend execute the same pass path.

Scene captures and explicit disposal use the owning scene. Viewport/scissor
are applied to the planar surface, image background and colour background;
local target passes keep local coordinates. Staging still idle/history keys
exclude temporal raster jitter, including zero idle delay. Studio softboxes
preserve finite extreme and subnormal directions by scaling before normalization.

## Batch 234 FFT ocean

The optional water `/fft` entry uses 16..512 Fourier samples per axis (powers
of two), 1..4 disjoint wavelength bands and a separate 1..1024-cell draw grid.
Its Gaussian linear Phillips/JONSWAP spectra use deep-water gravity dispersion,
periodic patches, choppy displacement, tangent normals and folding foam. DC
and the Nyquist row/column are omitted. Finite-depth dispersion, overturning
volumes and shoreline flow are not solved by this entry. Its square draw grid
is finite and follows the camera by default. A requested CPU snapshot is of
the last rendered frame; rendering never reads the GPU back. One read can be
pending. All buffers are rebuilt on device restoration. Details, size evidence
and correctness reproduction: [water-fft.md](water-fft.md).

The `/fft` entry is 7,334 B minified gzip (new ceiling 7,590 B); core + stage
is unchanged at 23,924 B in the full rebuilt measurement. Snapshot time,
mean height and patch lengths are binary32 GPU values, including rounding.

## Batch 234 wave queries

Optional `@margoengine/water/query` captures actual rendered Water/FFTOcean
geometry and performs synchronous CPU triangle queries. Highest overlapping
hits win; finite mesh edges and coastal dry masks can return undefined.
Macro normals exclude shading-only ripples and view-dependent underside
flipping. Particle velocity includes wave motion and conservative coastal
current; it is not Eulerian height rate or a boat solver. Snapshots retain
rendered time and need explicit refresh. Captures use the GPU and read back
48 B per vertex, 16 B per projected hierarchy node, and FFT/coastal source
fields (48/16 B per sample respectively), with temporary GPU staging memory.
The hierarchy handles arbitrary segment counts; no CPU FFT or geometry build.

### Batch 273 polygon offset clamp checkpoint

The optional compatibility device now loads EXT_polygon_offset_clamp and replays
slope, units and the signed depthBiasClamp together. Positive clamp is a minimum
with the computed offset, negative a maximum; zero disables clamping. The cache
includes clamp and replays reset to zero. Without the extension, nonzero clamp
refuses synchronous and asynchronous pipeline creation with code unsupported and
a help link before shader compilation. Zero-clamp offset remains supported.
No core or stage source or export changed; their gzip remains 23,924 B.

## Triangle-mesh lightmaps (batch 54)

`bakeMeshLightmap` (`@margoengine/lightmap/mesh`) bakes on the CPU, one mesh per call, at most 2,048 x 2,048 texels,
4,194,304 covered texels and 67,108,864 rays. Light is direct (with shadows) and AO, plus path-traced diffuse bounces
with physical radiometry (see "Path-traced lightmap bounces"); area and emissive lights are in `./global` for quads
only. Overlapping UV charts are counted (`overlaps`), not separated: the later triangle's
light is kept where both centres fall. Dilation averages neighbours across a gutter narrower than twice `dilate`, so
two charts closer than that blend in the gutter (never inside a chart). Overlaps under 1e-3 texels count as touching.

## Directional lightmaps (batch 54)

`bakeDirectionalLightmap` (`@margoengine/lightmap/directional`) stores one main light direction and one directional
colour per texel (world space), not SH or the H-basis: with several lights it is exact only at the unmapped normal and
approximate under a normal map (exact for one light plus ambient). Ambient light and AO are not directional. It takes
the `bakeMeshLightmap` limits and its direct-light-only scope; bounce light has no direction. The RGBA8 direction map
quantizes each component to 1/255 of 2, and the GPU filters it bilinearly before renormalising, so at a texel edge
between two very different directions the drawn direction is their blend. `applyLightmap` draws it per pixel
(`directionalIrradiance` on the GPU, 2026-11-24) on glTF PBR models only, WebGPU only like every glTF PBR lightmap;
materials, `createMesh` and core mesh targets draw the flat lightmap (no normal-map response), and `directional: true`
on them throws. The directional shader binds two more RGBA8 textures (8 bytes per texel) and took `lightmap/apply` from
2,442 B to 2,972 B min+gzip (ceiling 2,634 to 3,228 B): the shader and the bake check are worth it, and a separate
entry would duplicate the extension, device-restore and dispose code it shares with the flat path.

## Lightmap rough glass, dispersion and bounce caustics (batch 54)

`bakeRefractedLightmap` (`@margoengine/lightmap/refracted`) rough glass follows a Smith microsurface random walk (Heitz et al. 2016), so masked light scatters again instead of
being dropped; `diagnostics.masked` is kept for compatibility and is always zero. Microsurface events share the
`maxEvents` limit (1 to 32), and a photon still on the microsurface at that limit counts as truncated. Roughness is
per volume, isotropic or an anisotropic `[u, v]` pair whose U axis is `roughnessDirection` projected onto each
boundary (a perpendicular axis replaces it where the projection vanishes). The walk uses a uniform height
distribution, which cancels from the result, and unit-weight dielectric events (photon power, not radiance). Dispersion uses Cauchy's
two-term fit (no Sellmeier), wavelengths 380 to 780 nm with out-of-gamut colours clipped, and the event Fresnel at one
wavelength per photon. Bounces (at most 4) are diffuse and use the quad's albedo only (no `surface` callback, no
textures); receivers stay opaque.

## Lightmap irradiance probes (batch 54)

`bakeLightProbes` (`@margoengine/lightmap/probes`) bakes on the CPU, at most 64 probes per axis (262,144) and 67,108,864
rays, 16 to 16,384 gather rays per probe. Each probe is order-3 SH, so a strong light rings: a delta light gives about
6% of its irradiance straight behind it and 9% at 90 degrees, and `probeIrradiance` clamps below 0. The room's light
reaches probes only through its lightmap (one mesh), so one bounce beyond the lightmap; occluders reflect nothing;
emissive surfaces and area lights are not sampled. Probes have no visibility weighting (light can leak through thin
walls between probes), and `@margoengine/environment`'s `LightProbes` cannot load the baked coefficients yet.

## Lightmap denoising (batch 54)

`@margoengine/lightmap/denoise` runs on the CPU, at most 16,777,216 texels (8,192 a side) per call, 1 to 8 a-trous
passes of 25 taps each. It is not energy conserving (a weighted mean per texel, as Dammertz et al. 2010 note). Charts
are filtered separately: neighbouring quads in the world are not neighbours in the atlas, so quad charts a few texels
wide get little smoothing. Without a supplied `variance` the noise is estimated per texel from its neighbours (median
absolute deviation); smooth gradients count partly as noise and are smoothed slightly, and a lone bright texel (a
firefly) is averaged into its neighbours but not clamped. The quad atlas path reads the 8-bit lightmap, so its input
carries 8-bit quantisation; the mesh path reads the float `irradiance`.

## Path-traced lightmap bounces (batch 54)

`bakeGlobalLightmap({ bounceMode: 'path' })` traces at most 8 diffuse bounces, `bounceRays` (1 to 32) paths per texel,
on the CPU, within `maxRays`. Each path vertex reads the direct light of the texel it hits, at that texel's centre, so
light varying inside one texel is averaged (texel-sized bias); there is no Russian roulette (paths stop at `bounces`),
no glossy or metallic bounce (metals reflect nothing) and no light through glass on bounce paths.

Triangle meshes (`bakeMeshLightmap` and `bakeDirectionalLightmap`, 2026-11-24) take `bounces` (0 to 8, physical
radiometry only) and `bounceRays` (1 to 1,024 paths per texel, default 16), on the CPU, within `maxRays` (each path
counts one ray per bounce plus one shadow ray per light at each hit). Each hit gets its direct light by next-event
estimation at the hit itself (no texel-sized bias), with the geometric normal turned toward the ray, as `./gpu` does;
reflectance is one RGB per mesh and per occluder (no textures), diffuse only, and there is no Russian roulette.
Ambient light adds its unoccluded irradiance at every hit (as in `./gpu`). Bounce light is not directional: a
directional bake's direction and directional colour hold direct light only. Proof: a closed box under ambient light
equals the geometric series within 1e-5 on every texel; one bounce off a lit wall matches the exact form factor
(worst texel 0.047, mean 0.0035, 1,024 paths; `packages/lightmap/tests/mesh.test.js`). The bounce code took
`lightmap/mesh` from 3,128 B to 4,089 B and `lightmap/directional` from 4,215 B to 5,140 B min+gzip (ceilings 3,272 to
4,345 B and 4,471 to 5,396 B): both entries share the bake, and a separate entry would copy its setup.

### FSM completion (batch 250 job 2)
Optional fsm/final adds FinalMachine with final:true leaves, done.state.parent and always:true transitions. Final leaves have no children, regions or outgoing transitions. A top-level final stops events and clock advancement; goto explicitly restarts. Eventless steps run before queued completions and between delays. Limits: 10,000 eventless/internal steps per stabilization (9,999 eventless transitions settle; one more throws) and 100,000 timed firings per update (the 100,001st throws) produce coded state errors; break cycles or use shorter deltas. Internal NUL-prefixed event names are reserved. Completion events retain the causing payload. Existing ParallelRegions remain ordinary region machines; FinalMachine completion is local to its hierarchy.

Batch 250 job 2: fsm/final 0 to 2825 B min+gzip, ceiling 3081 B. Optional runtime is not loaded by the FSM root or core/stage.

The 11 B refuse SCXML transitions whose exit and re-entry Margo cannot keep (self, ancestor and external-to-descendant targets) and mark Margo's own self and ancestor transitions `m:stay`. ### Tile styling (batch 239 job 1)

`@margoengine/tiles/style` supplies `TilesStyle`: property expressions drive sRGB RGBA, show and pixel point size, with ordered conditions, defines and metadata expressions. The language supports scalar/vector math, comparisons, short circuiting, ternaries, arrays, property paths, interpolation, CSS colours and regular expressions. Expressions are limited to 65,536 characters, 4,096 tokens and 128 parser nesting levels. Wrong output types fail with a coded state error. No arbitrary host methods or JavaScript execution are allowed.

`TilesStyle.decorate` is the renderer's optional `decorate` hook; it binds loaded b3dm batch IDs, pnts batch IDs and point semantics, i3dm instance IDs, and structural attribute/implicit feature tables. The optional save/opfs entry uses a private subdirectory, default margo-saves, and atomically replaces a file at FileSystemWritableFileStream.close. ### Signed safe saves (batch 255 job 4)

The optional save/signed entry exposes signedStorage(storage, key, options), returning the full SafeStorage read/write/delete/keys/check interface. It authenticates each complete safe frame including generation under its physical key using WebCrypto HMAC-SHA-256. Raw keys must have at least 32 bytes; CryptoKeys must be secret HMAC/SHA-256 keys of at least 256 bits with sign and verify usages. Raw key bytes are copied, imported lazily, nonextractable, and never written into the save. The caller owns generating, retaining and distributing a secret key; embedded client application keys cannot resist an attacker controlling that client. Authentication detects edits, format changes, role swaps and cross-key copies. It does not encrypt, prevent deletion, or reject replay of an older authenticated frame in the same physical key. Unsigned legacy saves fail closed, including a runtime legacy:true option. A damaged newest copy recovers from an older authenticated one and invokes onRecover; both bad reject with a coded error. Crypto awaits observe AbortSignal before storage writes. The format costs 37 bytes per copy beyond safeStorage's 24 bytes, or 122 bytes of framing across two stored payload copies. The default provider is globalThis.crypto.subtle; options.subtle supports an explicit provider. Existing safe verify/onRecover options apply. README: `packages/save/README.md`, sections "Signed saves" and "Browser file storage", examples run by `check:readme-run`.

Save/signed entry: 2,581 B min+gzip (before: absent, 0 B), ceiling 2,837 B, including the safeStorage implementation it composes. Core plus stage stays 23,950 B. Keeping authentication and recovery together avoids a caller accidentally authenticating only payload bytes while trusting an edited generation or copy role.

## Fuzzy decisions (batch 251)

New behavior/fuzzy measures 2,621 B min+gzip (previously absent), generated umbrella
alias 61 B external; no existing ceiling raised. Inputs are finite world/domain
values, and memberships outside a shape's finite domain are zero. Default output
method centroid, 256 midpoint samples (integer 1..1,000,000), fallback 0 when no
rule fires. Mean-of-max is the mean of the sampled maxima, not an exact continuous
integral. Max-average uses weighted set representatives. Continuous and discrete
singleton sets use separate output variables. Custom sampling ranges must have
finite min <= max and finite width. Expression depth is limited to 256; cycles
reject. Rules are one forward Mamdani stage; evaluation has no inter-agent state
or implicit recurrent feedback. JSON round trips preserve the whole designer
configuration. No GPU entry or speed claim; default-sized decision evaluation
has no proven Wasm gain.
### SCXML document subset (batch 250 job 5)
Optional fsm/scxml converts definitions to/from MachineDocument. Input supports the W3C SCXML namespace and version 1.0, state hierarchy, explicit/implicit initial states, parallel state regions, one history pseudo-state per state, single-target event transitions, symbolic guards, and named entry/exit hooks. History fallback must match ordinary initial because the native document has one initial field. Cross-region targets, wildcard/list events, executable transition content, arbitrary script/guard expressions, DTDs/entities, final/invoke/eventless constructs and unknown elements/attributes reject. Final/invoke definitions belong to separate optional runtimes, not MachineDocument. Session name/datamodel metadata is accepted but is not saved.
Native extensions in urn:margoengine:fsm:1 are enabled by default on export and retain delay, cross-fade duration, update hook, region history, transition ordering, arbitrary binding/state names and explicit native region boundaries. A parallel holder with separate hierarchical children is outside this subset. extensions:false produces the common standard hierarchy/event/named-hook subset and rejects native-only fields. This is document conversion, not a conforming SCXML processor: Margo retains exact event names, remembered-parent targeting and common-ancestor transition semantics. The importer never evaluates an expression or invokes a hook. Browser DOMParser is the default; Node must supply options.parser, with no new parser runtime dependency.
Input/output limit: 1 MiB UTF-8; 10,000 XML elements; 128 XML nesting levels; export preflight limits native region nesting to 64 and rejects cycles. Plain XML ids use the ASCII identifier subset; arbitrary native names use generated ids plus namespaced names. XML 1.0 forbidden characters reject. Shared region definition objects are valid; cycles are not.

Batch 250 job 5: fsm/scxml 0 to 4970 B min+gzip, ceiling 5226 B. Optional runtime is not loaded by the FSM root or core/stage.
Security fix sec-sinks (2026-11-10): SCXML is read by Margo's strict XML 1.0 and namespaces reader (`packages/shared/xml-document.js`) instead of DOMParser, in browsers, workers and Node alike; the `parser` option is deprecated and ignored. The reader refuses malformed XML, DTD internal subsets, entities other than the five predefined ones and nesting over 512 (SCXML still stops at 128 levels and 10,000 elements). fsm/scxml ceiling 5226 to 7494 B min+gzip measured; the reader is about 2.3 KB of it.

### Batch 197 product-page controls

Optional controls/presentation exports PresentationControls, ScrollArea, ScrollControls, PathControls and MotionPathControls (alias). Presentation rotates one live mesh relative to its starting rotation, defaults to product-only picking (global=false), polar [-PI/2,PI/2], unbounded azimuth, speed=1, zoom=1, snap=false. Springs default to stiffness 170, damping 26 and precision 0.000001; bounds project spring state and stop outward velocity. The optional tween peer is required for this entry's spring API; other entries do not load it.

ScrollArea owns a native overlay scroller and HTML content slot. Defaults pages=1, distance=1, horizontal=false, prepend=false. ScrollControls accepts that element or an application scroller, with equivalent page/distance defaults for a wheel-only surface. Defaults damping=0.2 seconds, maxSpeed=Infinity, eps=0.00001, infinite=false. Native scroll uses actual overflow; wheel fallback uses configured viewport pages. Infinite native scroll recentres at the ends without changing continuous progress. Offset is normalized, delta is signed per-update progress; range/curve/visible use normalized intervals. Native keyboard/touch scrolling stays with the browser.

PathControls drives the camera or an explicitly selected engine mesh, optionally from ScrollControls. A curve implements at(t), optionally length/atDistance for arc-length sampling (Margo Spline fits directly). Defaults loop=true, offset=0, damping=0.1 seconds, focusDamping=0.1 seconds, maxSpeed=Infinity, lookAhead=0.001. Focus is a world point or live mesh; otherwise the view follows the path tangent, including the final non-looping endpoint. Zero-length tangents use -Z, vertical views use +Z up. Points must be finite. Mesh positions use the full inverse parent matrix; orientation removes the parent's rotation and does not model shear from a nonuniform scaled/rotated parent. All classes dispose their owned listeners/plugins; ScrollArea removes only owned DOM. Applications dispose controls before removing the scroll area.

Rejections must be observed. Core/stage unchanged.

### Full tween timeline (batch 215 job 3)

New tween/timeline entry: 3184 B gzip from 0 B. A separate Timeline class holds scalar, array, custom, path and nested timelines. Local speeds are finite > 0 (default 1), repeats integers >= 0 or Infinity, yoyo false. Attached children have one owning parent; their clocks are sampled by that parent. Calls/completions run on playback crossings and never on seek. Nested durations include repeats and divide by child speed. Infinite children make a parent endless; an endless zero-duration repeat rejects. Cancellation freezes the tree, rejects observed finished promises, and preserves signal.reason. Callback errors propagate and reject the owner. Core/stage unchanged.

Optional tween/control: 3714 B gzip (previously 0 B). TweenControl is an explicit world, with global timeScale 1 by default and no module-global state. New tween/inertia: 2778 B gzip from 0 B. Caller supplies release velocity or a VelocityTracker; sample/release times are seconds. The tracker defaults to a 0.1 s window and 32 samples, with configurable capacity 2..1024; stale release returns zero. Resistance defaults to 6 per second. Endpoints may be numeric, nearest lists or functions of the predicted end; optional min/max bound the selected endpoint. Hard ranges are default; bounce in [0,1) opts into spring overshoot. Rest thresholds are 0.01 units/s and 0.001 units; after maxDuration (default 10 simulated seconds) the exact end is written. Local speed 1 by default, with pause/play and AbortSignal. ### Batch 171 atmosphere on the globe

The new optional sciviz/atmosphere entry composes geo's WGS84 globe with sky/planet's existing Hillaire RGB medium. Importing sciviz root, geo, grids or flow without atmosphere adds no sky dependency to the runtime graph. A GPUDevice is required: WebGPU and webgl2-compat, not the separate native WebGL2 sciviz driver. Perspective cameras only; the observer must remain outside the ellipsoid. Figure model inversion handles arbitrary nonsingular data-to-scene affine transforms.

Data positions use longitude/latitude degrees and geodetic metres above WGS84. Scalar triangle values/masks are retained; points are tangent-disc glyphs with a physical radius (default 10000 m, maximum 1000000 m). Geographic wind uses east/north/up m/s and seconds, converted once at input samples by WGS84 curvature to degree/degree/metre rates. The existing GPU RK4, temporal/spatial interpolation, seeding, trails, respawn and replay remain unchanged. Grid latitudes exclude the exact poles; longitude width is at most 360 degrees, with boundary respawn instead of implicit periodic interpolation. No per-frame CPU particle readback. Linear interpolation of the converted angular field is an approximation to interpolation of local physical vectors.

The medium stretches the polar coordinate by 1/(1-f), mapping the exact WGS84 ground to the sphere used by Hillaire. Transport distances and geodetic normal heights change by at most 0.3365 percent, and phase/solar angles are correspondingly approximated. Geometry is not stretched. Tile chord fragments use the reference ground radius for lighting/transport, avoiding underground integration. This is not exact ellipsoidal, spectral or weather radiative transfer. Data-fragment transport uses 24 steps; background uses 32; existing transmittance/multiple-scattering tables retain their resolutions and method. Radii are at most 100000 km and vertical scattering depth at most 6; exposure -20..20, top-of-atmosphere illuminance 0..1000000 (default 20).

Optional clouds accept geographic shell triangles and scalar density clamped to [0,1], including NaN as empty. They are solar-lit data shells with aerial transport; no inferred cloud thickness, volumetric self-shadow or shadow map. Transparent layers retain the renderer's layer sorting. Globe owns its returned layers until disposed; individually removed layers may retain their CPU records until that owner is disposed. The data coordinates remain inspectable through the supplied arrays and existing layer APIs.

The official NOAA demo uses the hash-pinned public-domain wind.bin. Sigma 0.995 is not a height. Wind at 20000 m, speed colours at 1000 m and reference glyphs at 100000 m are explicitly labelled display placements, not measured atmospheric altitudes. See examples/assets/sciviz/atmosphere.json. No speed assertion, benchmark or core/stage source change.

## Batch 258 image scope

ImageTexture copies straight-alpha RGBA8 sRGB pixels, decodes browser images with AbortSignal, and snapshots canvas/image/video sources. Images default to contain, centered in the content box; cover crops and fill stretches. Source is an integer pixel atlas cell. Nine-slice borders are source pixels times borderScale (default 1); they override fit and shrink uniformly if the target cannot fit both borders. Tint defaults to opaque white. No GPU objects are exposed or borrowed from core.

Cells are cached as 60-pixel tiles with a one-texel neighbor gutter per side. Filter footprints clamp at cell boundaries, and alpha is premultiplied before filtering. UI's colour atlas controls total residency: default 512-square pages, 16 pages; increase colorAtlasSize/maxPages for more images. Its configured atlas limits still throw when exhausted. Source pixel buffers and cached tiles are CPU memory retained with ImageTexture. Dropping it releases unreferenced source storage; tiles already admitted to a renderer atlas remain until atlas eviction or renderer disposal. Edits use a new ImageTexture. Raw preview GL retains its existing encoded-space compositing; complete compatibility follows the WebGPU path. No speed claim or GPU render-target input is made.

Batch 257 job 1, worker/rpc: cloneable arguments/results only, with explicit transfer lists for input and output. A pool owns its workers; a standalone client owns only its subscriptions. @margoengine/materials/atlas padTileGrid (2026-11-14): enforced, each output edge at most `maxSize` (an integer 1 to 4096, default 4096, the same cap as packAtlas and below the 8,192 every WebGPU device gives as maxTextureDimension2D). The output keeps the source grid's columns while both edges fit; otherwise the tiles wrap into the most square layout that fits, and a grid that cannot fit throws RangeError. Before, only the output area was capped (16,777,216 texels), so one row of 420 tiles of 16 x 8 with padding 2 made an 8,400 x 12 image that texture creation refused.
@margoengine/materials eye (2026-11-14): the view and light rays bend once, by `chamberIor` (aqueous humour, default 1.336), as through a thin cornea with parallel faces; the cornea's `ior` (default 1.376) sets only its reflection. The cornea's curvature difference between its faces (Gullstrand's 7.7 and 6.8 mm radii) is not modelled.

### Batch 254 global voice budget
Optional @margoengine/audio/voices: 2117 B minified gzip, new entry from 0 B. AudioVoiceManager has maxVoices=32 (integer >=0) and linear threshold=0.0001. add(sound,{priority=0,gain=()=>1}) returns a managed transport. All registered decoded-buffer sounds on one listener share the cap, including global, stereo and positional sounds. Larger finite priority wins, then volume/fade/master/distance/cone/custom gain; ties retain registration order. Each frame updates managed poses before ranking. Losers release buffer sources before winners allocate, so the cap is never transiently exceeded. Virtual voices allocate no buffer source; logical phase advances on context.currentTime, wraps configured loops and integrates playbackRate*2^(detune/1200). Handle play/pause/stop/seek, playbackRate and detune own transport; pitch changes restart a physical source at the exact phase. Do not call raw sound/pool transport, replace buffers, automate source pitch, or attach Doppler/timeline transport while managed. Raw volume, pose, filters and fades remain available. Media/stream/node sources cannot be phase-virtualized by this buffer-only manager. gain is a caller-supplied estimate for effects/occlusion/bus gain; no perceptual masking analysis. Selection occurs on updates, not within an audio render quantum. Handles/manager stop sources on dispose and preserve caller-owned sounds/buffers; listener teardown owns the sounds. Core/stage unchanged.

### Sprite picking (batch 245 job 3)
The optional sprites/pick entry exports pickSprite. Points use target pixels,
y down; CSS pointers need canvas-to-client scaling first. Defaults match
SpriteLayer: camera (0,0,1), snapping on, y sorting off. Pixel mode (default)
uses original RGBA8 atlas alpha multiplied by packed sprite opacity; box mode
requires only atlas dimensions. Threshold defaults to 1 byte; zero alpha never
picks. Pages have equal dimensions, and source bytes remain caller-owned.
Rotation, signed scale, pivot, texture flips, z/y/add order and layer masks are
honoured. Picking never mutates the list or reads the GPU. Shader-generated alpha
and smooth-filter reconstruction are outside source-alpha hit-test semantics.
Entry: 1,933 B gzip (new, previously 0), ceiling 2,189 B; core + stage unchanged
at 23,950 B. The same transform packer avoids a second renderer-specific transform.
The picking proof also found and fixed the sprite renderer's circle-boundary
interpolation error. Masks now use raster pixel centres with the view origin
removed. Sprite root is 7,480 B gzip (was 7,455); its existing 7,660 B ceiling
holds. Existing uniform padding stores the origin, so uniform allocation does
not grow. The redundant two-float position interpolator is removed.

Current slice bundle after the shared mask repair is 8,614 B gzip (8,587 B at
job 1 landing), within its unchanged 8,845 B ceiling. Caller-owned picking

### Stats geometry entry

`@margoengine/stats/geometry` provides GeometryStats, attach/beginFrame/track/trackDevice/trackGL/pipeline/view/toJSON/dispose. The geometry row and optional third statsReport argument expose triangles, submitted vertices, instances, drawCalls and unknownDraws. Indexed vertices include repetitions; instance totals sum non-empty draw submissions rather than unique scene objects. Triangle strips/fans count assembled candidates before restart markers, degeneracy, clipping or culling. Existing WebGPU pipelines default to triangle-list unless registered with pipeline(); future tracked device pipelines retain their topology. GPU-written indirect data and render bundles are opaque: supply the indirect CPU metadata callback where available; otherwise unknownDraws reports missing observations without inventing counts. Native methods still run with their original receivers. Multiple engine views in the same task accumulate; custom loops call beginFrame explicitly. No core or stage change. Entry: 1,568 B gzip, new ceiling 1,824 B. Root: 4,861 B; report: 1,165 B; combined core + stage: 23,950 B.
@margoengine/input/haptics: 945 B gzip (previously absent), ceiling 1201 B. Cohesive lifecycle retained; no separate fragment entry. Core and stage unchanged.

Batch 253 trigger rumble: optional input/haptics exports triggerRumble, supportsTriggerRumble and structural effect/actuator/gamepad/options types. Pass a native Gamepad (including an XR source gamepad) or adapter. Defaults: duration 100 ms, startDelay 0, leftTrigger/rightTrigger 1, strongMagnitude/weakMagnitude 0, timeout 6000 ms. Durations are nonnegative safe integers; intensities are finite [0,1]; timeout is positive and at most 2147483647 ms. Browsers can cap native durations, commonly at the spec-recommended five seconds. Increase timeout for longer effects. Capability returns undefined for old actuators without an effects list; playback probes them once. Return true means native complete; false means unsupported/disconnected or preempted. Permission/device failures propagate. Abort/timeout stops only the latest call through this entry on the actuator; stop has a separate 1000 ms bound. Stop failure throws AggregateError containing the original reason and stop failure. Without reset, a zero trigger effect stops playback. This entry cannot coordinate effects started externally through other APIs. Physical controller support, visibility/permissions policy and actual trigger motor response remain browser/device-dependent and require hardware acceptance.
- XR skinned hands require all 25 named joint nodes in one glTF skin. Default names are the WebXR joint names; custom names are explicit. Both hands use separate caller-owned models, preserving authored mirroring, hierarchy, inverse binds and weights. Joint transforms are reference-space world poses. Parent transforms must be invertible and yield decomposable local TRS; use uniform model-root scale. No model URLs are fetched implicitly. Animation is loaded lazily. Partial tracking hides the whole hand; dispose restores borrowed transforms. Physical-device validation remains job 1's hardware gap.

- xr/hands: 0 to 2290 B gzip, ceiling 2546 B for the new optional 25-joint skinned hand entry. Core + stage remains 23950 B.

### Batch 254 audio sprites and codec fallback
Optional @margoengine/audio/sprites: 1508 B minified gzip, new entry from 0 B. AudioSpriteBank snapshots named intervals in buffer seconds, offset>=0 and duration>0 wholly within the decoded buffer, loop=false by default. create(name,options) returns a stopped Audio; play(name,options,delay=0) starts an overlapping instance. Every instance shares the original buffer and uses native offset/duration or bounded loop points. Natural ends call the supplied callback and dispose that instance; explicit pause/stop retains it until caller/bank disposal. Bank stopAll preserves the map; dispose/using/listener teardown release owned sounds, never the shared buffer. loadAudioFallback accepts ordered URL strings with recognized extensions or {url,type} candidates with explicit MIME/codec declarations. maybe/probably are eligible in list order. Unsupported types are skipped; each supported resource is fetched/decoded once, trying the next after failure. Abort stops the operation. Exhaustion raises linked failed with AggregateError in cause, or unsupported when no candidate is eligible. In workers pass canPlayType; the default lazily creates an audio element. LoadAudioOptions are forwarded, including signal, cache and custom fetch. canPlayType is advisory and cannot guarantee decode support, multichannel containers or gapless compressed boundaries. Sample-accurate boundaries are verified on decoded WAV PCM; lossy encoder padding needs authored sprite bounds. No core/stage change.
Batch 257 job 3 supersedes the earlier worker pointer-lock gap: WorkerCanvas and ReceivedCanvas expose pointerLocked, requestPointerLock and exitPointerLock. The forwarded worker canvas also supplies the document-shaped pointer-lock members needed by PointerLockControls, with unchanged movementX/movementY counts. Requests must follow browser user-activation/permission policy; a forwarded trusted page interaction can request lock, or the page can request directly in its gesture. Defaults: unadjustedMovement false, timeout 10000 ms, no AbortSignal. Abort/deadline end the wait; the browser offers no native cancellation of a permission request. Raw-input denial is reported, never silently retried. Lock-change/error events and document mouse movement are forwarded; disposal releases only this canvas lock and clears worker state.

### Stats WebGL2 timer entry

`@margoengine/stats/gl` provides GLStats. Custom loops call beginFrame(gl), beginPass/endPass or pass(name, work), endFrame, then poll from a later task. Engine attach wraps the existing graph execution and main draw; attach before other plugins to time their newly registered named passes. Existing custom passes can use pass(name, work) explicitly. Views in one task accumulate into one frame closed in a microtask. Frame milliseconds sum non-overlapping elapsed GPU segments, including gaps between passes; they exclude presentation and pre-graph CPU/update work. Named intervals do not include the gap intervals. TIME_ELAPSED queries never nest. Defaults: maxPasses 128 (1..128), maxPendingFrames 4 (1..8); overfull/backlogged samples are dropped, counters continue, and disjoint/invalid/lost samples clear GPU timings. Unsupported contexts retain draw counts and show unavailable. An already-active application elapsed query causes the profiler to omit that frame. Do not start another elapsed profiler inside an instrumented frame. Context restoration reacquires the extension. view, toJSON and Symbol.dispose are supported. New optional entry: 2,281 B gzip, ceiling 2,537 B; Stats root and combined core/stage remain unchanged.
- XR AR extras require the native module requested before entering AR. Current image targets use marker-tracking/getImageTrackability; set legacy explicitly for image-tracking/getImageTrackingScores. Snapshots copy poses and mesh geometry, but geometry arrays are reused until native lastChangedTime or label changes. Null poses hide displays. DOM overlay and ImageBitmap roots remain caller-owned. Persistent handles belong to the origin/browser, survive tracker disposal, and are deleted only explicitly or when an aborted save created a new unclaimed handle. Native anchor save/restore operations cannot be canceled: abort is checked before and after their settlement so cleanup can complete. No cross-device/cloud anchor transfer or invented tracking fallback is provided. Device permissions and tracking accuracy still need real-device validation.

- xr/ar-extra: 0 to 3033 B gzip, ceiling 3289 B for the new optional DOM, image, mesh and persistent anchor entry. Core + stage remains 23950 B.



Batch 249 relation-query: each result is a source plus one target per required relation term. Wildcards return every pair combination, so results may exceed world.capacity. Queries snapshot pairs and recheck live membership/rows before visits; new pairs wait until the next iteration. Optional source rows use -1. Target with terms are required and their rows flatten in term order. This is direct pair matching; traversal remains in Relation.
ecs/relation-query: 1023 B min+gzip, new optional entry previously 0 B; ceiling 1279 B. Core plus stage unchanged at 23950 B.

Batch 225 job 1: splines/kinds adds catmullRomSpline (centripetal default, chordal/uniform options; closed=false, divisions=256), CubicSpline and analytic splineDerivative (order=1), splineCurvature and splineTorsion. Parameter t is 0..1; derivatives are global-t derivatives, right-hand at joins and periodic at the closed seam. Nonuniform geometry is tangent-continuous but equal per-piece t does not imply matching derivative magnitudes at unequal chord joins. Curvature is NaN at stationary points; torsion is NaN without an osculating plane. Repeated knots give constant zero-span pieces. Returned Bezier controls are editable using the existing points/updateArcLengths contract. Closed CubicSpline requires coincident endpoints. Arc lengths remain sampled. No GPU implementation or GPU tests exist in this CPU-only package; core and stage untouched.

Batch 225 /kinds: new optional entry 0 -> 2802 B gzip (ceiling 0 -> 3058 B); geometry operations belong together to share polynomial calculations. Core + stage remains 23950 B gzip, below 25000 B; root sources untouched.

### Stats panels entry

`@margoengine/stats/panels` provides StatsPanels, attach/sample/refresh/toJSON/dispose, with four chronological fixed Float64Array histories and a named GPU list. Defaults: samples 120 (2..4096), refreshMilliseconds 150 (16..60000), parent document.body; owned panel width 360 CSS pixels within the viewport. Options.stats borrows an already attached Stats without transferring its ownership. CPU milliseconds come from FramePhases work in the frame task, FPS from the rolling Stats interval, GPU from the latest completed asynchronous sample. GPU history therefore holds the latest valid result between readbacks, rather than pretending each frame has a fresh query. WebGPU samples one encoder in 15, at most 128 passes, preserves existing timestampWrites and needs timestamp-query enabled on the device. Pass descriptors supply names, with deterministic render N/compute N fallback names. WebGL2 uses the gl entry's limits and early-registration naming rules. Memory defaults to tracked WebGPU descriptor bytes created after attachment; without WebGPU, performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize is used only where exposed. Those sources are labelled separately, omit driver padding and are not interchangeable. A custom memory callback can supply another byte measurement, or null. Unsupported readings appear as gaps and unavailable text, never zero. Custom loops may supply PanelSample values directly. Sampling does not write DOM; refresh draws and labels the graphs. Disposal removes owned collectors and DOM, and restores a borrowed Stats graph. New entry: 9,895 B gzip, ceiling 10,192 B. Its bytes provide coherent collector ownership and all four graphs on both backends; splitting would require users to assemble and manage the collectors themselves. Root and core/stage are unchanged.

Batch 257 job 4, browser matrix evidence, not native Safari certification: Firefox 157.0 on Windows/headless has transferControlToOffscreen, worker OffscreenCanvas, RAF and WebGL2; worker WebGPU adapter is unavailable with the default test profile. The unchanged shared WebGL2 scene selected worker mode, transferred its buffer, displayed centre RGBA [213,26,1,255] and disposed successfully. Windows Playwright WebKit 27.2 exposes neither canvas transfer, worker OffscreenCanvas/RAF nor worker graphics contexts. It selected the original page canvas, retained the input buffer and displayed the same centre pixel, then disposed. Its Safari-shaped user agent and Apple GPU renderer string do not establish an Apple host or native Safari support. Both page hardware probes report no WebGPU adapter. The strict full suite therefore fails on the absent WebGPU/worker capabilities; those assertions were not loosened. Apple no longer updates Safari for Windows, and Playwright WebKit is a separate build. Native Safari/macOS hardware proof remains owed in the finish-later list (git-excluded, outside a clone); job 4 is DONE under Scott's 95% rule.

### Batch 245 per-sprite blend modes

The optional `@margoengine/sprites/blend` entry exports BlendLayer, BlendSprite, blendBatches and their types. Modes are normal (default), add, multiply and screen; addBlend creates sprites and blendMode is mutable. Ordinary add sprites use normal. Contiguous visible runs share a draw, with original z/y/insertion order retained. Multiply uses two interleaved draws per sprite to keep uncovered source colour on transparent backdrops. No core or stage change. Atlas pages, nearest/linear filtering, mipmaps, camera, masks, view layers, targets, normal output and lifecycle are inherited; custom fragment shaders are excluded from BlendLayerOptions because the entry owns premultiplication and correction.

Blending uses premultiplied colour in the target's blend space. Add sums colour and alpha, clamped by normalized targets; the other modes use source-over alpha. Smooth sRGB targets blend decoded linear colour; nearest keeps the base layer's numeric texels. Render targets contain premultiplied colour. Intermediate RGBA8 multiply rounding is at most one byte in the asserted single-sprite fixtures. No universal accumulation error bound or speed claim is made. The readback fixtures cover 146 cases on each backend, including sRGB/unorm targets, both filters, transparent/partial/opaque backgrounds, three atlas alpha values, mixed runs, nonzero instance starts and overlapping multiply sprites.

Batch 225 job 2: splines/query provides splineBounds, splineExtrema, intersectSplines, intersectSplineRay and intersectSplinePlane. Bounds and extrema solve each cubic analytically; joins are candidates on all axes and constant coordinates have no isolated stationary roots. Plane equation normal dot point + constant = 0; rays use origin + direction * otherT, so otherT is not world distance unless direction is unit length. Results separate isolated points and continuous overlaps. Defaults: tolerance=1e-7 world units, parameterTolerance=1e-7, maxWork=200000 curve-pair nodes. Increasing maxWork or splitting the curves resolves the explicit limit error; no incomplete result is returned. Parameters within parameterTolerance are merged, so reduce it for closely spaced hits. Interval boxes include a machine-roundoff margin, then hits verify spatial residuals; this is floating-point geometry, not symbolic certification. Closed t=0 and t=1 remain distinct parameter endpoints. No GPU state or GPU tests; core/stage unchanged.

## WFC 3D overlapping (batch 237)
Optional wfc/overlapping3d learns N x N x N patterns from finite-number voxel labels, X fastest, with N 2..5 (default 2). Input wraps by default; identity symmetry is default, with optional four Y turns or 24 cube rotations and reflections (2, 8 or 48 orientations). Sample limit 1,048,576 voxels, pattern limit 4096; nonperiodic source dimensions must still be at least N. Output defaults to nonperiodic, seed 1, four attempts and 10000 backtracks per attempt; dimensions must be at least N unless periodic. Output limit 1,000,000 voxels and 16,777,216 lattice cell/pattern pairs. Voxel pins constrain every covering pattern, including seams and outer corners. Samples and rules are copied. Chronological backtracking never undoes pins; exhausted budgets throw coded failed with help link, and cancellation preserves the exact reason. CPU-only synchronous solving cannot receive event-loop aborts while running; no worker or Wasm backend is claimed for this new model. Arc propagation is generic within the optional entry; neither core nor stage imports it. Hashing overlap slabs avoids pairwise voxel comparisons; no timing gain is claimed. Memory remains proportional to domains, pattern adjacency, and pinned domains.

Batch 225 job 3: splines/offset exports offsetSplineAt (exact offset point), offsetSpline (cubic approximation plus ranges/maxError/work), reverseSpline (exact geometry and t -> 1-t). Positive distance follows normal cross source tangent; normal defaults to [0,0,1] and can define a lateral offset of a spatial curve whenever transverse to the tangent. Defaults: tolerance=0.001 world units, maxDepth=20 (0..30), maxSegments=16384 (1..333333), maxWork=1000000 interval nodes, divisions=max(256,8*outputPieces) capped at 1000000. The local approximation has a conservative floating-point interval enclosure plus roundoff allowance; formal exact-arithmetic certification is not claimed. maxError excludes bevel joins, whose ranges have equal endpoints. Output t distributes equally over output pieces, so ranges maps it to source t. Closed paths get a closing bevel if needed. Stationary/parallel-normal source points have undefined nonzero offset and reject with singular; zero offset remains valid. Exhausted depth, work or piece budgets reject with limit and no partial result. Raw offsets retain loops/cusps and do not perform outline trimming or Boolean cleanup. Controls are independent copies, closure is preserved by reverse, arc lengths stay sampled. No GPU implementation, GPU tests or core/stage changes.

### BVH parallel construction (batch 221)

Optional bvh/parallel adds buildParallel(source, options). workers defaults to min(8, hardwareConcurrency - 1), at least 1, accepts integers 1..64 and counts leaf workers plus one coordinator. The shallow frontier targets four tasks per requested worker; actual workers are capped by unfinished subtrees. The existing maxDepth, maxLeafTriangles, bins and strategy apply globally. Every numeric build, planning and packing pass runs off the main thread when Worker exists; source normalization/cloning and final result validation still have linear caller-thread costs. No Worker means the existing synchronous builder on the next microtask, with pre-build cancellation only. Worker builds have a finite positive timeoutMs (default 120000, maximum 2147483647). Abort/deadline/error terminates the coordinator and its nested worker pool. No transfer option: caller buffers stay attached and unchanged, including source face order. Source positions must remain stable until completion; later edits plus refit are supported. SharedArrayBuffer permits one shared immutable position snapshot across leaf workers; otherwise each leaf worker retains one cloned position buffer. This fallback uses additional memory proportional to worker count. Subtree indices/results are transferred. Parallel and serial packed topology/index/face arrays are byte-identical in the retained correctness cases. No speed ratio claimed.

Five package-local regressions cover these terminal transitions.

Batch 220 job 2: @margoengine/math/curve is CPU-only and optional. Curve accepts [time,value] pairs or flat pairs, defaults to smoothstep, sorts keys and replaces duplicate times. Keys/get/closest return copies; closest ties choose the later key, empty closest returns null. Empty curves evaluate to 0 and one-key curves are constant. type is linear/step/smoothstep/cubic, also exported as CURVE_LINEAR/CURVE_STEP/CURVE_SMOOTHSTEP/CURVE_SPLINE string constants. Cubic tension defaults to 0.5, with derivatives scaled by 2*tension; zero flattens derivatives. Input times/values/options must be finite. Sampled Interpolant data must have strictly increasing times and one sampleSize tuple per time. LinearInterpolant, StepInterpolant/DiscreteInterpolant, SmoothstepInterpolant and CubicInterpolant clamp outside the key range and reuse a result array (default Float64Array). Cubic endpoints default to natural zero second derivative before optional tangentScale (default 1); flat and wrap endpoint derivative policies are available. Wrap is a tangent policy, not repeated time evaluation, and periodic data should repeat its endpoint value. Cubic interpolation may overshoot; quantizeClamped explicitly bounds sampled output. CurveSet supports channel count, channel arrays and variadic flat keys; add/remove/clear/clearKeys and clone preserve independent channel ownership. Sample tables are Float32Array, precision >=2 with endpoints included, sample-major channels; Curve.quantize defaults to 0..1 and accepts a custom interval. Reusable typed buffers must fit all channels. No GPU work, I/O, global state or import side effects. math/curve adds 2403 B gzip, ceiling 2659 B; its coherent interpolation/editing surface avoids multiple modules and duplicate validation. Existing math root/per-type entries and core + stage 24209 B remain unchanged.

Batch 220 inspector isolation repair: GL capture/debug obtains the existing native WebGL2 canvas context without a compatibility-package import or peer dependency. Overlay shaders are owned locally; allocation/compile/link failures release created objects and remain coded failures. inspector/gl grows 4504 to 4742 B gzip, within the existing 4760 B ceiling; the bytes remove the forbidden backend dependency and preserve shader diagnostics/cleanup. Core + stage remains 24209 B.
## Procedural skeleton trees (batch 230)
`@margoengine/procedural/tree-mesh` adds meshTree, generateParametricTree and meshTreeLODs. TreeSkeleton from /trees is accepted directly. Parent-first XYZ nodes become capped, smooth tapered tubes with duplicated UV seams, arc-length V and tangents. Optional radii and architectural orders override the derived support-length radii. Leaf cards are single, crossed double, or three-plane clusters, with UVs and an owned alpha atlas. Material descriptors carry tint, alpha cutoff, two-sided foliage and bark texture settings. Default seed 1, species oak, recursive levels 2; seven species are available. All per-order defaults and bounds are in the emitted API comments.
Limits: 16384 nodes, 1 million vertices per output part, 65536 planned leaves, 0..4 recursive orders, 1..64 axial sections, 3..32 radial segments, at most 8 strictly increasing LOD thresholds starting at zero. Degenerate edges, cycles, malformed radii and invalid controls reject with a coded error. Synchronous work checks AbortSignal before execution; use a worker for in-flight cancellation. Root-only skeletons produce empty meshes. Fork surfaces overlap within parent tubes, rather than forming a Boolean-unioned manifold. Procedural 64x64 RGBA bark/leaf atlases are authored patterns, not photographic species reconstructions. Mesh LOD preserves branch endpoints and forks; leaf thinning is deterministic and card enlargement is caller controlled. No core or stage changes, no frame-time generator, no speed claim.
Entry size: tree-mesh is 4420 bytes min+gzip (previously absent, 0 bytes). Its optional size ceiling is 4676 bytes; the bytes contain geometry, validation, presets and material atlases, and splitting them would duplicate settings or add asynchronous boundaries to synchronous meshing.



## Batch 258 preview GL world panels

Import WorldPanels and WorldPanel from ui/world-gl for one world-panel renderer supporting both native backends. GlWorldPanels is also exported explicitly. On WebGPU and complete compatibility it delegates to the original renderer; preview GL uses framebuffer UI textures, mipmaps, depth testing, non-depth-writing quads and readable double-sided UVs. Existing options/defaults, rays and controller methods are preserved. Use Engine.create with the preview webglRenderer fallback for an explicit webgl2 backend.

Panel dimensions and pixel ratio obey the existing WorldPanel contract and MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE. Panel UIs retain their own CSS dimensions. Raw GL retains the preview renderer's encoded-space UI compositing and baseline trilinear filtering; full compatibility retains the WebGPU colour/filter path. Removing or disposing a renderer frees its panel framebuffers, textures, painters and program; panel Ui objects remain caller-owned. Restore hooks recreate context resources, but hardware context-loss/XR stress certification and anisotropy tuning remain fix-phase follow-ups. No speed claim is made.

Optional /graph includes find/findOne/findByName/findById, attach(newParent,mesh), localToWorld/worldToLocal, translateOnAxis/rotateOnAxis/rotateOnWorldAxis, traverseVisible/traverseAncestors and removeFromParent. ## Plane sections (batch 224)
The optional @margoengine/mesh-edit/section entry exports splitMeshByPlane, trimMeshByPlane and sliceMesh. Plane normals may have any nonzero finite magnitude; normal dot position = offset uses local units. Inputs are closed consistently wound outward PolygonMesh solids, or empty meshes. Multiple components, concavity and cavities are supported. Outputs own arrays, preserve surviving source face IDs/UV interpolation, identify caps and map source faces. Slice returns an orthonormal basis plus CCW contours and CW holes. Tangent-only contacts return no section area and no zero-volume solid. Source data is never changed. Caps use independent unit-square planar UVs.
Classification/interpolation use float64 with no user tolerance, not an exact-predicate claim; resulting faces must pass the existing mesh validity and closure checks. Numerically unresolved or overflowing configurations reject with rescaling guidance. Existing mesh limits apply (200000 vertices/faces, 3-64 corners); clipped large faces are decomposed. Triangulation adds no cap interior vertices and retains collinear boundary points. Cancellation is cooperative between faces/caps. No timing claim; no core or stage bytes added.
Section entry size: 0 to 5299 gzip bytes, with a 5555-byte quality ceiling. The added bytes provide split, trim, slice, provenance and cavity caps in one optional entry; splitting those APIs would duplicate their shared clipping work. Core plus stage remains 24209 bytes in the package build.
