## Procedural PBR sets (batch 230)
`@margoengine/procedural/textures-pbr` exposes createPBRTextureBaker(device or engine). Its bake returns four owned GPUTextures (albedo, normal, roughness and height), width, heightPixels and mipLevelCount. Defaults: bricks, 256x256, seed 1, full mipmaps, normalStrength 1, heightScale 0.05 UV-tile units, roughness 0.7, roughnessVariation 0.3, time 0. Other shared defaults match /textures, with motif-specific default palettes. All colour values and mip arithmetic are linear; convert albedo during export to a format requiring sRGB encoding. Roughness and height are grayscale RGBA8, normals encode tangent XYZ with green +Y and blue +Z. Use a repeat/trilinear sampler. Fire/cloud are material motifs, not volumetric simulation; animated motifs require rebaking at the chosen explicit time, and fire's radiance uses the albedo as an emissive input supplied by the consuming material.
Dimensions 16..2048 and the device limit; complete NPOT mip chains end at 1x1. Existing repeat/grout/seed/offset limits apply; normalStrength 0..8, heightScale/roughness/variation 0..1, time 0..1e6. Four storage texture outputs are required, matching WebGPU's minimum limit. Each smaller mip covers all source texels with exact area overlap, including odd edges; normal vectors are decoded, area averaged and renormalized. No CPU pixel work or readback in the public implementation. The full WebGL2 compatibility layer runs the same shader API, and preview-only fallback engines must install that layer first. Cancellation/disposal/device loss releases incomplete textures; disposal of the baker releases all retained sets. Recreate the baker after device replacement. Mip normals do not preserve unresolved microfacet variance; no BRDF-equivalent filtering claim is made.
Entry size: textures-pbr is 4946 bytes min+gzip (previously absent, 0 bytes), with a 5202-byte optional ceiling. The bytes keep the coherent field, four-map lifecycle and filtered mip pyramid together; splitting would duplicate settings and resource ownership. Core and stage are unchanged.

Batch 249 parallel: SharedWorld has fixed capacity and numeric/tag fields; object/reference components remain on the main thread. SharedComponent adds one 4-byte-per-slot sparse row table beside existing storage. ParallelSchedule defaults to two workers (1 to 32), a 30000 ms per-system deadline (1 to 2147483647), default export and no implicit accesses. Explicit dependencies order systems, physical buffer conflicts serialize, and independent groups execute in bounded worker batches. Modules must be loadable worker ESM, with dependencies resolved by the app bundler; no function source is serialized/evaluated. Isolation requires COOP same-origin and COEP require-corp. Workers must honor read/write declarations, must not alter entities/row metadata, and must settle all work before returning. Applications await update before raw shared-field reads/writes. Main structural operations reject in flight. Failures/abort can leave partial numeric writes, close the schedule and terminate all workers without replay; failed host termination leaves the world structurally locked and requires discarding it after stopping the host. Written components are touched once per physical store after successful updates. No GPU work or Wasm numerical kernel is introduced.

### UI curved panels (batch 259)
`@margoengine/ui/curved` exports `CurvedPanel` and `layoutPanels`. Import `WorldPanels` from `@margoengine/ui/world-gl` for both backends, or `/world` for native WebGPU. Panel dimensions are arc metres; default cylinder radius 2 m, 64 segments per curved axis (4..512 allowed). Width is less than 2*pi*radius; spherical height is less than pi*radius. Panels retain the inherited mipmapped texture, depth, input capture and XR controller behavior. ## Batch 210 job 1: animation/mixer
New optional entry: 4158 B min+gzip, ceiling 4414 B, previously absent (0 B). It contains action scheduling, binding and blending together; splitting these would add lifetime coordination and async loading to a small synchronous API. Core/stage source and their 25000 B limit are unchanged.
AnimationMixer accepts an existing Animation, PBRModel (creates and owns an Animation in the model scene), or Skeleton; existing Animation clocks are paused and stay paused on release. Clips may be names/indices on glTF roots, parsed glTF clips, or createKeyframeClip results. Actions cache by clip identity, root and blend mode. Defaults: time=0, timeScale=1, weight=1, enabled=true, paused=false, LoopRepeat, repetitions=Infinity, clampWhenFinished=false. Mixer defaults time=0, timeScale=1. Replacement weights below one retain original properties and above one normalize. Additive clips contain deltas (translation/property offset, unit-relative scale, quaternion delta). Property accessor tracks need get/read so original values can be restored. Warps use rates evaluated at each update endpoint, matching the action contract; no frame-partition invariant integration is claimed.
Fades/warps/crossfades take finite nonnegative seconds; zero applies at the next update. Crossfade schedules envelopes, and callers play the destination action. Roots must have compatible track targets; no automatic retargeting or contact-preserving motion alignment is implied. clipAction supports code property bindings and already-bound pointer channels. Uncache releases bindings; stopping the last action immediately restores originals. update(delta) or engine.use(mixer) drives it; do not also drive a borrowed Animation clock.

The mixer intentionally shares the existing animation root and its transitive gltf/pbr-model runtime (recorded dependency allowance), rather than duplicating model/deformation ownership or making synchronous model/action construction asynchronous. The 4158 B entry measurement leaves shared bare package imports external; it is not a standalone all-dependencies download size.

## Batch mesh booleans (batch 224 job 2)
@margoengine/mesh-edit/boolean-batch exports batchBooleanMeshes(meshes, operation = 'union', options = {}). Intersection is n-ary; difference is the first solid minus the union of every later solid. Empty list gives an empty mesh. Empty union/subtraction operands are identities; an empty intersection operand absorbs. Inputs are closed outward consistently wound PolygonMesh solids (empty meshes allowed), up to the existing per-mesh limits and 400000 combined input vertices plus faces. Result faceMap is indexed by operand; sources use original operand index and face ID. Inputs may reuse IDs; surviving faces retain original IDs when unique, with createId (default crypto.randomUUID) for collisions. UVs interpolate from original faces, not intermediate results. Output owns all arrays.
All operands and internal shell unions use one exact space; balanced reductions do not materialize intermediate meshes. Rational corners round once, followed by the existing validity-preserving thin-face fold and junction closure. collapsedFaces and nonManifoldEdges retain binary-exact semantics. work records exactSpaces, materializations and treeBuilds, without elapsed-time claims. AbortSignal is checked during traversal and assembly. Existing limitations on unresolved float64 output and single-surface self-intersection remain. No core/stage bytes are added.
Entry sizes: boolean-batch 0 to 10461 gzip bytes (10775-byte ceiling); binary boolean-exact remains 10308 bytes by the same entry measurement. The combined implementation shares exact clipping and final repair rather than duplicating either. Core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.
### Batch 226 job 3: scene/tags
tags(mesh) is a stable DOM EventTarget TagSet, with add/remove/clear/list/size/has and add/remove/change events. Tags are unique nonempty arbitrary strings, insertion ordered; mutation inputs validate before changes. has/findByTag use OR between arguments, AND within nonempty arrays. matchesTags/queryTags accept !, &&, ||, parentheses, quoted tags and unquoted true/false constants, maximum 16384 characters and 64 nested operators. Quoted true/false remain literal tags. An empty boolean expression matches all; empty has alternatives match nothing. Queries include the supplied root, preserve depth-first attach order and stay in its scene. Clone copies independent tag sets without subscribing copied listeners.

new SceneEvents(engine) explicitly observes successful createMesh/setParent/remove calls on existing and future meshes of that engine, with one active observer per engine. Existing parent relationships are not replayed. added is creation or attachment; removed is detachment from a parent or removal from a scene, parent=null meaning scene root; disposed follows mesh removal. Disposing a parent detaches its children under existing core rules. Subscriptions support mesh/scene filters, once, signal and idempotent unsubscribe. Events are immutable snapshots and synchronous after compound attach/clone commit. Failed clone allocation publishes no transient lifecycle events. Listener exceptions reach engine.onError in a microtask. Dispose/Symbol.dispose removes subscriptions and restores only instance wrappers it still owns; external replacement wrappers are preserved. Calls through method references saved before observation or direct private-store writes cannot be observed. Tag mutation listeners follow native DOM dispatch semantics. ## Batch 265 useFrame priorities

`useFrame(callback, priority = 0)` orders finite priorities ascending; equal values retain subscription order. Negative values only order work. Any positive live subscription owns rendering, even when it draws nothing; removing the last restores automatic rendering. Demand mode still advances only on invalidate. Callback additions start next frame and removals apply immediately. The optional XR manager accepts `onFrame` returning false and `renderFrame()` inside that callback; React manual full-scene draws use the tracked eyes, while inline sessions retain the desktop loop. Core and stage are unchanged.

id is retained in each tracer's last prepared scene. Content changes invalidate

in the package README; legacy scenes report zero for the three new counters.

## Batch 265 adaptive performance

The optional @margoengine/react/performance entry exports PerformanceMonitor, AdaptiveDpr, usePerformanceMonitor and PerformanceController. Defaults: 250 ms windows, 10 windows per decision, 0.75 required fraction, factor 1, step 0.1, unlimited direction reversals, fallbackFactor 0. Bounds default to [50,57] FPS, or [50,90] when a measured window exceeds 90 Hz. A 60 Hz presentation can therefore recover quality. FPS is frames divided by summed measured milliseconds; observed refresh is a high window average, not a display capability query. It is cadence, not GPU execution time. A sample prop accepts measured milliseconds or null from an application's collector; default intervals use the monotonic performance clock without the engine's delta cap. Hidden tabs and unsampled demand frames discard incomplete windows. Active slow frames remain measurements. Snapshots retain at most 4096 frame intervals per window while all intervals count toward the average. A direction reversal beyond flipflops fixes the factor at fallbackFactor until reset.

AdaptiveDpr defaults to min 0.5, max 1, pixelated false. Fractions apply to the Canvas's native resolution, not CSS layout. A package-owned target scales scene raster dimensions; native MSAA stays intact. Reduced frames add one full-canvas presentation triangle. Scale 1 returns to the original renderer, allowing exact restored pixels. Multiple holds use the lowest scale and nearest presentation if any requests it. Named Scenes and Canvas views retain their scene, camera, layers, clear and scissor. Explicit offscreen targets and tracked XR eye targets retain their owner's resolution. Picking uses original Canvas view coordinates. Removing the last hold destroys its texture immediately and retains only logical picking until the next Canvas draw; engine disposal always releases the adapter. Resources recreate after device restore. WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer are supported; native preview reports unsupported. No timing or throughput gain is claimed during the build phase.

Adaptive performance size: optional entry 0 -> 5619 B minified gzip, ceiling 5769 B. Keeping measurement, presentation and picking in one optional entry avoids duplicate lifetime and asynchronous render boundaries. Core + stage stays 24209 B on the current main baseline.

Adaptive diagnostics use stable MargoError codes and help links. The final React root is 10259 B gzip, React XR 4159 B; the performance entry above includes coded presentation-owner diagnostics.
Batch 219 job 1: optional geometry/nurbs-edit supports immutable rational curve/surface knot insertion and degree elevation on either surface axis; knot parameters and interior multiplicity/continuity are preserved. Unclamped inputs are restricted to the same active domain with clamped endpoints for elevation. Default insertion/elevation count is 1; zero copies, invalid counts and excess multiplicity reject. Trimming accepts retained UV polygons or closed 2D rational curves, holes and multiple islands; regions outside [0,1] are clipped. Default slices/stacks=32, trimTolerance=0.0001 UV units. Surface tessellation has explicit resolution, no model-space error guarantee. Trim curve sampling inherits the existing 12-level subdivision limit. Polygon intersection snaps to its 2^26 grid and features below two steps may disappear; cell pieces retain separate vertices and normals from their own side of knot creases. Degree elevation uses floating-point homogeneous arithmetic, not symbolic arithmetic. Surface file parsing remains in loaders. New entry absent -> 11646 B gzip, ceiling 11996 B; refinement and trim operations share surface evaluation, clipping and triangulation, so splitting would fragment the editing workflow. Core + stage unchanged at 24209 B gzip.

Batch 219: NurbsSurface.derivatives(u,v,leftU=false,leftV=false) exposes the exact side of a repeated knot on either axis. Trimmed cell endpoints take their own side, so fully discontinuous surfaces retain their separate sheets rather than stretching across the jump. No extra approximation is introduced for crease normals; only a genuinely degenerate pole uses an inward normal sample. The generated margoengine/geometry/nurbs-edit alias and current umbrella alias completeness ship with the same job.


## Mesh repair (batch 224 job 3)
The optional mesh-edit/repair entry exports repairMesh(input, options). Input is a polygon soup with unique nonempty face IDs, xyz vertices and index loops; corner UVs are optional. Defaults: distance 0 (exact duplicates), fillHoles true, maxHoleEdges 256. Up to 200000 input vertices and faces and 4096 corners per input face; output remains within standard PolygonMesh limits. Near welding is non-chaining and keeps the earliest eligible position. Nonfinite positions and invalid-index faces are discarded and named; structural array/ID errors reject. Missing or invalid UV corners reset to [0,0] with diagnostics. Concave/warped polygons split through existing mesh editing rules; unresolved, pinched and degenerate polygons are discarded.
When more than two faces compete for an edge, descending face area then input order select the retained manifold subset. A contradictory orientation constraint removes the encountered conflicting face and reports it. Disconnected vertex fans split identities. Existing hole filling uses triangles, refine false and fair false, so it adds a closure without moving surviving scan vertices; holes above maxHoleEdges stay open and are reported. Nested closed shells orient by solid-angle containment (cavities inward). Self-intersections and intersecting-shell intent are not reconstructed or certified. readyForBoolean checks closed opposing edge incidences and positive volume, followed by the actual solid validator; it is false for empty, open or zero-volume output. It does not promise valid geometric self-intersection behavior for arbitrary damaged scans. Result fields include every removed face/vertex, flipped/filled face, weld/fan counts and source face/vertex maps. Source and output arrays are independent. Cooperative AbortSignal checks bound work between traversal steps; no interactive latency claim.
Repair entry size: 0 to 9631 gzip bytes, with a 9920-byte ceiling. The optional entry includes the established hole filler and topology validation so repair stays complete; splitting them would add API complexity without reducing bytes when closure is needed. Core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.
### Legacy VTK datasets (batch 202)
`@margoengine/loaders/vtk-legacy` adds `parseVTKLegacy` independently of the root parser. All five legacy geometric dataset types support ASCII and big-endian binary, old packed cells and explicit OFFSETS/CONNECTIVITY. Source connectivity, offsets, cell types, point/cell/global FIELD data and source cell IDs for every drawn primitive survive. Numeric arrays retain float64 precision; rendering positions remain float32. Structured coordinates are x-fastest; ORIGIN defaults to [0,0,0] and SPACING/ASPECT_RATIO to [1,1,1]. `maxCells` defaults to maxTriangles; existing vertex/triangle bounds remain. `surface: 'outer'` suppresses shared volume faces; `'all'` retains them. Both readers reject inexact 64-bit integer values. Binary native `long` is eight bytes, matching the existing legacy reader. ASCII bit arrays and MSB-first packed binary bit arrays are decoded; polyhedron type 42 retains its original face stream in connectivity. Higher-order cell drawing retains corner points and warns; intact source topology is always returned for supported cells. Global FIELD arrays with tuple counts unlike the active association are kept in fieldData. No core or stage changes.
The optional /vtk-legacy entry is 6,336 B min+gzip (new, previously absent). Its 6,592 B ceiling retains the shared reader and complete dataset metadata instead of splitting user-facing APIs. Root loaders: 52,868 to 53,022 B; existing /vtk-xml: 7,514 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.
Legacy VTK texture coordinates (loaders audit, 2026-11-15): `parseVTK` and `parseVTKLegacy` return `uvs` with v = 1 - t, as `parseVTKXML` does, since VTK puts t = 0 at the image's bottom; `pointData` keeps the file's own values. All three VTK readers fan a convex polygon from its first corner and ear-clip one that is not convex on the plane of its Newell normal; a self-intersecting polygon, which VTK does not allow, gets a best-effort result.

### XML DTDs (loaders, 2026-11-15)
`@margoengine/loaders/xml` reads the DOCTYPE as XML 1.0 Fifth Edition (W3C, 2008, https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/) section 5.1 asks of a non-validating processor: the whole internal subset, parameter entities included (4.4.8, enlarged by a space either side), attribute defaults and type normalization (3.3, 3.3.3), and entities holding markup read as content (4.4.2, each holding whole elements, 4.3.2). External entities, the external subset among them, are read only from `external`, which `resolveDTD` fills through the caller's `resolve`; nothing is fetched otherwise, because a document from an untrusted source must not make the reader fetch the URLs it names. Browsers' DOMParser, which the common web 3D loaders use for COLLADA, X3D, 3MF and KML, does not fetch external DTDs either, so the default matches them and `resolveDTD` is an addition. Without `external`, an entity the unread part may declare is a `LoaderError` with code `unsupported` (4.4.3 lets a non-validating processor skip it but asks it to say so; there is no result to give without its text), and entity and attribute declarations after an unread parameter entity are skipped unless `standalone="yes"` (5.1). Limits: `maxExpansion` (default 1 Mi characters) for all entity and parameter entity text brought in, the external subset itself not counted; `resolveDTD` reads at most `maxFiles` (64) entities and `maxCharacters` (16 Mi) in all. Not done: validation (element content models are skipped, IDs are not checked), NOTATION use, and `xml:base`. Every format parser that reads XML (`parseDAE`, `parseKMZ`, `parseX3D`, `parse3MF`, `parse3MFLattice`, `parseAMF`, `parseKML`, `parseGPX`, `parseTMX` with its TSX tilesets, `parseSVG`, `parseMaterialX`, `parseVTKXML`, `openVTKXMLDataset`) takes the same optional `external` (type `XMLExternalOptions`), the result of `resolveDTD`; the parsers never fetch. The relationship parts of 3MF and the OPC `.rels` files are read without it, as they carry no DTD in any producer's output.

### G-code arcs (loaders audit, 2026-11-15)
`parseGCode` draws G2 and G3 arcs as chords no more than 0.002 mm from the arc, at least 16 per turn, so a 10 mm radius quarter turn takes 40 chords (80 vertices against `maxVertices`). Centre offsets (I, J, K) and radius (R) forms, full circles, P turns and helices are read in the G17, G18 and G19 planes. G90.1 (absolute centres: I, J and K are the centre itself, both of the plane's words required) and G91.1 (incremental, the default) follow the LinuxCNC G-code reference (linuxcnc.org/docs/html/gcode/g-code.html, G90.1 and G91.1, and G2 and G3). What P counts differs by firmware and is the `arcP` option: `'turns'` (default) is LinuxCNC's number of turns, P1 the programmed arc alone and each step above 1 one more full circle; `'circles'` is Marlin's (marlinfw.org/docs/gcode/G002-G003.html, `ARC_P_CIRCLES`, "Specify complete circles"), P full circles added to the arc, so Marlin's Pn draws LinuxCNC's P(n + 1) and P0 is allowed. Marlin's page does not say in so many words whether P counts the first turn; 'circles' reads it as full circles on top of the arc, as its wording and parameter name suggest. RepRapFirmware documents no P parameter for G2 and G3 (Duet3D, "GCode dictionary", "G2: Controlled Arc Move", docs.duet3d.com/User_manual/Reference/Gcodes, read 2026-11-15): a full circle is an end point equal to the start with the centre given by I and J, which `parseGCode` already reads as a full turn whatever `arcP` is, so `arcP` has no RepRapFirmware reading. RepRapFirmware 3.6.2 and later rejects an arc whose start and end radius differ by more than 0.0022 mm in CNC mode or 0.05 mm in FDM and laser mode; `parseGCode` keeps LinuxCNC's tolerance below, so it accepts some arcs that firmware refuses and does not model the firmware's mode. Its G90.1 behaviour is not checked. An end off its circle by more than LinuxCNC's tolerance (0.5 mm, or both 0.005 mm and 0.1% of the radius) and an R shorter than half its chord are `range` errors. Not read: G17.1 to G19.1 and the 5 to 9 axis forms.

### STL colours (loaders, 2026-11-15)
`parseSTL` reads both binary colour conventions described in the colour section of the "STL (file format)" article (Wikipedia, read 2026-11-15; neither vendor publishes a format note). VisCAM / SolidView: bit 15 of the facet attribute set marks a colour, red in bits 10 to 14. Materialise Magics: the 80-byte header holds `COLOR=` and four RGBA bytes for the whole part, optionally `,MATERIAL=` and diffuse, specular and ambient RGBA (the diffuse is used for the part colour, as Magics prefers the material), and bit 15 has the opposite meaning: clear marks a facet's own colour, red in bits 0 to 4, set takes the part colour. `colorVariant: 'auto'` picks Materialise only when `COLOR=` is in the header, so a Magics file saved without a part colour reads as VisCAM unless `colorVariant: 'materialise'` is passed; the two cannot be told apart from the bits alone. Header alpha is returned in `materialise` but `colors` holds RGB only. ASCII per-facet colours have no shared convention and are not read.

### Pixel-exact area queries (batch 199 job 3)
`@margoengine/selection/area` exports AreaPicking and AreaPickingOptions. Attach instead of Picking, retaining ordinary pick/pickMany and add(source). `rect({x,y,width,height}, view?, signal?)` accepts CSS pixels and normalizes negative dimensions; `polygon(points, view?, signal?)` accepts 3-4096 finite xy vertices and uses even-odd filling. Only included raster pixel centres count, including fractional CSS/DPR boundaries; empty/fully clipped regions return no hits. Results are unique visible triangle IDs, preserving model, primitive and instance identity, in first raster occurrence order. Fully occluded geometry, unrendered bounding spheres, approximate proxies and non-mesh overlays are excluded. Opacity, clipping, sidedness and current deformation use the same replay as point queries. With multiple views, pass the desired view; omitted view uses the engine camera/scene across the canvas. Queries honor viewport, scissor and layers.
Each area query owns one cropped r32uint target, one depth32float target and a 256-byte-pitched staging buffer. Default maxPixels is 16777216, additionally bounded by device texture dimensions and maxBufferSize. AbortSignal is checked before queued work and after mapping; pending GPU resources remain alive through completion and are destroyed in finally. Point capture defaults false and may be enabled separately. Concurrent area and ordinary point calls retain separate operations through the engine queue. New entry 15287 B min+gzip, ceiling 15719 B; selection root 21308 -> 21464 B and hit-details 15002 -> 15152 B remain inside existing ceilings. The entry includes its common picker rather than duplicating replay/resource ownership. Core plus stage stays 24209 B.
## Batch 210 job 2: animation/playback
New optional entry 1817 B min+gzip (previously 0), ceiling 2073 B. It intentionally imports the existing Animation root/model runtime; the reported size leaves shared bare package imports external. Core/stage source stays unchanged, below 25000 B.
Import Animation (alias of PlaybackAnimation) from animation/playback for plain play/pause/seek and existing deformation with loop/finished events, finished promise, loop modes and total traversal counts. Defaults inherit loop=true and speed=1; loopMode defaults LoopRepeat (LoopOnce with loop=false), repetitions=Infinity, timeScale=1, no signal. LoopOnce always uses one traversal. Negative timeScale plays backward; play starts negative-rate clips at their end. Ping-pong counts each traversal. A multi-boundary update emits one loop event with signed loopDelta, while the final boundary emits finished once after the terminal pose.
play renews completion, rejecting an interrupted run with AbortError. dispose and constructor signal abort reject pending completion; waitForFinished accepts independent cancellation without stopping playback. seek accepts nonnegative total seconds, emits no events and resets traversal counting; use play to renew a finished run. Events use on or EventTarget-style listeners; listener signal cancellation is supported. Loop counts must be safe positive integers or Infinity, and boundary jumps must be countable as safe integers. A zero-duration clip finishes once, without an infinite loop.

### Headless tiled stills (batch 209)
Optional @margoengine/headless/tiles is 2,210 B min+gzip (previously absent), with a 2,466 B entry ceiling. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B, below 25,000 B. renderTiles streams row-major RGBA tiles; renderTiled collects them in CPU memory. Output dimensions are positive safe integers; the assembled buffer must fit the runtime. Samples 1..1024, default 1; tileSize defaults to min(1024, device maxTextureDimension2D); padding defaults to 0 and must leave a positive interior. GPU allocation never exceeds tileSize in either dimension. WebGPU on createHeadlessCanvas only, as the headless readback contract requires. WebGL2 refuses with unsupported. Camera projection and canvas dimensions are preserved. Do not render concurrently on the same engine. Temporal/nonlocal effects need disabling, and local filters need sufficient guard pixels; arbitrary postprocessing cannot be made tile-independent automatically. No performance claim.
The full WebGL2 compatibility layer runs the WebGPU capture contract and passes the same exact tile proof; the unsupported route above means the small backend=webgl2 preview.
### UI localization tables (batch 259)
`@margoengine/ui/i18n` exports Localization. Constructor accepts locale-to-flat-key tables; locale and fallback default to the first table or en. Lookup tries canonical exact locale, progressively less specific parents, then the configured fallback and its parents. Messages are strings or cardinal plural objects with required other; exact =count wins, then Intl.PluralRules in the resolved table locale. Named {parameters} interpolate as text. Missing policy defaults to key (unresolved placeholders remain literal); error is opt-in. bind(ui, bindings, {signal}) updates text/label/placeholder setters and Ui.direction automatically; layout runs next frame. refresh re-evaluates dynamic parameters. ### Batch 243 mesh PBR channels
Optional mesh-pbr supports normals, four UV sets, RGBA vertex colours, base-colour, tangent normal, metallic/roughness and emissive RGBA8 maps, explicit affine instances and OPAQUE/MASK coverage. Mesh material ids are independent of the 255-entry voxel palette. Surface/texture/vertex packets share the existing 128 MiB geometry limit. Samplers support repeat, mirrored repeat, clamp, nearest and linear-light bilinear reconstruction at the base mip. Normal XY scale can be negative; finite UV/transform/tangent values stay within +/-1e8. Colours are linear factors; base/emissive image RGB decodes sRGB before interpolation, data maps and alpha stay linear. BLEND coverage (2026-11-25) is stochastic transparency: each traversal keeps a BLEND candidate with probability equal to its coverage, from a hash of the ray's current random state and the hit distance rounded to 13 mantissa bits (no extra random number is drawn, so scenes without BLEND trace exactly as before; triangles sharing an edge take one decision; two BLEND layers closer than about 1.2e-4 of their distance along the ray take the same decision); sampled light points on a BLEND emitter emit their coverage times the emission. Converged images are the coverage-weighted mix; single samples are binary per ray. There is no ordered compositing of layers (order-independent by construction) and no refraction: use transmission for volumes. Skinned and morphing glTF models (2026-11-25) trace the pose last drawn: `traceSceneFromGLTF` reads deformed vertices back from the GPU (`readPickingGeometry`), copies them with the materials and images, and `setScene` rebuilds the BLAS of every mesh whose content changed (a full spatial-median rebuild in the lazy Wasm kernel, not a refit) while unchanged meshes reuse theirs. Each pose therefore costs one GPU readback, one image copy per texture and one rebuild per deformed mesh; there is no in-place GPU skinning into the trace buffer and no BVH refit, which suits offline frame-by-frame renders rather than an interactive viewport at full rate. Motion blur across a pose change is not traced. The glTF adapter reads current geometry and source material definitions, with an explicit imagePixels callback for compressed/streamed images. It preserves borrowed-image ownership and rejects merged primitives without source identity. No new core or stage feature is added.

Entry size: mesh-pbr 0 to 37,233 B min+gzip, with a new 38,350 B optional ceiling. This includes the existing geometry Wasm/traversal and the material, sampler and glTF snapshot boundary; splitting the surface channels would duplicate the same packet/frame/lifetime coupling. The existing mesh entry is 32,933 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B, below 25,000 B.

### Optional CPU occlusion on the full WebGL2 layer

`@margoengine/culling/webgl2` supplies `WebGL2Culling` for opaque core meshes on
both the full WebGL2 layer and native WebGPU. It rebuilds a 128 by 128 CPU depth
buffer each view using actual triangles, then redirects compacted 96-byte rows.
Resolution accepts integers 1 through 2048. It uses no hardware queries, no GPU
readback and no previous-frame visibility. `readCounts()` returns the last view's
counts synchronously. Use one redirect owner per batch. Picking and shadow data
stay complete. Surface-changing core shaders disable occlusion for that frame.
The preview renderer is unsupported. Models and dynamic GPU-only geometry retain
their existing cullers; this entry culls core batches. Near-plane-crossing triangles,
triangle seams and partially covered cells can retain hidden objects. This is
conservative excess drawing, never an excuse to cull visible surfaces. CPU work
scales with occluder triangles and covered software cells; no speed claim is made.

Batch 223 job 1 size: culling/webgl2 new entry, 0 to 2442 B gzip. Its CPU depth
and upload code stay together because both implement this one optional feature.
Core plus stage remains 24,209 B gzip (under 25,000); no frozen code changed.

and external TGA, DDS, TIFF/TIF and BMP through decoder entries, lazily, then encodes PNG. Default
FBX byte and pixel budgets still apply. DDS material images must be 2D; only the base mip is embedded
in GLB, whose runtime generates its mips. Float TIFF/DDS values clamp to 0..1 and encode to sRGB PNG. The decoder entries define
format support; damaged recognized inputs reject instead of silently dropping a texture. Unknown
formats and missing files retain the existing missing-texture record. Multiple image hooks are tried
in extension order, and the first successful conversion wins.

`@margoengine/decoders/bmp` exports `parseBMP`, `BMPOptions`, `DecodedBMP`. Default maxPixels is
67,108,864. OS/2 core and Windows 40/52/56/108/124-byte DIB headers, indexed 1/4/8-bit, RGB 16/24/32-bit,
RGB/alpha bitfields, RLE4/RLE8 and top-down uncompressed rows are supported. BI_RGB 32-bit spare bytes
are opaque. JPEG/PNG-in-BMP, OS/2 v2 compression and embedded colour-profile transforms are not supported.

The texture-rgba decoder entry shares the existing textureFileToRGBA implementation with decoders/image, without container/transcoder imports. BMP and texture bridge defaults do not add a core/stage feature.

The FBX worker grows from 83,143 B (ceiling 85,638 B) to 97,769 B (ceiling 100,703 B), buying all four image decoders in the classic worker. ### Batch 243 optional learned denoiser
`voxel-pathtracer/denoise-ml` exposes DenoiseML.create(engine, {signal}), denoise(image, {signal}), whenIdle, dispose and Symbol.dispose. It requires an engine WebGPU compute device (the existing WebGL2 compatibility device is supported), finite RGB Float32 color/albedo/normal guides from renderImage with aovs:true, positive integer dimensions totaling at most 16,777,216 pixels, positive samples and optional coverage in [0,1]. Color is signed, each value within the Float32 representation of 1e16 of zero (renderImage gives few-sample pixels negative channels behind dispersive glass; the luminance features use x/(1+|x|), equal to the trained x/(1+x) on the nonnegative training data, so the weights are unchanged), albedo [0,1], normal components [-1,1]. Device binding/buffer/grid limits apply in addition. Device changes rebuild weights and the pipeline; each request snapshots every input AOV, owns its output and preserves alpha, albedo, normal, depth, instance and palette arrays. Cancellation rejects queued/active waits promptly and disposal releases owned buffers. GPU failures use coded failed errors with their platform cause.
The 321-parameter, two-hidden-layer network predicts a single 3x3 positive reconstruction kernel; it is spatial, with no temporal history, downloaded weights or external inference runtime. Input guides are required. HDR normalization and softmax preserve finite constant fields and bound reconstructed RGB by observed neighbor radiance. Synthetic training and the licensed Box holdout are narrow correctness/quality evidence, not a claim of universal image-quality superiority.
The entry measures 6,781 B min+gzip after the signed-colour fix (6,767 B before; ceiling 7,023 B), previously absent. Root/core/stage gain no code. Core plus stage is 24,209 B on this main base, unchanged by the entry and below 25,000 B. The difference from earlier 23,950 B batch records is the upstream version guard. No speed or wall-clock claim is made.


### GPU-free stage (batch 209)
Optional @margoengine/headless/null is 2,721 B min+gzip (previously absent), ceiling 2,977 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. createNullStage defaults to a 1x1 logical viewport, capacity 1024, normal core camera defaults, no signal or custom onError. It creates real engine scenes through renderer injection without a DOM, graphics context, GPU binding or global mutation. NullStage.step(delta=0) accepts finite seconds in 0..1 and advances global ticks, onFrame callbacks and every live scene's plugins once. Successful steps accumulate in time. Reentrant steps and stepping after disposal reject. The dispatch label engine.backend is webgl2 because that is the existing injection path; isNull identifies the stage and gpu/renderTarget are null. CPU property/skeleton animation works; GPU deformation, render passes, capture and GPU-specific packages require a rendering stage. No timing or rendering equivalence claim.
Batch 172 job 3: optional sciviz/clip supplies scalar/plane/box/sampled-sphere cuts, iso-volume, whole-cell crinkle, point/cell threshold and Cartesian/curvilinear structured subsets. imageGrid supports 2D/3D topology and up to 1000000 samples. Sphere boundaries are piecewise-linear sampled implicit values; coarse cells can miss an interior sphere. Structured cell tuples sample the source lower cell, not aggregate across strides. Inputs stay borrowed until async operations settle; validation/materialization/compaction are synchronous. Tuple arrays and source cell IDs are retained in f64 output. See docs/sciviz-analysis.md for full conventions. No speed claim or core/stage source change.

Sciviz threshold components (2026-11-10): `thresholdGrid` tests a component index, the Euclidean magnitude (the default for arrays wider than one) or all/any components against an inclusive range; one end may be infinite for a one-sided threshold. Magnitude is computed in f64 from the stored tuple, so a range edge equal to an irrational length needs a tolerance chosen by the caller. NaN never passes and is never a bound. Evidence: packages/sciviz/tests/clip.test.js.

Sciviz MinIP (2026-11-10): `mode: 'minip'` takes the smallest finite sample of each ray; colour and opacity come from the transfer function at that value. It covers the Volume, bricked, AMR, curvilinear, tetrahedral and quality volumes; the CPU fallback renderer keeps its own path and is not covered. Evidence: packages/sciviz/tests/volume-modes-browser.mjs, packages/sciviz/tests/minip-kinds-browser.mjs, packages/sciviz/tests/bricks-browser.js.

Sciviz connectivity (2026-11-10): `connectivityGrid` in sciviz/clip joins cells through any shared point (no face or edge adjacency mode) with union-find, then keeps all, the largest, listed, point- or cell-seeded or closest-point regions. Region IDs follow cell count (descending by default, or ascending) or lowest cell ID; equal sizes order by lowest cell ID. Scalar connectivity tests point scalars only. Inputs are bounded by the clip entry limits (imageGrid 1,000,000 samples). Evidence: packages/sciviz/tests/clip.test.js.

Sciviz multi-volume (2026-11-10): sciviz/multivolume draws 1 to 4 channels, each 2 to 2048 samples an axis, as r16float textures (about 3 significant digits after range normalisation), with one 256-entry transfer row per channel, no lighting, clip planes, scene-depth occlusion or 2D classification, and no drawing while the camera is inside the union box (back faces are culled). At most 2048 steps a ray, at the finest channel's voxel divided by quality. Evidence: packages/sciviz/tests/multivolume-browser.mjs.

Batch 172 job 3 size: sciviz/clip 0 to 5140 B min+gzip, new ceiling 5396 B. A shared owner for cut geometry, tuple interpolation, provenance and the four pipeline operations avoids duplicated array/topology code. Core + stage remains 24209 B under 25000 B. CPU gate: 505 affected sciviz/react/umbrella tests pass, including 11 clip cases. No timing claim.
Batch 206 PointInstancer: /instancer expands a selected time into ordinary glTF nodes sharing prototype meshes. Default added-node ceiling 100000, override maxNodes. Optional timeCode selects a stage pose; this entry does not turn point arrays into playback channels. OpenUSD 26.11 oracle: five time codes, masks, prototype transforms and nonuniform scale within 1e-5. No wall-clock claims. Core/stage unchanged.

Batch 206 entry size: usdz/instancer 0 -> 2229 B gzip, ceiling 2451 B; optional node expansion and schema evaluation warrant these bytes. Keeping it in one entry avoids fragmenting the API.

### Selection glow and fill (batch 199 job 4)
`@margoengine/selection/highlight` exports Highlight and HighlightOptions. Attach an effect, then set live core meshes, loader nodes or whole models, or register caller-owned custom PickingSources. Only visible selected surfaces contribute, including the existing current-pose, alpha, clipping, sidedness, MSAA and mask-provider contracts. Empty selection stops compositing. Default colour is linear orange `[1, 0.5, 0]`; fillOpacity 0.15, glowOpacity 0.85, radius 8 drawing pixels, innerGlow and outerGlow true. Separate fillColor/glowColor default to color; colours and opacities are finite 0-1. Radius may be fractional, 1-64, with sigma radius/3 and support ceil(radius). Options are mutable each frame. Separate named effects style independent mesh groups.
Two single-sample r16float blur targets cost four bytes per drawing pixel, in addition to Selection's r8unorm visible mask and its MSAA mask when needed. The mask-only consumer creates no JFA distance targets, jump buffers or compute pipelines, and performs no distance-field dispatch. It adds horizontal/vertical blur and one blended composite. View/scissor bounds are zero padded; cached target views and bind groups survive steady frames, with uniform copies for multiple views. Resize/device restore recreate resources; dispose owns targets/passes only, and models/source buffers remain caller-owned. Preview-only WebGL2 refuses through Selection's coded unsupported guard; native WebGPU and full compatibility are supported.
New highlight entry 13082 B min+gzip, ceiling 13475 B. Selection root 21464 -> 21514 B and xray 12322 -> 12374 B stay within existing ceilings. Keeping the existing mask replay and coherent glow/fill resource owner avoids a duplicate renderer or mask-lifetime protocol. Core plus stage remains 24209 B, below 25000 B.

### Geospatial vector formats (batch 202)
The optional `@margoengine/loaders/geo` provides parseGeoJSON, parseShapefile, parseGPX, parseKML and parseMVT. All return source features, owned double xyz positions, explicit point indices, line-segment indices, polygon rings with holes, and a float32 triangle mesh with feature groups. Per-primitive feature arrays keep attributes addressable after tessellation. Coordinates stay in source units: GeoJSON/GPX/KML use CRS84 lon/lat/altitude; Shapefile preserves supplied .prj text without guessing a projection; MVT defaults to tile-local y-down coordinates. Its optional tile address converts to lon/lat. Geographic dateline cuts are expected in the source geometry, as in GeoJSON. No implicit globe/terrain projection is promised.
Defaults: maxFeatures 100,000, maxBytes 256 MiB, maxDepth 64, existing maxVertices 8,000,000/maxTriangles 16,000,000. Parsers accept AbortSignal. Polygon fill uses existing Margo hole-aware planar triangulation in x/y; a vertical ring (a MultiPatch wall, whose x/y outline has no area) is triangulated in the plane its Newell normal faces instead (2026-11-15). MultiPatch rings group as the ESRI technical description orders them: an Outer Ring with the Inner Rings after it, or a First Ring with the Rings after it, is one polygon. Boundaries are also line segments. Source geometry retains Shapefile Z/M ordinates, while draw coordinates use xyz. Shapefile points, multipoints, polylines, polygons and multipatches are covered; optional dBASE rows retain record alignment, null geometries and deletion flags (deleted rows omitted unless includeDeleted). Its encoding defaults to windows-1252 and is configurable; unsafe numeric integer attributes remain strings. Sidecars are supplied directly rather than fetched implicitly.
GPX keeps waypoint metadata, route/track elevations and timestamps, with no segment-spanning line; empty/singleton paths become null/points. KML reads placemark Point/LineString/Polygon/MultiGeometry and gx tracks, IDs and ExtendedData; styles remain source attributes rather than an automatic map style engine, and external links/models are not fetched. MVT retains layer/extent, tags, repeated point commands and polygon holes; 64-bit IDs and integer attributes outside exact Number precision remain decimal strings. Unknown protobuf fields are skipped by wire type, and truncated payloads/illegal geometry commands reject.
New /geo: 8,246 B min+gzip, ceiling 8,502 B. It leaves the shared geometry triangulator as its existing optional dependency (6,805 B ceiling), rather than duplicating that implementation. Loader root remains 53,022 B and core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

### UI visual layout editor (batch 259)
`@margoengine/ui/editor` exports LayoutDocument and LayoutEditor. Browser page: `examples/ui-editor/`. The document edits markup and style sheets live, validates both before committing, retains the previous valid preview on errors, supports text/attributes, insertion/removal, hierarchy moves and bounded undo/redo (default 100 edits, configurable positive historyLimit). Project JSON version 1 saves exact markup/styles; markup/XML and CSS can also download separately. Invalid drafts visibly prevent save/export. ## Batch 210 job 3: animation/discrete-tracks
New standalone entry 0 -> 2280 B min+gzip, ceiling 2536 B. Mixer categorical binding/selection and safe original-value restoration increase mixer 4158 -> 4805 B; ceiling 4414 -> 5061 B. Keep one shared clock, action cache and property lifetime rather than splitting categorical actions into a parallel scheduler. The existing intentional mixer/model dependency remains; discrete-tracks itself has no rendering-runtime dependency. Core/stage source stays unchanged and their combined gzip limit stays 25000 B.
BooleanKeyframeTrack and StringKeyframeTrack take name, strictly increasing finite times and one exact typed value per key. They hold the previous key through the next key, clamp outside, and select a key at its exact time. Times use owned Float64Array data; values are frozen ordinary arrays. Default and only interpolation is InterpolateDiscrete (2300); sample returns its boolean/string type, and createInterpolant reuses a plain array. clone, shift, nonzero signed scale, inclusive trim with held boundary samples, optimize (keeps duration endpoints), validate and JSON round trips are supplied. Do not mutate retained times directly; bind/create the clip again after editing keys.
track.bind resolves leading-dot, dot-name, numeric bracket and quoted-key paths once, or accepts explicit get/set. Unsafe prototype paths reject. createDiscreteClip produces a bound clip for AnimationMixer, which also accepts plain property-root objects. Per-property categorical output chooses the highest effective action contribution; leftover original weight competes when the sum is below one, and ties select the later action. Strings/booleans are never numerically averaged; additive arithmetic rejects. Keep a property in one value family across its tracks. Last-stop/dispose restores original values on live roots, cache eviction releases writes, and dead model roots release bindings without invoking disposed Mesh setters. A default infinite-repeat single-key action holds its constant value.
Batch 239 job 4: tiles/fade covers meshes, i3dm, pnts and globally sorted Gaussian splats. Ordered 4 by 4 screen-door coverage has 16 ranks; it is spatial coverage with ordinary material opacity/depth behavior preserved. Default full replacement duration is 0.3 seconds with a monotonic performance clock; a supplied simulation clock makes replay deterministic. Hierarchical intervals preserve complementary masks through reversal and nested replacement; ADD content keeps additive semantics. A fade temporarily retains both drawable levels and their budget bytes. Point coverage uses two spare existing uniform slots; a splat cloud lazily adds four bytes per original splat, restored on device recovery, and tile splat budgets include those bytes. Mesh extension factors add 16 bytes per primitive. Completed hidden REPLACE parents no longer remain permanently wanted just to provide an unused fallback; pre-eviction selection observation protects visible outgoing content until completion. Core and stage source and their 25000 B combined limit are unchanged.

Batch 239 job 4 optional entry sizes (min+gzip bytes, parent to completed job): points/surfels 14674 to 14933, points/pick 5267 to 5759, splats/index 30679 to 31291, splats/lod 29246 to 29793, splats/set 28036 to 28564, tiles/splats 1580 to 2060, tiles/fade 0 to 1766. The added bytes retain cohesive material validation, original-ID splat masks and shared tile ownership; splitting would duplicate that lifecycle. ### Batch 243 sampled mesh emitters and spot/IES lights
`voxel-pathtracer/mesh` adds world-area/power-selected emissive triangle NEE with reciprocal path-hit MIS. Affine placements have independent world areas and lookup records over shared BLAS geometry. Emissive PBR maps, alpha masks and one-sided material visibility are evaluated at the sampled UV; textured power selection uses the material factor as a proposal, without changing radiance or its exact proposal PDF. Zero-probability CDF entries retain full path-hit weight. Triangle metadata remains inside the existing 128 MiB geometry packet limit.
`MeshTraceScene.spotLights` accepts up to 4096 delta spot/IES sources. Positions use world units, color is linear RGB, intensity uses candela (or multiplies absolute IES candela), direction defaults down, range defaults infinite. Ordinary spots default inner 0 and outer pi/4 radians, inner strictly below outer and outer at most pi/2. With IES and no explicit angles, the full photometric sphere is used without a cone envelope. Type C profiles retain horizontal and vertical tables, 90/180-degree symmetry or full 360-degree azimuth, nearest boundary values in tilt, bilinear intensity interpolation and explicit lamp tilt degrees (default 0). Unrepresented vertical angles emit zero. External tilt text is caller-resolved; there is no implicit fetch. Type A/B profiles require conversion to Type C and reject with coded unsupported. Up must not be parallel to direction.
The Rust scan and shader additions increase mesh from 32,933 to 40,351 B and mesh-pbr from 37,233 to 43,550 B min+gzip. Ceilings rise from 33,913 to 41,562 B and 38,350 to 44,857 B, respectively. The bytes buy sampling, file parsing and reciprocal PDF correctness in the existing optional entry; a split would duplicate geometry feature ownership and prevent the requested mesh entry from accepting these lights directly. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. No timing or speed claim is made.

## Batch 207 job 2: exported and imported lightmaps
Blender lightmap entry 0 to 4636 gzip bytes (ceiling 4892); lightmap/imported 0 to 1279 bytes (ceiling 1535). The former briefly bundled the latter and its texture runtime (14642 B); externalizing the owning API keeps one shared runtime rather than paying twice. Required bare dependencies are image decode and the existing PBR model; lightmap/imported uses materials for managed linear textures and the PBR model for extension-slot rendering. Core plus stage remains 24209 B. These are per-entry sizes, not all-dependency download totals.
lightmap_size defaults to 0 (off), otherwise integer 16..4096. Static visible meshes need node materials and Object Mode. UV0 remains the material coordinates, UV1 is retained or generated with four-texel chart margin, and temporary mesh copies/images/nodes/selection/render engine are restored, also after export errors. Cycles uses CPU, scene sample count, direct and indirect diffuse passes, excludes material colour and specular, then converts its E/pi to physical irradiance. Nonnegative finite HDR RGB is normalized by one scale >=1 into linear RGBA8; row orientation is flipped with the exported UV1. Quantization error is bounded by scale/255 per channel. Bake lighting is fixed at export time. Geometry instances and animated illumination are outside the current bake path: Cycles bakes the original view-layer mesh objects, so a generated collection instance is not baked on its own and shows the lightmap of its source object (two instances under different shadows get one irradiance); export real mesh objects (Object > Apply > Make Instances Real) for spatially distinct irradiance.
readLightmap copies RGBA8 data, checks width/height 1..4096 and scale 1..1e20. applyLightmap uses UV1, the free material extension slot, and replaces direct and ambient illumination while preserving material colour, metalness and emission. It owns its texture, restores the previous slot on disposal and rebuilds on device restoration. Existing custom material extensions must be removed first. The three analytic irradiance channels (0.5,1,2) import within quantization bounds; both backends draw (56,56,56) through the existing PBR Neutral display curve, invariant under a large increase in engine light. No Cycles film/BSDF or speed equivalence claim.
Batch 219 job 3: optional geometry/teapot exports teapotGeometry(size=1,segments=10,options={}). Y-up, centered, size is the half-height with familiar Blinn proportions. Positive size must remain representable after scaling into Float32 positions; overflow and complete underflow reject. segments is an integer 2..175, keeping all 32 patch grids below core's million-vertex limit. options.body/lid/bottom default true; body includes handle and spout. fitLid=true expands the lid horizontally by 14/13 to meet the inner rim; blinn=true uses the familiar historical squashed shape, false restores 4/3 height. UVs cover [0,1] per patch, normals use analytic derivatives and inverse-transpose scaling, and degenerate pole normals sample derivatives 0.000001 inward. Material indices are body=0,lid=1,bottom=2. Cusp triangles are omitted; the full shape has 32*(segments+1)^2 vertices and 64*segments^2-8*segments triangles. The historical model retains intersecting handle/spout/body surfaces and a separate lid, without a solid interior. Very coarse tip/knob facet chords can oppose exact corner normals because of high curvature; default and dense resolutions agree at every corner. New entry 0 -> 2339 B min+gzip, ceiling 2595 B; model data, validation, parts and shared patch evaluation belong together rather than duplicating the evaluator across part entries. Core + stage remains 24209 B. The margoengine/geometry/teapot alias is generated from the same entry.

### Headless GIF and exporter palette (batch 209)
Entry bytes (min+gzip, bare package imports external): headless/gif 118 B (new, ceiling 374 B), exporters/palette 2,597 B (new, ceiling 2,853 B), exporters/capture 6,944 -> 7,667 B (ceiling 7,241 -> 7,923 B). The 118 B wrapper requires the optional exporters peer; its codec bytes are in the capture entry, sharing palette quantization. These bytes retain one writer, stream cancellation, explicit duration/repeat policies and correct rounding. Splitting another codec would duplicate LZW and quantization or add lazy-loader plumbing. Core plus stage stays 24,209 B.
encodeGIF accepts sync/async RGBA8 frames; only one raw frame is retained plus the compressed result. fps defaults to 30, in 100/65535..50. dither defaults false; loop defaults 0 (forever), -1 plays once, 1..65535 repeats. Per-frame duration overrides fps and accepts 0.02..655.35 seconds. Sizes are consistent and <=65,535 per side; data must fit memory. Alpha <128 is transparent, otherwise opaque, as GIF supports one-bit alpha. Each frame has a local <=256-colour RGB palette (255 opaque colours with transparency). Exact colours are preserved when they fit; other frames use shared median cut and optional ordered Bayer dithering. The signal interrupts waiting for the next frame; producers must also observe it to release their own pending work. No CPU speed claim or speculative Wasm rewrite.

## Mesh convex hull and Minkowski sum (batch 224 job 4)
geometry/hull exports convexHullTriangles(points, {signal}) with outward indices into the original flat/nested xyz positions. Empty or lower-dimensional sets return empty indices. The existing Quickhull predicates use a translated unit frame and a 1e-10 coordinate-scale tolerance; this is a floating hull, not an exact predicate claim. Source coordinates are never narrowed to float32. Legacy geometry/extras convexGeometry retains its original errors and float32 rendering buffers.
mesh-edit/hull exports convexMeshHull(oneMeshOrArray, {createId, signal}) and minkowskiSumMeshes(a, b, options). Hull includes all supplied positions (including loose vertices), emits newly generated triangle IDs/planar UVs, and returns an owned empty solid for empty/flat input. Maximum hull input is 200000 positions and normal output mesh limits apply. Minkowski inputs are closed outward consistently wound solids or empty; output has mesh, cells [a,b], convexPairs, planeTriples, collapsedFaces and diagnostics. Empty operands absorb. Concavity, disconnected components and cavities are supported by BSP interior cells and union of convex pair sums. Every output face has a new ID; caller corner attributes are not meaningful under the sum and UVs are planar.
Minkowski defaults: maxCells 2048 per operand, maxPairs 65536, maxPlaneTriples 2000000 per operand. A convex pair may contribute at most 200000 vertex sums; the batch input/output limits also apply. Budgets are positive safe integers and exceeding them rejects with guidance, not partial geometry. Cell decisions/intersections use the existing exact representation, but exported cell coordinates and additions are float64 and Quickhull uses its documented tolerance; a positive cell too thin for that hull rejects explicitly. The final union's validity-preserving thin-face folds are counted. This is not exact arithmetic Minkowski output or a geometric self-intersection repair API; normalize intersecting component soups first. AbortSignal is checked throughout. Worst-case BSP decomposition and pair enumeration can be large, so no interactive or speed claim is made. Core/stage remain unchanged.
Entry sizes: mesh-edit/hull 0 to 11992 gzip bytes (12352-byte ceiling); geometry/hull 0 to 2071 bytes (2327-byte ceiling). Shared Quickhull keeps geometry/extras growth at 5570 to 5617 bytes within its existing ceiling. The optional bytes cover nonconvex and cavity-capable sums rather than a convex-only partial API. Core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.

### FBX large entry (batch 205)

`@margoengine/fbx/large` exports `largeFBX(overrides)` and `FBXImportLimits`. Pass the returned
immutable extension in `extensions` to convertFBX, parseFBX, loadFBX or their worker forms. One
limit configuration per import; unknown names and nonpositive/noninteger/unsafe values reject.
Ordinary imports keep every existing default. All figures below are caps, never reservations.

| Field | Ordinary | largeFBX default |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| inputBytes | 64 MiB | 512 MiB |
| decodedBytes | 128 MiB | 2 GiB |
| arrayBytes | 128 MiB | 512 MiB |
| nodes | 100,000 | 1,000,000 |
| properties | 2,000,000 | 16,000,000 |
| parseWork | 128,000,000 | 2,000,000,000 |
| sceneBytes | 128 MiB | 2 GiB |
| sceneWork | 128,000,000 | 2,000,000,000 |
| morphBytes | 64 MiB | 512 MiB |
| vertices | 1,000,000 | 8,000,000 |
| corners | 3,000,000 | 24,000,000 |
| geometryWork | 40,000,000 | 320,000,000 |
| textureBytes | 64 MiB | 512 MiB |
| texturePixels | 16,000,000 | 268,435,456 (1 GiB of RGBA8) |
| outputBytes | 128 MiB | 512 MiB |

MiB = 1,048,576 bytes; GiB = 1,073,741,824 bytes. `vertices` bounds control points,
expanded vertices and the cumulative scene vertices (including instances); `corners` bounds
polygon corners and triangulated indices. Allocation/work accounting remains conservative,
so dense seams/instances may need higher caps. Raising a cap cannot create available memory.
The 4,096-corner polygon, hierarchy depth, animation/key/sample limits and GLB uint32 format
limits are unchanged. Imported meshes are never decimated or truncated to meet these caps.

Measured default ceiling (2026-11-11, RTX A6000 workstation): the defaults hold a 996,004-vertex mesh with every corner
its own vertex (normals, one UV set, tangents; binary FBX with compressed arrays, 6.7 MiB): it converts, attaches with
`parseFBX` and renders on WebGPU and on the WebGL2 layer, uploading its GPU geometry once; the converted file holds
one primitive, which gltf/pbr draws as parts of at most 262,144 vertices (its default `maxPartVertices`), one draw
each, covering every vertex and every triangle once (`packages/fbx/test/large.test.js`, `test/default-scale-browser.mjs`,
`test/part-coverage.js`). What bounds it: the
1,000,000 expanded-vertex cap (a second primitive starts past 999,997 vertices and repeats the corners of a polygon
split across it). The memory caps sit just above it for this layout: the geometry build reserves 94 B per corner for
a mesh of unique vertices with normals and one UV set (each term a typed array of exactly that size; it was about
267 B, which stopped such a mesh at about 480,000 corners under the 128 MiB scene cap), decoded arrays are about 75 MiB
of the 128 MiB array cap (an inflated array is counted while it lives, not added to the total after its typed copy is
made), and an uncompressed file reaches the 64 MiB input cap first, at about 860,000 such vertices. WebGPU's default
device limits do not bind: a converted primitive holds at most 1,000,000 vertices and a drawn part 262,144 of 80 B (under the 128 MiB storage binding)
and its index buffer is far under the 256 MiB buffer size. Past the default ceiling `largeFBX` raises every cap.

The large configuration also reaches GLTFAsset attachment and worker prepareGLTF: the converted GLB uses outputBytes and nodes as its downstream caps. Ordinary attachment retains the pre-existing 64 MiB glTF cap. The 2,500,002-vertex test produces a buffer above 64 MiB and attaches both directly and from prepared worker output.

Large material partitions are emitted as additional child mesh nodes at triangle boundaries, with at most 1,000,000 vertices per primitive, matching the existing PBR storage-binding safety cap. Every triangle and layer is retained; control-point maps still drive skin and morph remapping. Shared vertices on a chunk boundary may be duplicated and count against the configured vertex cap. This adds draw calls rather than reducing geometry. The 2,500,002-vertex independent-triangle fixture emits three full primitives and retains every position/index.

Batch 172 job 4: sciviz/probe accepts up to 8000000 points/snapshot and 1000000 profile samples. Uniform cell buckets max 32 per axis; cells spanning over 128 buckets use a separate candidate list. ### Oriented box culling subclasses

`@margoengine/culling/bounds` exports BoxCulledMeshes, BoxCulledModels and
BoxDynamicInstances. They inherit the corresponding ordinary culler's options
and methods, retaining stable compaction, picking and complete shadow lists.
Frustum tests use transformed local boxes, including shear and reflection;
BoxCulledMeshes and native BoxCulledModels also use them for Hi-Z occlusion.
Model padding expands each local half-extent. Deformed model primitives still
retain their original conservative bypass. Ordinary sphere cullers do not load
box mathematics. BoxCulledModels runs box frustum/size culling on the full WebGL2
layer; its Hi-Z remains native-only. BoxCulledMeshes uses current CPU depth there.
BoxDynamicInstances adds box frustum tests on both backends; its base class has
no occlusion option. Geometry position arrays are treated as immutable, as for
ordinary core Geometry; model array replacement refreshes cached bounds.

Batch 223 job 2 also joins exactly coplanar convex triangle pairs before CPU
depth rasterization, using exact dyadic predicates for the float32 positions.
This removes their internal seam while preserving real holes, folds and back
faces. Larger triangulations may still retain extra candidates. Snapshot
validation refreshes cached patches when software geometry changes in place.
The software entry's earlier 28-of-81 figure is job 1's historical measurement;
the current entry can reject additional hidden rows with the same pixels.

## Batch 207 job 3: meshopt .margo geometry
New blender/meshopt is 8304 gzip bytes (before 0, ceiling 8560), including optional variant validation paths. compressMargoMeshopt losslessly encodes packed 24/80-byte vertices and 16/32-bit indices with existing meshopt version-0 attribute streams. Indices are encoded as raw four-byte groups (zero padding is discarded), preserving every index and provoking vertex rather than rotating triangles. Small/uncompressible sections remain native; the entire original file is returned if it is smaller. expandMargoMeshopt supports static, animated, shapes and KTX2 containers without changing metadata/image/animation bytes; decodeMargoMeshopt is the static prepared reader. parse/load default to parseMargo; use options.parse for compatible PBRModel parsers such as parseAnimatedMargo, parseMargoKTX2 or parseMargoLightmap. Shapes can use the expanded bytes with the curves loader. AbortSignal is checked between sections, before allocation and before load; a single existing synchronous codec call cannot be interrupted.
Expanded file and aggregate section allocation are bounded at 256 MiB before decode; vertex count per section at 1 million, original table/manifest limits retained. PNG/KTX2/animation sections stay uncompressed. No lossy quantization, triangle reordering or geometry simplification. Seven own fixtures keep every section byte and manifest value; anim 28924 to 19516 B, objects 13940 to 12348 B, lightmap 1396 to 1276 B, curves 18180 to 17988 B. Native/compat frames are identical for original and compressed static/animated models, with zero validation errors. These are deterministic byte counts, not timing benchmarks.

### Native 3MF lattice and slice data (batch 202)
`@margoengine/loaders/threemf-lattice` exposes async parse3MFLattice. It returns the existing textured/material preview mesh plus source objects, exact native lattice parameters, source-double xyz, triangle topology, per-build affine instances, slice stacks and property resources. Radii and contours remain in file units; instances retain the composed row-vector affine transform and unitScale (meters by default, 1 for units:file). This preserves nonuniformly scaled spheres/frusta without replacing their radii with an inaccurate scalar. Clipping mode/volume and representation meshes remain explicit references to validated earlier source meshes; consumers choose their native construction or the file's preview representation. The returned triangle stream is the file's mesh representation, whose lowres/fullres label is retained. It is not a new manufactured union of beams or slices.
Caps are sphere/hemisphere/butt, default sphere. ballMode defaults to none; mixed/all require ballRadius. Source beam indices remain stable; activeBeams applies minlength before transform, and effectiveBalls applies mode and active beam-end membership. Native-only valid beam builds can have empty triangle arrays. Default maxBeams is 1,000,000 for beams and explicit balls each, with at most twice that many set references. Default maxSlices is 100,000 source layers/references and separately expanded referenced layers. Source/slice vertices share maxVertices; segments are bounded by 3*maxTriangles, source objects by 100,000 and the existing model-part/instance/ZIP caps remain active.
External slices require their model-part OPC relationship and a single reference level. Tops strictly increase, void layers remain, model/solidsupport contours close explicitly, and composed slice transforms preserve the slicing plane without an epsilon tolerance. Component stacks override descendant stacks. lowres requires the slice namespace in requiredextensions. Slice properties retain endpoint gradients and object defaults. Materials keep raw entries plus normalized composite weights and defaulted multi rows/blendMethods. The shared materials reader now mixes in linear RGB, supports multiply, treats all-zero weights uniformly and retains opacity in attributes.opacity. Existing byte, count and AbortSignal options propagate through all part reads.
Entry sizes: /threemf-lattice is new, 0 to 12,275 B min+gzip (ceiling 12,644 B). /threemf-materials is 7,661 to 8,082 B; its ceiling rises from 7,917 to 8,338 B for linear mix/multiply, normative defaults, alpha and shared format hooks. The optional rigging/mtoon entry adds 9,540 B min+gzip (previously 0 B), ceiling 9,827 B. World outlines use metres and screen outlines use view height; tests cover perspective distances 2 and 4. Material queue offsets order blended primitives across every MToon model of a scene (queue, then model draw order; 2026-11-11, KB5289a); plain gltf/pbr models without MToon keep their own blended order inside their model draw. Spatially masked UV animation is applied to beauty, normal, emission and outline paths, and (2026-11-11, KB5289b) to the cut-out of shadow casters (cascades, virtual shadows, clustered local and cube maps, staging contact shadows), TAA object velocity and selection picking; each animated MASK material costs one 80-byte buffer write per frame and its casters redraw every frame. UV animation is sent as float64 phases (2026-11-15), so it keeps 1/60 s steps after days of uptime; scroll wraps by 2 only on an axis every moved map samples alike after a step of 2 (whole-number texture transform columns, no clamp on an axis it reaches), and an axis that cannot wrap, or a fractional mask value, keeps float32 rounding of the scroll. Custom material resources have the existing same-device isolated-renderer restriction. Evidence is native WebGPU and complete WebGL2 compatibility on RTX A6000, not cross-vendor or speed certification. README examples remain owed.

### Rich blend trees (batch 211 job 2)

animator/blend-trees exports createBlendTree and blendGradient2D. RichBlendTree accepts clip strings, type 1d with parameter and samples {value,tree}, Cartesian/directional with parameters [x,y] and 2D sample values, or direct with children {parameter,tree}. Compiled trees work as Animator/AnimatorGraph/layer states, root motion and sync retain leaf clip weights. Optional PlaneTileMap draws ordered tile, tile-object and image-layer quads using the active view core camera. transform is a copied, mutable column-major affine 4x4 matrix from map pixels to world coordinates; default is the XY plane at z=0, 16 pixels/metre, downward map y. ### Optional front-to-back instance ordering

`@margoengine/culling/sort` exports FrontToBack for kept core batches (including
DynamicInstances) and registered model instances, SortedInstances for the static
CulledInstances draw path, and InstanceSorter for 96-byte GPU lists. Sorting is
optional; enabled and sortEnabled default true on the respective optional
classes and can change at runtime. Core and model sorting executes after culling
and before drawing, independent of registration order. Model tint/transmission
lists and alphaMode BLEND primitives retain their existing order. Plain model
primitives keep their original draws; deformed models retain their bypass.
Each range orders by its transformed local center along the current view
forward direction, with original row indices breaking equal-depth ties. It
supports perspective and orthographic views, reflection and node transforms.
Ordering is per batch, as with specialised batched renderers, rather than across
materials or geometries. Counts, picking/caster buffers and every record field
stay unchanged. Opaque surfaces that overlap at equal surface depth but have
different center depths can resolve in the new order, the usual draw-order
consequence of sorting. Transparent geometry must never be passed to the raw
sorter. Importing ordinary cullers does not load ordering code.
InstanceSorter accepts capacity 0 through 4,194,304 within device storage limits;
its key network rounds to a power of two. It binds only the rows a range reads (from the last record at or before
`start` meeting minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment to `start + capacity`), so a core instance buffer that has doubled past
one storage binding still sorts (2026-11-11; before, it bound the whole buffer, a validation error every frame past
about 1,048,574 meshes of one geometry on a 128 MiB device). A list past one binding itself (1,398,101 records at
128 MiB) is refused by `encode` with RangeError; `InstanceSorter.fits(device, capacity, start)` tells, and
FrontToBack leaves such a list in its original order (drawn the same, unsorted). Scale check
`packages/culling/test/gpu/sort-scale-check.mjs`: 1,200,000 meshes, frames equal to core's natively and on the WebGL2
layer. O(n log-squared n) key comparisons and
one gather are encoded; no per-instance CPU work or GPU readback occurs. Each
view and stage owns distinct parameter storage. Input instance buffers require
STORAGE; supplied argument buffers require STORAGE and COPY_SRC. Software
occlusion arguments now expose those flags too. No speed claim is made.

Removed sort owners release all their view resources with InstanceSorter.forget;
FrontToBack also collects owners absent from the preceding frame and releases
registered model resources on removal. Cleanup happens before a later frame,
after the prior frame's command submission; existing view uploads stay distinct.

Batch 223 job 3 minified gzip: /sort is new, 0 to 14060 B. /webgl2 stays 3028 B while exposing storage/copy access to its argument buffer. /bounds stays 19447 B. The sort entry shares one network implementation across drawing routes and reuses the existing static culler; a split would duplicate resource state and complicate import/use. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. firstInstance prefixes are included in capacity; their indirect word and draw offset are preserved, along with every other indirect word.

@margoengine/scatter/textured exports TexturedScatter.attach(engine, model, transforms), plus validated setMatrixAt/getMatrixAt and disposal. ### Graph transition offsets and interruption (batch 211 job 3)

GraphTransition.offset defaults to 0, accepts finite 0..1 and sets destination entry time relative to its longest clip. Events start at that entry, including a marker exactly at the offset. Crossfades retain their own seconds clock, so a large offset cannot prematurely end an uninterruptible fade. interruptionSource is none, current, next, both (alias current-next), current-next or next-current. Default next preserves existing behaviour; legacy interruptible:false defaults to none, and an explicit source overrides it. Each source checks transitions in declaration order, with any-state rules eligible for that source; only the selected rule consumes triggers. Source clocks advance for exit-time checks and chained interruptions retain their selected source. Manual animator.transition uses next semantics. Snapshots retain optional fade.fromTime and reject nonfinite/negative source times. Graph controller parameter/trigger and interruption-policy state is separate from Animator playback snapshots.
Entry costs: graph 9,719 -> 10,177 B gzip, ceiling 10,011 -> 10,483; layers 10,281 -> 10,730 B, ceiling 10,436 -> 11,052. The bytes keep source selection and graph clocks in one implementation, avoiding an incompatible alternate controller entry. Core and stage unchanged.

Chains are transitive; cluster diameter may exceed radius. Unclustered labels pass to an optional nested layout. Clusters expose original label handles for picking/drill-down and HTML elements for styling/events. clear/dispose removes bubbles; no permanent member visibility change.
