## Mesh-surface scatter (batch 231 job 2)

scatterSurface(geometryData, count, options) from @margoengine/scatter/surface returns owned transforms, positions, normals, uvs and colors arrays. Defaults: seed 1; scale [1,1]; yaw [0,2*pi] radians; align 1; offset 0; source matrix identity; no weights or painted colours; no cancellation signal. Count is 0..1000000. Source triangles must have positive weighted area even with count 0. Vertex weights are nonnegative and interpolated linearly within each triangle. Areas are measured in world space after options.matrix, including nonuniform scale; normals use its inverse transpose. Arrays and source geometry are not mutated. Sources and outputs must fit finite f32 values; placements are nonsingular affine world matrices with uniform scale. Use an identity TexturedScatter model root for world placements, or convert into that root's space.

Output costs 112 bytes per placement (16 matrix, 3 position, 3 normal, 2 UV and 4 colour floats), plus the sampler's triangle CDF and transformed source copies when a matrix is supplied. Alignment is the shortest rotation from world +Y, then optional local yaw; the antipodal -Y case chooses +X as its turn axis. Offset is along the sampled normal. No mesh-to-heightmap projection: cliffs, roofs and undersides are sampled directly. Resample when source geometry or weights change. Entry gzip 0 to 1259 bytes, ceiling 1515 bytes; core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.
Batch 172 /glyph: optional instanced glyphs and scalar/vector warp, with at most 1000000 input points (images follow imageGrid's existing 2D/3D limits). Stride/mask apply to original row IDs; an all-zero instance scale is omitted, while a zero component (components scaling of a planar field) draws the glyph flattened along that axis with the plane normal. Cell centres are vertex means. Finite f32 render transforms/bounds; grid warp coordinates are f64 and surface output is f32. Line sources are thin tubes; custom meshes use +X and retain their own origin. Bounds are conservative spheres; explicit triangle normals rebuild after warp, while arbitrary field arrays remain borrowed. No tensor transport, element-inversion guarantee or timing claim. Core/stage unchanged at 24209 B gzip.

Batch 172 /glyph entry: new 0 to 4388 B min+gzip, ceiling 4644 B; optional placement, shapes, warp and ownership stay together to avoid API fragmentation. Core/stage unchanged at 24209 B.

Batch 205 job 4: `@margoengine/fbx/surfaces` exports `surfaces`, an optional extension on page and worker conversion. It tessellates Nurb/NurbsSurface and Patch geometry, including older inline Model geometry after legacyFBX normalization, independently of extension ordering. NURBS orders 2..32, positive rational weights, open/closed/periodic nets and every nonempty knot span use loaders/nurbs. FBX Step controls subdivisions per span; absent Step defaults to four times degree. Bezier cubic, BezierQuadric quadratic, Cardinal cubic, uniform cubic BSpline and Linear patch bases may differ on U and V. Open Bezier nets require 1 modulo degree control points; closed nets add their seam point; Cardinal open spans interpolate the interior controls and closed spans wrap. Closure wraps the necessary weighted rows/columns. Parametric UVs, analytic/pole normals, FlipNormals, material links, model transforms and animation remain in the ordinary FBX path. UCapped/VCapped generate flat-normal cap polygons, with the existing 4,096-corner polygon limit. All generated work and buffers charge the import budgets before allocation; vertex/corner limits include caps. Blend shapes on a surface are exact morph targets at every weight (normals exact at full weight); a skin is exact where the control points a vertex reaches share one weight set, and where they blend it is exact through four helper joints for each joint whose weight changes there (KB5330c, 2026-11-25), so two such joints fit the eight influences glTF and the engine take; three, a negative share (Cardinal patches) or a blend in an Additive or TotalOne cluster is refused with the polygon-bake remedy. Each weight set costs one more tessellation of the grid, and each changing joint two. Deformers on legacy inline Model geometry are refused.
The output is the whole parametric surface, not trimmed topology. Control-point skin deformation needs a bind position per joint, which one glTF vertex position holds only through helper joints: up to two changing joints a vertex are exact that way (KB5330c), and anything past that fails with coded unsupported/help and a polygon-bake remedy, rather than misapplying original control-point indices to generated vertices. Ordinary polygon skin/morph import is unchanged. Separate Maya ASCII/binary exports contain different near-zero control coordinates; exact front-end parity is proven by encoding the same real control net both ways, without rounding the product output.

### Weighted bone masks (batch 211 job 4)

animator/masks provides createBoneMask(nodeCount, entries?, defaultWeight=0) and addWeightedLayer(owner, {clip or graph, mask, weight?, blend?}). The builder returns a mutable Float32Array in glTF node order; entries are unique [node,weight] pairs. Weights and defaultWeight must be finite 0..1. An attached mask has exactly one value per model node and is read and validated every frame. Each value affects its own node; ancestry is not expanded automatically. Effective influence is layer strength times bone weight; zero retains the lower pose and one applies full influence. Defaults are layer weight 1 and override mode. Additive uses the owner's loaded local pose and identity scale delta on a zero reference axis. Morph weights use the corresponding node influence. Vertex skin weights remain asset data. The returned StateLayer exposes its independent graph controls and shares the layers entry's class identity. Disposal removes the complete layer; owner pause/speed and lifetime apply as for graph layers.

### Painted 2D geometry (batch 247 job 1)
`@margoengine/lighting2d/sdf` exports `SDFScene2D`, consumed as borrowed `GILighting2DOptions.painted`. Source alpha at least alphaThreshold (default .5, always positive) defines opaque axis-aligned pixel cells; RGB is linear straight albedo. Separate emission defaults to source, uses RGB times alpha times emissionIntensity (default 1, nonnegative), and only occupied cells emit. Black art blocks without emitting. Camera defaults {x:0,y:0,zoom:1}, top-left origin, pixels per world unit, independent of the receiver camera. Changes are sampled every GI frame before cascades. Inputs are single-sample 2D single-layer RGBA/BGRA unorm/sRGB or RGBA16/32 float TEXTURE_BINDING textures of matching dimensions; textures and the SDFScene2D are borrowed by GI. Source and output must be distinct textures. sRGB textures decode on load. HDR needs a floating emission image and output.
The exact sampled-centre signed distance field stores R distance in pixels, G occupancy in rgba32float (16 B/pixel). All-empty/full opposite-class distances use finite magnitude 1e10. Three GPU passes plus scratch cost 48 B/source pixel plus 32 B uniforms (row 8, hull 16, squared 8, field 16); scratch buffers must fit device maxStorageBufferBindingSize/maxBufferSize and dispatches must fit maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension. The transform is exact at pixel centres, not a continuous vector outline; opacity is thresholded, not transmissive. Nearest opaque cell emission terminates each ray, including inside a source. No frame-rate or general transport-error claim. Painted surface reflection and temporal reuse are batch 247 job 2.

## Batch 207 job 4: live Blender node graphs
blender/nodes is a new optional entry; entry size and ceiling are recorded with the job's size evidence below. Core and stage are untouched. Export live_nodes defaults false. When true, reachable unsupported nodes or surface lobes fail by material/node name, with the existing baked export available by disabling live_nodes. No silent baking in the live path.
Supports Value/RGB, reroutes, Math (41 scalar operations including safe divide/power/log domains), MixRGB and Mix (Float/Vector/RGBA, 19 color blend modes; Hue and Color keep A when B is grey, and Saturation keeps a grey A grey, since a grey has no hue), Color Ramp (2..32 stops, Constant/Linear/Ease/Cardinal/B-spline, RGB/HSV/HSL and four hue directions), Noise (1D..4D, Fac/Color, fractional detail 0..15, normalized fBM, multifractal, ridged, hybrid and hetero terrain, roughness/lacunarity/distortion/offset/gain), UV/Generated/Object/Normal coordinates and RGB/XYZ separate/combine. Principled live inputs: base, alpha, metalness, roughness, emission/color strength and IOR. Other shader types, groups, images, arbitrary mapping/vector nodes, custom object coordinate sources and physical surface lobes are outside this entry's common-graph row and reject explicitly. This entry does not replace the existing baked or extended-material entries.
Limits: 256 live output nodes, 1024 vec4 parameters (16 KiB), 3601 animation frames, 262144 parameter samples, file limit 256 MiB. Original metadata is cloned, cycles/forward links and shader-injection enums reject. seek(seconds) clamps to the sampled scene range without looping; per-frame samples interpolate linearly. Runtime set overrides remain through seek until reset. Blender frame/subframe and images/mesh counts are restored during export. Coordinate conversion preserves Blender Z-up, UV bottom-left and scene units. Ramp stop positions/colors remain paired and sort live when they cross.
Noise uses Margo's independent hash and gradient field, rather than Blender's private stochastic ordering: the procedural field and animation controls remain live, but exact noise texels are an accepted difference. Per-frame sampling also approximates subframe curves between samples. No speed, bandlimiting or full Blender material equivalence claim. Both are recorded for later quality work rather than hiding the difference.
Live Noise against Cycles (KB5339e, accepted difference, 2026-11-25). Cause: Cycles' lattice hash and gradient order are not in a published description (the Blender manual's Noise Texture page gives the controls only), an integer hash cannot be recovered from samples by curve fitting, and the clean-room rule bars reading Blender's source. What Margo does: the live Noise keeps Blender's controls, animated and evaluated per pixel at any resolution, on Margo's own lattice; for Cycles' exact pattern the add-on's `bake_noise` option (off by default) bakes every material a Noise Texture feeds with Cycles, and on the 32 x 32 fixture (a coloured 3D noise on base colour, a 4D noise inside a node group on roughness, Blender 5.3 Beta, CPU, 4 samples) 0 colour and 0 roughness texels differ from an independent Cycles emission bake (`tools/blender-addon/tests/blender_bake_noise.py`). Trade-off: a baked material is a still image of `bake_size` pixels per side for each mesh that uses it, needs a UV map and texture memory, and loses detail below a texel and all animation (an animated node tree is refused by name); a live one animates and has no texel limit but shows another pattern.
Socket curves (KB5339b, KB5339c): a parameter driven by plain F-curves seeks to Blender's value between frames (Bezier, constant, linear and every easing, Elastic included; constant or linear extrapolation, with linear extrapolation flat from a CONSTANT end key, along the last span from a LINEAR one and along the outer handle from any other, as Blender 5.3 evaluates it, KB-P3d). A colour wired into a float socket becomes its Rec. 709 luminance with the weights a Cycles bake gives (0.2126391, 0.7151691, 0.0721927), within 1e-6 of the bake; Geometry Nodes rounds them to 0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722, within 1e-4. A vector wired into a float socket becomes the mean of its three components (KB5339h). Elastic matches Blender 5.3 within its single-precision rounding (under 2e-5 of the larger of 1, the value and the decaying swing, on 135 probes); a curve's keys count toward the 262144 samples. An F-curve with a Noise modifier (KB5339d) is sampled in Blender by fcurve.evaluate at an eighth of a frame or finer (finer for short noise octaves, down to 1/1024 frame) and played back as LINEAR keys: at every sampled step the value is Blender's within one float32 step; between steps it is interpolated linearly, measured at most 5.9e-4 off on the KB5339d fixture (frame + k/3 + 1/7 offsets, noise strengths 0.2 to 4). The old frame samples missed the same fixture by up to 0.078 between frames. Margo has no noise model of its own for F-curves. Drivers, other F-curve modifiers, NLA and muted curves interpolate frame samples linearly. Seeks clamp to the scene range.

### Painted GI and temporal intervals (batch 247 job 2)
`GILighting2D.temporal` defaults true; false recomputes all intervals, and resetHistory() forces the next rebuild. Identical frames retain spatial/angular cascade and finite-bounce surface buffers, and their compute invocations return before tracing. Source and emission RGBA comparisons are exact on GPU. Any alpha, color, emission, source transform, cutoff or gain change invalidates painted intervals. Analytic geometry, emitters, lights (including nested masks), layer, cascade options, view camera and output dimensions are compared on CPU. No old radiance is blended into changed input. A camera move rebuilds rather than reprojecting; ambient is applied at presentation and needs no interval rebuild. Device replacement and changing painted/no-painted mode discard all GI history. One SDFScene2D snapshot per command encoder serves multiple consumers; submit a manually managed frame before starting another. GI borrows the painted scene and textures.
Painted occupied cells have four outward surface slots; internal faces are inactive. Each exposed face gathers 32 cosine-weighted directions per requested bounce from the preceding order, at its midpoint offset .001 source pixels into empty space. Painted RGB clamps to [0,1] for reflectance and multiplies the configured albedo; emission retains HDR. Finite bounce orders 0..4, source resolution, interval reach and angular quadrature limits still apply. GI is now covered by the named opaque visibility, energy, finite-bounce, painted-input and temporal correctness fixtures; no general physical-exactness, converged transport, continuous vector-outline or frame-rate claim is made. Historical README exceptions and no-history language await the README phase.
SDF adds 32 B/pixel exact RGBA history and a 16 B change flag to its previous 48 B/pixel transform storage (80 B/pixel plus 48 B fixed uniforms/flag). Painted GI surface buffers use 192 B/source pixel (two persistent fields and immutable zero order, four vec4 faces each), plus analytic patch geometry and cascade storage. Analytic surface fields use 96 B/patch including zero order, replacing the earlier 64 B/patch. Changed-input comparisons and distance generation still run every frame; presentation traces the near connectors. Reuse avoids surface gathers and upper-cascade interval traces, not every GPU operation.

### Compute shape entry (batch 274 job 1)
The optional @margoengine/compute/shape entry adds concatenate(arrays, axis=0), stack(arrays, axis=0), flip(x, axes=all), tile(x, repetitions), repeat(x, counts, axis=null) and pad(x, widths, options). Concatenate axis=null flattens; repeat omitting its axis flattens. Negative axes normalize against the output rank for stack and input rank otherwise. Joining promotes element types; other operations preserve dtype. Every output owns its buffer. CPU, WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility share the same logical indexing. f16 uses the existing shader-f16 device requirement and is unavailable on CPU.
Pad defaults to constant zero; scalar constantValues is converted to the input dtype. Modes: constant, edge, wrap, reflect (excludes endpoints), symmetric (includes endpoints). Widths may be one nonnegative integer, a shared pair, or one pair per axis. Nonconstant padding cannot fill an empty source axis. This entry does not expose NumPy callable/statistical/ramp padding or odd reflection. Tile prepends singleton axes or repetition factors as required by the Array API. Repeat counts may be a number or a host list of length one/axis length. Counts stay on the host to determine output shape. Arrays are bounded by device storage limits and signed 32-bit gather indices; split larger inputs.

### Batch 218 GLSL transition import

The optional transitions/glsl entry translates user-authored GLSL ES 1.00 with vec4 transition(vec2 uv) into the custom WGSL contract. translateGLSLTransition is pure; createGLSLTransition and createLiveGLSLTransition validate asynchronously before attaching. progress and ratio are supplied, along with getFromColor/getToColor and the from/to sampler2D aliases. GLSL UVs default to bottom-left; flipY:false preserves top-left coordinates. Additional uniform values are snapshotted as constants from options.uniforms or // = JSON annotations. Vectors, column-major matrices and fixed arrays use flattened component arrays; boolean values or 0/1 are accepted for boolean components. Numbers must fit finite 32-bit values; integer uniforms must fit their signed/unsigned type. Array lengths may be integer literals, const names or constant expressions over them (folded at parse time, 2026-11-11); helper parameters may be unnamed. Since the batch 132 audit (2026-11-15) lengths fold over local constants too, decimal, octal (leading 0) and hexadecimal (0x) integer literals carry their values, a declared name comes into scope after its initializer, a precision statement may stand in a function, matrices negate and take every compound assignment and increment, a scalar constructor takes a vector's or matrix's first component, a sequence may start with a void call, the last operand of `?:` is an assignment expression and only l-values take assignments. Still refused: inverse and array equality in a GLSL ES 1.00 source (neither is in that language; `#version 300 es` sources get both), and a swizzle of a swizzle as an assignment target; each fails with an error, never a wrong image. Since 2026-11-15 a vector built from a matrix (`vec4(mat2)`), a matrix built from mixed vectors and scalars and a constructor whose last argument is partly used lower, spread into scalars in GLSL's order.

Preprocessing supports object/function macros, conditionals, define/undef, `#version 100` and `#version 300 es` (2026-11-15). Expressions use typed precedence parsing, including scalar/vector arithmetic, matrix operations and casts, struct/array access, overloads, swizzles, short-circuit boolean expressions and conditional side effects. Structured if/for/while/do control flow and copy-in/copy-out out/inout parameters are lowered to WGSL. No extra textures or arbitrary binding interface is supplied beyond the two transition images. Other GLSL versions (3.10 and up, desktop GLSL) are refused when declared, with code `unsupported`. This is a transition-function importer, not a complete vertex/fragment program or an external include loader. Source is limited to 65536 UTF-16 units, 32768 tokens, 128 nested statements/expressions, 64 macro expansion rounds and 262144 expanded units; uniform arrays have at most 16384 elements. The custom wrapper also limits emitted WGSL to 65536 units. Compiler diagnostics carry failed and a help link; GPU compilation, cancellation, exact endpoint bypass and shader trust requirements follow the custom entry. Shader execution itself is not bounded by these parser limits.

Native GLSL and WGSL may round floating-point arithmetic differently, especially at exactly-on-texel-boundary nearest samples. Pixel fixtures choose coordinates away from those ambiguous ties and compare with the existing one-byte unorm tolerance. No bit-exact arbitrary GLSL or speed claim is made.

Batch 218 job 3 glsl entry is 15718 B gzip (new entry, before 0 B), with a ceiling of 16190 B. After the batch 132 audit fixes (2026-11-15) it is 16475 B gzip, from 16167 B (+308 B), ceiling 16970 B: the bytes are the GLSL ES 1.00 forms the importer now lowers instead of rejecting. The compiler carries a real parser, preprocessor, typed aggregate/control-flow lowering, diagnostics and both validated factories. Splitting those mutually dependent stages would complicate deterministic diagnostics and lifecycle without improving shader quality. Core + stage stays 24209 B.

The GLSL front end (parser, preprocessor, emitter) moved from `packages/transitions/src` to `packages/shader/src/glsl` behind the `GLSLHost` interface (progress, ratio, from/to samplers, getFromColor/getToColor, the y flip and the entry wrapper stay in transitions), so the shader package can take GLSL input too. Transitions bundles it from source; the transitions/glsl entry measured 16519 B gzip (default zlib, `entry-sizes.mjs` method) after the move, from 16475 B (+44 B for the host object), under its 16837 B ceiling; shader root stays 18664 B and core + stage stays 24837 B. The WGSL emitted for every recorded transition source is byte-identical (`packages/transitions/test/glsl-wgsl-identity.test.js`).

GLSL ES 3.00 input (2026-11-15, The OpenGL ES Shading Language 3.00.6): `uint` and the bit operators and their compound assignments (a shift amount is converted to the unsigned type of the left operand's width, as WGSL needs), `switch` with `case`/`default` labels folded at parse time (constant integer expressions over literals and constants in scope), cases that fall into the next (each WGSL case holds its own statements and those it falls into, up to one that ends in `break`, `return`, `continue` or `discard`; WGSL cases never fall through), `matCxR` types with GLSL's product shapes and `transpose`, `outerProduct`, `matrixCompMult` and the uniform layout for them, `float[3] a` and unsized `float a[] = float[](...)` declarations, array constructors, `.length()`, array equality and arrays as parameters and results, `texture`, `textureProj`, `textureLod`, `textureProjLod`, `textureGrad`, `textureOffset`, `texelFetch` (rows counted from the bottom under the y flip) and `textureSize`, `inverse` (adjugate over the determinant; a singular matrix is undefined in GLSL and gives non-finite values here), `outerProduct`, `trunc`, `round` and `roundEven` (both round half to even, which GLSL allows for `round`), the hyperbolic functions, `isnan` and `isinf` (decided on the IEEE 754 bit pattern, so a compiler cannot fold them away), `modf`, `floatBitsToInt`, `floatBitsToUint`, `intBitsToFloat`, `uintBitsToFloat`, the 2x16 snorm, unorm and half pack functions, boolean `mix`, the `flat`, `smooth`, `centroid` and `invariant` qualifiers and skipped `layout(...)` qualifiers. A signed integer literal keeps its 32-bit pattern (0xFFFFFFFF and 3000000000 are negative), and one beyond 32 bits is refused. The transition images have one level and are read at their nearest texel, so a lookup's level, bias and gradients select nothing there. Not lowered: samplers other than the two images (no binding exists for them in this entry), integer samplers, shadow samplers, `textureGather`-style ES 3.10 functions and uniform blocks. Each of seven original GLSL ES 3.00 fixtures draws the same pixels, within one level per channel, as the browser's own GLSL compiler over 16 x 16 pixels at three progress values, natively and on the WebGL2 layer (`packages/transitions/test/glsl-es3-fixtures.js`). One fixture's reference takes a `continue` out of its `switch`: ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end (Chrome 157, RTX A6000) cannot compile a `continue` inside a `switch` and loses the context, so the translated fixture keeps it and the layer avoids it (KB-SW1, below). The transitions/glsl entry measured 19,498 B gzip after this, from 16,519 B (+2,979 B); its ceiling rises from 16,837 to 20,083 B. The bytes are the GLSL ES 3.00 language the shared front end now reads; it is one front end for transitions and shader, and a lazy split of the ES 3.00 parts would need a second fetch on the first translation of any source that uses them. Core + stage is unchanged.

KB-LOOP-D3D11 and KB-SW2 (fixed 2026-11-26): on ANGLE Direct3D 11 (Chrome 157, RTX A6000) a loop whose header holds `?:`, `&&` or `||` (a WGSL `select` is `?:`) ran its update and condition at the `continue` of a loop nested in it, and a switch with one case and an empty default ran that case whatever the selector. The WebGL2 layer now writes such a loop with no header when a loop inside it continues, and an empty default clause first. Regression: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-control-flow-browser.mjs` and `test/glsl.test.js`.

KB-SW1 (fixed 2026-11-15): a WGSL `continue` inside a `switch` inside a loop reached ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end as a GLSL `continue` inside a `switch`, which it fails to compile ("Error compiling dynamic pixel executable", then a lost context). The WebGL2 layer's GLSL now sets a flag and breaks out of the switch, and the loop continues after it; a nested switch hands the flag outwards. Regression: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/glsl.test.js` ("a continue inside a switch leaves the switch by a flag").

Batch 244 job 3: CRT adds `colorBleed` [0,1], default 0, and `chromaticOffset`, `redOffset`, `greenOffset`, `blueOffset`, each a horizontal number or [x,y] source-pixel tuple in [-32,32], default 0. Symmetric offset adds to red and subtracts from blue; independent offsets add on top. Positive offsets select texels to the right/below, so those channel images move left/up. Effective combined offsets may reach 64 source pixels. Color bleed retains source luma and alpha, filters I with normalized 5-tap and Q with 9-tap horizontal binomials, then clips to the premultiplied gamut. Offsets use bilinear sampling with edge-repeat borders; alpha is the maximum selected channel alpha. Tube beam/mask/brightness modulate the processed color; glow still adds the unshifted raw-source 3x3 halo. Both effects default off and preserve all previous CRT pixels, including exact boundaries. This is a selectable composite-video look, not RF encoding, dot crawl, interlacing or a calibrated TV standard. No extra pass or intermediate image; no timing claim.

Batch 244 job 3 min+gzip: pixel/crt 2816 -> 3775 B, ceiling 3072 -> 4031 B. These optional bytes retain one CRT pass with independent RGB sampling, YIQ chroma filtering and existing restoration/lifetime plumbing; splitting would add pass wiring or duplicate source processing. Core plus stage remains 24209 B.



### Streamed SOG (batch 238 job 3)
splats/lod-sog accepts v1 and unversioned pre-release lod-meta.json, null/omitted environments, sparse leaf levels, optional errors and relative arbitrary chunk paths. Each chunk is unbundled SOG v2/v3 with 1 to 3,000,000 records. All small metadata is fetched up front with concurrency 8 to validate runs/counts and choose a uniform SH degree; textures remain lazy. Spatial depth limit 128. Complete non-overlapping single-level chunk runs and supplied totals must agree. A referenced chunk is decoded whole, then its range is copied. cacheChunks defaults 2 (0 disables completed caching), plus active loads and the existing SplatLod node cache. Independent caller aborts share requests; disposal aborts all loads. A manifest `model` other than `antialiased` (such as `2dgs`) is refused with code `unsupported` before any chunk is fetched (2026-11-11).
SplatLod structural nodes have count 0 and refine unconditionally; the renderer never calls their load. Minimum coarse coverage must fit the fixed-slot budget, otherwise construction rejects with the required budget. Slot-count and splat-count limits both constrain refinement. Errors are used only with lodErrors true; otherwise radius * cbrt(max(0,1-count/finestCount)) estimates omitted detail. Environment stays selected regardless of camera distance. No transition blending or new training algorithm.
SOG v3 preserves exponential-map rotations, squared opacity through 1.5625, 24-bit labels and SH degree 4 (25 RGB coefficients including DC). Unused blind attributes are ignored as permitted by the format. Images use the existing lossless WebP decoder. Extended opacity is retained until the existing fragment alpha cap min(0.99, opacity*Gaussian), preserving extra off-center coverage. Colours retain the existing first-order display/linear SH conversion. encodeSog chooses v3 for extended opacity or degree 4, otherwise v2. SPZ v3, .splat and Gaussian PLY reject opacity above 1 rather than wrapping/clipping; SPZ v3 rejects degree 4. Standard PLY now carries degree 4.

Batch 238 job 3 minified gzip: lod-sog new 0 to 20,369 B (ceiling 20,981 B). Shared degree-4/v3 support takes data to 22,273 B (prior ceiling 22,135 B, raised to 22,942 B) and animate to 20,381 B (prior ceiling 20,263 B, raised to 20,993 B). The bytes retain a single validated data representation and codec instead of splitting degree/opacity formats. Root splats 32,073 B; lod 30,582 B; progressive 31,464 B; formats 20,705 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

## Lightmaps drawn at draw time (batch 54)

`@margoengine/lightmap/apply` adds the bake as indirect light (diffuse reflectance times occlusion times the bake),
the way `Material.lightMap` does; it does not turn off live lights the bake already holds. A glTF PBR material record
that already has a material extension (clearcoat, a custom one) is refused, since a record holds one extension. A core
mesh needs its lightmap UVs passed (`uv1`), is drawn by a materials stand-in in the engine's default scene, and its
stand-in copies colour, roughness, metalness and sidedness only (no core textures). A live GPU baker must share the
model's GPU device. WebGPU only for glTF PBR models. After a device restore a CPU bake on a glTF PBR model draws the
same light from the new device (uploaded again from its pixels, 2026-11-15, KB-OWN-LIGHTMAP1); a live GPU baker
lives on its device and goes with it, so the model draws no baked light until a new baker made on `engine.gpu` is
applied. That fix took `lightmap/apply` from 2,476 B to 2,442 B min+gzip (ceiling 2,634 B unchanged).

## Batch 196 non-XR stereo

Optional cameras/stereo is 3,144 B min+gzip (previously 0 B), ceiling 3,400 B. StereoOutput.render replaces the application's engine.render call in its frame loop; it uses two scene draws and one fullscreen packing pass, with one plugin update per pair. Default mode side-by-side, eye separation 0.064 world units, convergence at the camera target, source engine.camera, source camera layers, default scene, unswapped eyes, column stripes and phase 0. Infinity focus gives parallel frusta. StereoRig also preserves custom projection hooks; orthographic eyes correctly have no depth disparity. The packed output is display colour (RGBA8 eye textures); anaglyph is the published red/cyan Dubois transform in linear light. Two RGBA8 eye targets use 8 * eyeWidth * eyeHeight bytes, plus core's normal render attachments. Rows/columns refer to physical backing pixels; a physical barrier needs calibrated optics and pixel-aligned presentation. On automatic canvas resize the projection follows the new aspect immediately and eye resolution catches up on the next frame; exactSize canvases give caller-controlled physical dimensions. No XR session or automatic engine.start takeover. Dispose the output before its engine. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility work; native WebGL-only engines reject.

## Camera sight clearance (2026-11-27)

Optional cameras/clearance (new entry). CPU only: each view casts 32 x 18 frame rays and 15 subject rays over a height function (steps of 0.5 m, 1 percent of the distance far out) and upright cylinders; it does not see buildings, overhangs or leaf shapes, and a feature thinner than a step or a ray gap can be missed. The Fauld shot generator reads plants within 600 m of the lens. Five Fauld rows stay blocked (KB-SHOT-FAULDSIGHT1).

## Four-view pyramid hologram (2026-11-26)

Optional cameras/hologram is 3,511 B min+gzip (new entry, previously 0 B); core + stage unchanged. HologramOutput.render replaces the application's engine.render call: four square scene views (front, back, left, right, a quarter turn apart about the source camera's up, at its height and `distance`) and one layout pass, with one plugin update per frame. Each view is (1 - `gap`) / 2 of the canvas's smaller side (default gap 0.2, range [0, 1)); below 1/3 neighbouring slots are cut along the diagonals to their wedges; outside the slots is black. Orientation per side is a quarter-turn rotation and a mirror (default every view mirrored, top away from the centre, for a pyramid standing on the screen). Four RGBA8 view targets use 16 * side * side bytes plus core's normal render attachments; the layout resamples them linearly, so a canvas not sized in whole pixels per slot blurs by up to half a texel. A source camera looking straight along its up axis has no horizontal side and throws. No calibration for a particular pyramid's angle or the display's brightness. Proof: the browser check compares every slot, turn, mirror and wedge cut with each camera drawn alone, on WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer; no physical pyramid was used.

## Interior mapping (2026-11-27)

Optional materials/interior-mapping is 4,837 B min+gzip (31,075 B while it made the material itself, which loaded
the Material classes and gltf/pbr-model and gltf/extended-materials with it); core + stage unchanged. It returns the
options and imports no package, so `new WgslMaterial(interiorMapping(options))` loads the material code only through
the app's own import of the materials package.
Rooms are boxes on one grid along each upright facade, 2 to 33 floor levels, rooms 0.1 to 1,000 m; level surfaces keep
their own material look, a bay window or dormer looks into its wall's grid, curved and leaning walls are not followed,
one furniture plane and either a curtain or a blind a window, room light casts no shadow and lights nothing outside, and
pictured rooms are read at one mip level a pixel without anisotropy (a cube's rim blends toward its window face). Checked
on the workstation GPU on WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer.

## Stencil portals (2026-11-26)

Optional materials/portal is 29,863 B min+gzip (29,788 B as a new entry; 2026-11-27 it holds StencilBuffer's depth give-back, KB-XR-AREFFECTS1, and the transmissive tint map, KB-MAT-TINTMAP1; most of it is the shared Material and WgslMaterial code the entry reaches, which an app that makes materials meshes already loads). Every portal holds one 8-bit stencil reference from `first` to `last` (default 1 to 255, so at most 255 portals at once); a portal past the range throws a coded `state` error. A mask and its contents are materials meshes; the portal edits their materials (colour write, depth write, stencil state) and render order, so a material can belong to one portal mesh only. Masks draw at render order 1000 + 2 x ref and contents just after, after the opaque meshes of order 0; a mesh with a higher order of its own draws after the window and is not masked by it. Same-scene contents are depth-tested against everything drawn before them, so a wall coplanar with the mask hides contents behind it; put such contents in a second scene. A second-scene portal draws that scene once per frame at the full canvas size into one texture in the canvas format (4 bytes a pixel per portal) and shows it unlit on the mask surface in screen space; post effects attached to the second scene do not run on that picture (not tested with main-scene post effects). Overlapping windows: the later mask wins where they overlap. Stencil does not cross views or targets (see Polygon offset and stencil). Proof: the browser check on WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer; no speed measured.

### Curved text (batch 248 job 4)
`@margoengine/text/curve` provides CurvedText, curvePoint and PathText. CurvedText extends Text, wrapping the entire local X/Y block around local Y at signed curveRadius (default 1; Infinity is flat). Default curveSegments is 8 horizontal subdivisions per glyph, integer 1..256. The analytic cylinder uses [r*sin(x/r), y, 2*r*sin(x/(2*r))^2]; glyph UVs and outline/shadow layers interpolate over the subdivided surface in one block draw. Anchors, lines, shaping, font styles and transform/mesh placement are preserved. Layout/caret/selection coordinates remain in the unwrapped plane; hitTestSurface maps a cylinder-local surface point back to that plane. That inverse is principal-angle only, so blocks winding more than one revolution need an application-supplied winding choice.
PathText accepts a TextPath with positive finite length and sample(distance) returning position/tangent/normal in local world units. startOffset defaults to 0; closed defaults false (out-of-range glyph midpoints hide), true wraps distances. Glyphs align rigidly to normalized orthogonal path frames as in SVG textPath align; whole shaped runs remain joined. Line baselines offset along the frame normal. Global transform and mesh attachment apply after path placement. Each visible nonspace shaped item is one Text draw. Call update after editing owned options, font state or path; addTo/removeFrom and dispose manage renderer membership, including rebuilds. Billboard is refused for PathText because the path owns glyph orientation; CurvedText supports a billboard cylinder. Arbitrary paths are supplied via the public frame interface, not parsed from SVG strings. No core or stage additions.
Batch 248 job 4 measured entries: /curve 10,487 B gzip (new), text root 16,701 to 16,860 B within its existing ceiling. The shared rendering avoids another renderer; core plus stage remains 24,209 B.
Extended dynamics entry: 2,856 B gzip, budget 3,112 B.

## Batch 212 job 4: mixer/dynamics
Extended dynamics entry: 2,856 B gzip, budget 3,112 B. New optional gate/expander/three-band compressor with explicit linked speaker channels 1..32 (default 2), fixed construction options, AudioWorklet/CSP/AbortSignal/owned bus lifecycle as the existing worklet entry. No lookahead (latencyFrames 0), automatic makeup, clipping or true-peak limiting. Crossover phase is inherent; flat magnitude does not mean sample-identical input. Use existing worklet limiting after this stage for peak safety.
Gate defaults threshold -40 dBFS (-120..0), hysteresis 3 dB (0..40), hold 0.05 s (0..10), floor -Infinity (silence, or -120..0 dB), attack 0.001 s and release 0.1 s (0..10). Peak >= threshold opens; while open, peak >= threshold-hysteresis resets hold. Exactly holdFrames below-closing-threshold samples remain open, then closing begins. Expander defaults threshold -40, ratio 2, knee 6 dB, range 80 dB (0..120), makeup 0; below-threshold slope ratio and a quadratic knee join continuously to unity. Band defaults threshold -24, knee 6 (0..40), ratio 4 (1..100), attack 0.003, release 0.1 (0..10), makeup 0 (-24..24). Attack/release are one-pole gain time constants: compressor attenuation/recovery, gate/expander opening/closing; zero jumps. Pure expanderCurve returns output dB and handles silent -Infinity.
Multiband crossovers default [250,2500] Hz, ordered 10..0.45*sampleRate; separate low/mid/high BandDynamics. Each split is two cascaded Butterworth biquads per low/high path (24 dB/octave). Low-band high-crossover phase compensation keeps the unity sum flat. Per-band detector is linked maximum absolute sample. Ratios 1 and makeup 0 retain the crossover's allpass response. Tests prove independent RBJ convolution, closed-form knees/gains and flat impulse-response magnitude across the spectrum; real renders beside both backends. Headroom, perceptual tuning, other browsers and performance remain unmeasured. No core/stage change.
## Batch 173: optional transfer classification
`@margoengine/sciviz/transfer` adds joint value/gradient histograms, rectangle, triangle and Gaussian classifiers, 1D ordered preintegration, CT/MRI/PET display presets and an owned HTML editor. LUT resolution is 2..2048 per axis; default 256 for widgets, 128 for preintegration. Colours are linear light, opacity per reference voxel. Points and widget coordinates use physical scalar units and scalar units/data unit for gradients. Histograms require 2+ samples per axis, at most 64 million samples, x fastest; NaN/nonfinite centres or derivative neighbours are excluded. Histograms own two float64 scratch arrays (16 bytes/sample) and a 4-byte count per bin. Scalar values/gradients outside the selected histogram axes clamp to the edge bins.
Volume textures retain signed normalized scalar values outside the display range so their gradients remain meaningful; binary16 limits normalized values to [-65504,65504] and rounds them. Histogram derivatives use original CPU values; render derivatives use the half-float, trilinearly sampled field. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported. Bricked volumes and extracted isosurfaces do not consume this scalar VolumeLayer API. The editor can bind any existing scalar VolumeLayer without recreating its data; function points are resampled into the layer's existing range. Slice colours update with the same classifier. Slice opacity remains its independently specified opacity.
Preintegration uses 8..2048 midpoint samples (default 128), linear scalar variation over an ordered front/back segment and RGBA8 output. Generate for the layer's `step=1/quality` and density. Regenerate after changing quality/density for the most accurate colour integral. The marcher corrects opacity when step/density differ, but unpremultiplied integrated colour remains an approximation in that case, at clipped segment endpoints and in the existing 2048-sample cap. Gradient classification is evaluated at march samples, not preintegrated in 2D. MIP is scalar-maximum projection, not a 2D classification maximum.
The HTML component has no import side effects, supports add/select/delete, pointer/key translation, colour/opacity, rectangle extents, Gaussian sigma and explicit triangle vertices. Disposing the editor removes DOM/listeners and restores the layer's original classifier. Preintegration and histograms accept AbortSignal and yield during work. No timing or superiority claim. Transfer entry: 5996 bytes min+gzip (new entry, formerly 0; ceiling 6252). Sciviz root: measured parent 50597 to 52045 bytes; its optional ceiling rises from 51813 to 53607 for physical classifier hooks and safe owned-buffer PNG capture. Core + stage: unchanged 24209 bytes. The combined editor, histogram and classification contract stays together; splitting would add import/ownership complexity without reducing full-feature bytes.

mesh-pbr now carries clearcoat, sheen, iridescence and specular factors and all specified extension textures from loaded glTF snapshots. Optional weather/lens is 3,601 B min+gzip, new from 0 B, ceiling 3,815 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. ## Batch 212 job 5: mixer/pitch
Pitch entry: 2,366 B gzip, budget 2,622 B. New optional time-domain transposer emits exactly one frame per input frame, with linked read-head phase for explicit speaker channels 1..32 (default 2). Defaults: pitch 0 semitones (-48..48, fractional), windowSize 0.1 s (0.005..1, fixed at construction), delayTime 0 s (0..1), feedback 0 (-0.95..0.95), mix 1 (0..1), antiAlias true (boolean). Pitch/mix/feedback/delayTime are native audio-rate controls; setPitch validates schedule atomically and defaults to immediate, or an exponential fade settling about 98% over seconds. Zero wet and default unison preserve bits, including initial samples. Unison with configured delay/feedback reads a fixed delay, minimum 1 sample for feedback.
Two half-cycle-offset read heads use complementary Hann weights and linear interpolation. Nonzero-pitch wet delay spans additional delay plus 1..windowFrames+1 samples; there is no single fixed latency. Source event times/duration stay on the same clock, with that bounded wet tail; keep feeding zeros to flush it. Memory per channel is ceil(sampleRate+windowFrames)+4 float64 samples plus filter state, allocated once. No per-sample allocation, FFT, offline resampling or timer. Upward antiAlias filtering is two Butterworth biquads at 0.45*sampleRate/ratio before the delay; aliases can remain and high frequencies are attenuated. Linear interpolation also rolls off high frequencies. No formant preservation, transient protection, speech-quality, polyphonic transparency or alias-free claim; this is the requested delay-line effect class and can have window coloration. Feedback is a creative transposed delay, not pitch-preserving echo. Requires secure AudioWorklet and blob CSP permission. Abort/disposal and bus-owned inserts follow the other optional worklets. No core/stage change; tested in Edge beside both backends, other browsers/listening/performance unmeasured.


### Voxel image and text generation (batch 241 job 1)
`@margoengine/voxel-edit/generate` provides `heightmapToVoxels` and `textToVoxels`. Grey8/RGBA8 row-major images produce Y columns: nearest whole-cell height, black zero, white `height` (default 32), X image columns and Z image rows. RGBA defaults to encoded BT.709 luma, with explicit red/green/blue/alpha and inversion options. RGBA alpha at or below `alphaThreshold` (default 0) is air; grey images have no alpha, so the threshold does not apply to them. `textToVoxels` crops to the ink of the lines that have ink, so a glyph's side bearing leaves no empty columns. Source RGBA is retained, with the existing deterministic reduction above 255 colours.
Text takes a required CSS `font`, default depth 1, coverage threshold 127 and opaque white colour. Native canvas shaping preserves Unicode, kerning, ligatures and holes; callers load custom fonts first. Multiline default spacing is 1.2 times measured Mg ink height. Negative bearings and descenders are included; Y is up, extrusion is positive Z. Empty text is empty storage with positive dimensions. An optional supplied context is resized and cleared; otherwise Canvas is created at call time. Fonts and platform rasterizers can differ, so font masks are not cross-platform bit-identical. There are no import-time DOM accesses. Both APIs take AbortSignal and the standard 16,777,216-cell default / 67,108,864-cell maximum budget, checked before grid allocation. Text needs a native 2D canvas; Node hosts can supply one. No new rendering backend or core code.
Entry size: /generate is new (0 to 2,479 B min+gzip, recorded ceiling 2,735 B). The bytes cover image validation, palette generation, native text bounds and extrusion together; splitting would duplicate their shared grid and validation code. Core and stage are unchanged.


### React component testing and offscreen scenes (batch 266 job 3)

The optional test entry needs a caller-provided browser DOM or jsdom; it never installs globals or requests a GPU by default. It uses ordinary react-dom plus act and the GPU-free headless null stage, not a custom reconciler. Null stages cannot validate pixels/GPU deformation; a borrowed rendering stage supports pixel tests. Frame deltas are 0..1 seconds and counts nonnegative safe integers. Events use explicitly selected live hits; await helpers in order. Canvas shadow-controller bindings still need a real rendering Canvas. Offscreen React stays on the page and runs native createScene modules through worker/auto. Data must be structured cloneable for workers; React components/context/functions are not transferable. Auto falls back before transfer when workers, transfer or renderer support are missing; runtime scene errors do not replay after transfer. Backing dimensions default to 300 by 150, timeout to 30000 ms, mode/backend to auto. The scene owns subsequent render sizing. Changed startup inputs create a fresh canvas. See docs/guides/react-test-offscreen.md for ownership, all defaults and evidence. No core/stage changes or speed claims.

Entry gzip sizes with external peers: react/test 5,944 B (new, ceiling 6,200 B); react/offscreen 1,167 B (new, ceiling 1,423 B). Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. Optional testing and lifecycle code stays together; splitting would add internal public contracts without reducing work.

### Batch 214: chain avoidance
The optional kinematics-constraints/chain entry supports CCD and FABRIK on 1..256 positive-length links, 1..256 candidate poses (default 32), and 1..1024 sweeps per candidate (default 64). The first candidate keeps the reached pose; candidate k is turned about the root to target line to that pose's swivel plus 2 pi k / candidates, so the swivel angles tried are evenly spaced and the widest gap left is 2 pi / candidates. Radius defaults to zero, required gap to zero and positional tolerance to 1e-5. The query protocol accepts capsule, convex hull, mesh and SDF obstacles. Every accepted capsule link preserves its length and target tolerance. Results certify a static pose only: use /swept for paths. Bounded local failure is not infeasibility; self collision requires caller-supplied pose acceptance. Full-body limb avoidance searches preserve the root and end and roll the entire body back when any callback rejects. Rollback restores the frame input, which is not itself certified against moving obstacles. No physics solver, rigging, core or stage change.

Batch 214 job 1 entry gzip: chain 0 (absent) to 1,904 B; animator/fbik 5,434 to 5,728 B. Optional ceilings raised in sizes.json for the new entry and atomic body rollback, which cannot be split out of the pose commit without losing atomicity. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B, under 25,000 B.

### Per-splat GPU modifiers (batch 238 job 4)
splats/modify supplies SplatModifier.create(cloud, options), attach(engine,cloud,options) and splatModifierShaders. Creation asynchronously snapshots current cloud data; signal abort rejects creation and later disposes the modifier. Already submitted readback work completes normally. One active modifier per cloud; combine hook logic into its WGSL bodies. Hooks position/opacity/color default to identity; declarations defaults empty; up to 64 parameter floats default zero, exposed as u.parameters[0..15] vec4f values. Each body has index, time and delta; position takes canonical position and returns vec3f; opacity takes the modified position and canonical opacity and returns f32; color takes modified position and evaluated linear RGB and returns vec3f.
time defaults 0, playing true, speed 1, enabled true. Clock advances once in the first view; seek with playing false. Geometry runs at -7.25 before projection/sorting, colour at -6.95 after SH/fog and before relighting. All SH degrees are evaluated at the modified centre. Covariances and SH remain the source's; this position-only warp does not deform ellipsoid axes. Geometry/opacity is written to the cloud inputs, including alpha readback, so existing geometric consumers see it. Colour changes are transient evaluated output. Opacity is clamped to 0..1.5625, colour to nonnegative HDR values. Shader/compiler errors remain visible through normal WebGPU validation.
Canonical position/opacity costs 16 bytes per splat on CPU plus 16 bytes per splat on GPU and a 288-byte uniform. Per frame: two compute passes, no canonical geometry readback. Ordinary source edits to centres/opacity must also call setRest with a full same-count SplatData; source RGB/SH/covariance edits flow normally. Disabling and disposal restore canonical centres/opacity; a fresh projection restores colour. Device restoration uploads the CPU canonical snapshot and retains clock/parameters. Composition with another position-writing animation needs an explicit canonical update; the plugin never silently stacks multiple owners.

Batch 238 job 4 minified gzip: modify new 0 to 20174 B, ceiling 20780 B. It retains canonical state, asynchronous snapshot/cancellation, typed WGSL hooks and both compute passes in one optional entry; splitting would add lifetime/ownership coordination without reducing a user's imported effect. The existing entries retain their job 3 sizes, including lod-sog 20,369 B; core plus stage remains 24209 B.

cutscene/nested-editor exports NestedTimelineEditor, discreteTrack and discreteOf plus DiscreteKey/DiscreteTrack types. Register discreteTrack() in the model/editor tracks option. Discrete values are boolean or string, held from the preceding key (first value before its time, last after its time); duplicate timestamps take the last key. A track keeps one primitive type and permits only absent or step easing. Values live in state.extras.discrete, read by discreteOf(), with literal dictionary names handled as own data. ### Screen-space voxel selections (batch 241 job 2)
`@margoengine/voxel-edit/select` exports `screenSelection`, `rectangleSelection`, `lassoSelection` and `colorSelection`. Camera input is the column-major view-projection (`engine.camera.matrix`); optional `modelMatrix` maps local cells to world. Shapes use NDC X/Y, Y up: pointer pixels convert as `2*x/width-1, 1-2*y/height`. Selection means occupied cell centres inside the shape and clip volume, boundary included. Rectangle drag order is free; lasso uses even-odd filling, 3 to 65,536 vertices, concave and self-crossing shapes allowed. WebGPU camera matrices use zero-to-one reverse depth and WebGL2 ones OpenGL's -1 to 1 depth (core `Camera.update`); pass `backend: engine.backend` (default `'webgpu'`) so the near and far tests and `visibleOnly` read depth the right way round. Cells behind the eye or outside near/far and viewport planes are excluded before divide.
Default select-through includes hidden cells. `visibleOnly: true` keeps a cell only when the camera ray through its projected centre first hits it; partly visible cells whose centres are occluded do not qualify. Singular camera matrices yield no visible-only hits. Colour selection is global inside the shape, compares actual RGBA values rather than index identities, and uses Euclidean RGBA8 distance divided by 510 (default tolerance 0, range 0 to 1); alpha participates. It is not a perceptual colour metric. Both dense and sparse inputs return sorted Float64Array edit indexes, retaining indexes above 2^32. Standard maxCells budgets cover dense cells or sparse occupied cells; AbortSignal propagates its reason. No pixel readback, DOM or new rendering pass.

### Shaped and variable-font extrusion (batch 248 job 5)
`text/extrude` accepts `shapedRuns`, ordered visual glyph IDs with xAdvance/yAdvance/xOffset/yOffset in em units, optional UTF-16 cluster and zero-based line. It respects ligatures, reordered RTL runs, mark offsets, vertical advances and multiple runs per line without remapping IDs through cmap. Letter spacing applies between distinct supplied clusters; omitted clusters space each glyph. A FontLike.shape(text) provider is called once when runs are absent; without either input, the existing Unicode cmap path remains. This is a shaping-result interface, with no built-in script shaper or network dependency. Normalize shaper positions by its font scale and use the same font instance and axes as the run.
`parseFontOutlines(bytes,{variations})`, FontOutlines.withVariations(values) and extrudeText's variations option select instances; omitted axes use fvar defaults, out-of-range values clamp, unknown/nonfinite axes fail with a linked coded error. variationAxes exposes tags/min/default/max. TrueType supports gvar shared/private/intermediate tuples, sparse contour interpolation, composite offsets and phantom widths when HVAR is absent. HVAR supports index maps and short/long delta rows, including null subtables. avar version 1 piecewise remapping is supported; later avar versions reject explicitly. CFF2 supports 32-bit INDEX counts, FontDICT/FDSelect formats 0/3/4, local/global subroutines, private and charstring blend/vsindex, implicit program termination and a 513-value stack. Existing 96-hint, 10-subroutine, 100,000-token and 16,384-flattened-vertex budgets remain; malformed ranges/counts reject. CFF1 and static TrueType behavior remain covered by the existing tests. Glyphs remain unhinted; font-wide MVAR/VVAR metrics are not consumed because block line height and supplied vertical advances own placement here. Parsed instances currently reparse their source bytes; no timing claim.
The existing optional extrude entry grows from 10,834 to 14,894 B gzip; its ceiling is raised in the same commit. Those bytes add the complete font-instance and positioned-run path in one parser; a split would duplicate sfnt state or add an asynchronous stateful bridge to the synchronous extrusion API. Core/stage and the text root are unchanged by this job, at 24,209 B combined and 16,860 B root respectively.

Variable font axes (KB5472d, fixed 2026-11-11): `text/extrude` and the text outline path normalize each axis as the OpenType "Coordinate scales and normalization" section specifies (Microsoft, OpenType 1.9.1 Font Variations Overview and the avar chapter, https://learn.microsoft.com/typography/opentype/spec/otvaroverview): the user value as 16.16 Fixed, the default normalization in 16.16, the avar segment map in 16.16, then the final F2Dot14 step `(v + 2) >> 2`. wght 350 on a 200 to 900 axis gives 0.21429443359375 before avar, not the floating 0.2142857. The outline oracle (packages/text/tests/generate-variable-reference.py) draws FontTools at that spec coordinate; FontTools' own floating normalization differs at every rounded weight and is kept beside it as `floatingAdvance`. Outlines stay unhinted.
### Batch 240 job 1: voxel custom block models

`@margoengine/voxel/models` defines a block as a union of 1 to 64 axis-aligned boxes, with finite cell coordinates 0 <= min < max <= 1. Each face has a UV rectangle (flips allowed) and texture layer 0..2047; animated layers must fit the same 2048-layer atlas bound. `modelState(id, orientation)` selects one of 24 exact proper cube orientations, identity 0. This is a discrete cube rotation, not an arbitrary-angle box rotation. Prepared metadata is structured-cloneable and the input box/UV arrays are copied.

`meshBlockModels(world,cx,cy,cz)` extracts model surfaces with exact box-union interior removal and neighbouring opaque/same-type boundary occlusion. It preserves interpolated UVs when clipping a face. Scalar sky/block light modulates vertex colour, with existing material PBR lighting, emissive/cutout/translucent options and caller texture-layer materials. `await VoxelModelRenderer.create(engine,world,{material?},signal?)` requires the optional materials peer and is updated after lighting and before engine.render. It streams on chunk add/remove and world edits and observes light changes without consuming world.dirty. It owns default materials and chunk meshes; callback materials/textures stay caller owned. Renderer meshes use the materials pipeline's existing frustum culling and shadows integration.

Queries and VoxelCharacter sweeps use exact boxes, VoxelPhysics builds model triangle surfaces, and scalar, worker and RGB lighting preserve model orientation and whole-face coverage. The existing flood light representation remains one byte per cell, as with slabs; it does not resolve separate disconnected light regions inside a cell. The packed quad renderer leaves these models to the optional renderer. Waterlogging, the GPU octant mesher and voxel path tracing do not acquire a custom-model feature in this job. No speed claim or new core/stage code.

### Voxel-net rooms (batch 242 job 1)
Optional /rooms owns independent VoxelServers in one process, one bound endpoint per world (public proxy endpoints may be supplied). Default capacity is 16 including reserved and parked seats; reservation life is 15,000 ms. Codes are unique 1 to 32 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/hyphen, random 12 hex characters by default. Private rooms are joinable by code but omitted from list(); full/locked rooms remain listed. Listing is a synchronous snapshot API for an application's HTTP or app-message lobby, with no built-in account service. Room identities are unique seat nonces; caller authentication still runs on upgrade and hello. Reservations claimed by a pending connection remain counted until it joins or all pending connections end, even after ticket expiry, so slow authentication cannot overbook. Server workers and all sockets close on removal. No GPU code or speed claim.

### Batch 214: limit-aware swivel
The optional kinematics-constraints/joint-limits entry provides JointLimitSet and jointLimitPredicate for SolveOptions.acceptPose. A caller supplies local rest-relative quaternions for every candidate joint. Euler bounds use Rx Ry Rz order and radians within -pi..pi; hinges enforce an axis and signed bounds; cones enforce swing plus optional twist. Defaults: unrestricted hinge twist, cone axis +Y, unrestricted cone twist, 1e-7 radian acceptance tolerance. Null limits mean free joints, but missing, nonfinite and zero rotations reject. A 180-degree swing has undefined twist and rejects restricted twist intervals. Bounds are copied at construction. Candidate rejection leaves accepted solver history untouched; predicate inputs are scratch copies that cannot alter the checked pose. This tests supplied rotations, not unsupplied rig orientation or future motion.

Batch 214 job 2 entry gzip: /joint-limits 0 (absent) to 1,212 B, with a 1,468 B ceiling. Root grows 11,567 to 11,687 B for the optional acceptance hook, within its existing 11,751 B ceiling. ## Batch 173: labels and registered multi-component volumes
Optional `@margoengine/sciviz/labels` adds `fusionVolume`, `FusionLayer` and `labelLegend`. One drawable, one fullscreen triangle and one march combine 1..4 sources; each source is categories, RGB, RGBA or 1..4 independent scalar components. Components are interleaved, x fastest. Arrays and transfer results are snapshotted. Each source retains its own dimensions and invertible affine unit-box-to-data mapping, with no registration resampling. Bounds default to [0,nx-1,0,ny-1,0,nz-1]; transform replaces bounds. Dimension and category counts obey the device's 3D/2D texture limits (palette needs one extra transparent slot). Each dimension is at least two.
Category IDs are exact unsigned 32-bit integers, including zero and 4294967295; never interpolate them. Unlisted IDs are transparent but retain distinct boundaries. Each listed category has linear-light RGBA and an optional separate outline RGBA and integer framebuffer-pixel width 1..16 (default 1). Eight nearest-category neighbours per radius detect label-to-label and external boundaries at each ray sample. This is a projected neighbourhood outline, not a smoothed subvoxel segmentation or mesh. `setLabels` atomically validates and snapshots replacements; `labelLegend.update()` refreshes accessible HTML text after edits.
RGB/RGBA channels are linear light, default divisor 255 for byte arrays and 1 otherwise; alpha shares that divisor. RGB opacity defaults to 0.1; RGBA uses its alpha. Colour and intensity sampling is trilinear; component functions are evaluated at 256 physical scalar values into binary16 RGBA tables, and source scalar components are normalized/clamped to their declared range in binary16. No gradient or preintegrated component functions in this entry. Component and source weight default 1; zero hides them. `TransferFunction.evaluate` can supply a 1D function directly; update a snapshotted function by rebuilding the layer.
Default optical mixing sums extinction and weights colours by optical depth; over gives earlier sources/components priority at each sample; maximum selects the largest corrected opacity (earlier wins ties). All three mix before front-to-back ray compositing, never as separately sorted volume draws. Quality defaults to 1.5 samples per projected voxel; density defaults to 1. Step opacity uses distance through each source's voxel coordinates. Each ray caps at 2048 midpoint segments and terminates at alpha >0.9999. Small features thinner than a step can be missed; increase quality within the cap. No native WebGL2 fallback driver; WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported. Internal opaque-geometry termination is the separate volume-quality job, not supplied here.
Entry min+gzip: 6292 B (new, formerly 0), ceiling 6548 B. Sciviz root remains 52045 B and core+stage remains 24209 B. Palette ownership, transforms, component mixing and the one march remain together; splitting would fragment the same source lifecycle without removing full-feature bytes. The MSD demo reduction is 60x60x39, gzip 180024 B intensities and 661 B labels; see its source record for exact output sizes/hashes. Data are demo-only CC BY-SA 4.0, separate from engine source. OpenNeuro RGBA uses the existing CC0 T1.


Batch 203 JPEG entries: decoders/jpeg is a new optional 3,774 B minified gzip entry (previously absent); exporters/jpeg-read remains 3,774 B through the shared implementation. Its size baseline adds 256 B headroom. Core plus stage is unchanged at 24,209 B. No new dependency, Wasm asset or CPU loop was added.

### Batch 240 job 2: object blocks

Optional voxel/objects provides VoxelObjects(engine,world). Its define(name,source,options?) snapshots a core Mesh or the root/meshes graph of a core glTF Model. Nodes copy local TRS, names and receiveShadow, while Geometry and PbrMaterial identities stay shared. Source meshes remain caller owned and can be disposed after definition. Object geometry is centred on x/z cell centres, with the cell floor at y=0; objectState(id,turns) supports 0..3 positive Y quarter turns. Storage defaults are solid=false, opacity=0 and light=0; optional solid=true uses existing whole-cell voxel collision, not arbitrary mesh collision. Material appearance belongs to source meshes.

Call update before render. World edits reconcile only touched chunks, retaining unchanged cell handles; chunk unload/disposal releases placements and subscriptions. at(x,y,z) exposes root-first handles, and stats counts chunks/cells/mesh nodes. Core performs instanced geometry batches and per-placement frustum culling, so objects crossing chunk bounds retain correct bounds. The packed voxel mesher does not draw object cube faces. Loaded-world and engine node capacity bound memory; each placement has a transform root plus its source graph nodes, so define refuses a source graph 64 or more meshes deep (the root adds one parent and core allows 63). A placement that throws part way through a chunk leaves the placements made before it owned by the chunk (dispose releases them) and the chunk pending, so the next update finishes it. Static core glTF materials are supported; animated/skinned PBRModel graphs belong to their existing packages and are not silently converted into core meshes. No new core or stage code, new Wasm kernel or wall-clock claim.
Batch 240 job 2 optional entry gzip: objects 0 to 1,678 B, ceiling 1,934 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. Existing geometry batching avoids a second instance-buffer implementation; no optional ceiling for an existing entry is raised.

### Voxel-net recording and replay (batch 242 job 2)
Optional /replay records the exact per-recipient outbound message stream using server.onSend, including welcome and spawn; attach before clients join. Default queued bytes 64 MiB, hard per-message bound 16 MiB. Overflow and I/O errors stop recording and reject flush/close. MVR1 carries protocol version 6, tick rate, recipient id, tick and raw payload; a complete-file footer is mandatory. readVoxelRecording has a default 256 MiB file limit, configurable; playback holds validated records in memory. Files include names, application messages and resume tokens and belong with private bug reports. Select one recipient and use a fresh VoxelNetClient/world with no-op send; advanceTo is forward-only, play defaults to speed 1 and a 1-hour hard bound with AbortSignal. Playback completion means packets delivered to receive; chunk decompression completes asynchronously through the normal client. Seeking backward requires a fresh client/world. This reconstructs server-visible states, not unsent predicted local inputs or deterministic server execution. No GPU work.

Voxel-net /replay entry: 0 -> 3584 B min+gzip, ceiling 3840 B. Server is 18031 B and rooms 19424 B, within existing ceilings. Core + stage unchanged at 24,209 B.
### Value clips (batch 206)
Optional usdz/clips exports valueClips({timeCode?,maxClips:10000,layers?}), valueClipFrames(), ValueClipPlayer and loadValueClips(). The resolver selects a stage pose (default startTimeCode or 0), preserving local/weak-layer strength, descendant namespaces, clip-set order, manifests/defaults/blocks, interpolation gaps, linear/held typed interpolation, quaternion slerp, retiming/holds/reversal/jumps, layer offsets and integer/fractional templates. composition() supplies synchronous layer/archive composition; composeUSDFiles/parseUSDFiles discover external clip files automatically. A manifest query reads the active clip and adjacent clips; absent manifests and interpolateMissingClipValues may require all clips, as in USD. maxClips bounds total candidate files across clip sets; existing maxBytes/maxDepth apply to every clip.
The frame iterator has inclusive start/end and a finite nonzero directional step (default 1). ValueClipPlayer.setTimeCode() is asynchronous and serial, retaining the old model until a new complete frame is ready, including changing topology. dispose aborts a pending request and releases the model. loadValueClips initializes timeCode 0 unless supplied. cacheBytes defaults to 64 MiB of encoded data retained across frames, not a cap on the files/decoded geometry required to resolve the current frame. The player currently recreates the model per pose; mesh-buffer reuse remains speed-phase work. Rendering works on both backends and through workers. No core/stage facade change.

### VFX moving space (batch 270 job 1)
Optional vfx/space supplies space.mode (world default, local follows the emitter), column-major rigid space.transform (identity default), inheritVelocity (0..1, default 0) and ratePerDistance (0..1,000,000, default 0). Position is the emission origin in that frame. State stays in world coordinates, preserving world gravity, collisions and render integrations. Scale and shear reject; skinned world-space births cannot combine with this emitter transform. Frame movement is a straight segment between samples, distance births are evenly spaced along it, and fractional distance births carry between frames. Capacity/dead slots limit births; reset and restoration forget previous movement and fractional distance. A 160-byte uniform is the only added GPU state, no extra dispatch or per-particle CPU operation. Space must be enabled at attach; numeric values and mode can change each step.

# Batch 185 job 2: volume and array storage

`@margoengine/shader/compute-volume` adds `storageVolume(width, height, depth, options)` and `ComputeVolume`. Default dimension is `3d`, format `rgba16float`, filter `linear`, wrap `clamp-to-edge`; pingPong and readWrite default false. `dimension: '2d-array'` uses integer z as the layer. `coord(i)` maps x-contiguous invocations; `uv(coord)` returns normalized voxel centres (for arrays sample with xy plus the original integer z). All 16 existing storage formats support typed load/store, a single mip and one sample. Integers and unfilterable float32 use load; readWrite requires an r32 format and the WGSL language feature. One image cannot be read and written in one pass without readWrite; pingPong reads the previous image and swaps after a writing dispatch. Device limits bound each axis and array layers; total voxels must fit u32. Data is tightly packed x, y, z and must match the exact byte count. Loss or disposal resets copies to CPU data, not computed state.

Size: new optional entry 0 -> 4,705 B min+gzip, ceiling 4,961 B. The bytes keep lifecycle, validation, typed nodes and image ownership together; splitting them would duplicate device state and validation. Existing compute-texture is 4,529 B. Core plus stage stays 24,209 B. Real WebGPU and full WebGL2 compatibility pass all 16 formats in both dimensions, every voxel and repeated ping-pong steps; filtered volume sampling passes too. No speed claim.

Optional /webrtc adapts two RTCDataChannels: reliable ordered with no retransmission limit, unreliable unordered maxRetransmits 0. The adapter's buffered counter remains zero as in the existing netcode connection bridge, so reliable queue monitoring belongs to the RTC provider. RTC carries no custom close code/reason. ### VFX lifetime dynamics (batch 270 job 2)
Optional vfx/over-life supplies overLife.spin (additional radians/second), speed (birth-velocity multiplier, with forces additive), size (birth-size multiplier, including growth), velocityLimit (absolute world speed). Each curve has 2..32 evenly spaced linear samples, read each step; spin is -1000..1000, speed/size 0..1000, limit 0..1,000,000. Limit accepts a constant too. Defaults: no added spin, speed/size 1, no speed limit. Each effect adds 16 bytes per slot for birth velocity/size and a 528-byte uniform, without extra dispatches. Growth updates simulation size, collisions, culling and every downstream particle draw. Spin is the curve's exact integral over the life lived, times the initial life, added where the angle is drawn (billboard and mesh vertex stages) in addition to stock angularVelocity; the stored birth angle stays fixed. Speed differences preserve force contributions and recover from zero. Local-space rotation also rotates stored birth velocity. Reset/restoration regenerate birth state, and removed channels use their defaults.

## Batch 203 standalone compression
Zstandard is an optional entry over the existing clean-room decoder: concatenated and skippable frames, checksums, a caller destination, default 256 MiB output and 128 MiB declared window. External Zstandard dictionaries remain unsupported with a coded error. LZ4 decodes standard and legacy concatenated frames, metadata, linked/independent blocks and raw blocks with an explicit decoded size. All descriptor/block/content checksums are verified. It accepts an external dictionary (last 65,536 bytes) and optional dictionaryId, rejects a missing required dictionary, caps total output at 256 MiB by default (configurable integer 0..2147483647), and yields after 8 MiB or 128 blocks for cancellation. Each call receives its complete compressed byte stream and returns all output bytes; no incremental transport API is claimed. Decoded blocks, frame assembly and final assembly may coexist, plus up to one 8 MiB legacy block and its dictionary; maxOutputSize bounds decoded bytes, not peak process memory. No timing claim.

FitViewCube extends the optional up-frame cube (default up 'y' here) and frames bounds on face, edge, corner, keyboard, Home, roll and projection requests. bounds is a six-number world AABB or a synchronous provider evaluated per request; undefined disables fitting. padding defaults 1.1 (>=1), aspect defaults to the selected view rectangle or canvas and may be a number/provider. fit(duration) retains direction and roll. ## Batch 173 job 3: sciviz/cinematic
`cinematicVolume(figure, volume, options)` wraps an existing composite VolumeLayer, shares its scalar and classifier textures, hides the base drawable and restores its previous visibility on disposal. No core or stage imports of cinematic lighting are added. Ordinary slices remain available. Gradient and preintegrated classifiers are accepted; preintegration is treated as local diagonal extinction for secondary paths, not a claim of exact nonlocal preintegrated transport. Source gradient surface shading is replaced by scattering lighting.
All three expensive modes default off. Ambient radius defaults to 8 smallest scene voxels, 8 directions (1..64) and 8 integration steps (1..256). Shadows default to 32 steps (1..2048), toward [0.4,0.6,1]. Ambient radiance defaults [0.3,0.3,0.3], directional irradiance [8.8,8.8,8.8], scattered by the Henyey-Greenstein phase normalised over the sphere in both the march and the path tracer (an isotropic scatterer returns light / (4 pi)). Path tracing defaults g=0 (-1<g<1), 8 bounces (1..32), albedo 0.9 ([0,1]), seed 1 (uint32), 4096 accumulated samples (1..16777216). Paths converge to the chosen finite-bounce, piecewise-constant integration model, not an unbounded-bounce exact solution. Local AO applies to the deterministic march; path tracing computes ambient visibility by physical path escape instead. Each segment uses the classifier's per-voxel alpha as extinction, scaled by density and the smallest scene voxel. Both ray direction and light distance use scene metric, preserving nonuniform volume transforms. The primary/each scattering march caps at 2048 segments and widens the step to cover the box; shadow/local integral resolutions are explicit quality controls.
Accumulation uses two RGBA32float images plus an RGBA32uint work image (48 bytes per viewport pixel), one integration pass then a display triangle. Counters are always available, so even the unlit wrapper pays those passes and writes compared with ordinary VolumeLayer. `cost({signal})` reads exact last-frame scalar fetches, shadow rays, ambient rays and collisions, with a 30-second mapping deadline. Camera matrix, transform, density, quality, clips, classifier/source replacement and resize reset accumulation. Call reset() after externally updating an existing GPU source texture. configure() validates atomically, snapshots inputs and resets. Sources rebuild through VolumeLayer after device replacement; lighting clears its own history. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are tested; native GL fallback is unsupported and fails before allocation.
Scene-depth termination is owned by batch 173 job 4; this entry currently has the same opaque-interior limitation as the ordinary volume path. Multiple translucent drawables sort as whole layers, not interleaved samples. The EMD-8117 demo contains 64^3 original density samples, reduced from 192^3 at stride 3, without intensity scaling. This is an educational view, not medical evidence.
