### Voxel-net native server hosts (batch 242 job 4)
Optional /server-runtimes provides serveVoxelBun and serveVoxelDeno, one owned native listener plus a normal VoxelServer, default loopback and free port. Factories reject unsupported runtimes with a coded error. Async disposal and AbortSignal close clients, worker threads and listener. Native socket APIs handle WebSocket framing; pending totals/per-address reservations, own-host origin defaults, authentication, 4096-byte input bounds, binary-only messages and all simulation/codec rules remain in voxel-net. Authentication receives method, URL, headers, rawHeaders and socket.remoteAddress through a Node IncomingMessage facade; it is not a readable native request-body stream. Bun cork/getBufferedAmount/ping/pong integrate with tick writes, slow clients and heartbeat counters; Deno uses WebSocket.bufferedAmount and ordinary message activity. Native buffers contribute to the server's existing queue bound. Deno idle native pongs are not observable by the adapter, so an idle client must keep calling update to send inputs or may be closed by clientTimeout even when reachable. Native TLS delegates to Bun or Deno; Deno requires PEM string key/cert rather than Buffer values. Runtime permissions and executable installation are application-owned. Local shared contract passed on Bun 1.4.4 and Deno 2.9.8 on Windows. No GPU or speed result. Deno answers WebSocket pings inside the runtime and shows no pong, so a Deno connection reports `livenessByRuntime`: Deno pings after floor(clientTimeout / 2000) idle seconds (at least 1) and closes a client that does not answer within as many again, and the server's byte-silence close does not apply to it (KB5545a, 2026-11-11). VoxelLobby room URLs: a used shard ticket, even past its reservation life, is let on again only while its seat's player is in the room (playing or parked), and only for a hello that resumes; a plain join on a used URL is refused with 1008 (KB5499a, 2026-11-11). `authenticate` now gets `resume: true` on such a hello.

Voxel-net /server-runtimes: 0 -> 19475 B min+gzip including its lazy server, ceiling 20060 B. Server 18050 B and rooms 19444 B remain within prior ceilings. Splitting a required factory would add setup without reducing loaded bytes. Core + stage unchanged at 24,209 B.

### VFX prewarm and schedules (batch 270 job 4)
vfx/schedule exports schedule; the root VFX includes it. schedule.prewarm is seconds before the first visible frame (0..3600, default 0); step is warmup seconds per step (0.001..1, default 1/60), with at most 10,000 warmup steps including the final partial step. Bursts contain time (0..1,000,000 seconds), count (whole 0..capacity), cycles (whole 1..16,384, default 1), interval (0..1,000,000 seconds, default 0) and probability (0..1, default 1). Up to 1024 definitions and 16,384 expanded cycles; seed is uint32, default 0. Configuration is captured at attach, not live edited. Each eligible cycle is decided independently by seed/index/cycle; event times are sorted, including simultaneous and time-zero bursts, and frame-end crossings emit once. Capacity/dead slots cap total births as usual. Reset/restoration restart both clock and decisions and repeat prewarm. Prewarm runs the full ordinary effect simulation with a separate command submission per step, preserving per-step uniforms; it adds no draw. No extra GPU buffers are allocated by the schedule itself.

### Batch 241 job 3: optional voxel format readers
voxel-edit/formats-extra exports parseKV6, parseCUB and async parseVMAX. The root and existing formats entry do not import this entry. KV6 reads sorted surface records, column/plane counts, optional SPal trailer and implicit solid interiors; lighting/normal bytes are not shading inputs. Its grid axes are (file X, reversed file Z, file Y), pivot (xpiv, zsize-zpiv, ypiv), position negative pivot. CUB retains file XYZ, reads X-fastest RGB and treats exact black as air, with no alpha/pivot metadata. True-colour input above 255 used colours uses the existing deterministic colour reduction and reports colorsReduced.
VMAX supports ZIP stored/deflate, a root or single nested scene.json, current v4+ snapshots and v0-3 dense legacy chunks, Morton slots in 32-cubed chunks, and coordinates 0..511. Each latest snapshot replaces the previous chunk, including an empty snapshot. A colour byte 0 is air; 1..255 samples palette texel 0..254. PNG palettes contain exactly 256 pixels; settings colors contain 1024 RGBA bytes. Material bytes are retained per cell and original settings/scene fields remain available. Groups retain parent links, hidden flags and local/world TRS. Apply each model's gridToWorld to local grid corners; position alone contains only its translated origin and cannot express rotation/scale. Empty objects retain a 1x1x1 air grid. Models crop to occupied bounds; authored work areas, camera settings and bounds remain metadata, not resampling operations. History, previews and external mesh conversion are not voxel geometry.
Default maxCells is 16,777,216, ceiling 67,108,864, across output models and visited voxel slots; default maxBytes is 256 MiB across extracted bytes plus expanded compressed plist bytes. Default archive maxEntries 10,000; at most 4,096 scene nodes and 64 hierarchy/property-list nesting levels. ZIP CRC/size and malformed plist reference/cycle checks reject damaged input. maxCells, maxBytes and AbortSignal are accepted; cancellation is checked at asynchronous archive boundaries and between objects/codec blocks. ZIP64, encryption and multi-disk archives reject through the existing ZIP API. decoders/lzfse defaults to 256 MiB output, validates block lengths, stream end and match distances, and supports all four LZFSE block kinds with v2 table reuse. Size measurements are recorded below after the fast build. No timing claim.

The optional entries contain the complete bounded readers; further splitting would add entry plumbing without saving any root bytes. Core plus stage stays 24,209 B. ## Batch 214 job 3: multi-goal IK
The optional @margoengine/kinematics-constraints/multi-goal entry accepts 1..256 joints and at most 256 combined goals and loop closures. Fixed, revolute and prismatic scalar joints compose into spherical and floating joints; rest/attachment quaternions use x,y,z,w and normalize nonzero inputs. Joint parents may be unordered but must form a forest; explicit attachment-frame closures join branches, trees or world anchors. World position and rotation-vector channel masks and nonnegative objective weights are supported. Hard scalar bounds apply to every returned pose, including failed solves. All active constraints must meet unweighted physical tolerances before resolved is true; conflicting weighted goals return a bounded best compromise with resolved false. Defaults: 128 iterations per seed, 4 deterministic seeds, 1e-5 metre/radian tolerances, 0.01 initial damping, 0.25 radian/metre maximum scalar step, +Z joint axes, identity rest/attachment transforms, unbounded scalars, initial value zero. Inputs and scalar bounds have magnitude at most 1e6; omitted bounds may be infinite. Weights are in 0..1e6, iterations in 1..4096, seeds in 1..64, damping in 1e-6..1e3. Point closures match position by default; orientation is opt-in. The dense local nonlinear solve is bounded and not a proof of global feasibility; iteration-limit and stalled are explicit. Returned failures are diagnostic poses, not certified closed chains. Rotation masks select world logarithm components, not Euler angles. No dynamic constraints, obstacle/path certificate, renderer, core or stage dependency is added. Use existing optional chain/swept entries for collision queries. No speed result is published.
For multi-goal IK, the numerical scalar envelope is -1e6..1e6 even when a bound is omitted, so every returned value remains valid as a warm start and for forward evaluation. It is enforced during every candidate and step.
Multi-goal entry size: 8,535 minified bytes, 3,375 gzip bytes (new entry, previously 0), ceiling 3,631 bytes. The optional bytes provide the complete coupled solver; splitting its math would complicate one isolated feature. Core plus stage remains 24,209 gzip bytes.

### Anisotropic painterly filter (batch 271 job 4)
`@margoengine/creative/paint-aniso` exports AnisotropicPainterly, an LDR PostStack effect. Defaults: radius 3 (integer 1..8), strength 1 (0..1), anisotropy 1 (0..1), sharpness 8 (1..8), enabled true. The RGB Sobel structure tensor receives separable 5-tap [1,4,6,4,1]/16 smoothing. Eight overlapping polynomial sectors follow its minor eigenvector; ellipse radii are r*(1+A) and r/(1+A), at most 2r and at least r/2. Weighted RGB variance combines means; centre alpha is preserved. The Gaussian radial weight has a Wendland C2 taper to zero at the ellipse boundary. This is a single-scale variant, not the papers' exact sampled weighting texture or a multiscale solver. All reads clamp to the current viewport. Two rgba32float intermediates cost 32 bytes per target pixel per retained view, capped at 512 MiB per view; inputs are display-space, without alpha-weighted filtering. Zero strength/disabled is an exact copy and omits both tensor passes. Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 are checked; the preview refuses. Per-view buffers/textures/groups are retained, resize replaces them, and device restoration recreates them. No speed, aesthetic or other-device claim.

Anisotropic paint entry: before 0 B, after 9827 B minified / 3746 B gzip, optional ceiling 4002 B; generated alias 67 B gzip. The tensor passes and sector filter stay together to share resources and lifecycle. Core plus stage remains 24209 B.

### Batch 240 job 3: per-block foliage sway and liquid waves

Optional voxel/wind exports defineWindBlock(blocks,name,blockOptions?,motionOptions?), VoxelWind(renderer,options?) and sampleVoxelWind. Define motion before putting a block into a world. Motion kinds are foliage or liquid; amplitude 0..0.5 blocks defaults to 0.12 / 0.04 respectively, speed and spatial angular frequency 0..100 default to 1.6 rad/s and 1.3 rad/block. Rooting defaults to true for crosses and false otherwise. Liquid motion requires the liquid shape; mismatched definitions reject before assigning an id. Supported shapes are cube, cross, liquid, slab and stair; model and object entries retain their own renderers. Existing unconfigured blocks retain their previous shaders and meshing.

Live direction is an XZ vector with finite components within +/-10000, default [1,0]. Length below 1 scales strength; above 1 is normalized; zero is exact rest. Optional explicit time is finite within +/-1e6 seconds, otherwise renderer time is used. The clock stays float64 on the CPU: the shader gets each distinct speed's phase (time times speed) reduced to 0..2 pi first, so motion keeps full float32 precision after any length of play (a raw float32 clock steps by 0.0625 s at 1e6 s). Other GPU values are float32. The CPU sample helper returns a block-space displacement and can flag a submerged liquid vertex as not a surface. Rooted foliage stays anchored at its cell floor. Liquid surface height is continuous in world XZ, including chunk borders; submerged vertices stay fixed. Unit-cell vertex sampling resolves the mesh, with high spatial frequencies subject to ordinary geometry sampling limits.

Motion metadata is worker-safe and makes animated faces remain unit quads. GpuVoxelMesher uses its existing detailed-shape CPU path for these chunks, including box models and object blocks; GPU-only cube merging is not claimed for them. The vertex adapter adds one 16-byte owned uniform buffer, recreated on device restore, and is used by beauty, translucent depth, shadows and surface capture. Bounds expand by the maximum amplitude. Wind disposal removes the adapter before destroying its buffer, retaining block metadata and fine tessellation. Shadow caches refresh while motion is attached. Native and WebGL2 compatibility rendering are covered; no new core or stage code and no speed number.

### VFX node particle systems (gap row: Node Particle system)
`vfx/node-system` holds a whole particle system, or systems that chain, as block-graph JSON (`format` margo-vfx-node-system, `version` 1). Limits: 512 blocks and 32 systems per graph, 16 MiB of JSON text by default, a `duration` of 0..1,000,000 s, and a `delay` of 0..1,000,000 s. A `random` block is drawn once per compile (deterministic from its seed and the compile seed); fed to a lifetime it stays a range so the GPU draws per particle. A system has at most one sub-emitter (`birth`, `death` or `collision` trigger, the `events` option's limit), and that child has no shape, update blocks or triggers. `start` and `end` triggers run on a CPU clock the caller drives with `update(dt)`; the system's own effect is made by the caller's `create`. Accepted difference from the rival: no editor UI, and no per-particle block evaluation on the GPU beyond what the existing options (`curves`, `overLife`, `nodes`, `events`, `schedule`) already do.

### Compute dense decompositions (batch 274)

The optional compute/decomp entry returns owned f32 arrays in the input context. It handles real finite matrices, arbitrary leading batches, broadcast solve RHS matrices (only 1-D RHS is a vector), strided/expression inputs, square/tall/wide/reduced/full and empty factors. Arithmetic is f64 in a lazily loaded per-call Rust SIMD Wasm instance on every backend, including native WebGPU and compatibility; GPU inputs incur a readback and results an upload. This is a correctness route, with no device-native decomposition or speed claim. Singular solve/inv, non-positive-definite Cholesky, nonsymmetric eigen/Cholesky input, nonfinite input, f32 output overflow and iteration exhaustion reject. det(singular)=0 and det(0x0)=1. SVD values descend; symmetric eigenvalues ascend. Real symmetric inputs must match across their diagonal exactly; complex/Hermitian arrays are outside compute's supported dtypes. Limits: each matrix dimension and RHS column count <=4096; 16,777,216 f64 workspace words by the checked algorithm bound, and that many f32 output elements per call; Jacobi maxSweeps 100 by default, 1..1000 configurable. Cancellation covers loading, readbacks and batch boundaries (event-loop yield each 16 matrices), not the middle of a synchronous matrix factorization. Concurrent calls own separate Wasm instances; no arena survives a call.
Batch 274 job 2 measured gzip sizes: compute/decomp 0 -> 3617 B (ceiling 3835 B); separate lazy decomp-kernel.wasm 64419 B raw / 25233 B gzip. Compute root remains 39118 B; combined core + stage remains 24209 B. Keeping the complete decomposition family in one optional entry shares validation/loading; splitting it would duplicate the Wasm ABI and factor conventions without reducing the runtime needed by a decomposition caller.
Batch 270 GPU registration correction changes test commands only; runtime entry sizes and the 24,209 B core-plus-stage figure are unchanged. The package gate now runs every parity case on each backend in addition to its existing checks.

## Batch 173 job 4: volume-quality and opaque scene termination
Optional `qualityVolume(figure, volume, options)` shares the source data, classifier, clips and transform, hides the ordinary drawable and restores its previous visibility on disposal. Defaults: emptySpaceSkipping=true; blockSize=8 cells (2..32); jitter=true; adaptive={tolerance:0.01,maxStep:4}, tolerance (0,1] in normalized scalar units and maxStep [1,16]; refinement=12 (4..24). isovalue defaults absent, selecting composite or MIP from the source; a supplied isovalue must be finite within the source range and selects the first detected crossing. Optional surface color is linear RGB [0,1], otherwise the classifier at the hit. Clipped samples do not create cap surfaces.
GPU block bounds contain a one-voxel interpolation halo. A 256x256 opacity-range table conservatively includes all gradient/front-back classification rows and interpolation support; classifier replacement rebuilds it. Source/device/block-size changes rebuild min/max blocks. Call invalidate() after updating an existing GPU texture in place. Max block-texture width/height is the device's 2D texture limit; increase blockSize if needed. Each block uses 16 bytes plus a 65536-byte opacity lookup and a 2048-byte rank texture. Original source storage is shared. CPU envelope preparation is bounded by the already uploaded classifier (at most 2048x2048) plus 32896 interval unions; field reduction runs on the GPU, and the expensive noise optimization is offline, not a browser CPU loop.
Adaptive integration widens steps in low-variation blocks and corrects opacity for actual segment length. It is a quality control, not a certified error bound for arbitrarily narrow transfer functions. Steps are bounded by block exits; base spacing is at least the ray interval/2048, with a 4096-iteration traversal cap. Bisection refines the first detected crossing; multiple crossings wholly between sampled endpoints may require higher source quality. Refined isosurface values use explicit float32 trilinear interpolation; general compositing uses hardware filtering. The input scalar texture is still normalized binary16, so source quantization is unchanged. MIP remains available; opacity-based skipping is disabled for it. Integration distances use the smallest scene voxel metric and sample centres map exactly to the first/last grid points.
Opaque scene depth now terminates ordinary, registered fusion, cinematic and quality paths, including cameras inside a volume. No core/stage change. One capture is shared per engine and existing post captures are borrowed; scientific opaque layers render before the snapshot and transparent integration. Depth capture presents at graph order 39; custom scientific renderer orders must remain before that. A single nearest reversed-Z depth is used per pixel (maximum covered MSAA sample), so volume coverage at opaque silhouettes is conservative, not independent per-sample integration. Whole transparent layers still sort by centre, not interleaved ray samples. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are covered; native GL fallback remains unsupported for these layers.
Cinematic history now stores per-pixel depth and count in two RG32float images. Changed opaque depth resets only affected pixels, even at the sample cap; unchanged saturated pixels perform no transport. Exact cost counters use RG32uint with mode-specific lossless packing. Total cinematic history/work image storage is now 56 bytes per viewport pixel (previous 48). Colour remains float32. cost() reports zero transport work for saturated pixels in a no-op frame; read it immediately after the frame to be measured, before an extra image capture render. ### Demand rendering (batch 195 job 1)
quality/demand renderOnDemand stops the continuous engine loop and schedules only dirty frames. Defaults: initial true, maxDelta 0.1 seconds, browser animation-frame scheduler, no sources/update/signal. invalidate(n=1) coalesces to the maximum outstanding count; animate() holds are independent and released idempotently; loaded(promise) wakes on success and preserves rejection. sources listen to start/change/end/load. Attached controls and plugins update in render; existing engine.onFrame app callbacks must be supplied as update instead. update returns true to continue animation. Unannounced scene mutation and autoRotate need explicit invalidate or an animation hold. Idle has no RAF or timer, and the app update callback first steps zero after idle; plugin rendering bootstraps with min(maxDelta, 1/60) seconds so damped controls consume queued motion. Abort, scene/plugin disposal and explicit disposal cancel pending work and listeners. Device restoration requests two settling frames. Temporal effects may request additional frames with invalidate(n). Does not restart the old continuous loop on dispose. Core/stage unchanged.

### Adaptive events (batch 195 job 3)
quality/events adaptiveEvents(handler, options) returns run(...args), regress, setMoving, flush, moving, pending and disposable lifecycle. Defaults: interval 100 ms during motion, debounce 120 ms after start/change/end, no sources or signal, performance.now and native timeout clock. Interval/debounce are nonnegative through 2147483647 ms; interval also accepts Infinity to suppress all motion picks. Control events reset the inactivity timer; setMoving(true) remains in force until false or a later regress timeout. At rest there is no intentional throttle. Queued calls retain only the latest arguments and resolve all coalesced callers with that invocation's result; active async calls finish first, so results cannot arrive out of order. Click/drag handlers stay direct. Rest immediately flushes queued input; a stationary pointer with no queued request is not polled or repicked. flush bypasses the interval without overlapping an active call. Handler rejection reaches every corresponding caller; disposal/abort rejects queued and active result promises, cancels timers and subscriptions, and ignores late completion without cancelling the caller-owned GPU task. No idle polling and no scene/core changes. Applications pass an AbortSignal for owner disposal. Native and compatibility picks tested.

Adaptive events entry size: new 0 to 967 B gzip, ceiling 1223 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. One optional entry keeps deadlines, latest-input promises and lifecycle ownership together.

## Batch 177: optional 2D contours

Entry size: 0 B before (absent), 3,802 B min+gzip after, 4,058 B initial ceiling. These bytes hold both interpolation models, exact triangulation predicates, bands, stitching and SVG export together; splitting would duplicate topology or force extra user orchestration. The core + stage root remains 24,209 B gzip. Work is bounded to 4,000,000 cell-level combinations per request; reduce either sampling or levels beyond this allocation bound.

`@margoengine/sciviz/contour2d` has no root/core/stage dependency. `contour2D` accepts strictly monotone rectilinear axes, x-fastest scalar samples, 2x2 through 1,000,000 points; `scatteredContour2D` accepts 3 through 10,000 distinct sites with a noncollinear hull. Coordinates and finite scalars have magnitude at most 1e100; NaN scalars mask incident cells. All 1 through 256 finite levels must strictly increase. Bands cover adjacent levels only; no under/over band is invented. Lines connect exact symbolic cell-edge identities; grid interpolation is bilinear with straight marching chords and the asymptotic decider, with the 0-2 diagonal for an exact saddle tie. Scattered interpolation is linear over the Delaunay convex hull; there is no extrapolation or inferred land mask. Cocircular ties follow input order. Exact dyadic predicates protect triangulation signs; exported intersections use float64 arithmetic.

Polygon rings use even-odd filling and include cell boundaries; they are exportable polygons, without a global polygon-union simplifier. SVG defaults to 800x500, 36 px padding, 1 px dark isolines, six blue-red band colours, labels on, title `Contour plot`. Labels are rotated at half the projected path length, omitted below 48 px, and use a white halo. Global collision avoidance is not claimed. Cancellation checks before snapshots and between bounded batches, with exact abort reasons. Inputs are snapshotted; results own their memory. CPU triangulation is quadratic in the worst case; no timing or Wasm acceleration claim. The demo is standalone SVG and does not mutate the existing Figure or core/stage. Known correctness defects found by this job: none open after the analytical regressions.


### Fresnel reflector floor (batch 188)

Optional environment/reflector-pbr adds PBRReflector, reflectorFresnel and reflectorBlurFraction. New entry 0 to 3,340 B min+gzip; shared reflector 11,355 B, refractor 11,312 B, cube-camera 5,756 B, prefiltered 3,693 B; core + stage stays 24,209 B. Reflection uses Schlick Fresnel (ior default 1.5, allowed 1..4, metalness default 0, allowed 0..1) mixed with baseColor (default #808080). Inherited color tints the reflection. baseColor is an artist-selected constant linear floor term, not direct-light shading. All options are live uniforms.

Inherited roughness (default 0) sets the maximum mip blur. Captured geometry at the plane stays sharp; its world normal distance / blurDistance (default 10 metres, a positive normal float32 from 2^-126 to 3.4028234663852886e38) scales the blur, saturating at the maximum. Empty depth takes maximum blur. Actual inverse oblique projection works for perspective and orthographic captures; there is no assumption of an ordinary depth projection. Up to eight existing box-filtered mips: this is mip blur, not a GGX convolution or screen-space ray tracer. Normal maps distort the lookup; Fresnel uses the geometric plane normal. The standard Reflector's visibility, passes, layer selection, transform convention, capture-only mode and lifecycle remain in effect. Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 compatibility are supported; the lightweight WebGL2 preview still refuses the capture.

### Mesh reflector (MeshReflector, MeshReflectorMaterial, 2026-11-16)

`MeshReflector` (environment/reflector-pbr) and `<MeshReflectorMaterial>` (react/materials) draw a planar reflection over a flat mesh's own surface. By method: the surface blends with one alpha, the mean of the three channel weights, so under a coloured F0 (a tinted metal) the mesh underneath keeps (1 - mean weight) of its colour while the reflection takes its per-channel weight; on a display (non-HDR) target the blend runs on display values. The weight clamps at 1, so a `mixStrength` above 1 / F0 turns into a mirror (drei users pass 40 to 80; here 1 / 0.04 = 25 already reaches a mirror at normal incidence). `blur` reads the capture's box-filtered mips (at most 8 levels) at the shorter axis' size and averages at most 16 taps along the longer axis, so a blur longer than 16 times its shorter side, or past 128 px per tap, is cut short. Depth is the reflected point's world distance from the plane times `depthScale`, not drei's depth-buffer value, so drei's threshold numbers do not carry over. `distortion` is a screen fraction per unit of the normal map (default 0.03), not drei's scale of a height map. The surface is biased 4 depth steps (slope 1) toward the eye to pass the depth test on the coplanar mesh: without it a 48 x 48 subdivided floor seen at a grazing angle out to 400 units showed the floor through 12,676 of 16,640 pixels (its triangles interpolate other depths than the surface's quad), with it 0, native and WebGL2 compatibility. The mesh's geometry must be flat in its local XY plane (within 1e-6 of its size); a box or curved geometry is reported and hides the reflection. Measured: tests/mesh-reflector-browser.js, worst 0.00048 against Schlick on rgba16float, 0 floor pixels left under mirror 1, native and WebGL2 compatibility. Sizes: react/materials 7,366 to 8,493 B gzip, environment/reflector-pbr 3,300 to 4,910 B; an app importing only MeshTransmissionMaterial from react/materials bundles none of MeshReflectorMaterial and keeps the native reflector off its initial chunks (tests/subpaths.test.js), so it does not need its own entry.

### Lightformer and Environment children (2026-11-16)

`Lightformer` (environment/lightformer) and `<Lightformer>` with `<Environment>` children (react/environment), drei's
studio lights. Accepted differences: a Lightformer is an unlit draw of its own (one uniform and one render pass per
form per view), not a mesh with an emissive material, so it does not cast shadows or appear in picking, and an
`<Environment>` capture draws only its children (the rest of the scene is excluded) over its `src` environment or
black. `ring` is open inside radius 0.25 (half the disc's radius). `frames` counts captures, not frames: a capture
waits for its background and every Lightformer inside, so `frames={1}` never misses one. The children are hidden in
the main view by setting `visible` on their meshes while the Environment is mounted; a child hidden before it mounted
stays out of every capture. With children and no `src`, the Environment adds no default sun (the scene keeps the
lighting it had). Measured: tests/lightformer-browser.js (exact `color x intensity` on rgba16float per form; captured
irradiance 1.84 toward a softbox against 0.07 away; refresh tracks intensity within 1%) and the lightformer modes of
react tests/reflections-browser.tsx, native and WebGL2 compatibility. Sizes: environment/lightformer new at 4,300 B
gzip; react/environment 5,763 to 7,105 B (the capture binding and `<Lightformer>`; splitting them into another entry
would break drei's `import { Environment, Lightformer }` path and repeat the Environment wiring). The capture binding loads with
`import()` once an `<Environment>` has children, so an app without children does not pay for it: react/environment's
whole-entry measure is 7,601 B gzip (every chunk joined), and a Vite build of `<Environment src>` alone loads 4,631 B
gzip up front (3,810 B entry and 821 B shared React code), against 6,762 B before (2026-11-16).

### Puff clouds (vfx/clouds, react/clouds Clouds and Cloud, 2026-11-16)

`Clouds` (`@margoengine/vfx/clouds`) and `<Clouds>` / `<Cloud>` (`@margoengine/react/clouds`) draw every puff of every cloud in one instanced draw of 4 vertices per puff, sorted far to near on the CPU each frame (equal depths keep the order added, so every run draws the same). `limit` (default 200) caps the puffs drawn; later puffs, and puffs past `range`, are counted in `stats.dropped`, not drawn. Culling tests each puff's bounding circle (its quad's half diagonal) against the side and near planes only. Lighting is per puff, not per pixel: the light reaching a puff is exp(-density x sum of Gaussian overlaps with the puffs nearer the light along `lightDirection`), within one cloud only (one cloud does not shade another), times the Rayleigh phase 3/4 (1 + cos^2) plus `ambient`; it is a fixed direction and colour, not the scene's lights, and the puffs cast no shadow on the scene. Differences from drei by design: the default seed is the cloud's number in its Clouds (React: a hash of the component's place in the tree), not a random value per render, so the same scene draws the same clouds; `material` takes Margo's shading (`'scatter'` or `'unlit'`), not a three.js material; `bounds` is the full size of the box the puff centres lie in; the default texture is generated (a soft, lumpy puff), not fetched; `speed` turns puffs at up to `speed` rad/s and breathes them by up to 1 / `growth` of their size. `softness` needs the scene depth (React adds `@margoengine/post/depth`, a depth pre-pass of the core meshes). Measured on the real GPU (packages/vfx/test/clouds-check.mjs, native and WebGL2 compatibility, 1x and 4x): three clouds of 21 puffs are one draw and one engine draw call; soft alpha within 4/255 of the contrast curve over a floor; near fade within 1/255 of smoothstep(0, fade, distance); the same deltas draw identical bytes. Sizes: vfx/clouds 8,006 B gzip (new), react/clouds 3,247 B (new); core plus stage unchanged. WebGPU or the full WebGL2 compatibility layer only: the small WebGL2 preview is refused at setup (`unsupported`), never attached to draw nothing (packages/vfx/test/clouds.test.js).

### Precipitation cover (batch 236 job 2)
Optional weather/cover is 1,539 B min+gzip, new from 0 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. PrecipitationCover takes an unattached WeatherFX and reuses its top-down depth map (graph order -3) for rain, core Puddles and Snow (order -0.5) and GLTFWeather (cover option). WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility. Bias defaults to 0.02 m (finite, 0 or more). The map is the WeatherFX square of side 2 x Weather radius centred on the camera, at WeatherFX resolution (default 50 m over 256 texels): surfaces outside it count as exposed, so set radius to reach the sheltered surfaces in view. A receiver is sheltered by the highest occluder of the four texels around it: every point under an occluder at least one texel wide stays dry, and up to one texel past an edge does too. A receiver facing up (normal y 0.5 or more) adds sqrt(2) texels times its slope to the bias, so a sloped shelter's own top is not sheltered by itself; a receiver steeper than 60 degrees keeps the plain bias, and an up-facing receiver less than that rise (at most 0.16 m at 30 degrees with the default 50 m over 256 texels) under a separate shelter counts as exposed. Receivers are tested at the shaded point; with multisampling an edge pixel is shaded at its centre, which can lie up to a pixel outside its surface, so a surface that ends exactly at a shelter edge can show a one pixel exposed fringe. Give shelters a small overhang. The capture splash and lens passes are not installed.

### Batch 186 job 2: shared shadow atlas
ShadowAtlas from /shadow-atlas replaces LocalShadows on one Clustered instance, retaining its maxLights (1..16, default 4), casters, PCF/PCSS, biases, receiveShadow and clipping. It allocates one depth32float array layer, resolution squared times four bytes, plus a 4096-byte uniform table of guarded rectangles. Default atlas 2048, minimum face 32, maximum face 1024, texelDensity 1. Dimensions are powers of two from 16 to 16384, minimum <= maximum <= atlas, limited further by the device. Point/hemisphere lights retain six faces, spots one; directional cascades and area faces share the image.
Point/spot face demand follows the conservative projected world-range box clipped to the viewport. A near-plane intersection requests full viewport demand; a wholly behind-camera bound requests minimum demand. Authored resolution caps demand. Directional/area faces use authored sizes or maximum face size. All tiles are square. Least-screen-important lights lose one resolution level at a time until all faces fit, retaining every face. If minimum demand cannot fit, RangeError asks for a larger atlas or lower minimum; lights are never silently dropped. At most 256 logical faces. Since batch 52 job 4 the atlas caches each face in its own tile (next section). No hysteresis claim.
Deterministic packing proof: sixteen six-face lights at 16 texels use 24,576 rasterized depth texels; four six-face lights requesting 64 texels use 61,440 after fitting a 256 atlas. Both retain every face. This is a work count, not a wall-clock speed result. Source tests cover non-overlap, input immutability, priority, camera-driven viewport changes and caching. Real GPU tests cover point, spot and combined rectangle/sphere filtering on native WebGPU and full WebGL2.
Min+gzip: shadows 11,791 -> 12,052 B (existing 12,145 B ceiling); new /shadow-atlas 0 -> 14,027 B, ceiling 14,448 B. The optional entry reuses the complete caster pipeline rather than duplicating render ownership. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

### Batch 52 job 4: cached shadow atlas faces
ShadowAtlas keeps a face's tile while its size class is unchanged: faces that change size or are new take free tiles from a buddy allocator, largest first; only when fragmentation leaves no room is every face placed afresh (and redrawn). A face re-renders only when its light changes (position, direction, range, cone, near/far, shadow size), its tile moves, or a caster whose old or new bounding sphere reaches the face's frustum moves, shows, hides, is added or is removed. A partial redraw keeps the atlas (load) and clears each redrawn tile alone with one depth-0 triangle under its viewport and scissor; a full redraw clears the atlas once. Casters without bounds (instanced or displaced), opacity-mapped and displaced casters (redrawn every frame), a source's shadowVersion, invalidate() and device restore still re-render every face they may reach or every face. Camera-fitted directional cascades follow the camera as before. Point/spot sizes have no hysteresis, so a camera moving across a power-of-two coverage boundary moves and redraws that light's tiles. LocalShadows (the texture array) keeps its whole-array redraw on a caster change. Work count (CPU test, two lights, seven faces): first frame 7 faces, a still frame 0, a box moved under the point light 1 (before this job 7), a hidden, shown, added or removed box under the spot 1, an added third light 1 with the other tiles in place.



## Batch 136: clean-room Draco encoder

The default exporters/draco entry loads one optional Rust/Wasm SIMD encoder on first compression, in a browser worker or in the Node process. The public compressDraco API, abort behavior, GLB preservation and caller-supplied Emscripten encoderPath remain compatible. Sequential and standard/valence EdgeBreaker preserve oriented triangles; independent attribute seams share exact values. Prediction and quantization are described in clean-room.md. A packet is at most 280 MiB (293,601,280 B; 256 MiB before 2026-11-11), the most whose measured peak Wasm memory fits 90% of the encoder's 4 GiB: positions only, the worst measured mix, peaks at 12.9 bytes per input byte (a 16,302,050-triangle grid of 293,505,456 B at 3,780,378,624 B), and a 9,999,392-triangle grid with float normals and UVs (280,126,152 B) at 9.1 (2,538,340,352 B); before, a 243 MB positions-only mesh passed the 256 MiB check and trapped at 4 GiB (KB0035, [draco-encoder-memory.test.js](../packages/exporters/tests/draco-encoder-memory.test.js)). A packet also holds at most 16,777,216 input points, 50,331,648 indices and 255 attributes; each attribute has one through four components. Floats must be finite. Normal quantization accepts 0 or 2 through 30 bits; a one-bit octahedron has no positive reconstruction range and is rejected. Other quantized floats accept 1 through 30 bits, or 0 for exact values. Fan splitting can increase output point count, which the result and GLB accessors report.

Initial replacement measurement: 181,081 -> 89,161 B min+gzip, with Wasm 156,788 B raw / 58,216 B gzip. The complete proof version below is 91,248 B min+gzip, with Wasm 160,900 B raw / 59,962 B gzip. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. The old prebuilt encoder files have now been removed from source and distribution. No end-to-end speed claim. The byte-output bridge uses eight Wasm boundary calls regardless of output length, rather than one GetValue call per output byte. This counts bridge calls only, not encoding arithmetic or wall-clock time. Quiet speed-phase timing is owed.

At default settings the development comparison preserves exact oriented corner identities and Margo/native-prebuilt decoded result equality on the real fixtures listed in clean-room.md. Box stream 119 vs 130 B; Fox 7,086 vs 7,566 B; the small refrigerator primitive's bounded seed choice gives 352 vs 358 B without changing decoded attributes. This is corpus evidence, not a universal compression-ratio guarantee for arbitrary inputs. The portable normal fixture's maximum Euclidean direction error is below the opaque old encoder at 2/3/8/10/16/24 bits, without weakening its bounds. More settings/corpus evidence belongs to the following proof job.
Batch 191 post/curvature is LDR view-dependent ridge/valley enhancement, not an object-space curvature measurement. Ridge/valley 0..100 (default 1), radius integer 1..16 px (2), gradient threshold 0..1 (0), relative linear-depth rejection >0..1 (0.02). Signed xyz normals come from owned SceneTargets or an any-size callback; supplied normalSpace is world (default) or view. Core meshes capture automatically; optional models use add(model). Empty normals, clear depth and rejected neighbours cannot add silhouette shading. Camera right/up convert world normal derivatives to view space, including rotated and orthographic cameras. The owned capture has the same rgba16float normal/depth footprint as Pixelate. Removing a supplied normal callback after attach switches Pixelate and Curvature to the owned capture from the next frame (it attaches in onPreUpdate, before the frame graph runs); changing the texture returned by a stable callback works. A callback set after the owned capture started leaves that capture attached until the effect is disposed (one extra capture pass).

## Scientific datasets (batch 176 job 1)
The optional @margoengine/sciviz/datasets entry normalizes structured curvilinear, rectilinear, mixed PolyData, unstructured, multiblock and partitioned inputs to an AnalysisGrid-compatible DataSet. Fields and geometry are owned snapshots; source cell IDs, sparse blocks, names and top-level block IDs are retained. Composite topology is concatenated without welding separate blocks. Flattened arrays are the intersection of block field names; heterogeneous fields remain available on the original blocks. Shared field widths must agree. Use each block when a field is not common. Empty blocks are null. Source dimensions live under dimensions, not the regular-image dims discriminator. Existing pipeline, contour, clip, calculator, probe and glyph entries consume the normalized type directly. Contours of line cells return points, and matching isolated vertices are retained; clipping supports these dimensions too. Constant line cells do not emit infinitely many contour points.

Defaults: maxPoints=1000000 (allowed 1..10000000), subdivisions=2 (1..64, rounded upward to a power of two). Source cells are bounded by maxPoints and output cells by 4*maxPoints; tessellated points are bounded by maxPoints. Lagrange curve/triangle/quad/tetrahedron/hexahedron/wedge orders 1..10 use equispaced nodes. A Lagrange hexahedron (VTK type 72) from a VTK XML file older than version 2.2, or with no version, has its edge 10 and 11 nodes swapped back to the numbering VTK 9.1 adopted (edge 10 runs corner 2 to 6, edge 11 corner 3 to 7); version 2.2 and later read as written, and a version that is not major.minor is refused. Quadratic curve, triangle, quad, tetrahedron, hexahedron, wedge and pyramid use the standard 3/6/8/10/20/15/13-node spaces. Explicit referenceNodes may permute the standard lattice. Higher-order cells are uniformly approximated with interpolated simplex vertices; callers raise subdivisions for finer approximation. This is deterministic h-refinement, not adaptive error-controlled refinement or an exact curved-cell filter. Matching generated nodes share original-ID interpolation keys across cells. Independent composite blocks remain independent, including ghost boundaries; ghost arrays are retained, not implicitly removed.

PolyData source order is vertices, lines, polygons, strips. Polygons must be simple and planar (relative planarity threshold 1e-10); concave polygons are ear clipped. Polyhedron face streams must be closed and consistently oriented with planar simple faces. Nonconvex cells use a face-plane arrangement, limited to 4096 regions per source cell, and signed solid-angle interior classification. Generated interpolation uses mean-value coordinates with boundary handling and affine checks. Arrangement point merging uses 128*Number.EPSILON times the source diagonal. Self-intersecting surfaces and degenerate cells are not supported input. Linearized filtering follows the existing filter entry's numerical domain and interpolation policy; source curved-cell interpolation is not re-evaluated after each filter.

Readers: .vtr, .vts, .vtu, .vtp, .vtm, .vtpd/.vtpc, with numeric VTK payloads decoded by @margoengine/loaders/vtk-xml. Raw-appended arrays use its bounded range reader; metadata sniffing and composite XML are bounded by maxBytes (default 64 MiB). Every retained array is decoded when creating the owned dataset. Composite references resolve against the input URL or baseURL, or an explicit files map; nesting is limited to 64 and cycles reject. Relative string inputs use baseURL, or document.baseURI in a browser. Files must fit the specified per-read and decoded-array limits. All numeric point/cell tuples are retained; scalar defaults to the first one-component point field. PLOT3D covers whole-grid 2D/3D, single/multiblock, formatted Fortran D/E exponents, stream binary and 4-byte-record-marker unformatted, both byte orders, 4/8-byte coordinates and optional iblank. Defaults: 3D, formatted, multiblock, no blanking; binary defaults little endian, float64, record markers. Options explicitly disambiguate variants. Iblank is retained as an array, not a rendering mask. Solution Q/function files, plane-record layouts and 8-byte record markers are not claimed. The NASA originals use the supported formatted whole-grid variant. No file is fetched or GPU device created on import, and cancellation preserves its exact reason. No core or stage change and no measured speed claim.

Dataset entry size: 35,806 minified bytes and 13,072 gzip bytes, previously 0, optional ceiling 13,423 bytes. The entry keeps topology normalization, interpolation, nonconvex scientific-cell decomposition and VTK/PLOT3D adaptation together; splitting would add cross-entry orchestration for the same bytes to users of this one feature. Core plus stage remains 24,209 gzip bytes.
### Batch 217 job 3: scroll and range playback

Optional cutscene/scroll exports RangePlayback and ScrollPlayback. Range defaults: entire timeline, iterationCount 1 (nonnegative fractions and Infinity supported), normal direction, speed 1. Directions are normal, reverse, alternate and alternateReverse. update(delta) runs the borrowed player's skip() for each crossed leg, preserving instant order; seek resets each repeated leg without firing its start instant. At most 1000 boundaries per update; larger deltas reject before mutation. play resolves true at completion, false on pause/stop, rejects on AbortSignal; pause resumes progress, completion restarts. Instants stay on the player, iteration/finish events on the controller. Controllers own advancement, so pause the base player and update the controller only.

Scroll defaults: window, physical y axis, start 0, end current maximum scroll offset, whole timeline range, scrub 0 seconds (immediate), automatic events/frames true. Pixel offsets and seconds are clamped to the supplied interval. A positive scrub is an exponential time constant; automatic smoothing settles to the target within 1e-7 seconds. automatic false uses update(delta) from the app's clock. refresh() re-reads content bounds; resize and scroll events refresh automatically. No-scroll sources hold the start. Physical horizontal offsets can use explicit signed start/end for RTL layouts. Abort/dispose cancels callbacks and keeps the borrowed player usable. No renderer or core additions, and no speed claim.

Batch 217 job 3 measured min+gzip: new scroll entry 0 to 2,048 B, ceiling 2,304 B. The optional entry combines clock ownership and cleanup for both timeline drivers; splitting those controllers would add entry and integration complexity. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

## Batch 177 job 2: statistical charts

Student-t critical values support positive fractional residual df through 100000, including LOESS df below one. Bracketing rejects critical values above 1e150 with a remedy to increase residual df; no fixed-range clipping or unconverged fraction is returned. The continued fraction has a 2048-iteration hard limit and checked relative convergence. The low-df regression includes independent SciPy values at df 0.2 and 0.5.

Entry gzip sizes: `/stats` absent (0 B) to 6,719 B, initial ceiling 6,975 B; `/maths` 5,703 B to 8,854 B, ceiling raised from 5,959 B to 9,120 B. Sharing the math functions between direct transforms and chart marks avoids independent implementations; splitting the public CPU utility entry would add import orchestration and break the requested `/maths` access. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

`/stats` creates owned CPU marks and standalone vector SVG with axes, ticks, titles and labels; it introduces no Figure/core/stage API or GPU pass. Error bars support x/y symmetric or asymmetric amounts, caps and points. Box plots use interpolated quartiles, median, Tukey adjacent-value whiskers and outliers; violins use 96 Gaussian KDE queries over data range plus three bandwidths, maximum half-width 0.4 per category. Area and pre/post/mid step lines preserve missing-data breaks. Signed area/bar stacks keep separate positive/negative bases, with optional independent unit normalization. ECDF is right-continuous, two-sample Q-Q interpolates common midpoint probabilities, 2D density is a diagonal Gaussian KDE, and hexagons expose exact input membership. All mathematics is also exported from `/maths`.

Defaults: SVG 800x480, padding 58 px (minimum 24), white background, empty title/x/y labels, six categorical colours, automatic linear axes with nice ticks; point radius 2.5 px, line width 1.4 px. Box width 0.6; whisker multiplier 1.5; area baseline 0; stack kind area, normalization off, bar width 0.8 of smallest positive x gap; step mode post; density queries 32x32 (2..256); hex radius supplied in data units. Silverman bandwidth uses sample SD and IQR/1.34; constant observations use 1% of max(1,abs(value)) before the Silverman factor. Optional bandwidths must be positive. Violins independently normalize maximum width, not sample count. Named box/violin groups label the categorical x axis. Stack series use category colours in input order.

Linear and LOESS confidence defaults to 0.95, accepted range (0,0.999]. OLS needs three paired finite samples and nonconstant x. LOESS local degree is one, span 0.5, two robustness iterations (integer 0..10), at least three neighbours and three finite pairs. Tricube weights exclude the furthest selected neighbour. Queries default to sorted observed x; optional `at` permits explicit positions. Local zero-weight or nonpositive residual-df cases reject with a suggested remedy. LOESS intervals condition on final robust weights and are approximate pointwise mean bands, not simultaneous, prediction or extrapolation guarantees. Missing xy pairs are removed from statistical fits; area/step drawings retain gaps, stack NaN contributes zero. Errors must be nonnegative magnitudes; signed NASA lower errors are converted to magnitude only when drawing their bars.

Inputs are finite with magnitude at most 1e100, with NaN denoting missing. At most 100000 observations per series, 100000 Q-Q queries, 1000000 stack cells, 4000000 sample/query or LOESS fit/sample pairs, and 200000 SVG marks. This bounds allocations/work; reduce the dataset or query resolution beyond it. Maths is synchronous and owns results; import has no DOM, network or global side effects. Argument failures are linked RangeErrors carrying code `out-of-range`. No speed gain, exact confidence coverage, journal layout or new interactive Figure claim. The 13-chart real-data demo includes downloads and a 390 px layout.
Batch 175 optional entry min+gzip: sciviz/omezarr 0 -> 20,866 B, recorded ceiling 21,492 B. These bytes include the shared Zarr region reader, store validation, scalar adapters and codec pipelines. Keeping them together preserves one reader and source contract; splitting the entry solely for a smaller recorded size would duplicate validation or require additional imports for a cloud source. Core and stage source are unchanged.

### Compute Rust SIMD CPU backend (batch 274 job 3)

createCpuWasm from compute/cpu-wasm returns the existing CPU API, with f32/i32/u32 values and all existing built-in CPU operations. Custom WGSL remains unsupported. Every context loads an isolated SIMD-required Wasm instance on demand; creation accepts AbortSignal and normalizes load/compile failures to a coded MargoError. Numerical calls are synchronous and cannot be interrupted mid-dispatch. No GPU or worker is required. Arrays remain normal owned host buffers, so memory growth never invalidates an array or a returned readback. The transient packet limit is 8,388,608 f64 words (including descriptors and parameters); larger work rejects with RangeError and can use smaller stream chunks. The module has a 512 MiB memory ceiling. Transcendental operations use host Math imports; exact A/B equivalence is against the JavaScript CPU backend on the same host. Expression intermediates cross the bulk bridge; there is no wall-clock speed claim. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B gzip. Final entry and Wasm sizes are recorded with the job's size gate.

Batch 274 job 3 measured sizes: compute/cpu-wasm 0 to 40,235 B gzip (ceiling 41,443 B); separate lazy cpu-kernel.wasm 62,493 B raw / 21,800 B gzip. Compute root 39,118 to 39,851 B stays under its existing 40,233 B ceiling; shared CPU dispatch hooks do not load the new Wasm entry. Core plus stage is unchanged at 24,209 B. Keeping the complete API on the shared context preserves validation, ownership and optional-kernel routing; splitting would duplicate that facade.

### Batch 195 job 2: resource quality knobs

`@margoengine/quality/knobs` exports `textureResolutionKnob`, `particleKnob`, `renderTargetKnob` and `msaaKnob`. Live ladders default to scales [1, 0.5, 0.25], weight 2, with custom names/scales/weights. A `FeatureScaler` or `watchFeatures` accepts the first three. Texture and target knobs require a device, original texture and synchronous `bind(texture)` callback; level zero and disposal restore the caller-owned original. Reduced allocations are released after rebinding. Recreate knobs and caller-owned resources after device loss.

Texture resolution accepts a retained matching ImageBitmap/canvas and RGBA8 (linear or sRGB) single-layer 2D texture with COPY_DST and RENDER_ATTACHMENT usage. It prefilters with the browser's high-quality canvas resampler into one-mip textures; sampler filtering is caller-owned. The original remains allocated for exact restoration, so no total-memory reduction is claimed. Target sizes allocate genuinely smaller single-sampled colour textures with the original format and usage. Their contents are redrawn. `bind` updates the view and any dependent resources together; omit caller depth to let the engine manage matching depth. Custom history/depth remains the consumer's responsibility.

Particle levels multiply live VFX rate, followed by a final zero-birth level. Existing particles finish normally; capacity, explicit bursts and simulation work remain unchanged. Level zero restores the original option, including its absence.

Accepted limit: live MSAA change needs an engine re-create. `msaaKnob.apply(0|1)` records 4|1 samples only. It intentionally is not a live FeatureKnob, so the scaler cannot attribute savings to a change that did not happen. Dispose existing engines, call `prepare()` and then public `Engine.create`, rebuilding scenes/plugins. `prepare` applies the existing page-wide quality tier and returns effective samples; phones and exactSize remain single-sampled. Keep that tier stable while engines live, including device restore. No renderer internals or core/stage changes.

Entry size: quality/knobs 0 to 2,181 B min+gzip, initial ceiling 2,437 B; generated umbrella alias 60 B. Resource allocation/restoration and deferred selection share one cohesive optional API; a split would complicate lifetime management without improving quality. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. No speed claim.

Import environment/exr-codecs explicitly for asynchronous decodeEXR and loadEXR. PXR24, B44, B44A, DWAA, DWAB and full-resolution tiled files decode to linear float RGBA via a standard prebuilt OpenEXR 3.5.2 Wasm decoder in a disposable worker, in browsers and Node. The root parseEXR loader is unchanged and still has its documented smaller codec set. Codec precision is the file's: lossy formats are not made lossless. Inclusive data/display windows and selected channel names are returned; tiled mip/ripmap files select level (0,0). ### Batch 201 job 3: glTF audio emitter entry
`@margoengine/gltf/audio` exports applyGLTFAudio and its controller/options/emitter types. The caller supplies an AudioListener; no context is created on import or by glTF metadata loading. KHR_audio_emitter and MSFT_audio_emitter remain draft formats. Audio-only glTF scenes are accepted when nodes/scenes reference audio metadata. Selection uses options.scene, else doc.scene or 0, and only that scene's reachable nodes/global emitters. KHR sources retain independent gain, loop and autoPlay; emitter gain multiplies source gain. Defaults are gain 1, no loop/autoPlay, inverse distance, refDistance 1, unlimited maximum distance (the largest Web Audio finite float), rolloff 1, omnidirectional shape, full cones 2*pi, outer gain 0 and -Z forward. MSFT defaults are exponential distance, refDistance 1, maxDistance 256, rolloff 1, gain 1, no looping or auto play, +Z forward; explicit cone half angles convert to full Web Audio degrees, absent cones remain omnidirectional. Scene emitters must be global. The inherited audio package panning default is HRTF and its live source panningModel setter remains available.
Embedded bufferViews, data URIs and safe relative/external URIs share each decoded clip within an attachment. maxDownloadBytes defaults to 64 MiB, decoded PCM has four times that budget, maxSources defaults to 256; raise the named option for larger content. Data MIME types are audio/wav and audio/mpeg; embedded bufferViews require a MIME type. Cancellation is prompt even while native decodeAudioData finishes privately. No media streaming is implied. Playback remains subject to the browser's user-gesture policy.
MSFT weighted choices are made on new play triggers, with nonnegative finite weights, at least one positive weight, and options.random in [0,1). options.autoplay true explicitly triggers either dialect; false disables authored autoPlay. sync(time,playing,animation) follows MSFT events and compensates missed frames, pause/resume offsets, stop, backward seek and paused scrubbing; repeated synchronization reuses the event's weighted choice. Call it with the animation clock each tick. Legacy EXT_property_animation is a separate optional extension; this reader consumes authored property values and the required event contract. Dispose releases this attachment's sounds, never the caller's listener/context, and model disposal invokes it. No core/stage change or speed claim.

### Batch 173 job 5: direct curvilinear and spherical volumes
Optional sciviz/curvilinear snapshots finite node geometry and scalars (NaN masks missing nodes). General structured cells use trilinear inverse mapping, a stackless spatial cell tree and 24 Newton iterations per candidate; singular or sign-changing corner/centre Jacobians reject. Caller must supply an injective, non-overlapping grid; the validation is not a proof of global injectivity. Spherical axes are strictly increasing, radii positive, latitude in [-pi/2,pi/2], longitude unwrapped across at most 2 pi with a duplicated endpoint for periodic fields. Node indices are x/longitude fastest. Scalar textures retain the root volume's binary16 precision; topology is float32. Masked interpolation support stays transparent, without filling holes.
ReferenceStep is the physical opacity distance (default smallest nonzero grid edge); quality controls samples per reference distance. At most 4096 segments cover each ray, widening the step when necessary. Discrete midpoint sampling can miss sub-step features; quality/refStep control that error. Gradient classifiers use physical finite differences; preintegrated classification shares step/density conventions. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported; the native GL-only sciviz driver is not. The node, cell-tree and axis textures each need at most maxTextureDimension2D rows of maxTextureDimension2D texels (the cell tree takes two texels per tree node, about four per cell, so a 4096 compatibility device holds about four million cells); a larger grid is refused before its source layer or any GPU resource is created.
Coordinate slices accept fractional indices and tessellate the original coordinate surfaces; spherical slices have node-spaced polygon silhouettes. Outline stride defaults to 8, retains all boundary curves and uses one-pixel lines. Owned source stays hidden, with classifier/density/mode/clip controls on layer.source; dispose the mapped layer to remove its source and all sections. Geometry and missingness are immutable; create a new layer to replace data.
NOAA demos use public-domain modified subsets: NEXRAD straight measured rays (no refraction or earth-curvature correction), WOA23 five-degree stride/11 original depth levels, depth exaggerated 231.67x. Attribution, processing and SHA256 records sit beside the binary subsets. No timing or speed claim.

### View-driven geography (batch 180 job 1)
New optional sciviz/geo-lod, no core or stage edits. Defaults: projection mercator, maxZoom 15 (range 0..24), tileBudget 64 selected leaves, tilePixels 256 physical pixels, cacheTiles 128 resident tiles, concurrency 6 tile jobs (imagery and elevation fetch concurrently per tile), fadeSeconds 0.3, segments 32 (1..256), skirt 1000 metres. Cache must exceed the selected budget to retain a root fallback. Coarse fallback plus fading children may draw at most twice the leaf budget; residency is capped independently by cacheTiles. CPU pixels and meshes are retained for device restore. Missing imagery (404 or undefined) keeps a cached ancestor; other errors reject ready and remain in error without retry. Frame-driven loading needs continuing rendering or explicit updateView; ready waits current requests only, with an optional signal. Disposing aborts requests and drops resources. Tiles whose texels are all opaque draw without blending once fully faded in (KB-GEO1: a blend that changed nothing still made frames differ by one level at a few pixels on the RTX A6000, D3D12); fading and translucent tiles blend, so frames during a fade, or of translucent imagery, are not promised bit-stable on every GPU.
Flat Mercator/equirectangular and WGS84 globe use XYZ Mercator source bounds, ending at +/-85.05112878 degrees latitude (polar caps are outside this raster source). View selection uses conservative projected bounding boxes, not terrain occlusion. Heights and skirts are metres; elevation is a pixel-centred bilinear grid. No vertical datum conversion is inferred. geoTerrainStreamSource wraps longitude and clips latitude at a fixed level, resampling to TerrainStream.tileTexels (2..1024); the caller supplies TerrainStream's physical tileSize, origin and colours. quantizedGeoElevation calls tiles/terrain's decoder lazily, rasterises pixel centres, rejects incomplete coverage and does not infer a geographic tiling scheme. Native WebGL2 preview is refused by requireGPU; WebGL2 compatibility uses the same draw path. No wall-clock speed claim.

Importing it performs no installation or Wasm load. The full tier requires highp fragment
precision and EXT_color_buffer_float; unsupported hardware rejects with coded unsupported.

triangles. They retain their source and rebuild on device restoration; caller-owned lost GPU
sources retain the existing hide-and-recreate contract. Installation is page-wide; dispose
figures before the app uninstalls it. Concurrent native WebGPU and compatibility contexts in
one page are not provided by this factory.

in any RGB channel and mean maximum-channel error <=1/255, including edges/background.

replacement preserves the isosurface bytes exactly. These fixtures do not prove every
possible dataset or every GPU matches exactly. Demos head, stars and wind accept

## Batch 177 job 3: specialised charts

The optional sciviz/charts-extra entry is 7292 B gzip (new entry, previous 0 B, ceiling 7548 B); core + stage remains 24,209 B. It provides polar/wind rose, ternary, candlestick/OHLC, pie/donut, sunburst/squarified treemap, Sugiyama Sankey/alluvial, radar and UTC calendar heatmaps. All paths, own axes/scales, labels and data titles export as vector SVG with no raster fallback. Layout coordinates are 1000x600, export width/height are positive and default to those values. Hierarchies: 10,000 nodes, 64 levels, nonnegative leaves, internal sums. Flow graphs: DAG, 10,000 nodes, 50,000 input/expanded vertices, 129 layers; one global width scale, default 12-unit padding/16-unit nodes/8 sweeps. Cyclic graphs reject; flow imbalance is shown as a source/sink, never silently rescaled. Long links use dummy vertices. Alluvial categories are stage-specific and adjacent transitions aggregate; individual records are not separately colored through shared categories. Calendar years 100..9998, UTC, Monday start by default, missing days empty. Wind speeds below 0.5 are calm; calm remains in percentage denominators; 16 sectors and [0,2,5,10,Infinity] speed breaks default. Radar domains are per spoke; polar radius is linear or positive logarithmic. Standalone layouts do not add DOM interactions or modify Figure. Inputs are scanned by loops, so a polar line or financial series takes millions of points (bounded by memory, not the call stack). Date axes take Unix milliseconds within +/-8.64e15, the Date range. Polar, radar and calendar scale labels carry the significant digits their step needs (3, 2 and 3 at least) in plain decimals. Text is escaped by the shared XML 1.0 writer (forbidden characters become U+FFFD).

### Compute NN extras (batch 274 job 4)

compute/nn-extra adds BatchNorm, GroupNorm, ConvTranspose2d, LSTM, GRU, upsample and Upsample. All support Tensor gradients and the existing JavaScript CPU, Rust SIMD CPU, WebGPU and compatibility routes. Data and parameters use the context's float32 primitives. Norm eps defaults 1e-5 and affine defaults true. BatchNorm accepts rank >=2 and a channel axis (default 1); training needs >1 value per channel. Running mean starts at zero, variance at one; momentum is the new-batch contribution (default 0.1, null cumulative); trackRunningStats defaults true. Inference uses saved buffers. GroupNorm takes NCHW-style [batch,channels,...spatial], channels divisible by groups, and the same statistics in train/eval. Module stateDict/loadStateDict include nested module state; BatchNorm stores running mean, running variance and batch count in addition to learned parameters. Batch count persistence uses f32, so integer counts above 16777216 lose unit resolution.

ConvTranspose2d input is [N,C,H,W], weight [inChannels,outChannels/groups,kh,kw]; stride/dilation default 1, padding/outputPadding 0, groups 1, bias true. Output padding must be below stride or dilation. withOutputSize selects dimensions in the stride-derived output range. Output geometry is (input-1)*stride-2*padding+dilation*(kernel-1)+1+outputPadding. Metadata uses O(outputH*outputW*inChannels/groups*kernelH*kernelW) indices/masks per group and a batch-offset table; backward scatter sums overlapping float contributions in the backend's order. Use smaller batches/images to respect device buffer limits; no tiling is claimed.

Recurrent input/output is [time,batch,features] by default (batchFirst false). numLayers 1, bidirectional false, bias true, dropout 0. Dropout applies between stacked layers while training. LSTM uses i,f,g,o gates; GRU uses r,z,n, with reset applied after recurrent candidate projection. run returns sequence, final h and LSTM c, with state shape [layers*directions,batch,hidden]. Optional lengths mask padded output and retain previous state for each batch item. forward returns sequence only; run's returned tensors share a differentiation graph and must remain alive through their backward uses. States are explicit, never held between calls. Recurrent state/table storage grows with sequence length through the tape.

Upsampling takes [batch,channels,1..3 spatial axes]. Choose size or scaleFactor (default 2), nearest by default. Linear/bilinear/trilinear use half-pixel centers unless alignCorners true; bicubic is 2D with a=-0.75 and clamped edges. Nearest uses floor(outputCoordinate*inputSize/outputSize). Scale-derived sizes floor their products. Interpolation metadata is O(outputPixels*taps^rank), with 1/2/4 taps per spatial axis. It does not implement antialiased downsampling. Different data layouts compose the existing permute operation.

Measured sizes: compute/nn-extra 0 to 20860 B gzip, ceiling 21486 B; compute/nn 19137 to 18873 B; compute root remains 39851 B and core plus stage remains 24209 B. One optional entry shares tape/selection helpers; a split would duplicate them. No wall-clock speed claim.
### Depth, MSAA and mip targets (batch 271 job 1)
`@margoengine/creative/targets-depth` exports DepthTextureRenderTarget, a TextureRenderTarget (cube, array or 3D; rgba8unorm or rgba16float) with per-surface depth, 4x multisampling and mip generation. Defaults: depth true, depthFormat depth32float (also depth24plus, depth24plus-stencil8), samples 1 (1 or 4), per pass depthLoadOp clear and clearDepth 0 (reversed Z, as the engine). Each mip and layer or volume slice owns its own 2D depth texture (multisampled when samples is 4); depth is not resolved or mipmapped, since WebGPU has no depth resolve. At 4x, cube and array layers resolve straight into their layer; a volume slice resolves into a 2D scratch that is copied into the slice when the pass ends. generateMipmaps(encoder) fills mips 1 and up from mip 0 with an exact area-weighted box footprint, so odd sizes (5 to 2 to 1) weight edge texels by their covered fraction; volumes also filter across slices. Allocation, counting colour, retained depth, multisample colour and volume scratch, is capped at 256 MiB per target. restore(device) drops every attachment and pipeline; callers redraw. On the WebGL2 layer, volume slices drawn with depth go through the layer's 2D stand-in (two blits per such pass; operational playbook 3.2). Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 are checked; no speed claim.

Depth target entry: before 0 B, after 3398 B gzip, optional ceiling 3654 B. TextureRenderTarget gains one protected textureUsage() hook (COPY_DST for the volume resolve copy); the /targets entry stays within its ceiling. Core plus stage remains 24209 B.

The umbrella npm test command discovers tests/*.test.js, matching its current test directory and the repository coverage invariant. This manifest-only repair changes no runtime entry, API or size ceiling; other test extensions and nested directories are outside that existing invariant.




## Typed tables and cross-filter (batch 174 job 2)

`@margoengine/sciviz/table` is an independent optional entry, 13,003 B min+gzip from 0 B, ceiling 13,167 B (13,092 B before the per-segment GPU aggregation kernel; 12,906 B before the Parquet FLOAT16, JSON, ENUM and UUID reading; 12,694 B before the CSV int64, blank-line and nan/inf reading). `@margoengine/sciviz/series` shares the Parquet reader: 14,137 B (13,943 B before), ceiling 14,169 B. `@margoengine/decoders/snappy` is 1,250 B from 0 B, ceiling 1,506 B. The bytes buy scalar CSV/Arrow/Parquet readers, null/int64 preservation, indexed filters and deterministic aggregation; splitting the table API would complicate shared column and filter identity. Core + stage stays 24,209 B.

Tables borrow immutable equal-length typed columns. Dictionary strings use Uint32 indices; validity is a separate bitmap. Integer and time values retain signed/unsigned 64-bit storage. Wide decimal and opaque binary scalars are lossless dictionary strings (unscaled decimal with its scale, or hex). Parquet FLOAT16 columns read as numbers (little-endian binary16), JSON and ENUM columns (logical or converted type) as UTF-8 text, and UUID columns as 8-4-4-4-12 hex text with unit `uuid`, per the format's LogicalTypes.md. readCSV skips empty and whitespace-only lines and reads nan/NaN/-nan and case-insensitive inf/infinity cells as NaN/+-Infinity, as pandas read_csv does by default; other missing markers (NA, null) are text unless listed in `nullValues`. Readers accept flat scalar tables, not nested/repeated arrays, tensors, encrypted/external Parquet chunks, obsolete LZO/Hadoop LZ4 or Arrow view layouts. Flatten nested sources before reading. Arrow files and streams support dictionaries, replacement/delta dictionaries and LZ4-frame/Zstd buffer compression. Parquet supports flat row groups, v1/v2 pages, plain, dictionary, RLE, delta binary/length/prefix and byte-stream-split encodings, six modern codecs and page CRC. The readers default to 100,000,000 rows and 536,870,912 input/decoded-block bytes; overrides are explicit. Streaming/range reads belong to the separate large-series job.

Arrow Time and Duration columns without a unit read the schema default, milliseconds (Timestamp's default is seconds). A Parquet page with no values may be empty or carry only its encoding header (dictionary bit width, delta block header); both read as nulls. Aggregation bin i holds lo + i w <= v < lo + (i + 1) w with w = (hi - lo) / bins, the last bin also hi, decided against those edges rather than a rounded quotient; a finite range wider than the largest double is binned through halved bounds. With `gpu`, the host sorts each 256-row tile's finite values by bin (row order kept) and one invocation reduces each (tile, bin) run, so the kernel holds no per-bin arrays (WGSL caps a shader's function variables at 8,192 bytes; the earlier per-tile kernel kept 80 KB at 4,096 bins) and makes three stores, which the WebGL2 layer runs as GPU point draws at every bin count (the earlier kernel fell back to the CPU above 204 bins). A chunk's output stays at most 8 MiB (3 floats per segment). Range filters are [lower, upper); set filters use exact typed equality, including explicit null. Dimensions intersect; a cleared dimension passes nulls. Every dimension builds its own index once. Boundary/set changes touch only changed row spans/postings and changed bitmap words; first-time indexing and switching filter kinds are full-index operations. Duplicate row values are retained.

Aggregation supports up to 4,096 1D/2D bins per call, final upper edge included. Host classification uses numeric column values; supplied GPU context performs all count, valid-count, sum, minimum and maximum tile reductions. Mean uses the merged sum/valid count. Rows without a valid coordinate do not enter bins. Null/nonfinite values do not enter numeric statistics. Counts are exact Uint32. Numeric inputs round to f32, each tile adds in fixed source order, and host totals merge in float64; this is not exact-real or float64-input summation. A tile's sum error relative to its f32 inputs follows gamma(255) times its absolute input sum, before host rounding. Rescale values if f32 inputs/tile sums overflow. Empty numeric bins return NaN. CPU fallback follows the same tile order. No timing or rival-throughput claim is made.

The 10,000,000-row correctness proof repeats the 4,096 licensed TLC observations, selects 9,670,406 rows and compares every bin statistic with an independent exhaustive reference on WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility. The linked demo selects 2,211 observations below two miles and changes both rendered charts.
