## Engineering file readers (batch 176 job 2)
Six optional entries: sciviz/hdf5, /cgns, /xdmf, /exodus, /openfoam and /ensight. No new core or stage code. FileOptions maxBytes defaults to 64 MiB per read/metadata object/decoded selection; normalized geometry uses the existing DataSet maxPoints/subdivisions bounds. Integer values outside JavaScript's safe precision reject explicitly. Readers take AbortSignal; lazy HDF5 files support dispose and Symbol.dispose. In-memory companion files use exact resource names via files or resolve; remote files use baseURL or the source URL.
HDF5: superblocks 0..3 including user blocks, object headers 1/2 and continuations, legacy local-heap symbol tables, compact links and dense links in fractal heaps, v1/v2 B-trees, compact/contiguous/chunked arrays, single/implicit/fixed/extensible/v2-B-tree chunk indexes including allocated pages, missing chunks as fill values, fixed numeric/string and variable-string data, deflate and shuffle. HDF5 2.0 layout version 5 filtered chunk records are also accepted. Numeric hyperslabs read only intersecting chunks or contiguous rows; opening does not decode dataset payloads. Attribute name projection avoids decoding unrelated reference/compound attributes. Metadata signatures, ranges and index structure are checked; HDF5 metadata lookup3 checksums are not currently verified. Unsupported shared/huge heap messages, virtual/external datasets, arbitrary compound/array/vlen numeric datatypes, applied filters other than deflate/shuffle and nonstandard float encodings reject by name. Deflate verifies its Adler checksum.
CGNS/HDF5: structured Cartesian/cylindrical grids (one complete X/Y/Z or R/Theta/Z set of equal lengths; spherical or mixed sets reject), unstructured linear and common quadratic/complete order-two cells, mixed sections and NGON/NFACE polyhedra. Primary cells follow base cell dimension; boundary elements do not inflate solution tuple counts. FlowSolution selection defaults to the first solution; Vertex/CellCenter fields are retained. All matching bases/zones become independent blocks. ADF files require conversion through CGNS tools. Boundary condition subtrees, rind arrays, non-node/cell solutions, external CGNS links and uncommon higher-order element families remain outside this entry's current semantic projection.
Xdmf 2/3: XML/HDF/raw Binary data items; numeric endian/precision; strided HyperSlab and JOIN; basic XML path references; uniform/curvilinear/rectilinear/regular and mixed linear/quadratic/polyhedral grids; spatial composites and selected temporal collections. timeIndex defaults 0. Other Function expressions, subset grids, arbitrary XPath/XInclude and compressed Binary items require writer materialization. Structured Dimensions and origin/spacing are converted from slow-to-fast file order to x-fastest dataset order.
Exodus: classic/64-bit-offset NetCDF through the existing /netcdf reader and NetCDF-4/HDF5 storage through /hdf5; coordinates, finite-element blocks, selected nodal/element/global time results, entity maps and node/side sets. timeIndex defaults 0. Element connectivity is read in Exodus II node order (SAND92-2137 Figure 4, SEACAS hex27 figure) and renumbered for the dataset: HEX20, HEX27 and WEDGE15 list their mid-edge and face nodes differently from VTK; TET10, PYRAMID13, QUAD8/9, TRI6 and BAR3 already agree. WEDGE18 is refused, since no public Exodus description gives its mid-face node order; write such blocks as WEDGE15. Results defined on only some blocks remain on elementBlocks with their true block IDs; only fully defined results enter flattened cell arrays. CDF-5, grouped assemblies, arbitrary polyhedral Exodus blocks and edge/face result families are not projected.
OpenFOAM: polyMesh points/faces or faceCompactList/owner/neighbour/boundary; ascii and raw binary, label/scalar widths 32/64 and either byte order; volume/point scalar/vector/tensor internal fields, patch values and owner extrapolation where no patch value is written. Defaults mesh=constant/polyMesh, time=0, fields=[], boundaries=true. Named patches become independent polydata blocks. boundaryField entries resolve as OpenFOAM does: an exact patch name, then a patch group named in the boundary file's inGroups (the last such entry wins), then the last quoted regular expression matching the whole patch name (OpenFOAM User Guide, boundary conditions; OpenFOAM 2.2.0 release notes, patch groups). A `$name` value resolves to a top-level entry of the same field file. Calculated boundary values must be written by the solver; this reader does not execute boundary-condition code, and `#include` style directives are stepped over without reading the included file, so a patch whose value comes only from an include falls back to the owner cell value. Binary lists are skipped by their element width, so raw bytes are never read as text. The binary-safe index and entry precedence took the sciviz/openfoam entry from 10883 to 11272 B gzip; a split would only move the same parser into a second chunk every field read loads. Multi-region/decomposed cases can be resolved as separate calls.
EnSight Gold: ascii, C binary and Fortran record binary geometry; unstructured common linear/quadratic (quadratic elements in the EnSight element figure's numbering, which matches VTK's except the bar3, whose mid node is listed second), nsided/nfaced and structured/rectilinear/uniform blocks; scalar/vector/tensor node/element files; case wildcards and timeIndex selection. littleEndian defaults true. Full transient file-set scheduling, partial/undefined result records, material/species files, complex constants and uncommon structured flags are not interpreted. Original part and source-cell boundaries remain intact. These are file-format limits, not speed or universal-format claims.

Engineering entry gzip bytes (new entries, each before 0 B): sciviz/hdf5 8990 B; sciviz/cgns 18306 B; sciviz/xdmf 19254 B; sciviz/exodus 20029 B; sciviz/openfoam 10566 B; sciviz/ensight 11539 B. Combined core plus stage remains 24209 B. The optional entries retain complete reader ownership, numeric decoding and dataset normalization; splitting them solely for smaller individual numbers would add cross-entry orchestration without reducing an importer's total bytes.

## Review 2: VTK wedge surfaces (2026-11-10)

The shared legacy/XML VTK volume surface builder follows the published type-13 wedge point order. All five faces wind outward for positive cell orientation, matching the tetrahedron, voxel, hexahedron and pyramid conventions. Vertex coordinates, cell-to-triangle ownership, surface extraction policies and public API are unchanged. The independent wedge regression checks every triangle normal and signed volume, including a translated/scaled/sheared cell. No timing claim.

## Review 2: spatial rays without canvas layout (2026-11-10)

SpatialPicking.ray uses half of clientWidth/clientHeight when each is nonzero, otherwise half of backing width/height for that axis, matching Picking and core's existing query coordinate convention. It therefore supports headless, detached and worker canvases that report zero or absent CSS layout dimensions. Camera orientation, range, projection, proximity selection and public API are unchanged. Regression: packages/selection/test/spatial.test.js.

The optional exporters/optimize-extra pruning pass retains animation targets, their transform ancestors, skins reached from those nodes and the complete joint dependency closure before compacting indices. This also retains marked roots outside scene node lists. Regression inputs and outputs pass the Khronos glTF validator. ## Batch 175 job 2: figure point clouds

The optional sciviz/pointcloud entry accepts any OctreeSource, including COPC and Potree, and lazily opens COPC, Potree, LAS or LAZ URLs. LAS/LAZ downloads the entire file before building a memory octree; remote COPC uses its existing Range reads, and Potree retains its lazy hierarchy pages. The figure must be 3D with linear axes. Origin defaults to local zero for an explicit source; the URL opener uses the reader origin. Bounds and attribute picks are in world data units; decoding and rendering retain source float32 local-coordinate precision. A statewide EPT tile can span hundreds of kilometres, so centimetre precision is not promised at every point. Use smaller tiles for local precision.

The point budget must be an integer at least the root count; the default is max(2,000,000, root.count). Nodes are additive and admitted whole, so drawn count can be below the budget. maxLoadedPoints defaults to three times the budget and is an LRU target; visible nodes and in-flight node reads can exceed that target. Retained attribute bytes count actual typed-column byte lengths. Attribute colours use a global explicit range (default source z extent for elevation, [0,1] for other fields); scalar and vector-component maps, RGB preservation and live changes share the same map for future loads. Missing columns/components reject. Picks and rectangle/lasso selections cover resident visible nodes; they do not infer unloaded rows. Open SelectionStore universes enumerate explicit selected keys only; inactive rowIds is empty while has(key) follows the empty predicate. Keys survive eviction and reload; selection history remains caller-bounded.

The real demo archives only the root and first level of the 167,692,896,718-point Iowa EPT collection: 188,887 original points in nine LAZ files, 2,266,644 attribute bytes resident. Both backends draw 188,887 with budget 220,000 and 34,923 with budget 40,000; selection and recolouring read zero additional tiles. This proves view and work bounds for the archived levels, not full-density Iowa. A metadata-only billion-point CPU test allocates and loads two visible points and 20 attribute bytes. GPU elapsed-time and country-scale streaming performance remain for the deferred speed phase.

Batch 175 job 2 size record: points/octree 9,179 to 9,372 B gzip (ceiling 9,267 to 9,654 B); points/copc 15,177 to 15,309 B, within its existing ceiling. New sciviz/pointcloud is 21,055 B gzip with ceiling 21,685 B. sciviz/link is 4,662 B. Core + stage remains 24,209 B. The optional bytes preserve typed attribute columns, stable source rows and all reader adapters; splitting those APIs would add consumer wiring and fragment a single figure-layer contract. The points renderer is lazy, so the entry introduces no static heavy-package leak.

KB5588c size record (2026-11-11, min+gzip, before -> after): the native selection mask adds its packing class and WGSL to every points and lines entry that carries a PointCloud or Line: lines 20,314 -> 21,714 B, lines/edges 4,821 -> 5,716, lines/pick 5,957 -> 6,328, lines/trail 5,369 -> 6,267, lines/hidden 4,062 -> 4,963, lines/stroke 4,521 -> 5,424, lines/texture 6,699 -> 7,604, lines/debug 9,706 -> 10,582, points 25,180 -> 26,315, points/octree 9,599 -> 10,392, points/surfels 15,223 -> 16,254, points/pick 5,471 -> 5,768, points/clip 7,420 -> 8,221, sciviz/export-vector 3,957 -> 4,371 B; ceilings raised to match. points/octree crossed the 10,000 B heavy line, so sciviz/pointcloud now loads it with import() beside the points renderer (22,087 -> 22,097 B, no static leak), and `maskColor` is a shared function only the sciviz vector exporters carry (about 100 B off each entry above). Entry sizes: new sciviz/format 0 -> 7,306 B gzip, ceiling 7,562 B; new sciviz/categorical 0 -> 21,719 B, ceiling 22,371 B. sciviz root 56,161 B fits its existing 56,635 B ceiling; core + stage unchanged 24,209 B. polishFigure borrows a 2D Figure's line/scatter traces and retains double-precision originals, then normalizes its plot coordinates; attach it before rectangle/image traces. It supplies its own axis SVG; use ChartPolish.toSVG for the complete export. Broken intervals are finite, disjoint and strictly inside the domain; gap fraction .035 each, total below .8. Domains must increase. Y2 has an independent mapping and formatter. Inset controllers/figures remain caller owned; attaching a controller to itself, a cycle or multiple parents rejects. Minor subdivisions 0..100 (default 4). Number digits 0..15; locale en-US, date zone UTC by default; SI prefixes q (1e-30) to Q (1e30), e<power> beyond them; date mode prints a value a Date cannot hold as a number. Resize observes CSS canvas geometry; unchanged chart layout does not rewrite SVG chrome. Controller disposal removes UI/listeners; normalized native traces remain caller owned.

Band domains are nonempty and unique, inner padding .1 and outer .05; jitter width .8 of bandwidth and integer seed 1 by default. RGB/RGBA input is row-major, top-left origin, integer bytes, up to 1,048,576 pixels; alpha composites against the Figure background. One instanced rectangle per pixel uses existing native drawing and vector export. Hierarchical clustering uses finite Euclidean vectors, single/complete/average linkage, default size-weighted average, at most 256 rows and 256 columns; deterministic compatible leaf order, not optimal ordering. Dendrogram heatmap owns its overlay/layer and explicitly exports them together. GHCN demos reuse the frozen table and credits from job 2; no new source/data licence is needed.



API lifecycle repair (2026-11-10): AutoScene cleanup is asynchronous. Its Symbol.dispose returns the
same promise as dispose(), but plain using does not await that promise; use await using or await
dispose() when completion matters. LensDrops.attach lazily needs the optional @margoengine/post peer,
accepts cancellation during loading, and joins the scene's PostStack, or makes one (GAP-POST-ADD1-WEATHER); use
the existing constructor when composing several effects into an application-owned stack. No core or stage API is added.
### Batch 173 job 6: direct tetrahedral volumes
Optional sciviz/tetvolume accepts conforming, non-overlapping VTK type-10 grids with shared node IDs. Point scalars interpolate linearly in barycentric coordinates; cell scalars are constant. Geometry/scalars are immutable snapshots; NaN at any supported vertex masks that cell. Adjacency is indexed by the opposite local vertex; boundary is -1. Degenerate cells, repeated nodes, invalid offsets/indices, more than two owners of a face and same-side owners reject. Normalized determinant must exceed 1e-10 times the product of the three edge lengths. Global self-intersections and nonconforming duplicate geometric vertices remain caller constraints.
The float32 cell packet is 96 bytes/cell, with approximately 64 bytes/cell for a binary bounds tree, plus padded texture rows, a 272-byte uniform and the shared classifier source. CPU replay retains those packets and 16 bytes/cell of adjacency. Float-encoded topology caps at 8,388,607 cells; the GPU 2D texture capacity can impose a smaller limit. CPU construction is synchronous; throughput evidence is owed to the speed phase.
The ray uses adjacency when a neighbour has a positive-length interval, then a spatial entry query for boundaries or disconnected pieces. Convex cells are integrated front-to-back once, with at most cellCount+1 traversal iterations. Up to 2048 midpoint segments per cell cover its entire clipped interval; long cells widen the step rather than truncate the ray. Default referenceStep is the smallest physical edge, quality 1.5, association point; other defaults follow VolumeLayerOptions. Physical extinction uses a normalized metric to avoid squared-unit overflow/underflow. Scene depth and up to four source clip planes truncate the ray. MIP finds the exact maximum of each cell's linear field along its ray interval, then uses the classifier opacity.
Point and cell scalars are normalised to the classifier range without clamping, as the regular volume stores its voxels, so a cell whose node values cross the range interpolates the given values, and a colorScale map (under, over and NaN colours, log and binned steps) is read through the shared float-table lookup (tests/tetvolume-browser.mjs `beyond` and `encoded`). Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported; the native GL-only sciviz driver is not. Classifier, density, quality, mode, shading and clips live on the hidden owned layer.source; disposing the tetrahedral layer removes all its owned resources and source. Opaque classifier alpha stays exactly opaque even for a very large referenceStep. Gradient classification uses the constant physical cell gradient; preintegrated classifiers keep the existing segment/density contract. Finite sampling and float32 plane/interpolation precision remain accuracy limits.
The NASA demo uses 2146 original sampled scalar values, extruded as a span-invariant field on 6048 tetrahedra, with height exaggerated 12x. Its 65x3x65 reference is resampled from those same cells with CellLocator; physical opacity is matched nonlinearly at each density. Original zip, output hashes and transforms are recorded in tmr-tet.json. No timing claim.

Tetrahedral entry size: 6322 B min+gzip (ceiling 6578 B), previously absent; core + stage unchanged at 24209 B. Colour scales (2026-11-15): 6403 to 7030 B (ceiling 7286 B) for the shared float-table colour lookup.

## Multivariate linked plots (batch 174 job 3)

sciviz/parcoords is optional: 0 to 8,860 B min+gzip, ceiling 9,126 B. The sciviz root is 56,484 B, within its existing ceiling. Core and stage receive no source change. The full scatter matrix uses one GPU canvas. Plots accept 2 to 32 distinct typed scalar axes and at most 16,777,216 rows, also bounded by u32 instance arithmetic and the device storage-binding size. Columns normalise into f32 once. Physical axis values use JS numeric conversion; integer/time storage remains exact in the source table. Linear, log, fixed-domain and dictionary-category axes share the same column scale in every matrix cell. Missing/nonfinite/nonpositive-log/out-of-domain values interrupt their adjacent segments rather than inventing boundary observations.

Reorder and flip reuse column buffers; each writes 8 bytes per axis. Shared selection uses one f32 row mask. Inclusive axis brushes intersect, and matrix brushes operate in physical coordinates. Diagonal histograms show selected rows. Header/control panels support drag reorder, keyboard Left/Flip buttons and numeric range brushes; canvas gestures brush axes/cells. Density shades log(1+count), with exact Uint32 counts returned separately. Width defaults to 256, height to 128; width >= axis count, height >= 2, dimensions <= 8192 and <= 16,777,216 pixels. One vote per valid segment/row at each pixel column, with endpoint quantisation and integer interpolation, is the raster definition; it is not alpha density or the hardware line antialiasing rule. CPU/GPU parity is exact. Native WebGPU density uses atomics; WebGL2 compatibility density uses the CPU compute tier (245 bounded chunks at 2M rows), while line/matrix rendering uses the GPU. Native legacy WebGL2 Figure fallback is not this entry's GPU device: use WebGPU or webgl2-compat.

The proof repeats 80 real NASA observations to 2,000,000 physical rows, not 2M unique planets: 24MB of normalised columns, 4,000,003 line instances, 6,000,000 exact density votes and nine matrix cells. Timing comparisons remain owed in the speed phase. Brush-handle/history and in-plot label layout polish are tracked for the fix phase.

### Scientific figure state, version 1 (batch 179)
`@margoengine/sciviz/spec` is optional; core and stage have no new imports or features. Saves are asynchronous: serialize `await fig.toJSON()`, then restore with `Figure.fromJSON(spec, canvas)`. Default binary allocation budget is 256 MiB per save/load, including timeline snapshots; `maxBytes` raises it explicitly. Depth is at most 128 nested values. Numeric arrays preserve little-endian bytes, dtype, NaNs and infinities; inline and URL data carry SHA-256. Network sources must have their exact declared length. URL-backed arrays come from `loadSpecData`; inline is the default.
A pipeline's versioned graph and rendered layers are retained without executing unknown operators. Supply the registry to restore a runnable graph; otherwise `pipelineState` retains the dormant graph. Custom layers need an explicit codec. Native factories and mesh, glyph, graph, geo, flow, LIC, fusion, bricked and cinematic factories record creation/state on opted-in figures. Transfer callbacks become their renderer's 256-entry table; arbitrary application callbacks and unregistered live objects reject. Applications choose which code to trust; JSON cannot fetch modules.
Timeline export pauses playback, captures each frame and returns to the original index; callbacks become concrete frame states. It does not serialize application timers, event handlers, simulation code or in-flight tasks. Interactive 2D limits, selection indices, camera, drag mode, annotations and layer order are saved. Exact pixel reproduction requires the same dimensions, backend and hardware plus the engine's `exactSize` capture mode. Default MSAA blending is not a byte-stability guarantee, including for repeated draws of one unchanged scene.

### Automatic scatter LOD rings (batch 64 job 5)
scatterLODs(mesh, { ratios, signal }) from @margoengine/scatter/simplify returns { meshes, triangles, deviation }. Defaults: ratios [0.4, 0.12], two triangle fractions decreasing within (0, 1]. Ring 0 is the source object; ring 2 is simplified from ring 1. Input is a core Geometry (positions and normals only) with triangles, up to 200,000 vertices. Every ring vertex is a source vertex, so normals are never interpolated or recomputed; a ring keeps more than its ratio when no collapse is left that keeps seams and hard edges closed (a box keeps all 12 triangles). deviation is a one-sided bound (source vertices to ring surface), tested over every vertex and triangle pair, so it costs source vertices times ring triangles: fine for scatter meshes, slow for a 200,000-vertex one. A collapse may lower a blade's tip: Scatter's blades check refuses a ring whose top falls to the root. ringDistance(deviation, pixels = 1, height = 1080, fov = pi / 3) is the pinhole projection of that bound, ignoring wind bend and instance scale (multiply deviation by the largest scale yourself). Needs the optional peers @margoengine/lod and @margoengine/mesh-edit; no GPU work and no speed claim. Entry size is in scripts/quality/baselines/sizes.json; core plus stage unchanged.

### Water bodies (batch 67 job 1)
water/bodies WaterBodies takes 1 to 64 bodies: closed outlines (3 to 4096 points, even-odd inside, self-intersections not checked) at one level, or river paths (2 to 4096 [x, level, z] points, width 0.01 to 10000 per point) on a uniform Catmull-Rom spline at 16 steps per span. The body map is corner-sampled rgba32float, 16 to 2048 texels on the longer side (default 256), with two texels of margin; past the margin the map clamps, so distances there read at most the margin. The CPU rasterization is brute force over texels and segments with a bounding-box skip and refuses more than 4e8 texel-segment visits. Shorelines are smooth at the map resolution, but the Water grid's triangles still carry level changes between bodies across one grid cell. The Water grid stays origin-centred and is shaded and discarded outside the bodies, so a large grid around a small lake costs its full vertex work. Overlaps: the later body covers the earlier one; there are no holes. Water's wave velocity is scaled by the body's wave share in WaveQuery; coastal flow is not body-aware.

### Wave subsurface scattering (batch 67 job 2)
water/scatter WaterScatter adds a backlit glow to one Water from its two directional lights. color is linear RGB 0 to 1 (default [0.04, 0.32, 0.24]), strength 0 to 100 (default 1, 0 is off), power 0.5 to 64 (default 4), distortion 0 to 1 (default 0.3). ### Procedural grass blades (batch 64 job 6)
GrassScatter(options) from @margoengine/scatter/grass is a Scatter with no mesh input; options.grass is { height 0.6, heightVariance 0.4, width 0.04, blades 8, radius 0.15, lean 0.35, round 0.3, segments [5, 3, 1] } by default, in instance units (ScatterOptions.scale scales the clump). Ranges: height 0.0001 to 10000, width 0.00001 to 1000, radius 0 to 10000, heightVariance and lean 0 to 0.95, round 0 to 1, blades an integer 1 to 64, segments three non-increasing integers 1 to 16. A clump draws blades * (2 * segments - 1) triangles a ring. blades shading is on unless options.blades replaces it; its root-to-tip shade uses the tallest blade's height, so a shorter blade's tip shades slightly darker. The shape is compiled into the WGSL, so it is fixed for the scatter's life. Blade randomness hashes the instance's world root bits, so two instances at one exact spot draw the same clump. GrassScatter.attach(engine, options) takes no meshes. Colour passes (diffuse and PBR) are proved on WebGPU. The shadow pass is proved from the picture on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (`packages/scatter/test/grass-shadow.browser.mjs`, 2026-11-27, RTX A6000): under a sun 45 degrees up, one upright blade 2 m and 4 m tall casts 2.05 m and 4.00 m of shadow, 1.12 m wide 1 m out and 0.68 m wide 3 m out (ratio 0.607, the blade's own 0.577), and 16 blades a clump shade 1,610 pixels against 91 for one; a pass that skips the blade pose casts 4.95 m of one width and fails the test. No speed claim. Entry size is in scripts/quality/baselines/sizes.json; core plus stage unchanged.

### List 3 batch 66 job 8: steep-bed rivers

Rivers options: substeps integer 1..64 (default 8); maxFroude 0.1..20 (default 4); at most 16 sources, each a finite [x, z], discharge 0..100000 m^3/s and radius 0..10000 m (square footprint, cells whose centres lie inside it). One Rivers per Water; it needs a Water with a terrain coast. Pipe speed is capped at maxFroude * sqrt(g a) and at half a cell per substep, so a fall of any height stays bounded, but the reconstruction drives flow by the depth above the brink only: on beds steeper than the depth per cell a chute front runs slower than the slope's gravity component (about 2 m/s on a 0.5 slope in the float64 oracle). No bed friction term beyond the 0.12 /s flux decay. Water's own coast flow (no Rivers attached) is since 2026-11-18 a momentum-conservative staggered step with Manning friction n = 0.02 (KB-WATER-SWASH1, below in Water surf), its face speed capped at half a cell per step, so its falls stay bounded too (a 10 m fall stays under free fall from the top); use Rivers for falls and chutes with sources (2026-11-11).

### Rain ripples (batch 67 job 3)
water/rain WaterRain draws rain rings on one Water: rain 0 to 1 (or a weather's, read every frame from `rain` or a WeatherMachine's `state.rain`), cell 0.05 to 5 m (default 0.4), lifetime 0.1 to 10 s (default 0.8), strength 0 to 1 (default 0.35). At most one ring per cell in each of three grids at a time; a ring spreads to a quarter of its cell. Rings fade out where a pixel covers more than 0.2 of a cell. Rings shade only (normals); optional splashes put real drops into a Ripples field: rate 0 to 1000 per second at full rain (default 20), at most 32 a frame, inside a square of side area (default 16 m) around the camera, radius default 0.5 m and depth default 0.02 m. The splash radius must cover one cell of the field, or Ripples rejects the drop when the frame renders. One rain per Water. Optional entry, so the water root entry does not grow.

## Astronomy and microscopy import, batch 176 job 3
- Optional sciviz/fits reads primary/IMAGE HDUs, all FITS BITPIX types, BSCALE/BZERO/BLANK and BINTABLE L/X/B/I/J/K/A/E/D/C/M plus single P/Q variable descriptors. Physical integers stay exact for unscaled 64-bit values; rendering explicitly converts to floating point. Cells retain vector/complex arrays, nulls, dimensions and units. ASCII tables, random groups, compressed-image table conventions and multiple P/Q descriptors per cell reject explicitly.
- WCS retains primary or A..Z axes, units, CRPIX/CRVAL, CD or PC/CDELT and legacy CROTA, with zero-based pixel input. Linear axes, SIP forward polynomials and TAN/SIN/ARC/STG/ZEA sky projections have independent WCSLIB tests. Other projection/rotation/spectral algorithms are outside this entry's current world() projection support; original cards and linear metadata remain available. No all-projections claim.
- sciviz/mrc reads MRC/CCP4 little/big endian modes 0/1/2/3/4/6/12/101, complex selection, labels and opaque extended headers, MAPC/MAPR/MAPS, starts, origin and triclinic unit-cell geometry. Storage order is never silently flipped; file handedness cannot be inferred from this standard. Vendor extended headers and crystallographic symmetry operators are retained as bytes rather than interpreted. ORIGIN and NXSTART/NYSTART/NZSTART both place the first sample (Cheng et al. 2015, section 4.6, same sign convention), so world() applies one, never both: a nonzero real-mode ORIGIN in angstroms, else the starts in grid steps; complex modes keep ORIGIN as a phase origin in pixels, not a position, and Fourier phase origins remain metadata, not an inverse FFT. Files carrying the IMOD stamp (word 39) follow its flags (word 40): flag 1 clear reads mode 0 as unsigned bytes (IMOD before 4.9), flag 4 clear negates ORIGIN (IMOD before 4.11). Mode 101 puts the lower-coordinate pixel in the low nibble, as the IMOD format page states for both byte orders. Remaining ambiguity: a mode 0 file written unsigned without the IMOD stamp (IMOD before 4.3, other old writers) cannot be told from a signed one and reads as signed, the MRC2014 consensus; when ORIGIN and the starts are both nonzero and disagree, ORIGIN wins; MRC2014 (Cheng et al. 2015, section 4.6) calls ORIGIN the outside corner of the first pixel, yet world() places sample index 0 at ORIGIN with no half-sample shift: the same section gives ORIGIN the sign convention of the integer START fields, whose index n is grid point n, and a file with ORIGIN 0 cannot be told from a crystallographic grid read through START, so a corner shift applied only to nonzero ORIGIN would move a crop half a sample against its parent; the CCP-EM page's subvolume example (ORIGIN 100, 120 inside a volume at 0, 0) holds under either reading. Shift by half the voxel size when a writer is known to mean the corner.
- sciviz/ometiff reads classic/BigTIFF Z/C/T stacks through decoders/tiff. Quantitative uint8/int8/uint16/int16/uint32/int32/float32/float64 samples remain unscaled. LZW, deflate, PackBits and uncompressed tiles/strips, chunky/planar samples and integer/floating predictors are supported. Explicit TiffData, series selection and multi-file FileName/UUID resolution are supported; unspecified planes reject on access. A TiffData with neither IFD nor PlaneCount covers every IFD of the file it names, so such a companion file is read when the stack opens. image() takes its origin from the Plane whose TheC is the channel holding the sample (an RGB channel's three samples share one Plane); a Position in a length unit converts to the PhysicalSize unit, while a 'reference frame' (the OME default) or 'pixel' position is added as written. The UnitsLength table and the channel lookup raised the sciviz/ometiff size budget from 3732 to 4192 B gzip; the table is needed by every image() call, so a separate chunk would save nothing. Metadata and individual planes are lazy after bounded full-file acquisition. SubIFD pyramids, BinaryOnly companion XML, JPEG/JPEG2000 microscopy payloads and vendor annotations are outside the requested lossless stack projection. The real IDR fixture is an explicitly identified, native-pixel, lossless crop of the original JPEG2000 image, not a claim that the runtime decodes JPEG2000 TIFF.
- Default per-file/per-read maxBytes is 64 MiB; TIFF default maxPixels is 2^26 and safe integer 64-bit offsets are required. The OME loader bounds each volume by maxBytes and planes conservatively by maxBytes/8 pixels. FITS and MRC accept gzip; FITS also bzip2. Non-axis-aligned/celestial world() coordinates are preserved exactly within supported transforms; generic grid/volume helpers preserve directed physical axes and reject rotation, shear, permutation or nonuniform sample spacing with code unsupported, without physical resampling. Readers retain full precision independently of Float32 renderer grids. Scientific volume helpers do not imply celestial reprojection or an affine/sheared volume renderer.

## AVIF still images (batch 203 job 4)

`@margoengine/decoders/avif` provides AVIFDecoder/decodeAVIF; /image dispatches lazily. The Margo-authored Rust SIMD decoder supports independent intra AV1 images, 8/10/12-bit 420/422/444 and monochrome, palettes, intra copy, grain, filters/restoration/superres, grids/identity, alpha/premultiplication and ordered clap/irot/imir. A 'prem' reference must name exactly the primary item's one alpha auxiliary item; any other 'prem' reference rejects as invalid. Output is straight RGBA8 by default or normalized RGBA16, retaining source bitDepth, CICP and ICC. ICC is metadata; output remains in the source encoded color space and has no automatic display profile or HDR tone map. RGB CICP matrices 0/1/2/4-14 are interpreted by H.273, with 2 defaulting to BT.601; derived systems require declared primaries/transfer. Reserved codes reject.

Defaults: maxPixels 2^26 per item, maxMemory 512 MiB (configurable through 1 GiB), workerLimit hardware concurrency capped at four (1-16), timeout 10 s plus 4 s/MiB. A conservative 128 bytes per padded luma sample bounds codec workspace before allocation; item/grid output also consumes the budget. The Wasm memory ceiling is 1 GiB. Input transfer defaults false. Aborting or disposing terminates the worker's active decode; later use creates a new worker. No core or stage code changes. Inter-frame/animated/progressive/layered streams, large-scale tile lists, protected/external items and derived tone-map/sample-transform items reject explicitly. These are outside the coordinator's independent intra still-image scope.

Evidence: 16 independently decoded files, 14,828,077 exact native/Wasm YUV samples; 912 inverse-transform contracts; real container/alpha/ICC/transform references; 4,762,292 exact GPU bytes per backend. RGB interpolation/rounding allows the declared per-file one/two 8-bit levels (zero for alpha), without changing normative YUV pixels. No universal conformance or speed claim.

### Batch 176: adaptive mesh refinement
sciviz/amr accepts nonoverlapping Cartesian cell-centred blocks with integer refinement ratios and finer faces aligned to coarse cells. Coarse masks hide completely covered cells; NaN denotes missing values. Native AMReX/BoxLib Header, Cell_H and IEEE32/64 FAB data support endian descriptors, scalar selection and stored ghost-box trimming. Enzo ASCII/HDF5 hierarchies and grouped HDF5 baryons support active or ghost-inclusive arrays. FLASH HDF5 uses only node-type-1 leaves. Non-Cartesian solver coordinates, AMReX headerless/raw and HDF5 plotfiles, staggered/nodal fields, Enzo particle arrays and FLASH CORNERS output need separate format extensions; readers do not silently treat these as the supported cell-centred layout. Points and in-face rays on a face follow the clamped cell index: cells own [lo, hi), an interior face belongs to the block above it (an empty region above it gives NaN and no interval), and the hierarchy's upper faces are closed, so sampleAMR and traceAMR agree everywhere.
Direct volume rendering uses a disjoint k-d tree of block boundaries and packed scalar textures; no finest-resolution dense volume is allocated. Default interpolation is linear inside each block, clamped at that block's outer cell centres. Composite and sampled MIP, scalar transfer functions, density, scene-depth clipping, up to four clip planes, device restoration and level outlines work on WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility. Gradient/preintegrated classifiers are rejected. There are at most 2048 integration samples per leaf interval. Construction defaults to 1,000,000 nodes, rejects depth over 128, and exact f32 indexing limits samples to 2^24 and packed texels to 2^23 (device texture limits may be lower). An explicit referenceStep defaults to the smallest physical cell spacing.
Masked slices preserve the original cell values and native resolution. Contours use a shared point lattice at finest spacing by default, bounded to 2,000,000 sample points, with explicit dims for coarser extraction. This resampling is analysis only and is never used by the volume renderer. The openly licensed demonstration is Natarajan's final oscillating-cylinder AMReX timestep (CC BY 4.0), with one unscaled float64 velocity field; same-level rectangular packing changes storage only. Nyx native plotfiles are provided by yt expressly for experimentation/testing, a narrower permission than the CC BY demo; no CC0 licence is asserted. No speed number is claimed during the build phase.

AMR optional entry size: new entry, 0 to 30,067 B gzip; ceiling 30,374 B. With the in-face ray rule (2026-11-15) the entry measures 30,377 B; ceiling 31,289 B. The bytes include native solver readers, HDF5 parsing, masks, k-d integration and analysis helpers. Splitting these into mandatory companion entries would complicate one coherent AMR API and its loading contract. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

AMR scalar transfer lookup also accepts the shared log/symmetric-log, binned and under/over colour encodings, using unfilterable float textures and explicit lookup. Below-range negative samples remain eligible for MIP; missing NaNs are skipped rather than confused with a numeric sentinel.

## Above-water screen-space refraction
With a borrowed scene color texture, Water traces up to 50 m along the
refracted ray inside the active viewport. It refines the intersection in at
most five depth-plane steps. If needed, it checks up to eight increasingly
spaced intervals for depth crossings, bisecting each candidate up to ten
times before validation. A bisected crossing whose texel lies within 5 cm or
2% of the ray's depth is the hit (KB-WATER-SEABEDMAZE1). A ray that leaves the
viewport in front of the scene takes the last texel it crosses on screen, so
the bed there is the one at the frame's edge, not the one the ray would reach.
This bounded first-layer depth approximation cannot see hidden or offscreen
geometry or resolve every narrow crossing. On an
open-water miss the body uses the 50 m deep-water fallback. A terrain-coupled
Water can use its modeled gap. The Water frame uniform is 576 B.

## HDR open water and partial camera waterline

Water estimates diffuse sky light with eight cosine-weighted directions. Sharp solar illumination remains the direct
light's job. Its HDR sky transform and scale occupy two unused float lanes of the existing 560 B frame.
Planar reflections feather their capture boundary and fade out toward the ocean horizon. The underwater near-plane
mask filters at the pixel footprint and keeps its physical ray-traversal limits. A planar capture still represents
one reference plane, so very steep or breaking waves can distort the captured geometry.

On the public base, water measured 30,644 B gzip and water/underwater 8,754 B. The changed builds measure 31,356 B
and 9,087 B respectively, with ceilings of 32,297 B and 9,360 B. Both share their existing rendering, capture and
resource paths. Moving them behind separate entries would duplicate that work. Core and stage remain at 24,797 B.

## Short wind waves and sky reflection

Each of the five baseline ripple lattices fades over a projected pixel width of 0.25 to 1.0 lattice
cells. The broadest keeps detail out to 13.33 m per pixel along its least sampled axis. Nonzero
`chop` adds normal detail at wavelengths near 3.7 m and 2.3 m, with nominal amplitudes of 0.060 m and
0.029 m before chop and wind-patch gain. Each band filters from 0.9 to pi radians of phase change per
pixel. Short-wave depth and forces are outside this shading model.

The reflection uses five taps in an angular lobe from either supplied sky type. Down-going rays on
open water lose at most 34% of their sky weight. This is an approximation of surface occlusion and
secondary reflection. There is one water fragment path and no extra binding, texture, or pass.

The root water entry measures 32,655 B minified and gzipped, up from 32,150 B. Its ceiling is 33,635 B.

The `create-margo` web starter's production build (every JS chunk, lazy ones included, gzip level 9) must not pass

## Shader comments in package builds

Package dists ship no WGSL or GLSL comment text (KB-WGSL1). Every package build strips the comments from the shader
strings it emits (`scripts/shader-comments.mjs`; conventions.md, "Shader comments"), keeping every token's text, order
and line; the sources keep their comments. The quality gate `shader-comments` fails when a comment ships. Two kinds of
comment stay on purpose: anchors that code searches for by text (`//INDICES` in compute's quantized kernels,
`/*lod:direct*/` in lod's imposter shader, five in voxel-pathtracer, one in scatter). Columns after a
removed block comment on the same line move; line numbers never do. Core and stage ship no shader comments, so core +
stage is unchanged. Rolled out in batches; min+gzip per entry before and after (entry-sizes.json's method):

## Batch 120 scaffold profile routing

The five create-margo starters install one engine profile each: web 40 engine packages, game 70, viz 42, React and Next 42 in the packed rehearsal. React, React DOM, Next and development tools remain explicit app dependencies as appropriate; Rapier's 3D solver comes with `@margoengine/physics`, and the game starter imports it from `@margoengine/game/physics` so its root ships no Wasm. All five production builds draw a first frame; Next runs its own production server. Profile entry sizes and core + stage remain unchanged. scripts/template-install-check.mjs and template-browser-check.mjs reproduce this route from packed engine and CLI tarballs with no workspace engine symlink. The starting-path review is docs/guides/kit-migration.md. Timing is deferred to the speed phase; template README examples remain owed.
- Batch 179 share: optional `/share` uses a version-1 DEFLATE/base64url fragment and repeated-array dictionary. Default payload/allocation bound 256 MiB and URL bound 32 MiB; browsers, address bars and messaging products can impose smaller limits. Use hash-pinned external raw arrays for short links, or offline HTML for large data. Standalone runtime is explicitly bundled by `packages/sciviz/scripts/bundle-share.mjs`; no remote runtime is downloaded. Native codecs and their assets are bundled, while application recipes/operator registries need an application runtime. Embed requires a known HTTP(S) origin and peer window, supports 32 queued requests, and times out client requests after 10 seconds. Opaque-origin iframe messaging is intentionally unavailable; offline file viewing remains supported. Camera and time index are validated before application. No speed claim.

- Batch 179 job 2 entry size: sciviz/share 0 to 5,033 B gzip, ceiling 5,289 B. The bytes provide compressed/dictionary links, hash-checked inline HTML and bounded iframe control with one ownership boundary. Splitting would make applications assemble the same feature and duplicate lifecycle handling. Core + stage remains 24,209 B; no rendering mathematics changed. The offline bundler is shipped under scripts/bundle-share.mjs and uses Vite as a development build tool.
Batch 178 accessibility: optional a11y provides complete pageable native point/line/bin/surface/volume rows; custom layer kinds need AccessibleSeries adapters. DOM page size defaults to 50 (1..1000), and sonification defaults to 100000 records, rejecting larger inputs without truncation. Lighthouse results concern loaded-page automated checks, not manual WCAG certification. See [contract and evidence](sciviz-a11y.md).

Measured job 5 gzip: a11y 0 -> 6233 B, sciviz root 60026 -> 61010 B, format 7306 -> 7598 B and spec 27106 -> 27127 B. Format ceiling rises 7562 -> 7826 B; a11y receives 6480 B. The bytes preserve complete data/keyboard/audio/lifetime contracts without application registration glue. Core + stage stays 24209 B.

Final integration: all 50 current scientific demo pages score 100. Rebased root 61327 B, a11y 6233 B, format 7598 B, spec 27443 B; core + stage 24209 B.

The share viewer audit uses a complete LIGO share URL as its input; no missing-link error screen is substituted for a restored scientific figure.



## Batch 181 job 5: progressive rendering

Optional sciviz/progressive reduces moving dimensions (default 0.5) and ray/lighting integration (default 0.25); after 2 settling and 8 refinement frames it returns exactly to the original rendering path. Soft submitted-frame latency budget defaults to 16.7 ms and is not a deadline or throughput claim. Temporary nearest-reconstructed single-sample images have no scalar/image error guarantee. One controller per engine, one reduced colour/depth target per view the previous frame drew (a view no longer drawn releases its target at the next frame; releasing them, 2026-11-16, took the entry from 5002 B to 5054 B min+gzip, the ceiling following it, since the shared per-view state helper is the engine's one pruning rule and a copy would be no smaller), normal device texture limits. Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 compatibility are covered; native preview rejects before attachment. CPU-backed layers restore through their owners; external GPU-only sources retain the documented application recreation contract. Full policy and options: docs/sciviz-progressive.md. Core/stage source unchanged.

New progressive entry: absent (0 B) to 4746 B min+gzip, ceiling 5002 B. The optional controller retains one target/depth/lifecycle owner and deterministic policy; splitting those parts would add orchestration without reducing the complete feature. Existing entry ceilings are retained. Core plus stage remains 24209 B.


## Batch 180 job 5: temporal analysis

The optional @margoengine/sciviz/temporal entry measures 3,901 B min+gzip (previously 0 B), ceiling 4,157 B; core + stage remains 24,209 B. It reads one field per step and retains O(field length) arrays. Statistics use equal step weights with population or sample deviation, not duration weighting. NaN handling is explicit; infinity, overflow, changed field length, duplicate/decreasing times and invalid series reject. Flat field correspondence belongs to the caller; fixed physical probes support moving meshes. Linear interpolation preserves missing endpoints and never extrapolates unless boundary clamping is requested. Charts use relative time origins, split missing runs, and use native lines/scatter; there is no hidden payload cache. Numeric source steps support model times; string time origins are proleptic Gregorian, millisecond precision, year 0000-9999, without leap seconds or calendar month/year units. Other calendar decoding belongs to /cf. The ERA5 demo contains eight six-hour samples (64x32), while NOAA contains eight daily 5x5 fields; interpolated instants are labelled. See docs/sciviz-temporal.md and its CPU/GPU tests. No speed claim.

Batch 181 job 4 density limits: optional sciviz/density uses borrowed interleaved float32 xyz, exact u32 count bins (at most 4,294,967,295 input points), 12 raster bytes per drawing-buffer pixel, 8192 per axis and 16,777,216 total pixels, further constrained by device storage and allocation limits. Source chunks have at most 1,048,576 points/12,582,912 bytes and shrink for binding/dispatch limits. 20M points: 240,000,000 source GPU bytes/20 chunks; 10M: 120,000,000/10, with every repeated real-data vote retained on both backends. Kernel bandwidth default 4 CSS pixels, (0,32], finite normalized Gaussian truncated at ceil(4*sigma), zero outside plot scissor. Opacity default 0.08, colour #56b4e9; opacity summary is floating point, analytical counts remain integer. Overlay ignores depth occlusion, clips offscreen halo, and quantizes positions to nearest screen bins. Compatibility atomic count currently runs on its CPU compute tier; no frame-time, memory ceiling or rival speed parity is claimed. Full contracts: docs/sciviz-density.md; timing comparison is deferred in speed-phase.md.
Entry size: sciviz/density was absent (0 B), now 4,815 B min+gzip with a 5,071 B ceiling. Core + stage remains 24,209 B. These optional bytes provide exact all-point accumulation, Gaussian mode, readback and scatter ownership; splitting those cooperating raster passes would add plumbing without improving quality.

Density rival pixel non-parity at 256 x 256 is retained, not hidden: mean red-byte difference 0.1480712891/max 246 against regl-scatterplot 1.16.0 at 20M, and 0.0787353516/max 255 against deck.gl 9.4.1 at 10M. Pixels above two bytes: 0.2227783203% and 0.1724243164%. The cause is measured (docs/sciviz-density.md, "Why the pixels differ"; docs/whitepaper/results/density-attribution-2026-11-27.json): both rivals snap a point to 1/256 pixel and give a boundary point to another pixel than the one containing it, which is 229 of the 236 regl-scatterplot differences (the other 7 sit within 0.000028 pixel of the grid's tie); deck.gl's one pixel disc drops 23.6% of points and its 8-bit accumulation stops at 249, which together rebuild its image exactly. Margo's own float32 projection puts 9 of 1,000,000 2MASS observations in another pixel than binary64 does (one output pixel, 2 bytes). The snap grid is measured on one device (RTX A6000, ANGLE Direct3D 11), not promised for others; no speed or byte-parity claim exists. Frozen pixel report: docs/whitepaper/results/batch181-density.json.

Batch 274 job 5 ONNX supported profile: the optional loader currently executes isolated CPU SIMD Wasm inference. Tensor dimensions are integers in 0..2147483647 and total scalar elements at most 16777216; packet/model bytes at most 512 MiB; persistent tensor storage defaults to 256 MiB and accepts 64 KiB..1 GiB. Loop/Scan/SequenceMap default maxIterations=10000, expanded maxNodes=1000000 and graph/container nesting=64. Random state persists per expanded lexical call site across runs, with at most one million sites per model. Seeded sequences are reproducible within Margo, not promised bit-identical across runtimes. FFT complex work vectors have at most 16777216 scalar components, including Bluestein scratch (2*nextPowerOfTwo(2*n-1)); inverse DFT normalization is 1/n. Cancellation yields between graph nodes, not within a synchronous kernel. Host bool snapshots are logical 0/1 values; a BitCast back inside the graph retains original byte patterns. Empty scanned outputs currently need static element shape information; string crop extrapolation remains restricted. The deferred operator/type/opset groups are listed below. The pinned 96-case external comparison and analytic tests establish only their named cases. PROBIT uses a more accurate tail inversion than the tested external provider; single-target regression honors post_transform. These accepted numerical/semantic differences are described with values in docs/clean-room.md and remain subject to the final catalogue review.


ONNX groups not built yet: the opset 29 operators (CausalConvWithState and LinearAttention version 29, DequantizePacked, Expm1, Log1p, GeGLU, GroupedMatMul, LogCumSumExp, Pack, Unpack), which no ONNX release carries yet (1.23.0 is opset 28). Old operator versions follow docs/onnx-conformance.md; Scan opset 8 needs at least one batch and one sequence step, and its output steps past a batch's length hold what the body computes from the padding (ONNX leaves them undefined). Unbuilt operators reject during load with code unsupported, domain/operator name, imported opset and help URL; onnx.test.js covers every named unbuilt operator group. Quantized operators and the element type review are in docs/onnx-conformance.md. RegexFullMatch matches RE2 syntax (patterns expand to at most 100,000 instructions, repetition counts to 1000; \p classes are those the JavaScript engine's Unicode tables know) in time linear in the text, on the JavaScript thread; DeformConv computes in float64, one sample at a time. ImageDecoder reads PNG, JPEG, WebP (an animation's first frame), BMP, classic TIFF, BigTIFF, JPEG 2000 and PBM/PGM/PPM through the optional peer `@margoengine/decoders`, at most 67,108,864 pixels; a damaged, oversized or foreign stream gives the empty matrix `[0, 0, channels]`; Alpha is dropped, samples wider than 8 bits scale to bytes, float TIFF maps 0..1 to 0..255, and Grayscale is the rounded Rec. ITU-R BT.601 luma of the decoded RGB. Subsampled JPEG chroma is filtered linearly as the operator describes but without libjpeg-turbo's alternating rounding, and the inverse DCT is Margo's, so a lossy JPEG is not bit identical to another runtime. Attention, RotaryEmbedding, TensorScatter, CausalConvWithState and LinearAttention are plain scalar loops (no SIMD, no speed claim). ONNX inference uses CPU SIMD Wasm, including on pages with WebGPU or compatibility, with no GPU inference claim.

Batch 274 job 5 measured ONNX entry: 0 to 10139 B min+gzip, new ceiling 10444 B; separate lazy onnx-kernel.wasm 684541 B raw / 244935 B gzip. The entry keeps validation, lexical graph execution and lifetime ownership together; splitting would duplicate its Wasm bridge and resource accounting. Core plus stage remains 24209 B under the unchanged 25000 B limit.
- Batch 179 notebook: optional /notebook AFM plus a thin local Python anywidget wrapper. Defaults: 480 CSS pixels (100..4000), auto backend, 256 MiB aggregate decode budget, empty 3D spec and plot limits [0,1,0,1,0,1]. SHA-256 binary attachments borrow aligned little-endian numeric views; dtype/offset conversions, comm framing, recorder snapshots and GPU uploads can copy. Null/multi-chunk Arrow converts explicitly; int64 outside +/-2^53 rejects. Borrowed mutations need refresh(). A render() whose signal aborts before its first load settles disposes the view and rejects with the abort reason. No Python renderer or runtime CDN. Static HTML retains interaction but no live Python callbacks. Actual GPU evidence covers both backends and offline files; actual kernel evidence covers JupyterLab. Other AFM hosts use the same standard contract; interactive VS Code/Colab/marimo acceptance remains separately owed. No speed claim.

- Batch 179 notebook sizes: new /notebook 0 to 1831 B min+gzip, ceiling 2095 B. ## Compute quantized inference (batch 274 job 6)

`@margoengine/compute/quant` uses signed int8 packed four per word. Matmul supports
vector promotion and broadcast batches, per-row activation and per-column weight
parameters shared across batches. Conv2d uses NCHW/OIHW, per-tensor activations,
per-output-channel weights, groups/depthwise, stride, dilation and explicit or same
padding. Output parameters are per tensor. Int32 accumulator overflow is rejected
conservatively, including bias. Dimensions and index products must fit signed
32-bit indexing and device storage/dispatch limits. Nearest-even f32 requantization
is lossy and saturates. Float-reference error bounds, scale representability and
finite-output assumptions are in docs/compute-quant.md. No latency or model-wide
accuracy claim; uint8, training and integer-only requantization are outside this
signed-int8 entry. Core and stage receive no changes.

The new optional /quant entry measures 3,927 B minified gzip (previously absent,
0 B), with a 4,183 B quality ceiling. The bytes provide both backends, packed
storage and validation in one optional module; splitting would add loading and
API complexity without reducing core/stage. The core + stage root remains
24,209 B gzip in this build, below its unchanged 25,000 B ceiling.


## GPU graph layout (batch 175 job 5)

Optional @margoengine/sciviz/graph-gpu has device-resident 2D/3D FR and ForceAtlas2, a sorted Morton grid tree, styled screen-space edges/arrows, GPU FDEB and collision-avoiding labels. CPU all-pairs references remain available. There is no root/core/stage import.

Graph counts are 1..16,777,216 nodes, subject to per-device buffer/binding limits; indices are exact u32. Grid side is a power of two, 2..512 in 2D or 2..64 in 3D. Defaults are 128 and 16. theta defaults to 0.7; 0 gives all pairs. Tree bounds use actual points even outside the Morton partition box. Sorting takes log2(padded N)*(log2(padded N)+1)/2 device passes; every node is represented, with no sampling. Concentrated/coincident leaves can require quadratic pair work. Force storage and accumulation are float32, not bit-identical to binary64 CPU results. Zero-length pairs receive a seeded index direction.

FDEB defaults to six cycles, 50 initial iterations, 0.1 step/stiffness and 0.6 compatibility; 1..9 cycles, at most 10,000 initial iterations. It is deliberately opt-in: compatible pairs are evaluated without truncation, O(E squared * subdivision points * iterations), and buffers must fit device limits. Rebundle after moving nodes; bundled endpoints are a snapshot. Arrows follow each edge's own direction. Self loops do not pull on their node; degenerate projected edge segments are not drawn.

Label candidates are explicit node/text records, default maximum 200 visible (`maxLabels`, any integer of 0 or more): candidates are placed in priority order and the first that fit are kept, so the ones left out are the lowest-priority or overlapping ones. Only candidate positions are gathered/read back by refreshLabels(); frame hooks reproject that snapshot for camera changes. Call refreshLabels after layout changes. Labels avoid each other and viewport boundaries; obscured labels can be suppressed. Device loss hides a GPU-owned layer; recreate layout/bundles/layer on the replacement device, as with other caller-owned GPU arrays. Dispose drawing layers before their caller-owned layout and bundles.

The million-node proof records all output positions, moved-node count, capped movement, persistent buffer bytes, dispatches, compare-exchanges and many-body interaction count. These are logical allocations/work, not physical VRAM, heap totals, FPS or wall-clock measurements. Million-node topology repeats the original OpenAlex citation subgraph; it does not claim a million unique works. Runtime speed comparisons await the speed phase.

The new graph-gpu entry measures 13717 B gzip (before 0 B), ceiling 14129 B. Core + stage remains 24,209 B. Full layout, bundling and drawing share one optional lifecycle; a split would add resource coordination solely to save optional bytes.
Batch 180 job 4 CF and projections: /cf reads existing CDF-1/2 NetCDF lazily, not HDF5/NetCDF-4. Independent dimension coordinates, scalar numeric and character labels, matching two-dimensional geographic auxiliaries and selected time-dependent auxiliaries are recognised. Every non-horizontal dimension longer than one requires an explicit zero-based index; no implicit first member/time/level. Projected x/y mappings supported: CF Lambert conformal conic, Albers, polar stereographic, Mercator and latitude/longitude; other CRS names require geographic auxiliary coordinates. The coordinate metadata is retained, not a complete CF validation or general UDUNITS implementation. Unit conversion covers documented climate SI vocabulary, compound integer exponents, pressure, degrees/radians and affine Celsius/Fahrenheit/Kelvin; unknown or incompatible conversions reject. As in UDUNITS-2, a plural is taken only on a unit name (meters, hours, days), never on a symbol: ms, Pas and Ns are not metre, pascal or newton and reject as unknown. A longitude cell's bounds name the arc that holds its centre, so a conservative remap keeps cells wider than 180 degrees. Units metadata temperature differences suppress affine offsets.
CF reference-time conversion supports standard/gregorian with the 1582 gap, proleptic Gregorian, Julian, noleap/365_day, all_leap/366_day and 360_day. Uses fixed SI durations, numeric timezone offsets, fractional/negative offsets, no Date conversion of model dates. Years bounded +/-1000000; standard/Julian require positive years. Leap-second instants, calendar=none and custom calendars require caller conversion, not silent Gregorian fallback. Appendix D vertical formulas broadcast by dimension names into Pa/down or m/up; dimensional positive metadata is preserved. ocean_double_sigma_coordinate counts k from 1 along the level dimension, so k_c is the number of upper sigma levels, as in the HOPS and NCOM Fortran formulas CF took the definition from (CF does not state the base). Its lower-set formula is evaluated as CF writes it; that text is self-consistent only in HOPS depths (positive down, lower sigma 1 to 2), so a writer using negative heights for z1 and z2 does not get -depth at the seafloor. Maximum broadcast 16777216 elements, caller configurable.
Source sampler cap 16777216 nodes, target default cap 4194304 cells. Rectilinear axes must be monotonic after longitude unwrap; full cycles inferred, regional seams explicit, duplicate seam values must agree. Bilinear default or nearest, strict missing corners by default or explicit renormalization. Curvilinear uses a 5 degree cell index and bounded inverse bilinear solves; folded/degenerate cells and missing geographic positions are holes. Curvilinear periodicity requires explicit periodic=true. No extrapolation beyond source nodal coverage. Land masks are independent fraction/percent grids sampled categorically; default threshold 0.5. Map-cell centre sampling is for display and is not conservative. conservativeCF separately preserves rectilinear cell-average area integrals using CF bounds or midpoint-derived edges; returns valid-area coverage, and rejects overlapping source cells. It does not invent arbitrary curvilinear conservative cell corners.
Projection angular inputs are degrees, outputs use radius units (default metres with radius6378137). Default WGS84 flattening for conics/polar/Mercator, zero for plate/Robinson/Mollweide. Conic defaults parallels30/60; origin0 except polar90; central meridian0, false origin0, scale1. Opposite standard parallels reject as a degenerate cone; singular poles return undefined, out-of-domain inverses return undefined. Robinson uses the published 5-degree table and a local monotone Hermite interpolant, so between-knot pixels can differ from other interpolants. Mollweide is spherical. Neither conformality nor equal-area properties are claimed for Robinson. Rendering uses retained finite-cell meshes, existing colour maps and both backends, with device restore.

Batch 180 job 4 entry sizes: cf 0 -> 14438 B gzip, ceiling 14872 B; projections 0 -> 2328 B, ceiling 2584 B. Optional CF semantics and independent Snyder transforms are retained together to avoid duplicated dimension/lifetime coordination; the existing mesh owner stays lazy. Core + stage source unchanged.



Batch 274 ONNX tree/SVM follow-up: TreeEnsembleRegressor and TreeEnsembleClassifier execute legacy ML1..4 encodings, plus a compatibility extension retaining their semantics under deprecated ML5 imports. TreeEnsemble uses ML5 with float16/float32/float64 typed splits/weights and membership sets. Legacy trees accept float32/float64/int32/int64 inputs and produce float32 scores, preserving exact int64 labels. Graph tuples, references, targets, flag vectors and all cycles validate before traversal. Combined modern nodes/leaves and legacy node counts cap at 16777216; output tensors share the existing element/storage caps. SVMClassifier/Regressor implement all four kernels, regression/one-class output, linear and support-vector classification, raw pairwise multiclass scores, labels, calibration and post-transforms. Uncalibrated support-vector output has K*(K-1)/2 scores (two for binary), calibrated output K. Calibration uses at most 16777216 workspace scalars, at most 4096 classes, residual <0.005/K and at most max(100,K) sweeps; exhaustion rejects. Model parameters must be finite. All inference remains synchronous CPU SIMD Wasm inside each graph node. Compatibility does not mean GPU inference. No throughput claim.
Accepted provider differences and exact evidence are in clean-room.md: top-class labels follow raw class scores, regression honors post_transform, and PROBIT retains the existing mathematical inverse-normal behavior. The external provider refuses deprecated ML5 legacy trees; analytic tests cover that compatibility extension. Single-score binary classifiers and calibration at extreme margins are covered by onnx-ml-calibration.test.js and described in docs/onnx-conformance.md. Remaining unbuilt groups listed above are unchanged.

Follow-up measured size: ONNX entry 10139 -> 10139 B min+gzip (existing 10444 B ceiling retained); separate onnx-kernel.wasm 684541 -> 753589 B raw and 244935 -> 270831 B gzip. The additional 25896 B gzip retains complete tree/SVM inference, topology validation and calibrated probabilities in the same optional per-model Wasm owner; splitting would add another ABI and attribute/resource lifetime bridge. Core plus stage remains 24209 B.

## Batch 175 job 4: series
Optional /series uses 1 MiB network chunks, 512 MiB per encoded/decoded block, 100M rows by default (override reader limits), and at most uint32 original row IDs. Exact selection retains loaded binary64 blocks; it is not constant-total-memory storage. Flat scalar Arrow/Parquet limits and codecs match /table. M4 is exact for the aliased pixel-column line model, not arbitrary antialiasing/thick-line blending. Min-max/LTTB are alternatives; LTTB defaults to retaining pixel extrema too. NaN gaps split lines and can exceed the usual four-vertices-per-column output. Spectra require finite uniform samples, explicit sample rate and 2..16777216 values. STFT defaults to 256-sample periodic Hann, half-window hop, mean removal, complete windows, 256 MiB output bound and one-window GPU staging. HTTP sources need valid 206 byte ranges and immutable versions; Range/CORS headers must be exposed. Details, defaults and physical PSD normalization: docs/sciviz-series.md. No speed claim.

Batch 175 job 4 measured sizes: /series absent (0 B) to 13801 B min+gzip, ceiling 14169 B; /table 12655 B after sharing progressive decoders. The bytes preserve one coherent reader/data/selection/spectral lifecycle instead of a split requiring applications to duplicate state. Core plus stage remains 24209 B before and after.
Batch 178 themes: optional named tokens, per-figure CSS bindings and journal final-column presets are documented in [sciviz-themes.md](sciviz-themes.md). Print safety requires device/profile proofing; PDF outline fonts are caller-supplied and Nature editable-text compliance is not claimed.

# Batch 175 job 6: worker reader limits

The optional sciviz/workers entry supports the seven named reader families through dedicated, disposable worker sessions. Existing per-format validation and codec limits remain authoritative. Input buffers clone unless explicitly listed for transfer; output buffers are snapshotted once inside the worker before transfer so lazy caches remain usable. Custom source callbacks remain on their owner thread. Progress reports start/complete operation milestones and unique backing-buffer bytes, not network totals or parsing percentages. Cancellation of any call terminates that session. Response deadline defaults to 30000 ms per operation. No worker pool, automatic retry, shared-memory input or page parsing fallback is introduced. See docs/sciviz-workers.md for the full lifetime and method-proxy contract.

Measured gzip: sciviz/workers 0 to 1589 B, ceiling 1845 B; its bundled reader worker 0 to 41506 B by the package-entry measurement, ceiling 42752 B, or 41409 B when served verbatim (116841 B raw). The worker includes all seven reader families and compression handling; splitting would duplicate RPC and complicate lazy session ownership. worker/rpc adds progress within its existing 2408 B ceiling, measured 2253 B after the change. Core plus stage stays 24209 B. No load-time or inflater speed result is claimed during the deferred speed phase.

## Integration

C2 composition J2 initially proves six of 276 target pass pairs (post/FXAA, TAA, DOF, Tonemap) on native WebGPU and full WebGL2 compatibility, at 1x and 4x MSAA. The generator independently covers all four binary states over the 24-member target; this CPU coverage is distinct from executed GPU coverage. Sciviz is excluded. C1 and C3-C10 are not proven by this suite. See docs/integration-composition.md for scenes, assertions and remaining scope.

### Batch 176: tensor fields
sciviz/tensor uses symmetric coefficients xx,yy,zz,xy,xz,yz. CPU eigensystems use float64; GPU systems use scaled float32 Jacobi, at most 48 rotations, and an absolute residual bound of 64 * 2^-23 * the maximum absolute coefficient. Nonzero GPU input magnitude must be between 2^-96 and 2^120; rescale tensor units outside that accuracy range. Zero and repeated spectra are supported, with canonical signs and a right-handed basis; individual eigenvectors in a degenerate eigenspace are not unique. Output eigenvalues are algebraically descending. FA uses its published formula, is zero for a zero tensor and can exceed one for indefinite tensors. Float64 spectral overflow is rejected. Device buffer limits are checked before copying a GPU field.
Glyphs are ellipsoids or Kindlmann superquadrics in one instanced draw, with GPU eigensystems remaining in storage buffers. Default superquadric gamma 3, resolution 16 polar by 32 azimuthal, per-tensor maximum-radius normalization, size .4 voxel spacing (.4 data units for scattered points), stride 1 (on a regular field it steps every axis i, j and k, so stride 2 keeps one sample in eight of a 3D grid; scattered points keep every stride-th sample), direction-FA RGB and opacity 1. FA colour uses the selected map (default viridis). Signed glyph geometry uses absolute eigenvalues ordered by magnitude; signed values remain available for interpretation. Positions and glyph bounds must fit float32. Exact quarter-turn parameters preserve poles and symmetry; normals use centred parametric differences and scalar-free normalization, including large physical unit scales. Empty selections draw nothing; disposal and device resource reconstruction are supported.
TensorField bounds are outer voxel faces of an axis-aligned, cell-centred, x-fastest Cartesian grid. Samples interpolate six coefficients before decomposing. Fibres default to bidirectional FACT, FA >= .15, maximum turn 45 degrees, maximum length 1000 per direction, 4096 steps per direction and 1000000 returned points. Euler defaults to one quarter of minimum voxel spacing. Tracking stops at masks, missing samples, negative eigenvalues, zero/degenerate principal directions, domain edges and the requested limits. Hyperstreamlines default to 12 sides, radius .5 voxel spacing times lambda2/lambda1 and lambda3/lambda1, with 1000000 triangles maximum. Explicit options raise output budgets.
Diffusion fitting is ordinary, unconstrained log-linear least squares, never a weighted, constrained or nonlinear estimator. Signals are volume-major, b-values s/mm^2, and output tensors mm^2/s. Gradients must be within 1e-4 of unit length and are normalized once; b=0 directions are ignored. Default signal floor is 1. A rank-deficient design rejects using the documented 1e-10 relative QR column threshold. Excluded voxels retain NaN coefficients; estimated non-positive spectra are flagged, not projected away. The demonstration says this method explicitly, preserves all 65 volumes in a 32x32x8 native crop, displays two-voxel glyph spacing in each axis and uses millimetres along the supplied FSL voxel-axis basis with equal physical plot lengths. No scanner-affine conversion, eddy-current/motion correction or anatomical validation is claimed. No speed number is published during the build phase.

Tensor optional entry: new 0 to 27,622 B gzip, ceiling 28,451 B. The bytes keep fitting, eigensystems, glyphs and tracking in one coherent coordinate/lifetime contract; mandatory companion entry splits would add wiring without improving results. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

Integration J2 second set historically covered 12 C2 members in 13 rows and 66/276 positive pairs. The full set below supersedes that intermediate coverage.

### Batch 176: molecules
sciviz/molecule consumes structures returned by loaders/pdb and loaders/mmcif and supplies an opaque, 3D linear-axis MoleculeLayer. Coordinates and radii are angstroms. Default ball-and-stick uses 0.3 times each van der Waals atom radius, bondRadius 0.2 angstrom; space-filling uses full van der Waals radii and no bonds; licorice uses bondRadius for both atom spheres and bonds. atomScale applies to ball-and-stick only. atomIndices defaults to all atoms and displays a bond only when both ends are selected. Empty selections allocate/draw nothing. The layer owns its snapshot, restores GPU resources and supports Symbol.dispose. GPU buffer size/binding limits are enforced; rendering uses float32 precision, so coordinates should stay near the molecular origin. Native WebGPU and compatibility WebGL2 are supported; native WebGL2 requires a separate backend implementation and is rejected before allocation.
One six-vertex instanced draw covers both analytic spheres and closed cylinders. Fragment depth comes from the ray hit, with endpoint element colours split at each bond's midpoint. Conservative projected boxes fall back to full-screen coverage across the near plane. Picking uses these same displayed surfaces: pick(x,y) uses canvas-relative CSS pixels; pickRay uses angstrom-space rays. The nearest atom or nearer bond endpoint returns a complete author residue identity (chain, author id, insertion code, name, all source atom indices). Other scene layers are not included in a molecule layer's pick query. It does not install a global Figure hover picker.
The loaders select the first coordinate model and first location of each alternate atom. mmCIF supports CIF 1.1 quoted values, semicolon fields, comments, loops/single values, first or explicitly named data block, author identifiers with label fallbacks, and identity-symmetry covalent/disulfide struct_conn bonds. Parse limits are the shared loaders maxVertices (default 8,000,000 atoms). Non-identity crystal connections warn and require crystal expansion; no biological assembly generation, BinaryCIF, CIF 2.0, bond order/valence inference or crystallographic symmetry expansion is claimed. GuessBonds defaults true and shares the PDB spatial grid: 0.4 < distance <= covalent radius sum + 0.45 angstrom. Existing common-element covalent radii/colours are shared by both readers; unlisted elements use pink and 1.5 angstrom covalent radius. Space filling has Bondi common-element radii (Ca from Mantina 2009), with 2 angstrom for unlisted elements. Deuterium/tritium and unsupported element labels use those explicit fallbacks. The default heuristics can connect nearby non-covalent contacts; disable guessBonds to retain deposited bonds only. Secondary-structure ribbons are the optional stretch goal, not part of the implemented sphere/stick row. No speed claim is published.

Molecule optional entry sizes: loaders/mmcif new 0 to 3,186 B gzip, ceiling 3,442 B; sciviz/molecule new 0 to 5,163 B, ceiling 5,419 B. Existing loaders/pdb changes from 2,208 to 2,269 B, within its existing ceiling. These entries keep complete coordinate parsing in loaders and rendering/picking lifetime in sciviz; forced splits would duplicate grammar or primitive ownership. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

## Batch 137 encoder limits

The default KTX2 encoder requires WebAssembly SIMD. A runtime without SIMD rejects
with MargoError `unsupported` and a help link; there is no automatic scalar fallback.
CSP compilation refusals use `failed` with the required permission and CSP help link.
Failed loads are cleared, so each later encode call may make one fresh load attempt;
successful modules remain cached. See [loader recovery](exporter-basis-loading.md).

The clean-room ETC1S/UASTC encoder replaces the bundled prebuilt encoder, with the
same public settings and a single lazy SIMD Wasm module. ETC1S uses shared endpoint
and selector codebooks; all nineteen UASTC modes participate at level 2 and above.
RDO reuses valid previous blocks over a bounded 256-block dictionary; lambda zero
preserves the unconditioned stream. Zstandard literals use at most eleven-bit
canonical Huffman codes, four streams for large literal sections and at most
128 KiB per frame block. Source pixels and fitted blocks are unchanged by entropy
coding. No throughput or peak-memory parity is claimed during the deferred phase.

On the unchanged full three-role CC0 corpus, all 66 PSNR and 42 valid 11x11 Gaussian
SSIM mip comparisons pass at or below the old complete-file byte budgets. Exact
settings, source and artifact hashes: whitepaper/results/batch-137-quality-r10.json.
The comparison tunes rate by ETC1S quality or UASTC RDO; it does not establish a
universal quality guarantee on other textures. Measured optional ktx2 bundle: 422537 raw / 147879 gzip B, from round 9's
395263 / 138922 B. The distinct lazy Wasm asset is 291861 raw / 91747 gzip B,
from 271457 / 84726 B. Bundle and file figures are not additive. These added
bytes buy lossless literal coding and quality parity; splitting would require
another codec ABI and fetch. Existing optional size ceilings suffice. Core plus
stage remains 24209 gzip B, below 25000 B.

AVIF review L2 (2026-11-10): OBU reserved header/extension bits are ignored as required for decoders; forbidden-bit, strict config-size and truncated-payload checks remain enforced. The standard CPU tests now include the native/Wasm spec regressions; see docs/avif-review-fixes.md.
### Node glTF image decoding (2026-11-10)

Without createImageBitmap, gltf/pbr lazily calls the existing decoders/image entry and retains RGBA8 rows with straight alpha. Browser bitmaps stay the default when available. PNG/JPEG data URIs, buffer views and fetched images use the same download and decoded-image limits as before; GPU dimensions still obey maxTextureDimension2D. The existing optional decoder owns its supported coding subsets and failures. Raw pixels stay in CPU memory for clone/device restoration, width * height * 4 bytes per image, plus independent React mount copies. Material uploads generate the same full mip chain as bitmaps; uploadImage itself returns a caller-owned single-level texture, as before. CPU decode time is not benchmarked in the build phase.
The Node image repair changes the gltf/pbr-model entry from 60,402 to 60,566 bytes gzip (+164), measured by the quality bundle method against the parent source. Its optional ceiling rises from 60,429 with the normal 3% margin. Splitting would require caller configuration and duplicate loading/upload/restoration paths for 164 bytes. Core and stage bytes are unchanged.

TAA reset restarts its eight Halton samples and discards history for the named view or every view. Motion frame identity remains monotonic until device recreation.
