The small spherical liquid droplet closure uses Stokes settling. In the ParisFog holdout it overpredicts visible
range at all twelve timestamps, with five of six F32 measurements outside the reported bands.

Open edges export the layer, and sealed edges retain it while surface inputs and settling exchange water with the
ground. Local phases use one, two or four native participants and require shared world memory for multiple
participants. The render layout and serial face order are unchanged. Each accepted step checks its CFL clock
progress and rejects nonfinite state before updating fields and their budgets. Old grey snapshots retain the same
layout. To continue a legacy fixed-emissivity setup under the same law, keep its prescribed emissivity.

The visual grid stores 16 bytes a column plus a 48-byte header. Its resolution is bounded by the device's
storage-buffer binding and buffer size. `FogGrid` samples optical extinction and vertical extent through the
optional volumetric medium on both renderers. The Physics optional entry is 7,972 B gzip. Each of
the two native assets is 13,174 B raw and 5,419 B gzip.

### Layered snowpack (ICE-01)

The model resolves a vertical column for each sample, with a fresh surface layer and the configured initial layers.
It represents freeze/thaw, surface-settling overburden, pairwise conduction, capillary storage and gravity drainage.
It uses bulk density and viscosity. Grain metamorphism, vapor diffusion and hydraulic travel time through the pack
require more state. The optional Weather renderer consumes the stored ground and snow depth directly.

Snow drift uses local near-surface wind and the flux capacity of adjacent columns, with closed lateral boundaries.
The overhang stores a labeled fraction of the rim mass and gives a direction and extension at its specified density
and thickness. It represents accretion and scouring. Fracturing a three-dimensional cornice requires a structural
model. The slab field reports a static interface safety factor, with no assessment of fracture propagation.
Weather's blocked footprints and drag act on the dense avalanche layer. The powder cloud is transported separately.

The optional snowpack entry is 5,737 B min+gzip. Its plain and shared Wasm variants are each 6,455 B raw. The
Weather avalanche entry is 7,195 B min+gzip with its obstacle terms.

### Dune and snow transport (EARTH-07)

The solver resolves a single grain material and a mobile surface layer on the uniform `TerrainBed` grid.
Set `mobileDepth` to the available layer above bedrock. Coarse grids describe dune evolution. For impact ripples,
supply `ripples.meanHop` and put multiple vertices inside a typical ripple wavelength. The short-hop model uses one
material and a fixed wind-relative incident angle. Suspension, snow cohesion changes and multi-grain sorting require
additional models. In an explicit world the latest bed change
may be in flight for one base step. Other contributors sharing the bed need to coordinate their erodible depths.

Open sides export saltating grains and closed sides retain them. The mass ledger reports mobile bed, airborne grains,
dust and open-boundary export. Snow uses a seasonal threshold and optional exposure. Wind stress and dust use exported
surface fields. ATMO-06 can consume mineral dust on the matching grid. ATMO-01 does not yet return a wind response
to the exported opposing stress. Snow emits no mineral dust.
The rendering entry uses the current ground and transport field, and maps moving mass to opacity with `referenceMass`.

The sand closure has a fixed 1.5 m/s default grain speed, a one-grain restart when the initiation threshold is
exceeded, and a configurable dust efficiency. The wind-tunnel comparison in
`packages/physics/scripts/earth07-creyssels-measured.mjs` underpredicts all six independent collected fluxes by
13.4–32.1%. Four runs remain outside the reported 5% measurement bands after wind uncertainty is propagated
separately. Settled sand tunnel flux is the only measured comparison here. Near-threshold snow, changing
cohesion, field dune migration and ripple wavelength still need measured validation.

Use a finite grid and a positive interval that a native CFL substep count can represent. If the interval,
initial mass, forcing or material values exceed numeric range, the solver reports a coded error before
publishing a new state. Lower the step, coarsen the grid or reduce the out-of-range inputs as indicated.
Signed origins translate wind sampling using the configured world cell size. Thread counts of 2 or 4
include the caller and require shared world memory and a blocking agent. Use one participant in a browser window.
The face, bed-hop and avalanche writes stay ordered, so native helpers cover the independent vertex stages.
The optional aeolian entry is 8,936 B min+gzip. Each separate Wasm variant is 14,142 B raw and 5,947 B gzip.
The shared helper script is 779 B gzip when loaded. The visual entry remains 11,061 B min+gzip.

### Groundwater and springs (HYDRO-06)

Use an unconfined aquifer with one active horizontal layer. Darcy conductance is integrated over the saturated
overlap and held during each implicit tick. Opposite face transfers conserve liquid volume. The water table follows
the terrain if bound. A drain below the aquifer floor is limited to that floor. Surface level limits saturated
storage and excess leaves as seepage. Springs and seepage supply the shallow-water solver in one direction.
Specify a physical groundwater time scale appropriate to the rate at which the saturated thickness changes.

Detailed unsaturated pressure and moisture profiles, multiple aquifer layers and surface-water backflow through
spring openings are outside this model. HYDRO-02 calculates recharge through the active soil.

In the 1 mm glass-bead experiment, measured outflow reaches 0.5 mL/s near 80 s on the rain clock.
This model reaches it at 65 s with immediate saturated recharge. At 195 s it predicts 4.69 mL/s versus
7.50 mL/s measured. For three 4 mm bead rain rates it predicts 1.27, 3.27 and 8.67 mL/s at 30 s
on the paper's outlet-aligned clock, versus observed 2.22, 5.28 and 15.28 mL/s. Doubling the cell count
and halving the step changes the largest of these rates by 0.31 mL/s. Independent conductivity and
rainfall sensitivity plus lower drainable yield cannot close the gap. The outlet-aligned comparison assesses
amplitude. The absolute recharge delay for the 4 mm runs is unknown. [Guérin et al. (2014)](https://doi.org/10.1017/jfm.2014.590).

The optional JavaScript entry measures 9,253 B min+gzip with a 9,531 B ceiling, including the confined
exports. Both lazy Wasm variants are 13,306 B raw and 4,443 B gzip. Native helpers split independent cell
and face setup before the ordered pressure solve and discharge recovery. Trials add 40 B per cell and
40 B for the staged budget. Each native participant uses an aligned 64 KiB stack. Core and stage receive
zero bytes.

The confined solve (`solveConfinedFlow`, for a confined aquifer slice or a Hele-Shaw cell) is steady and single
layer: one potential per cell, five-point faces with harmonic transmissivity, fixed sides half a cell from the
centre, and a Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate-gradient solve to a relative residual of 1e-12. A Hele-Shaw gap takes
T = b^3 / 12 mu, the gap-averaged Poiseuille flow, so it holds while the gap Reynolds number is small and the cell is
much wider than its gap. Solid cells are blocky (staircase edges, no cut cells). Streamlines are stream-function contours
found on each column face, with travel time as the trapezoid of dx / u between faces, so they suit flows that run
from the minX side to the maxX side without turning back. A free cell with no path to a fixed potential is refused.

### Pipe flow, hydraulic structures and machines (HYDRO-07)

`@margoengine/physics/hydraulics` is a set of steady and lumped models, measured against exact solutions:
Hagen-Poiseuille laminar friction to rounding, Colebrook against an independent fixed-point solve within 1e-12
(relative), Haaland within 2 percent of it from Re 4,000 and Churchill within 3 percent from Re 10,000 (its blend
departs most near 4,000), Torricelli and the closed-form basin equalisation against a fine Runge-Kutta run within
1e-9 m, Belanger's conjugate depth to rounding with
momentum balanced, Chow's tabled depth ratio 8.0 at F1 = 6.0, and the three-reservoir network against bisection
within 1e-9 m. Limits by method:

- Pipe and channel flow are steady (no distributed transients, no method of characteristics, no column separation
  after cavitation; `siphon` reports `cavitates` but does not model the broken column).
- Minor losses are single K values; Venturi and orifice coefficients are inputs with handbook defaults (ISO 5167-4
  machined Venturi 0.995, sharp orifice 0.61).
- `HydraulicRam` is one lumped drive line (inertance, compliance and resistance) with an air vessel under a
  polytropic law, integrated by the explicit midpoint rule at 0.75 ms. A fast closure gives the Joukowsky surge within
  2e-3 of rho a dv; the travelling wave inside the drive pipe is not resolved.
- `solveNetwork` solves steady flow with a dense Cholesky step; it is meant for tens of nodes, not city networks
  (no sparse solver, no extended-period simulation, no tanks or pressure-driven demand).
- `peltonRunner` is the one-dimensional momentum theory: windage, bucket entry losses and jet spread are not
  modelled beyond the bucket retention factor.
- `hydraulicJump` is for a rectangular, horizontal, frictionless bed; the roller length is Hager's 1990 fit,
  stated for 2.5 < F1 < 8.
- Water properties are valid from 0 to 100 degrees Celsius at atmospheric pressure.
- These are functions, not a `PhysicsWorld` solver: nothing steps with the world or couples to the shallow water.

The optional entry measures 7,681 B min+gzip and loads no Wasm. Core and stage gain zero bytes.

### Grounded glacier and ice-sheet flow (ICE-02)

The rectangular x-z grid resolves isothermal, grounded, no-slip ice with the shallow-ice approximation,
a constant Glen exponent of 3, and constant or per-cell climatic inputs. It uses the world's gravity
component along the vertical axis. External edges are closed to ice. Horizontal stress transmission,
basal sliding and lubrication, floating shelves and evolving bed topography are outside this model.
At an open-water boundary, waterline or flotation failure removes a whole grid cell's ice. Dry cliff
release needs full crevasse penetration. Resolve the terminus with smaller cells for smaller events.
The volume ports support downstream motion and impact solvers.

The step lags the nonlinear face weight and uses a symmetric backward-Euler solve with a relative
residual norm target of √(f64 machine epsilon). The initial residual is evaluated from differences
in surface elevation. Limit accelerated time steps for accuracy on steep or rapidly evolving terrain.
D8 drains each source to an outlet or local depression during the same tick. It represents no
routing delay, subglacial storage or lake spill. Discharge is in m³ per world second even if the ice
runs on accelerated physical time. A failed tick leaves its published banks and cumulative budget at their
last accepted values.

An independent borehole comparison at Athabasca gives 75.99 m/yr depth-mean downslope flow against
49.6 m/yr measured. The model's geometry sensitivity is 60.47–94.67 m/yr. At Insunnguata Sermia the
nominal modeled no-slip surface deformation is 19.46 m/yr against the borehole estimate of 4.6
[0.4, 10.8] m/yr. The published GPS surface speed is 114.8 m/yr with 110.2 m/yr attributed to
basal sliding. The model's geometry sensitivity is 9.42–34.93 m/yr for deformation. The two checks
use independent thickness and surface-slope observations and the default ice softness. They show where a
grounded, isothermal no-slip strip loses accuracy under strong lateral stress, depth-varying ice
temperature or basal sliding. [Raymond (1971)](https://doi.org/10.3189/S0022143000012995).
[Maier et al. (2019)](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aaw5406).

The optional entry is 5,930 B min+gzip with a 6,186 B ceiling. Plain and shared Wasm are 17,775 B
and 17,863 B raw, or 7,305 B and 7,371 B gzip. A solver reserves 260 B of arena and scratch per cell,
144 B of fixed config and budget, 104 B of native job data, 40 B of work receipt and a 64 KiB aligned
stack for each participant. With helpers, the control words add 4 B per helper and 20 B of fixed
storage. Worker jobs are partitioned by cell. The caller assembles and solves the grid, applies
ordered face transfers, then routes meltwater and accepts the complete result. Core and stage
receive zero bytes.

### Ground animal locomotion (LIFE-02)

`@margoengine/physics/locomotion` hosts independent body rows, with a one-dimensional clocked chain for a snake
and fixed world-space stance contacts for lizards, insects, spiders and crabs. Each legged animal has an additional
torso contact. Body state uses 112 B per row, published contact uses 104 B per element, and three f64 foothold
values per element are part of replay. Both optional modules import the same world memory and use one static
slot. Each native participant uses an aligned 64 KiB stack. The world rate ranges from 60 to 7,680 Hz.
Configuration rejects stiffness, damping or gait frequencies that require a faster step. Storage scales with
body and contact counts. The caller prepares all contacts and samples the bed in order. Native helpers advance
disjoint bodies before the accepted state and both publications change. Numeric or terrain failure preserves the
previous accepted pose, anchors, contacts and work receipt.

The snake's motion uses a planar travelling wave across a heightfield and yaw about world up. The compiled leg
templates use a single rigid torso and massless compressive legs, with stick-phase anchors and contact forces
limited by the ground friction cone. These models resolve terrain height and contact normals. A terrain with
caves or overhanging holds needs a collider-based foot placement system. The pose/contact ports expose
kinematics and reaction wrenches for downstream animation or an erosion consumer. Inter-animal collision and
feedback into the live terrain require downstream coupling.

With independently measured cloth friction and published shape inputs, the held-out flat snake speed
is 0.144 modeled versus 0.22 ± 0.08 body lengths per cycle. At +5° the model moves downslope at
−0.241 body lengths per cycle while the tracked animals move uphill at +0.13. The first observed reversal
lies in 5°–9°, while the model reverses between 0° and 1.9°. Doubling the links leaves that reversal gap.
Two steep runs leave the reported plank dimensions before a complete comparison. The solver lacks the
contact-load redistribution and nonplanar movement observed in living snakes. [Hu et al. (2009)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0812533106).

The optional entry measures 25,353 B raw and 9,726 B gzip with a 10,018 B ceiling. The plain and
shared Wasm assets measure 11,448 and 11,536 B raw, or 5,236 and 5,298 B gzip. Native jobs store
72 B of fixed call data, an 8 B range per body and a seven-word work receipt per participant.
Core and stage receive zero bytes.

## Material ageing (BIO-04)

State is one uniform column per material patch. Atmospheric loss uses ISO 9223 annual inputs
and the ISO 9224 carbon steel or copper average curves. Instantaneous local climates are a
piecewise-constant equivalent-exposure approximation when used in these empirical annual curves.
Current density sets uniform immersion attack. Localized pits, galvanic pairs, coatings
with delamination or adhesion, and loss of a structure's load capacity require extra models.

Wood decay represents untreated pine sapwood at 0–30 °C and at least 95% RH. The exposed wood
model uses that calibration. Wood loss is expressed as equivalent thickness at unchanged surface area
and density. The immersion fraction suppresses atmospheric pine decay. Marine fouling is one
aggregate population limited by free area, with caller-provided rates to distinguish conditions.
Submerged loss of wood by marine borers is outside the fit.

Limestone models carbonate dissolution from incident water and an optional dry deposition term.
Physical exfoliation and freeze-thaw are separate effects. The appearance result uses per-patch
diffuse layer transport for the metal colors and a coverage mix for the aggregate fouling.
The material consumes linear PBR values. Multi-spectral gloss, grain, individual corrosion
pits and run-off streak geometry require authored patch variation or other algorithms.

The accepted history and surface use 96 bytes per patch. The corresponding trial adds 96. Optional native
execution adds 72 bytes of model input and 80 bytes of climate input per patch, a 32-byte job and 48 bytes
of counters per participant, plus a 64 KiB stack with alignment per participant. The registry mirrors the
surface. Optional workers join before the complete state changes. A rejected trial leaves the accepted fields intact. The optional entry measures 8,069 B gzip. Each lazy, slot-free Wasm variant is
6,058 B raw and 2,782 B gzip.

### BIO-04 measured copper and carbon-steel coupon losses

For Rapa Nui copper exposed between April 2010 and April 2013, the measured cumulative losses are
2.10 and 3.75 µm at years one and three. The ISO-based production path predicts 1.26 and 2.83 µm
using independent year-specific deposition values and weather read from the publication. The weather
readout sensitivity spans 1.14–1.40 and 2.57–3.13 µm. It remains below the observed reporting bands.
[Vera et al. (2022), Table 1 and Figs. 3 and 6](https://doi.org/10.3390/met12122082).

Milan carbon-steel coupons lost 6.92 µm over ten months. The model predicts 5.28 µm when the first-year
ambient averages stand in for the shorter exposure window and chloride is set to zero as treated by
the investigators. A 0.4 mg/(m² day) chloride sensitivity gives 6.12 µm. The diagnostic uses the
published atmospheric SO₂ concentration converted to deposition. Neither study's measured loss is fitted
or used as an input. Refining from 12 to 48 updates per exposure year changes the predictions by less
than 4 × 10⁻¹⁵ µm. The coupon comparisons test two settings for uniform atmospheric penetration.
Pitting, fine runoff streaks, measured spectra and predictive marine current remain open.
[Paterlini et al. (2024), Tables 6 and 9](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma17246211).
[Diagnostic](../packages/physics/scripts/bio04-ageing-measured.mjs).

### Iceberg rigid-body dynamics and calving (ICE-03)

The optional 60 Hz solver handles homogeneous rectangular solids with exact planar hydrostatic
loads, six degrees of freedom, quadratic normal-pressure drag and prescribed wet-face recession.
It uses dyadic substeps from hydrostatic stiffness, rotation, and drag. The ablation step moves the
centre of mass with the shape. It preserves lost solid volume in the freshwater budget at
1000 kg/m³. Release sources and WakeSolver must publish at the same 60 Hz and use one origin cell.
A WakeSolver receives two area-scaled patches per changing body and gives the linear wave response.

Wind and water currents are each uniform and use the still-water plane. The model excludes large
wave feedback on the body, fragment collisions, grounding and sea-ice resistance. Calving sites
have explicitly allocated body rows, with queued volumes retained across snapshots when full.
At its original landing, the optional iceberg entry measured 5,162 B gzip with a 5,418 B ceiling. The plain and shared
assets each measure 9,128 B raw and 4,318 B gzip. Physics/sea measures 7,745 B gzip
with the field reader, with an 8,001 B ceiling. Core plus stage remains 24,820 B gzip.

### Live forest ecosystem (BIO-03)

The optional forest entry measures 10,378 B gzip. Each lazy Wasm variant is 3,337 B raw and 1,757 B gzip.
The shared Biomes native helper measures 601 B gzip and starts for multiple participants only.

The optional `@margoengine/biomes/forest` advances individual crowns with millimetre radii, centimetre positions
within 100 km of the origin and Q16 competition. Default capacity is 16,384 trees including snags. Set capacity for
a plot with `limit`, up to the offline model's one million trees. The annual transition uses one grid of crown
neighbours sized to twice capacity or the next power of two. Native workspace bytes scale as four times
`(capacity + 3 * tableSize)`, with a further four per capacity row for shade output. Native scratch is rebuilt
each year. One participant builds the table in the established order. The optional workers query disjoint range
rows with SIMD pairs for overlap distances. Work records use 32 bytes for the job and 40 bytes per participant,
with a 64 KiB stack plus alignment for each participant and control words for shared jobs.

Population and permanent lean hold 44 bytes per reserved tree in each of two banks. Clock metadata uses
64 bytes per bank. Each bank also holds four f64 annual channels and one duration per distinct species
flood depth per patch, plus four accepted patch fields. The registry mirrors those four publications.
The patch banks change together after valid input or a completed annual transition. Match extent and signed
origin with water, landscape and snow readers.

The patch placement approximation bins an entire crown at its stem. Cover is the sum of projected crown shares
limited to unity. Fuel sums individual crown mass so overlapping live crowns still carry fuel. The wind rule
updates the crown axis in proportion to new projected area. It represents long-term flagging by changing the crown
axis rather than tracking individual branches or modelling physiological dormancy, burial or ice damage. Flood
tolerance represents measured depth and duration for one species and life stage. The burn and fuel-moisture input
is an explicit versioned port. Cover, roots and canopy fuel update at annual boundaries.

The offline and native stand models share a geometric crown-overlap approximation, a logistic crown-radius
increment and authored age and shade mortality. Vertical gap light, photosynthetic carbon balance, measured
species-specific mortality and allometry remain outside this model.

#### BIO-03 Douglas-fir survival in the Wind River spacing trial

The production diagnostic models the planted cohort in 0.4 ha plots, using the published 1–6 m spacings
and two-year-old stock. It uses ideal lattices, eight fixed seeds, a generic fir and no simulated recruitment or
replacement. Year-40 survival increases with spacing in both the model and the trial. At 3, 4, 5 and 6 m the
modeled survival fractions are 0.586, 0.830, 0.955 and 0.962, against 0.68, 0.81, 0.83 and 0.90 measured.
Three of the four modeled means lie outside the reported 95% intervals. The largest error is 17.81 percentage
points at 1 m spacing after 16 years, where the solver gives 0.978 versus approximately 0.80 measured.
At 2 m after 32 years, changing the unmeasured initial crown radius from 5 to 10 cm moves modeled survival
by more than 24 percentage points. Figure reading contributes an estimated ±0.025 to graph-only values.
The field trial included early replacements, ingrowth and disturbance beyond the modeled cohort.
[Slesak et al. (2025), §3.1 and Fig. 1c](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.foreco.2025.122724).
[Curtis et al. (2016), installed layout](https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70173842).
[Diagnostic](../packages/biomes/scripts/bio03-forest-measured.mjs).

### Grounded biped and quadruped gait (LIFE-01)

The optional `@margoengine/physics/legged` entry and the ground-animal entry share one slot-free SIMD kernel.
Each moving body has 16 B of stored target, 40 B of gait state and two or four persistent foot contact points,
plus the torso. A deck uses its declared planar rectangular support and the rigid body's pose. The projected COM
sets the approximation for angularly varying contact-surface velocity. A highly articulated surface needs a
contactable support-patch field. Planting and flight follow a reduced spring-mass model with a finite support
couple. The renderer's baked export clips keep a single pace for each clip, while runtime horse posing uses the
actual instantaneous stride.

The native dispatcher partitions disjoint body rows. Within each row, stance forces retain their deterministic
order. The legged adapter keeps one backup of its controlled drive profiles and foot clocks. It validates gait
and signed deck reaction candidates before accepting the ground pose, stance anchors, contacts and native receipt.
Its deck adds a staged six-word f64 impulse row alongside each published body row.

#### LIFE-01 measured treadmill gait and forelimb loading

An independent instrumented-treadmill study reports 55.13, 51.46, 89.58 and 82.44 strides/min for
Franches-Montagnes and Warmblood cohorts in walk and trot order. The four representative models at the reported
speeds give 62.77, 61.02, 97.22 and 95.14 strides/min. The observed vertical impulse share on the forelimbs is
59.26%, 58.11%, 56.27% and 56.42%. The model gives 44.24%, 45.01%, 40.70% and 40.84%, or 13.10–15.58
percentage points less. Separately varying speed by the study's reported standard deviation or the default
leg length by 10% keeps the predicted front share below 47.28%. These central comparisons use the reported
mean mass and belt speed, equal default engine leg geometry and independent measured response. The published
sample deviation describes the cohorts. The source lacks matching Warmblood lower limb geometry. A validated
fore-hind load distribution and articulated horse model remain open. [Gmel et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jevs.2024.105005)

The legged entry measures 38,252 B raw and 13,912 B gzip with a 14,330 B ceiling. The shared ground entry
measures 25,543 B raw and 9,785 B gzip against 10,015 B. Both use the existing ground kernel files.
Horses measures 40,737 B raw and 16,724 B gzip. Its gait utilities measure 2,738 B raw and 1,266 B gzip.

### Pack ice and floe contact (ICE-04)

Planar circular floes have constant mass, a shrinking level-ice footprint and conserved raft and
ridge volumes. The pile is a subgrid volume on the originating floe. Independent ridge blocks,
finger rafting, bending under waves, welds between floes and shoreline grounding require explicit
geometry outside this model. The deterministic contact sweep approximates multiple simultaneous
contacts. Vessel bounds are horizontal waterline capsules and send XZ impulse and yaw torque to
the rigid world. The method resolves broken pack ice rather than applying a continuous-sheet
resistance regression. The Water adapter displays equivalent thickness and a water-surface tangent.

The optional Physics entry measures 5,112 B gzip with a 5,368 B ceiling. Each lazy Wasm asset uses 5,716 B raw and 2,534 B gzip. Water/ice measures 13,297 B gzip with a 13,364 B ceiling. Core plus stage stays at 24,820 B gzip.

### Crush response for civilian barriers (BREAK-03)

An already contacted patch maintains a unilateral damped backing response while its geometric gap remains
compressed inside the patch radius. A sustained 30 N load settles to 90.23 mm against a fixed support and
95.11 mm between the movable specimens. Both match the discrete loaded equilibrium derived from the
contact step and rigid substeps. The movable pair conserves total momentum with reciprocal inputs.
The fixture preserves one material impact through six seconds of applied load and exact snapshot replay.
The durable damage ledger records material work. Optional dry friction applies one isotropic coefficient
for sticking and sliding, with a circular limit from the current normal impulse. The normal solve runs
first, and the friction solve includes its change to the velocity at the same contact point. Coupled
contact evolution is resolved on successive ticks. Distributed panel collapse remains open.

The short hollow square-tube curve predicts 940.1 J at 100 mm axial compression from geometry and
independent AA6063-T5 tensile properties. The five measured Yob et al. specimens absorbed 897.4–1048.77 J.
This is mean progressive folding work for that tube and loading range. Initial peak load, force
oscillations, global buckling and material rate dependence need higher-fidelity constitutive and geometry
models. The same envelope transfers work to the tube in a separately tested rigid-sled simulation.
Continuous contact yields under sustained compression and preserves its permanent stroke and work on unloading.
A live displacement-controlled rigid fixture yields 940.075 J at 100 mm, within the same
measured range at both 32 and 128 driving increments. Its implicit integration adds numerical damping.

The Smith-method section balances plate and stiffener axial forces and evaluates the moment at an imposed
curvature. It follows authored load-shortening curves and needs the prior reference strain to select among
multiple stable branches. It reports 153.6 MN·m² for the independently measured N200 box-girder elastic
reloading case, with an observed 140–160 MN·m² band. The section uses a sectional constitutive envelope.
Cyclic unloading and dynamic hull deformation remain open.

The supported rectangular plate resolves the first elastic buckling mode and returns a sampled deformed
surface. Three early measured loads for Stein’s five-half-wave bay agree within 0.02 on the normalized load axis. The supports stay
straight in-plane and free of in-plane shear. High deflection, mode switching, post-yield rupture and
full hull shell coupling remain open. The fixture renders an 8.48 mm crest with the sampled normals on
native WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer.
An optional continuous patch can also drive that mesh from its own contact stroke. The current and
residual shapes use the station's authored force curve and the first-mode shape model. The live steel
fixture renders an 8.46 mm crest under load and 7.45 mm after release on both backends. Fully exhausted
span exposes the stroke and seal state. Topology-changing breakup remains open.

An authored girder seam can hold and release two adjacent dynamic rigid parts. It resolves
one projected bending curvature with aligned rest frames and three-axis point-spring
translation. The angular and point reactions are split within each step. The joint preserves
its failure curvature and peak tensile strain after release. Use pre-separated meshes and
body-local collider assets for each part. A compartment's authored aperture can latch when
the seam breaks. Its location and dimensions come from the hull opening, independent of the
subsequent gap between the halves. Distributed shell fracture, cyclic plastic history,
automatic shell-part generation and the measured floating-tank breakup remain open.

Ground stations intersect a finite triangulated heightfield along their local linear trajectory
for one coupling tick. The first intersected face supplies the reaction normal throughout the
tick. Each station has its own authored anchor and material. The bed acts as an immovable
support. Deforming sediment, obstructions with overhangs, and distributed plate tearing around
a rock require additional models. The oblique and cross-grid tests use analytical terrain input.
Measured time histories of a grounded hull and plate tearing during raking remain open.

The circular indentation law covers a thin clamped sheet loaded centrally by a smooth
sphere. It treats the plate as an axisymmetric membrane with plane-strain plastic flow.
Initial elastic bending, edge sliding, unloading, and post-rupture force and crack growth
remain outside this law. The solver prepares a 96-interval loading table and uses 48
log-radius midpoint panels for the deformation integral. The rendered shape retains the
fixed edge. Against four measured circular sheets, rupture stroke differs by at most 5.5%
and work up to rupture by at most 11.8%. The 13 mm case has the largest energy deficit.
The native station resolves a rate-independent normal contact event with no elastic rebound.
It supports continued contact up to its last intact load. It retains the pre-failure dent and
sets the seal flag at rupture. The SEA-10 aperture uses its authored geometry. An actual
distributed crack surface, plate fragments and strain-rate dependence remain open.

The distributed shell uses constant-strain membrane triangles and elastic interior hinges on
a consistently wound manifold sheet of uniform thickness. It accepts fixed supports and
vertex loads. It uses one through-thickness material state per face and a small material-strain
law in the rotating element frame. The optional Hill-48 yield uses the projected rolling
direction and three uniaxial strain ratios. Its held-out AA5086 initial biaxial yield is within
1.80% of the three measured values. Large-strain anisotropy and anisotropic fracture remain open.
Hinge stiffness depends on triangulation. Each explicit
substep is at most 0.5 divided by the rest mesh frequency bound. Large deformation can
increase the true frequency, so refine the time step and compare the result at the applied
load. The solver rejects more than 8,192 substeps per world tick. Rigid contact accepts centred
spheres, a matching shell and rigid tick rate, and at least two rigid substeps for a moving
body. Each sphere uses the closest live triangle by default. The optional contact manifold
uses separate local minima and counts a shared feature once. It checks one geometry candidate
per face per sphere per force evaluation, plus incident vertices for a boundary candidate.
With friction it repeats the same geometry check before the half-kick. The step bound
includes the maximum Hertz tangent of every face when the manifold is enabled. Both modes
use an authored Hertz interface modulus and a compliant skin. Positive optional Coulomb friction uses barycentric
material-point mobility and the sphere's staged angular inertia. Multiple spheres apply their
half-step projections in authored order, with multiple contacts for each sphere processed in
face order. A simultaneous global friction solve, arbitrary rigid shapes, distributed pressure,
sheet self-contact, swept time of impact and layered plastic bending remain open.
Analytic tests cover world motion, reactions, elastic bending, plastic history and contact
momentum. The measured rupture check above uses the separate circular station.
The distributed seam model opens authored coincident boundaries after both quadrature
points release. It uses the same separation law for tensile and tangential relative motion.
An already released seam preserves its fracture work even if its physical opening closes.
The aperture area is the two-triangle surface between the current edge pairs.
SEA-10 converts both live triangles to 16 hydraulic cells each. Their integration preserves
triangular area and approximates the height density within each strip. The sea level is read
at the area-weighted centroid. This supplies inflow and adds carried water to the hull.
The geometry source is the shell's separate world trajectory, so align the panel with the
compartment and use the same world scale. Closing the geometric gap stops flow while the
seam remains fractured. The optional pressure feedback uses the previous same-rate
flooding step, a level sampled at each opening, and current shell normals and
waterline clipping. It supports stationary fixed hulls with downward Y gravity.
Structural support reactions stay with the shell, and the authored-force ledger
excludes pressure work. Moving hull attachments, transient fluid pressure, feedback
from wall displacement into compartment volume, unilateral lip contact,
automatic crack paths, mode-dependent cohesive properties and independent measured
shell fracture remain open.
[Return pressure tests](whitepaper/reproduce.md#break-03-hydrostatic-shell-feedback)
The optional shell loader fetches the 19,230 B plain Wasm asset (8,975 B gzip). On hosts with
shared-memory support it also fetches the shared asset, the same raw and gzip size.

The optional native shell work record holds six f64 words per solver. Counts
report interval work at the chosen resolution. Candidate face checks include
the AABB visits even when a sphere misses and the repeated manifold friction
checks. Pressure face visits include unassigned faces. At fixed element size
the 32/128-face shell fixtures use 1,152/4,608 membrane evaluations.
[Work counts](whitepaper/reproduce.md#break-03-native-shell-work)

Staged contact can use a positive piecewise-linear virgin loading envelope with increasing total
and recoverable-adjusted permanent stroke. The only supported unloading law is one linear
stiffness followed by elastic backing at compaction. Continuous contact requires a rigid
rate fast enough to keep the implicit response monotone across each traversed falling branch.
Use the same rate and place crush before rigid in their staggered group.
The held-out single-coach test qualifies compression from a pretest design curve at 960 and 1920 Hz.
It predicts rebound speeds of 1.49–1.61 mph versus about 3.3 mph measured. An independently tested Accord coupe qualifies the full-width 56 km/h road-car pulse for one vehicle family. Rebound speed is 0.42–0.44 m/s high. Occupant motion, other road-car families, oblique impacts and inter-car joints remain open.

Two held-out Tabri model-ship trials predict compression work within 6.5% at 960
and 1920 Hz with one separate calibration specimen. Strokes match to within half
a 125 Hz motion sample. Peak force is up to 12.7% high. These checks use
published instantaneous wet inertia for the foam-panel test ships.
[Model-ship comparison](whitepaper/reproduce.md#break-03-held-out-model-ship-contacts)

The paired HullSolver and circular panel station also compare dry and
carried-water recoil in a moving hull. That case uses the specimen's
measured geometry and coupon inputs. It reaches rupture with water and
an intact permanent dent when empty. The panel model is a local
rigid-plastic station, with its retained shape sampled in the hull's frame.
[Carried-water rupture case](whitepaper/reproduce.md#break-03-carried-water-and-hull-panel-rupture)

Station-level input curves represent creased plating, rail absorbers, or road crumple members. The default event mode resolves normal loading and release during one 60 Hz coupling interval. Continuous patches evaluate one normal load and return map per tick. Use distinct contact pairs and exclude their ordinary rigid response during the crush event. A paired optional hull contact channel includes instantaneous exterior added mass and carried water at a station. It requires the same-rate order hull, crush, rigid. The calculation freezes the six-axis mobility over each 60 Hz contact interval. Unpaired bodies, rigid bodies with locked angular axes, and distributed shell contacts use the dry rigid response. Hydroelastic impact, radiation forces generated by the contact itself, and fully coupled pressure on a deforming shell remain open. A linked authored compartment aperture opens at full seal loss from the stroke threshold and supplies inflow and carried mass through SEA-10. A shell seam can link its live opening geometry instead. With compartments, hull snapshots include inertial history for any carried floodwater even when exterior added mass is disabled. ### Lubrication films on moving surfaces (FLUID-07)

A depth column assumes a film thin compared with the distance it varies over. The model fits
water rivulets, flattening droplets and puddle margins. One film patch has planar orthogonal
coordinates and can carry a sampled substrate height. Viscous shear is held at its midpoint
over each coupling interval. Strongly curved glass needs multiple patches and flying splash
droplets need a separate ballistic solver. Rim coalescence is by the shared depth field.
The film accepts registered impact events and transfers their pressure to a local wake, while
the film keeps their deposited water. The `suspended` option includes adverse normal gravity
and requires positive surface tension. It resolves the early growth of an underside film
within the long-wave approximation. With the silicone oil properties in Fermigier et al.
(1992), the predicted most amplified wavelength is 13.2 mm and their observed roll spacing
was 12.5 mm. Pinch-off, steep contact lines, optical interference and ocean rain damping
remain open.

The optional `wetting` model gives the film a finite equilibrium contact angle by adding
Schwartz–Eley disjoining pressure. The shallow-slope approximation applies to gently sloped
free surfaces. A linear continuation replaces the singular sub-precursor pressure at unresolved
thicknesses. The tests check the derived precursor-mode decay, nonlinear energy dissipation and
water balance. The complete-wetting capillary limit matches the independently measured
0.094–0.125 radius exponent on 40 × 40 and 80 × 80 grids. A separate gravity-dominated release
on horizontal Perspex predicts the measured absolute radius history within 3% on two grids.
This comparison uses the bulk radius inferred from the radial mass moment. Absolute capillary
contact-line traces and measured partially wetting slip remain open.
[Reproduce](whitepaper/reproduce.md#fluid-07-measured-horizontal-spreading)
The optional backing angle map adds one f64 value per film cell. Its pressure and
implicit stiffness both vary by cell, and the exact two-cell check covers conservative
motion toward the more wettable side and snapshot replay.
The optional advancing and receding angles add a rate-independent resistance on the
resolved precursor. It uses seven f64 scratch values per cell. The residual ceiling is
512 iterations per wetting substep. Evidence covers a two-cell force balance, both
directions on a 32 × 32 tilted film, and deterministic replay. Independent measured
sliding and cases with a steep contact slope remain open.
An explicitly placed, wetted circular rim can collect a single boundary cell's discharge and
release timed droplets. Its quasistatic size uses Mori (1990) with a 0–1.4 diameter-to-ideal-volume
scale ratio and negligible gas density. The 3.2 mm, 1 mL/min water control predicts 50.17 μL
per drop, 2.6% below the 51.5 μL cycle volume from Zhang and Basaran (1996). Each event carries
the rim pose and velocity. `ThinFilmDropFlight` uses that velocity as constant over the source
tick to recover the release position, then advances the drop relative to the air. It tracks
diameters from 1 μm to 7 mm at a configurable capacity and expires each drop by age. An
optional planar receiver absorbs incoming drops in its UV bounds. Static planes deposit
volume in the film and can send normal momentum to its wake. A rigidly mounted receiver
follows the linear translation between consecutive rigid poses and sends relative normal
momentum to its mounted film. The default holds orientation fixed. `followRotation` uses
the normalized shortest chord of the sampled orientations and sends the contact normal
and lever arm. The endpoint poses represent at most a half-turn of rotation between samples.
`captureEdges` includes the wet rectangle's edges and corners on its liquid side.
Splashing, rebound, satellite breakup and free pinch-off away from a configured outlet remain open.
[Reproduce](whitepaper/reproduce.md#fluid-07-circular-sill-drops)
The optional `hydrostaticLoad` adds the film's normal gravitational force and moment to
its rigid mount. The coupled test checks both a supported tray and an off-centre underside
patch. The optional `impactRecoil` sends the resolved volume's incoming normal impulse
and its moment to the rigid mount over one world tick. Transient added mass, tangential
wall traction and the time profile of the collision force remain open.
For fully developed glycerol flow on a 20° glass plate, the modeled depths at the 350 mm probe
are 0.422, 0.470 and 0.506 mm for the three calibrated flows of Wang, Jia and Duan (2020).
Each falls in the independent PIV/PLIF depth band on two grid resolutions. These measurements
cover steady laminar flow. [Reproduce](whitepaper/reproduce.md#fluid-07-measured-inclined-film)
An independent glycerine release video also supports the cube-root law for the incline front
before fingering. It supplies a normalized front increment. The absolute movie lengths,
recording-to-laboratory clock relationship and finger growth remain outside the validation.
[Reproduce](whitepaper/reproduce.md#fluid-07-incline-front-history)

`surfaceGeometry()` draws the cell-centred height field as a triangulated free surface in
the backing's local frame. This geometry has the spatial resolution of the film grid.
The window fixture uses screen-space refraction and spherical drop geometry. Its interior
view captures the distant film before the glass to test both interfaces. The fixtures
compare the same rigid pose with each liquid mesh hidden in turn. Complete production-cut
review remains open.
[Reproduce](whitepaper/reproduce.md#fluid-07-moving-window-render)

One-row and one-column strips use a direct banded pressure solve with optional advancing and
receding contact angles. The capillary regression covers a 128-cell strip at 20 μm spacing.
Two-dimensional patches use the iterative pressure solve. It preconditions each row and
column as a block when the ratio of maximum to minimum positive face mobility exceeds
four. If a face diagonal times floating-point epsilon exceeds the relative pressure tolerance,
the solver reaches that tolerance with up to two cell-space corrections. Each correction
allows two conjugate directions per cell and the true face residual determines acceptance.
The strip retention check uses a derived force bracket. The circular cap force predicts the
measured SLIC water tilt to its reported degree on both grids. Direct dynamic onset
qualification remains open.

Suspended films use the full curvature of a height graph with gravity and pressure in the
same wet-face flux. The held-out pendant-drop thinning check covers the attached drop at
five minutes. The graph cannot represent an overhang or the topology change at pinch-off.
[Reproduce](whitepaper/reproduce.md#fluid-07-suspended-film)

The optional thin-film entry is 15,193 B gzip with a 15,631 B ceiling. Both Wasm assets are 30,756 B raw and each is 11,743 B gzip.

### Environmental airborne transport (ATMO-06)

The optional `@margoengine/physics/airborne` advances mineral dust, freshwater mist and sea spray at 240 Hz.
A representative parcel carries its combined mass and 16 f64 state words. A separate candidate region keeps
accepted parcels, pending releases and the ledger intact if the next interval fails. At capacity, source mass
waits for a deterministic emission turn. Origin cells are signed integers and parcel coordinates stay in local
metres. Wind points translate to the Wind's origin cell. The caller samples inputs and folds mass and terrain
contact in stable order. Browser threading needs an isolated world Worker and shared memory. Work receipts
are outside snapshots.

The drag law assumes rounded particles. The Stokes option is restricted to Re ≤ 0.1. The default has the
Schiller–Naumann transition and a constant-drag high-Re approximation. Prescribed Wind and drag are frozen
over each 1/240 s interval. Turbulence is homogeneous and Gaussian, with zero initial gust. Diffusion-limited
evaporation uses prescribed humidity and a salt-dependent equilibrium diameter. Dry salt is conserved. The
terrain sweep subdivides the path every half horizontal grid interval up to 4,096 samples per tick. Contact
moves mass into the deposition ledger. Rebound and resuspension remain open.

The natural spray volume draws accepted mass, droplet diameter and material density. The render resolution
sets the Gaussian footprint for a representative parcel. Its normalized kernel conserves optical area in
the continuous limit. The original film installations and the separate Water spray pool remain open. Independent Gunn–Kinzer and
Beard–Pruppacher settling comparisons cover 0.1–0.5 mm. Several Gunn–Kinzer results exceed the reported
measurement resolution and uncertainty. Ventilation, wet-bulb cooling, inhomogeneous stochastic drift, other
materials, droplet collisions and feedback to the air remain open.

The Physics entry measures 11,050 B gzip within 11,319 B. Environment density-volume measures 5,140 B gzip
within 5,396 B. Each local native image is 1,444 B raw and 918 B gzip. Core and Stage gain no bytes.

### Developmental wood growth (BIO-02)

The parametric solver places shoots on developmental season boundaries on the 60 Hz world clock. Branches
persist. The allocated topology follows the supplied productive lifetime and the minimum eligible extension.
The light grid uses cubic voxels with a vertical, distance-attenuated penumbra and a local light gradient.
Sites outside the grid receive open light. Roots transform the signed soil-grid origin when `cellSize` is
supplied and sample a configurable storage response for the corresponding HYDRO-02 row. Branches and soil
history update together after a successful season. The renderer adapter rounds local geometry to f32.
The model leaves root extraction, root branching, leaf physiology, permanent branch re-bending, shedding
and moving obstructions open. The topological and resource passes run in parent order on the caller.

The world scratch and accepted banks store 104 bytes per reserved internode each, 32 additional bytes
per reserved internode for resources, and 16 bytes per plant for accepted and candidate soil history.
Each bank has a 16-byte header. Both branch registry mirrors are additional. Shadow scratch takes
8 bytes per voxel. The fixed occupancy takes 8 bytes per voxel outside the arena. Native helpers
use the same scratch grid and retain obstacle-then-internode addition order. Source records reserve
24 bytes each, with a 40-byte batch and 32 bytes of counters per participant. Each participant has
a 64 KiB stack plus alignment. Shared jobs have an additional control block. The optional entry measures
8,689 B gzip. Each lazy Wasm build is 2,016 B raw and 1,215 B gzip, and the shared Biomes helper is 601 B gzip.

### BIO-02 red maple growth under field shade

Gottschalk's field shade-tent experiment reported two seasonal height means at eight treatments for red
maple germinated after the experiment started. The production diagnostic drives the generic README species
with the reported light fractions and no fitted growth data. After two years, 8% and 57% light produce
38.4 cm and 80.0 cm. Their held-out measurements are 9.3 cm and 33.7 cm. The model overestimates all
16 means, by up to 57.3 cm. The modeled two-year heights from 20% to 94% light coincide at the internode
length cap. The measured means across those treatments range from 22.7 cm to 33.7 cm. Halving voxel side
from 7.62 cm to 3.81 cm leaves predicted heights unchanged. Reducing the assumed relative water supply
from 1 to 0.75 moves predicted heights up to 10 cm and still overestimates all means. The one-decimal
published heights carry a 0.05 cm reading half-width. The source gives no per-treatment dispersion.
[Gottschalk (1985), Tables 2 and 4](https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/47682).
[Diagnostic](../packages/biomes/scripts/bio02-growth-measured.mjs).

### Enclosed and urban acoustics (SOUND-02)

`@margoengine/physics/room-sound` separates finite specular paths from a linear low-frequency wave field.
Paths accept convex planar faces and trace direct and reflected segments through the requested order, default two.
The bounded search reports when its candidate image budget is exceeded. The ray gains are relative to a one-metre
monopole and keep pressure signs. Their fractional sample impulses use two-point interpolation.

The native scheme has cubic voxels and one real reflection coefficient per air cell at its closed faces.
Normal-incidence wall admittance is exact in the model. Grazing and mixed-frequency impedance need finer
geometry or a richer material boundary. For an axis wave resolved with ten cells per wavelength, the
sinusoidal stencil bounds numerical phase speed from below by 1 − π²/600 of the configured speed.
Use a finer grid for higher frequencies. The grid has reflecting edges and one pressure coefficient per
mask cell. The default 0.85 is a generic pressure coefficient. Supply measured wall coefficients for a
specific room. A measured frequency-dependent boundary, air absorption by frequency, absorbing open edges
and a live terrain geometry consumer remain open. The path model uses finite specular polygons and
leaves geometric edge diffraction and a coupled late reverberation response for later.

The valid wave volume and substep count must fit Wasm memory with accepted and candidate arrays.
Inputs or derived samples outside the numeric range report a coded action before publication.
Choose shared world memory and a blocking agent for two or four native participants. Each
sample needs a synchronization point before publishing its source and receiver, so the default
one participant suits small rooms. Work includes padded guard and solid pairs actually visited by SIMD.
The optional room-sound entry measures 9,125 B min+gzip. Each lazy Wasm variant is 2,717 B raw and 1,393 B gzip.

The BRAS RS1 comparison in `packages/physics/scripts/sound02-bras-measured.mjs` holds out ten rigid-floor
excess delays. All fall within the engineering allowance of roughly 0.16–0.18 ms, and the predictions
are consistently 0.042–0.133 ms early. The estimate combines the experiment's position cross-check,
44.1 kHz sample resolution and a ±1 m/s air-speed sensitivity. Amplitude, decay and other measured
scenes remain open.

### Three-dimensional viscoplastic material (FLUID-06)

The material point field follows finite strain and plastic shear in a uniform three-dimensional
grid. Longitudinal elastic waves limit its internal step. Rest density is fixed, while current
volume changes with the volumetric strain `J`. Coulomb contact applies on closed box faces
and a triangulated sampled terrain bed. The optional implicit solvent diffusion is on occupied
grid nodes. Resolve strong gradients with several points per cell. Very thin stretched
filaments can become under-resolved until an adaptive particle split/merge pass is available.
Bulk elastic stress is weakly compressible, with no incompressible pressure projection. The
entry emits positions and stresses for a separate renderer and leaves grain segregation and
bed entrainment to their own solvers.

A tick must keep the incremental deformation determinant strictly positive throughout each
microstep. Near singular, numerically indeterminate paths are rejected.
The explicit tick has a 4,096-microstep limit. The solver stages its grid return, point records
and cumulative inlet and outlet ledgers before acceptance. The 0.25 terrain and wall friction
default is a starting parameter. Use the material and substrate's measured friction when available.
A timed field can feed the solver and replay exactly. The original PA-60 scene inlet and two-way
sediment entrainment still need their own work. The screen-space surface reads accepted particles,
using their chosen render radius and float32 positions. Use a nearby render cell and the particle
limit in the Water package.

The shared path partitions native node normalization and contact and each 27-node
grid-to-particle return. Particle-to-grid scatter and implicit solvent PCG remain
serial in their original order. Per-row escape values are folded in particle order.
The extra scratch is two f64 words per allocated point and a stack per helper.
Node or a cross-origin-isolated browser worker can run the blocking solver. The
renderer's optional destination uses a separate ArrayBuffer to protect the physics
arena, even after shared memory grows. Counts describe work assignments. Wall-clock
throughput is unmeasured.

The optional viscoplastic entry is 8,737 B gzip with an 8,826 B ceiling. Both Wasm assets are 36,124 B raw and 13,261 B gzip. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Skeletal tissue attachments (SOFT-05)

`@margoengine/physics/tissue` drives finite tetrahedral tissue from the rigid solver's layout-2 bodies field.
Each particle takes at most one bone binding. The prescribed bone can be fixed or kinematic. Its local anchor
either pins the particle or supplies a plane with normal compliance and damping. The local sliding plane has
an unbounded frictionless tangent and no curvature. Its normal-only backward Euler update is partitioned from
the native volume solve. Fast changes to bone orientation are sampled on the solver tick. Skin and fat
layer calibration and active fiber contraction remain open.

The pinned tetrahedron fixture matches the analytic small-displacement response with an allowance of 16 binary32
epsilon times the specimen length. A 0.5 m tangent translation leaves its entire particle state bit-identical.
The same native surface shows a 40.167 mm normal displacement under the rendered control and unchanged render
pixels under the tangent shift on WebGPU and WebGL2. The fixture is a material coupon.

Three authored layers share their tetrahedral vertices and contribute independent elasticity, damping and
density. The layered entry uses reversible isotropic Neo-Hookean materials. A one-step specimen matches the sum
of the independently derived axial stiffnesses and nodal masses within 16 binary32 epsilon times the measured
quantity's reference scale. The density-weighted cut fixture's fragment mass agrees with the exact tetrahedral
volume fraction under the same bound. The renderer reads the native soft geometry. Increasing the skin modulus
changes the loaded surface on WebGPU and WebGL2, with an exact same-backend replay.

### Volumetric vertex blocks (SOFT-04)

When a soft surface is torn or cut, its new query colliders retain the live contact and event
settings. The rigid shape's density is carried when the original collider supplied volume mass and the
new, outward-wound collision mesh still encloses positive volume. Open cloth pieces keep their
triangle colliders without volumetric mass. Soft-particle masses transfer separately.

**Large-strain rubber.** `CellMaterial.rubber` adds the finite-chain series and a second-invariant term to
the native vertex-block solver. It preserves the specified Lamé coefficients at rest. It recovers an inverted
tetrahedron and reproduces the restored continuation bit for bit. The Treloar test takes traction from actual
vertex-block acceleration and removes the hydrostatic contribution to compare with the measured nominal tensile
stress. A two-resolution extrapolation bounds the finite-step error. At 20% extension or greater, the 23
withheld readings stay within the calibration-derived prediction envelope. The largest observed relative
errors in that set are 10.9% uniaxial and 12.5% equibiaxial. The reported specimen at 2% biaxial extension
has about 55% relative underprediction. Small biaxial extension, hysteresis and independent large-strain
gelatin and ice tests are still open. This material curve is available for reversible isotropic vertex blocks.

`@margoengine/physics/soft` accepts `'vertex-block'` for isotropic stable Neo-Hookean
tetrahedra. Each sweep solves the local elastic and inertial energy exactly to working precision.
An entire body still needs enough sweeps for load to propagate through its mesh. Linear tetrahedra
can lock near incompressibility or need refinement to resolve bending. This mode uses a serial sweep
and shares the rigid/soft contact passes. Its optional entry and kernel sizes are recorded in the
[entry-size results](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/entry-sizes.json).

Free vertex-block bodies get one exact translational minimization per native substep, preserving
their inertial linear impulse to working precision before contact. The pass visits live cell
ranges and reads and translates unpinned body particles once each. It applies to the linear
movement of the center of mass. Bodies with pins instead exchange reaction with their supports,
and authored whole-body drag still changes momentum. The optional entry measures 137,827 B
gzip with the translation correction, including 95,068 B for its lazy native kernel.

The local/global `'projective'` mode uses the corotated material. A local rotation and unit-determinant
projection per live tetrahedron precedes each global solve. Each matrix application visits its four
corners once, then the preconditioner acts once per particle. The iteration limits are the configured
soft iterations and the existing preconditioned conjugate-gradient limits. Extreme expansion also
searches the small-root volume branch before accepting a feasible unit-determinant target. This CPU
mode retains the existing rigid contact solver. Both nonlinear modes also accept a single rest-space
fiber modulus for longitudinal reinforcement. It captures the parallel/transverse axial contrast
while the transverse base remains isotropic. Distinct radial and tangential elastic and shear
coefficients are outside that material model. Fiber rows join the snapshot when the scene authors them.

The optional orthotropic vertex-block material assigns one full stiffness tensor per body. For
each tetrahedron it applies the symmetric Hooke tensor to Green strain in the rest-space material
frame. The three axial and shear moduli and three Poisson ratios are small-strain measurements.
A fourth-order determinant term resists compression as volume collapses and has zero tangent
stiffness at rest. Each vertex update recomputes its incident cells' elastic energy to enforce
descent with the stored f32 positions. The material uses one 18-word record per tetrahedron in
the snapshot only when a body has authored orthotropy.
The optional soft entry measures 128,798 B gzip, with 36,140 B in its base and 91,828 B in the
lazy native kernel bundle.

The tetrahedral energy follows Green strain as described by Eftychios Sifakis and Jernej Barbič,
2012. [Theory and Discretization of Finite Elements](https://viterbi-web.usc.edu/~jbarbic/femdefo/sifakis-courseNotes-TheoryAndDiscretization.pdf)

The material example uses Douglas-fir moduli and Poisson ratios from Tables 5–1 and 5–2 of
C. Adam Senalik and Benjamin Farber, 2021. [Mechanical Properties of Wood](https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/62244)

Geoffrey Irving, Joseph Teran and Ronald Fedkiw described the inversion problem in 2004.
The fourth-order determinant term here keeps the calibrated tangent at rest.
[Invertible Finite Elements for Robust Simulation of Large Deformation](https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~jteran/papers/ITF04.pdf)

`SoftBodies.cutPlane` handles complete planar sections of solids represented by their tetrahedra.
Each fragment inherits the original material, pins and plastic rest basis. A child of a very close
intersection still needs a rest basis and nodal mass representable in the native f32 state.
The operation validates all pieces before replacing the body. It builds the edited topology once
and uses the normal native solve for the fragments. The finite triangle blade in `SoftBodies.cut`
continues to slice along existing faces. Geometric cuts and face tears retain live rigid anchors
at the same point in the rigid frame for every surviving copy of the attached vertex. Embedded
skins, separate spring or cluster constraints and separately bound meshes need a separate transfer.
The built-in surface collider is rebuilt from each piece's boundary, including open incision faces.
Its contact, sensor, filtering and event settings carry over. Each collider has a new identity
and derives its mass properties from its boundary and copied density. This brings the optional
soft entry to 137,978 B gzip. Snapshots
of a cut restore in worlds with the same cut topology. The optional soft entry is 131,482 B gzip,
with 38,973 B in its base and 91,849 B in the lazy native kernel bundle.

`SoftBodies.cutTriangle` handles a finite planar incision, including one wholly inside an
existing tetrahedron. Tetrahedra that meet the supporting plane may be subdivided so that
neighboring faces remain conforming. Only the triangles covered by the blade are released.
Cells outside the blade keep their material connections. Tiny subdivisions must fit the
same f32 geometry and rest-basis requirements as a full plane cut. The API accepts one
triangle per operation. Embedded skins, springs, cluster constraints and separately bound meshes still
require their own state transfer.
An optional tensile seam opens one authored triangle inside a cell. It samples the cell after
the soft step, and consumes the seam when the topology changes. Use it with an unskinned tetrahedral
solid without springs, clusters or other native fracture criteria. The intact body has the usual
elasticity up to the strain threshold. The authored option can combine tension, in-plane
sliding and tearing along the first edge of the triangle. A shear term is inactive unless
its limit is supplied. Normal compression contributes zero, pure rigid rotation preserves
the strain and inverted cells wait until they recover. Restore an intact snapshot into the
same topology with the same authored seam to replay the event.
With tensile seams the optional entry is 138,830 B gzip, including 43,642 B in its base.

Unseeded tensile nucleation scans the cells once after the soft step. It selects the largest
principal elastic Green strain and opens the full centroid section of that cell. The scan skips
inverted and previously nucleated material and uses an eigenvalue bound to avoid diagonalizing
cells whose strain is too low. Other cells remain eligible after the topology changes. The
remesher subdivides the selected tetrahedron and only the original neighbors that share its
split faces or edges. An existing front advances through an eligible adjacent tetrahedron
when its projected principal plane crosses the material. Front edge flags travel with
their material through cuts and snapshots. The advancing front drops its released edge from
all incident tetrahedra. General mixed-mode propagation remains open.
An authored finite blade seeds eligible tensile fronts where its paired lips share two
particles. Complete separation leaves no bonded lip edge. A candidate still needs a current
principal plane that crosses adjacent cell material or coincides with a bonded face. A plane
that only touches an exposed face cannot advance.
Coplanar fracture toughness uses a small-strain isotropic displacement correlation.
It needs two actual boundary lips with a shared front edge and matching detached
material positions, ahead of which there is a coplanar bonded facet. An unmatched
or inverted candidate is ineligible. The option fits the leading linear-elastic
plane-strain term at one matched radius. It leaves crack kinking, large-strain and
orthotropic toughness outside this mode. Snapshot replay needs the same authored
material and toughness. If tensile nucleation is enabled, it starts a new crack when
there is no recorded front and the strain threshold is exceeded.
Use tensile nucleation on unskinned cells without independent springs or clusters.
Automatic cracks preflight rounded rest coordinates, basis terms and nodal masses before
editing topology. A candidate below the native resolution remains intact for that step.
Nucleation can select another eligible cell in the same step. An authored blade still reports
a geometry error when its exact requested cut cannot be represented.
With coplanar mixed-mode toughness, the optional entry measures 145,660 B gzip.
The base is 45,885 B and the lazy native kernel is 100,020 B.
Measured gelatin and passive flesh stiffnesses are checked in the small-strain elastic
regime. The thin freshwater ice case checks elastic fracture against strain inferred
from measured beam stiffness and failure load. Gel and tissue rheology, time-dependent
ice flow, fracture under changing temperature, and ice-water feedback are separate models.
In the loaded ladder fixture, one finite incision subdivides 240 original tetrahedra into
600 tetrahedra. With live rigid-anchor transfer, the optional entry measures 137,034 B gzip, with a 42,494 B base
and a 94,249 B lazy kernel.

Optional orthotropic failure uses nine stress limits in the material frame. It compares the
stress conjugate to Green strain with each positive tension, compression, or shear strength.
Its failure data adds 18 f32 words per cell when a body authors strength limits. Nine store
the limits and nine store independently filtered utilizations. A cell reaches the tear threshold
when its largest utilization exceeds one, or its interior-strength factor for an interior cell.
The event splits the mesh along existing tetrahedral faces. It represents brittle onset without
a directional fracture-energy or post-peak softening law. The optional soft entry measures
133,213 B gzip, including a 39,449 B base and 93,115 B lazy native kernel.

With `strength.fractureEnergy`, each tetrahedron also stores a six-mode energy calibration,
nine irreversible damage quantities, and its active signs and fracture state. The law
regularizes work per area using `h = (6V₀)^(1/3)`. To represent a descending branch, the
tetrahedron must satisfy `h < 2EG/f²` for each tensile or shear mode. Refine the mesh if the
authored material cannot satisfy this condition. The closed-form fracture work applies to
a single localized mode. Mixed-mode cracks use independent histories and the existing
inter-element crack path. For interior cells, `interiorStrength` scales the stress thresholds
and its square scales the work per area. Cuts retain the accumulated damage and recalculate
the geometric length for the smaller child tetrahedra. Snapshot layout includes the optional
damage rows only when a body authors fracture energy.
The optional soft entry measures 134,833 B gzip, with a 40,017 B base and 94,249 B lazy kernel.

### Gas-filled soft shells (SOFT-06)

`@margoengine/physics/soft` solves the pressure of an outward-wound, watertight hollow triangle mesh. The chamber
has uniform pressure and a fixed pressure–volume product between fill changes. A changing external pressure or an
independent chamber uses an explicit fill or a separate body. The model has no through-mesh gas transport,
thermodynamic heat solve, or automatic gas loss when an edge constraint tears. Use a valid shell without
self-intersections, and its existing material, contacts and substeps still determine the membrane's mechanics.
Geometry uses f64 local coordinates for signed volume and f32 particle positions in the existing native step. The gas
product and ambient pressure also use f32 state columns. Each constraint pass takes work linear in vertices and
triangles and allocates no new scratch while stepping. The same optional soft Wasm runs under either renderer.
The complete optional soft entry measures 110,995 B gzip, up from 108,726 B, within its 111,864 B ceiling.
The separately loaded kernel chunk is 75,819 B gzip, up from 74,174 B, and the native kernel is 211,555 B raw.
Core plus stage remains 24,820 B gzip.

### Arcade car and vehicle debug lines (DYN-04)

`Vehicle.car` lays out exactly four wheels on a chassis whose up axis is its own +y; a six-wheeled truck or a chassis
modelled on another up axis takes `new Vehicle` with its own wheels. Its size comes from the chassis's box colliders
(spheres, capsules, cylinders and cones count by their bounding spheres); a chassis of hulls or meshes needs
`halfExtents`. The springs rest at the designed sag, so the body rides at `0.8 r` (the dampers read the step's mean speed,
KB-PHYS-VEHICLEREST1, fixed 2026-11-28). The tyre models
and grip keep the `Vehicle` defaults: the full MF 6.x tyre is beyond parity (docs/physics-parity-bar.md, P5).
`debugRender()` allocates its two arrays on every call, reads the last step (the chassis pose and each wheel's cast),
and colours a tyre-model wheel as sliding at a combined slip of 0.1, about where the default Magic Formula peaks,
not at its own model's peak. Speed against the three.js example is measured in the quiet speed phase.

### Wheel contact and lane tracking (DYN-04)

The clocked driver tracks authored open or closed lanes with measured traction. It uses one wetness word per vehicle with the documented bank convention. It brakes smoothly before an open lane ends. The current driver routes an individual car and uses the supplied route around obstacles. Road colliders reuse their rendered triangle tessellation. A calibrated soft patch uses a constant footprint and the measured pressure exponent. EARTH-05 owns wear and terrain-volume feedback. The paired road and dynamics fixtures cover the existing tyres, drivetrain, motorcycles and tracks alongside the new road controls and terrain interface. The optional road driving entry measures 12,776 B minified and 5,373 B gzip. The Physics root measures 1,339,661 B minified and 865,782 B gzip. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Natural long waves, moving bathymetry and run-up (SEA-06)

Use the regular-grid model where wavelength is long compared with depth. It moves a
wet/dry shoreline, can reflect from closed edges or transmit an open coast's outgoing
characteristics, and reports signed boundary and source volume. The wet-patch shallow
Padé approximation of Kajiura's response is intended for rapid bottom movement about one
representative depth. The dynamic model is depth averaged. Short-wave dispersion,
three-dimensional impact generation and nested grid corrections require separate models.
Inland arrival can differ from the linear still-water travel time.
Supply fault displacement as moving bed elevations. The solver leaves fault displacement to its source. The coastal renderer
uses the accepted shallow-water depth and velocity and requires a shared grid, coordinate frame and datum.
It displays the moving wet/dry boundary and depth-averaged surface, without an overturning wave crest.
A world tick accepts only finite depth, discharge, volume and inundation records. If the explicit solver
would need more than 4,096 CFL substeps, use a coarser grid or smaller forcing. No partial step is published.

The optional tsunami entry is 9,077 B gzip with a 9,278 B ceiling. The plain and shared Wasm assets are
each 23,068 B raw and 9,530 B gzip. Its optional worker asset is 767 B gzip and is shared with ATMO-07. Extreme finite Coriolis rates retain the midpoint rotation's bounded
half-turn limit. Resolve the rotation in time when phase accuracy matters.

An incoming wave is uniform along its configured open side and is sampled once per tick. Give its
surface and velocity in the same local datum and axes as the bed. Smooth-bed laminar attenuation uses
a single incident period and solves only the dissipative part of the harmonic stress. It requires
positive viscosity and period, and disables the use of positive Manning roughness. It omits
unsteady shear history and phase lag, transitions to turbulent flow, and surface tension. Both
friction models leave plane-beach run-up mismatches in [SEA-06 laboratory evidence](../packages/physics/scripts/sea06-measured.md).

One CPU thread is the default. Shared-memory execution can split flux lines and pressure updates among
1–64 threads in Node or a cross-origin-isolated browser worker. The browser window uses the serial
path. Each native phase joins before the following stage begins. Binding or joining a worker
that fails or stalls returns a coded error before exposing incomplete state. The solver uses one
rectangular resolution and has no tiled or adaptively refined grid. `workCounts()` reports the face
evaluations in the two sweeps of both RK stages, exactly `2 * substeps * (2 * nx * nz + nx + nz)`.
It separates the same work by each worker's assigned whole rows and columns.

### Accretion and compact-object trajectories (SPACE-03)

The disk is axisymmetric, Newtonian and geometrically thin. Viscosity is supplied. Its blackbody effective temperature
comes from local dissipation, so it assumes the heat radiates where it is generated. Flows involving magnetic fields,
self-gravity, radiative transport or the inner stress and plunge require additional equations.

The Kerr tracer uses the fixed test-particle metric in the exterior observer chart. The polar angle is unfolded at the
pole for zero axial angular momentum. The horizon offset is a separate value while f64 can represent it. The tracer
subdivides each world tick by a power of two chosen from its local phase rate. An observer step requiring more than
16,384 subdivisions fails before it updates any accepted coordinates. Increase the rate or shorten the step.
Rendering the disk with light bending requires a separate light-transport stage and an emissivity source.

The optional TypeScript entry is 8,119 B gzip against an 8,375 B ceiling. Each lazy Wasm variant is 2,753 B raw
and 1,331 B gzip. Neither uses a shared static window. Core and stage add zero bytes.

The native disk's implicit tridiagonal solve and radial ledger sums are serial in index order. Density, one-face
heating and phase use f64x2 pairs and can use up to four participants. An odd final annulus keeps the scalar tail.
Accepted and trial regions, geometry and Thomas scratch take `(17n + 13) × 8` bytes for `n` annuli, before the
56 B descriptor, 16 B per participant receipt, 65,544 B per participant stack, pool control and alignment.

#### SPACE-03 observed Sagittarius A* emission and exterior geodesic widths

The signed capture-or-return diagnostic launches light tracers at 40 and 80 gravitational radii, using the
stellar mass-to-distance ratio published by GRAVITY in 2019. The resulting equatorial vacuum critical widths
are 52.080, 51.288 and 48.494 µas for spins 0, 0.5 and 0.9. Halving the maximum phase increment moves a
bracket by at most 5.96 × 10⁻⁷ gravitational radii. Independent double-root equations agree within
2.67 × 10⁻⁷ gravitational radii. The EHT measures a 51.8 ± 2.3 µas emission ring at 230 GHz, with a
68% credible interval. Its lensed plasma brightness and finite width differ from the vacuum critical curve,
so this receipt makes no observational pass or spin inference. Predicting the measured observable requires
relativistic emission and transfer. [GRAVITY stellar dynamics](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201935656)
[EHT image measurement](https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ac6674)
[EHT imaging methods](https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ac6736)

### Regional rotating weather (ATMO-10)

The periodic beta plane transports one moisture column per cell. Use regional domains away from equatorial and
polar geometry. Pressure follows horizontal balance. The high tier can activate two equal-depth potential-vorticity
layers, with wind interpolated between their representative altitudes. Vertical shear can amplify temperature
disturbances through baroclinic growth. The initial fields control the starting contrast and terrain boundary.
The high tier filters the mean wind's terrain wave with a fixed moist stratification. Local flow anomalies add their
direct upslope component. The advected temperature sets the saturation capacity in the assumed exponential
moisture column. Dry ascent uses up the column's saturation deficit before any cloud forms. Saturated ascent,
descent, conversion and fallout conserve the available water in the column budget. The phase-change tests are
manufactured calculations. The gauge comparison below documents reduced-model limits. A measured downstream
vapour-transport comparison remains open.
Cloud output is column mass and Weather uses a display opacity derived from it. The atmosphere uses
