fixed stratification, upper and lower pressure levels, and a vertically integrated moisture budget. Nonhydrostatic
vertical momentum, explicit ice microphysics, latent heating feedback and data assimilation require separate models.
Forecasts and film-length time acceleration use different clock scales. Keep coupled physical budgets on the same scale.

The optional Physics entry measures 9,456 B gzip against a 9,740 B ceiling. The Weather adapter measures 964 B gzip
within a 1,196 B ceiling. Both optional native assets are 24,580 B raw and 8,410 B gzip.
These entries leave Core, Stage, Physics World and the Weather root unchanged.

Independent native cells prepare the 12-column publication, using f64x2 temperature and vapour-transport products.
The Fourier transport and moisture ledger remain in fixed order. The trial bank adds 200 B per atmospheric cell,
56 B more per cell with two layers, and two f64 values per water cell for its candidate force. Atmospheric and layer
ledgers and the force state accept together. A bad borrowed water row leaves the accepted atmosphere and the native
work receipt intact.

#### ATMO-10 observed OLYMPEX warm-sector rainfall

At Quinault 4 NE and Buckinghorse, the observed 8 December 2015, 13:00–17:00 UTC totals were 32.60 and 35.56 mm.
Four-kilometre simulations initialized from the earlier Quillayute sounding and 3DEP terrain give 13.56 and
23.84 mm. Simulated totals are lower by 19.04 and 11.72 mm. Refining from 8 km raises modeled rain by 0.30 and 2.49 mm.
At 8 km, using the independently observed 3.524 K/km shallow sounding lapse instead of the default 6.5 K/km gives
zero rain at both stations. Height on the four-kilometre model grid interpolates to 146 and 1,197 m, compared with
station elevations of 87 and 1,478 m. The observed hourly rainfall amounts were withheld from the atmosphere.
The diagnostic uses a frozen initial sounding, wide periodic domain, uncertain point-gauge exposure and a reduced
column closure. The upstream sounding IVT is an input-derived value. [OLYMPEX event context](https://doi.org/10.1175/JAS-D-23-0177.1) [USCRN hourly records](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/uscrn/products/hourly02/2015/CRNH0203-2015-WA_Quinault_4_NE.txt) [Buckinghorse gauge](https://wcc.sc.egov.usda.gov/nwcc/site?sitenum=1107)

### Cloud-to-ground discharge (ATMO-07)

The optional lightning solver follows one natural strike in a homogeneous dielectric with insulating sides, a
prescribed cloud plane and a grounded bed sampled at initialization. Resolve terrain and charge gradients with
several lattice cells. The leader is voxelized, optical strength is relative, and the charge field is fixed for
one flash. The optional initiation and propagation thresholds apply to forward grid bonds, with
one authored seed on the cloud plane. They do not solve storm electrification, upward connecting leaders
or the choice of a cloud-to-cloud initiation site. Use the electric potential and timed segment outputs
for visualization and relative acoustic delays. Predicting strike locations, current waveforms and
absolute sound pressure requires storm observations and additional plasma and atmospheric models.
The live Sky field borrows accepted geometry and a relative radiance envelope at the requested world time.
Points between accepted physics ticks use the last accepted geometry. Weather retains its own light schedule. Grid capacity follows available wasm32 arena space, including each
published field's two mirrors. The optional entry measures 9,005 B gzip within a 9,072 B ceiling. Both native
modules measure 3,272 B raw and 1,648 B gzip and load with that entry. Sky's bolt measures 6,103 B gzip
within a 6,300 B ceiling. The optional worker asset is 767 B gzip and is shared with SEA-06. Core and Stage
gain zero bytes.

The default serial solve runs on every supported host. Use two or more threads in Node or a
cross-origin-isolated browser worker with a shared-memory world. Workers partition independent
Jacobi rows without changing the residual, order of additions or stochastic branch choices.
The browser window runs serially. Iteration count still increases as the grid grows or the requested
tolerance tightens. Each work receipt counts the accepted sweeps, stencil pairs and halo writes.
Receipts describe recent execution, while snapshots retain the physical state.

### Thermo-viscoplastic lava and nearshore occupancy (EARTH-10)

Lava uses a regular depth-averaged heightfield patch with closed edges. It resolves laminar Bingham resistance, advected crystallisation enthalpy, diffusion, radiative and convective skin transfer and basal cooling. The optional terminal transport removes inertia for creeping flow, using Bingham discharge at each face and conservative enthalpy transport. It requires a thin, slowly varying sheet and has no imposed initial discharge. A point vent omits the real basalt experiment's chute momentum. Terrain, cooled crust and the pressure gradient drive channel confinement and arrest. The shallow-layer aspect-ratio approximation applies to patch-scale flow. Individual crust fractures, elastic lava tubes, three-dimensional overturning and a separate bubble phase need higher-dimensional models. The coastal source is the signed change in displaced volume under a fixed reference sea level. This estimate covers gravity-wave forcing from submerged occupancy. Rapid interface chemistry and water-side multiphase overturning are outside the model.

The native microstep respects transport and thermal diffusion bounds. It refuses a tick above 4,096 explicit microsteps and publishes only finite, accepted volume and heat ledgers. With zero conductivity the well-mixed bulk is exposed, so radiation, convection and the water film act without a conductive skin or basal term. The default positive conductivity resolves a resistive skin. The ICE-05 contact is a 60 Hz staggered heat exchange. Match the terrain and render frames to the lava grid. Weather draws accepted skin emission and basalt coverage from the depth and crust with no guessed exposed crack area. Physics lava is 9,762 B gzip under 9,824 B. Weather lava is 15,291 B under 15,750 B. Both Wasm assets are 19,038 B raw and 8,497 B gzip. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

The optional native worker path needs shared memory and a blocking host (Node or a
cross-origin-isolated browser worker). On each microstep it partitions stability and local
cell work, orders inertial flux sweeps by axis, and gathers terminal fluxes in the serial
per-cell order. The source and cooling ledgers are folded in cell order. Worker scratch
adds four f64 words per cell, two more for terminal face rates, and a stack per helper.
Publication and ICE receipt application stay on the caller. Deterministic counts cover
the actual recurrence partitions. Elapsed-time speed depends on grid size and host.

### Divergence-free particle liquid (FLUID-01)

The DFSPH entry measures 8,526 B gzip. The plain and shared native assets measure 36,539 and 36,533 B raw, and 14,808 and 14,802 B gzip.

The solver advances one liquid with a uniform rest density and particle mass. Its two pressure passes
remove compression and positive divergence. Tolerances describe average residuals and the actual residuals
are reported when iteration budgets are reached. Both pressure passes use the coupled rigid inverse mass
and inertia. This adds 104 bytes of scratch per registered rigid row to store mobility and predicted motion.
Direct liquid–solid contact uses the same rigid mobility to stop inward motion and damp tangential
slip. Its unilateral impulse preserves the normal constraint. Penetration is corrected on the
liquid side, and the model has no particle spin. The world owns the separate rigid–rigid solve.
Dynamic boundaries with viscosity reserve another 192 bytes per registered rigid row. The same
implicit solve moves the fluid and rigid samples. The conjugate directions preserve the reciprocal
wrench even when the viscosity iteration cap stops the solve.
The clock switches to smaller advective substeps above
0.4 spacings of travel. The support radius, contact radius and arena capacity control resolved detail.
Plain and shared Wasm preserve the same clocked state and snapshot. Shared memory does not parallelize the
native loops. The grid reuses 27 connected-list head indices per fluid row between position updates.
This takes 112 extra bytes per reserved particle row, including alignment. A rebuild refreshes those
indices before new density or divergence calculations. Capillary interactions centred on solid samples
take their own neighborhood query from the same grid.
A second scratch allocation can hold each complete pressure neighborhood's exact 40-byte pair records.
The default reservation uses the kernel's spherical support and the reserved particle count, limited by
three times the base solver region estimate and the wasm32 arena. If a row cannot fit, the same kernel and
order are evaluated from the indexed cell heads. Disable scratch reuse with `cacheNeighbors: false`.

Closed planar walls sample the outside volume of the cubic pressure kernel on a rest lattice. The sample
spacing fits each axis of the domain and every exterior site belongs to the union of closed faces.
For a support wider than four fitted spacings, the analytical half-space integral controls work. The same
integral is available explicitly and uses an overlap approximation at perpendicular walls.
The same lattice contributes zero-velocity exterior samples to implicit viscosity. In analytic mode, angular
cone moments and five-point radial quadrature give the planar viscous tensor. Its overlaps add at corners.
Rigid boxes, spheres and capsules use sampled boundaries and hold their last published pose during the
fluid substeps. Contact audio represents an impulse on one selected modal track. Capillarity uses one liquid and
uniform material energies on its solids. The interface spans a three-spacing kernel neighbourhood.
The capillary force runs before pressure and leaves out the paper's simultaneous nonlinear pressure and friction
solve. The coarse and interactive narrow-channel surges arrive early. Bubble acoustics and production
bindings for crests and shorelines are open.

The parcel interface moves one particle rest-volume per ticket. Fractions remain with the sender.
It reports all momentum components and resolves origin-cell offsets. The live shallow-water test is a
closed 1 m² periodic wet cell, with reciprocal volume and horizontal momentum and an independent
vertical ledger. Production wet/dry cells and the breaking crest need owner-side reservation and receipt
of applied fluxes.

The integrated cubic-kernel colour energy equals the prescribed surface tension per flat area.
The measured quadrupole period of a 20.10 mm free water drop is 0.885 s, compared with the
0.742 s Rayleigh limit for the same density, tension and rest volume. The separated surface
energy and pressure updates need more validation for shape frequencies.
The optional layout-1 hard-contact impact record is 56 B per solver. It combines hard contacts
within each tick at one energy-weighted position and substep arrival time. The value in joules is the
dissipated mechanical energy. Bubble geometry, gas resonance and acoustic radiation are separate models.

### Position-based particle water (FLUID-02)

The dedicated PBF entry measures 6,244 B gzip. Each Wasm variant is 18,143 B raw and 7,317 B gzip.

The fast and precise presets apply four and twelve projections per advective substep. A closed box can keep or
release each face. An open face leaves the particles in the native set with their existing mass and momentum.
Resolution follows particle spacing and the available Wasm arena, including field publication buffers. The
support must resolve the smallest solid and jet feature. Rigid box, sphere and capsule surfaces carry kernel-normalized pressure
samples as well as hard contacts. The staggered exchange holds the last rigid pose during the fluid substeps.
The model uses one rest density and only corrects compression by default. The optional signed constraint adds
apparent cohesion without a measured water–air tension law. The higher-iteration preset
usefully reduces residual compression but retains the same explicit rigid exchange. Automatic shallow-water
handoff, generic mesh contacts, and physical surface tension are tracked separately.
The `tensile` coefficient is referenced to 60 Hz. Its position increment scales with the squared substep,
and free-water pairs outside the active density constraints receive zero artificial pressure.
PBF input failures expose `PHYSICS_INPUT_TYPE` on `TypeError` and `PHYSICS_INPUT_RANGE` on `RangeError`.
The XSPH velocity blend uses particle kernel weights from [Macklin and Müller, *Position Based Fluids*, 2013, eq. 17](https://mmacklin.com/pbf_sig_preprint.pdf).
For each pair, the larger of its two fluid-neighbour weight sums and one is the shared denominator. This is a weighted
variant of the symmetric local averaging in [Xiao, Boyd and Lall, *Distributed Average Consensus with Time-Varying Metropolis Weights*, 2005, eq. 4](https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/pdf/avg_metropolis.pdf).
Reciprocal mass-weighted coefficients conserve linear momentum. Their row sums are at most the configured smoothing
fraction, so a convex velocity average cannot increase total kinetic energy. Optional vorticity confinement still uses a
separate energy budget. The tests cover the exact sparse-pair velocity, the effect of a detached dense cloud, and the
cloud's momentum and energy at the maximum smoothing fraction.

### Rail wheelsets and catenary (DYN-05)

The reduced model covers two four-wheel bogies per car, one shared spin coordinate per wheelset,
four local lateral contact evaluations, and one supplied surveyed route per car. Turns use its
centreline curvature and cant. The field accepts separate rail height irregularities. A turnout
is chosen before the world starts. Contact tracks the two tread reactions and a flange restoring
load. Post-rail motion retains an arclength and independent spring and fall coordinates. The
catenary uses a tensioned fixed-anchor contact wire with linear waves and a single sprung pickup
per configured car. The wire's vertical gravity and contact geometry are aligned with world Y.
The powered separation event is for animation.

The default creep and Hertz stiffnesses are effective constants. Spin creepage and resolved
wheel and rail profiles are open, as are flange climbing and a Nadal criterion. Leaving the
authored support enters a fall without an off-track collision model. The wire omits messenger,
droppers, wire bending and wind response. The contact comparison in
`packages/physics/scripts/dyn05-vtrack-measured.mjs` misses 14 of 19 dry lateral adhesion bands
on the scaled V-Track rig. At the largest tested slip the model gives 0.295–0.297 against
measured values of 0.375–0.394. The fixture leaves full train and catenary validation open.

The stable world rate comes from wheelset, suspension, draft-gear and wire frequencies.
Nonfinite geometry, forces or native updates report a coded error before changing the
accepted car or wire. The optional 2- and 4-participant arrangements require shared world memory
and a blocking agent. Participants parallelize each catenary node pass. The coupler and pantograph
force sums and independent vehicle dynamics run on the caller.
The optional rail entry is 12,230 B min+gzip. Each lazy Wasm variant is 2,914 B raw and 1,062 B gzip.

### Tracks and footprints on a physical bed (EARTH-05)

Terramechanics treats one prepared material per prescribed footprint. The mean tier uses uniform pressure.
The resolved tier uses normalized pressure on the bed grid and accepts rectangular, elliptical or sampled
projected contours. Bearing and shear parameters come from the soil's material tests. Resolve the patch and its adjacent berm
with several grid vertices. Surface repose uses one ordered face sweep over the newly displaced loose material.
The candidate set follows newly moved soil and can spread far when the specified repose slope approaches zero.
The ground is a height field with peak indentation per vertex. Enable `material.unloading`
to follow Wong's linear unloading and reloading branch. The largest stress already experienced at a
vertex controls its elastic slope. A larger stress can add permanent settlement. Each vertex adds
24 bytes of elastic state and four bytes of active-index capacity, plus fixed parameters and a count.
The release step visits only previously compressed vertices. Overlapping footprints in the same
step retain their greatest elastic displacement. The dry granular model treats identical repeated
loads below the previous peak as elastic. Progressive fatigue and same-pressure ratcheting remain open.
Accepted topography changes, contact outputs and history are kept separate from the native trial.
The ordinary mean trial adds 24 bytes per vertex for deformation, dust and peak settlement, plus
4 bytes of staging capacity for an independently allocated terrain input. The resolved trial adds
8 bytes per vertex for pressure and approximately 0.26 bytes per vertex for ordered face flags.
Unloading and the cross-track bank add their own history to the trial when enabled.
Optional hardpan adds one subsurface pressure
transition sampled at the footprint centre. Resolve changes in layer depth at the scale of the footprint.
Shear and displaced material use the topsoil fit. Shared layer exchange, overhangs and accumulated
subgrade fatigue remain open. The rolling
wheel option resolves the driven rim's average stress envelope below its axle. Evenly spaced lugs can stamp
individual contact marks from live spin. Their projected strip uses 65 along-track stations. Indexed tread
triangles can instead intersect the local horizontal bearing plane at configurable resolution (17 by 65
profile samples by default). Supply three finite coordinates per vertex and three zero-based indices per
triangle. The optional single-value camber field accepts the right-axis vertical component in [-1, 1],
default zero. It tilts indexed tread geometry. The analytic bearing arc remains upright while
determining load. The optional reaction field
reports vertical and longitudinal force and resisting axle torque for the forward driven arc.
Its reciprocal rigid binding applies the previous contact result on the same collider. A tyre provides
independent wheel spin and lateral grip. Lower actual load and the discrete kinetic-work bound
limit the paired impulse. A configured skid exponent adds signed two-region shear under forward
braking, including lockup. A configured shear radius uses actual wheel and ground speed.
The optional side-force field combines rim shear and passive sidewall earth pressure with default
gravity 9.81 m/s². The sidewall assumes a straight soil chord between angular entry and exit.
A supplied `lateralShearLength` resolves directional shear in forward rolling within the same
yield magnitude. Measured FJS-1 cases cover side force near 0.6 slip and four yaw angles.
The resistive-force solver uses the Li, Zhang and Goldman quasistatic dry-grain law.
It takes nine caller-calibrated coefficients in N/m³ and integrates 1–128 midpoint samples
per strip, with a maximum of 65,536 configured samples across the solver. It samples the
surface under each strip centreline and evaluates motion in a vertical plane. Motion
parallel to the projected transverse axis, fully dry points and exactly edge-on motion
produce no load. This tier uses 64 scratch bytes per configured sample and an extra sample
when padding an odd count. It returns forces and moments through the rigid body's force
field. It currently reads the bed without modifying soil distribution or emitting dust.
One, two or four native participants can evaluate disjoint pairs. The parent joins all work before
reducing in body and strip order. Two and four require shared memory. Footprint sediment deposition
and repose remain ordered because overlapping contacts can change the same vertices.
The optional cross-track berm mode places the loose soil in separate triangular banks. Its
physical width uses the configured repose slope; slope zero uses the default ring. Unresolved
or off-grid banks report their volume as exported. With an effective `grouserFill` fraction in
[0, 1], rotating lugs fill the solver's cumulative rear depression or transfer loose soil between
banks at large obliquity. At travel angles under 10°, partial backfill placed within the trench
forms a flat bottom from the deepest part of the rear depression. At intermediate angles,
backfill first forms a step across the projected trailing lug band. Cross-track banks settle
with one simultaneous sparse transfer pass per solver step. The solver stores eight history
bytes per grid vertex and a second sparse bitset
for affected vertices, approximately 0.26 bytes per vertex. Steep loose slopes can take more
than one step to settle. The separate excavation maximum prevents counting a cut twice.
The optional `grouserDig` uses 16 phase-history bytes per external row. Positive slip can
excavate more soil as the wheel turns, up to the configured bedrock or the axle depth
supported by this bearing model. Supply continuous phase samples over two loaded steps.
The response still reports local bearing sinkage. The changed terrain carries the deeper rut.
The cylindrical raster interpolates the cross grade between two bed samples. Its central
depth uses the normal bearing arc. Camber with no projected width is outside that geometry.
Reverse travel keeps the tyre response. Transient contact angles and measured skid forces at oblique
slip angles remain open. The measured rover comparison covers steady
drawbar force and torque at 60% lug-tip slip for the reported wheel and sand and relative
crest-to-trough relief at one straight locked-wheel condition. Supply the same excavation floor
and TerrainBed bedrock data. The volume ledger records material crossing the modeled bounds,
compaction and lofted mineral dust.

#### Independent plate shape and repeated pressure

At 48 kPa Apfelbeck et al. (2011) observed 26.06, 36.90 and 39.49 mm of sinkage for equal-area
1:3, 1:5 and 1:7 rectangles pressed into quartz sand. The resolved solver uses the separate
circular-plate material fit at the same penetration speed. It gives 26.42, 27.89 and 29.38 mm.
The latter two miss the measured ranges [32.7, 41.1] and [35.5, 43.3] mm even after the
figure-reading uncertainty is included. The 128-to-256 resolution shift is at most 0.056 mm in
these three cases. The mean solver also underestimates the slender plate sinkage.

Rashidi and Gholami's 40 × 60 mm plate bearing test at 200 kPa accumulated 57, 83 and 98 mm
of sinkage at cycles 1, 3 and 10. Relative to the first peak, the plotted ratios at cycles 3 and
10 are 1.456 and 1.719. For repeated equal pressure, both solver tiers give 1.0 at both cycles with
either unfitted unloading stiffness. This check compares the normalized shape of the response.
Absolute soil calibration and independent test repeat variance were unavailable for this comparison.
[Reproducible comparison](../packages/physics/scripts/earth05-plates-measured.mjs).

The optional entry is 19,702 B gzip with a 20,294 B ceiling. Each lazy Wasm asset is 42,097 B raw,
17,337 B gzip and 15,090 B Brotli. The accepted pose and native workers add zero Core or Stage bytes.

## Colour enhancement and channel mixer (`@margoengine/tonemap/enhance`, 2026-11-26)

Enforced: mixer rows three numbers -2..2; shadows and highlights -3..3 stops; midtones -1..1 stops; vibrance and dehaze
-1..1; haze colour 0.01..16 per channel. Applies to scene-linear colour after exposure, white balance and local
exposure and before the display curve; auto exposure meters the source without it. The tone ranges are weights of Rec.709
luminance over 7 stops each side of middle grey and are not adjustable: diffuse white (2.5 stops up) takes 29% of
`highlights`, and 8 stops from grey a control has its full effect. Dehaze reads one pixel (no neighbourhood, transmission
map or depth), is capped at half the haze model's strength, and leaves channels at or above the haze colour as they are
when removing haze. Under an HDR `ColorOutput` a colour already outside sRGB keeps its part below zero through the
nonlinear steps. Not baked by `exportCube` or `export3dl` (they take a display-linear `Grade`), and no
settings-table rows. One 80-byte uniform buffer, one more pipeline when added to the list, no pass or texture; GPU time
not measured. Measured: new entry 1,282 B min+gzip; tonemap root, grade, hue, core and stage unchanged. GPU frames are
within 0.5 of an 8-bit level of a CPU oracle on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (`tests/enhance-browser.mjs`). Margo's
units are its own, so values from another engine's colour enhancement do not carry over one to one.

### Granular material points (EARTH-01)

The native entry uses sparse 3D quadratic MLS transfer, Hencky sand with a
Drucker–Prager return and snow with finite-strain hardening. All material points
share the grid velocities. The return map records the rejected volumetric strain;
every point retains its reference mass. Passive terrain contact applies Coulomb
friction on occupied grid nodes. Grid spacing and the clock govern resolution and
stability; a step that inverts an elastic deformation is rejected before committing
its trial state.

At 252 material points, the collapse occupied 337 grid nodes on its last step,
changed 3,771 pixels and dropped the tracked point 0.2205 m on both WebGPU and
WebGL2. Plain, shared and restored state hash to `032e9f9a1ed80ade`. The sparse
grid visits only the occupied nodes, with storage sized for the maximum support
of the input points. The kernel uses one deterministic scatter and gather order.
The optional JavaScript entry is 6,162 B gzip against a 6,217 B budget. Both
native assets are 16,409 B raw, at 6,501 B gzip for plain memory and 6,502 B for shared memory.
Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

The optional layer projection deposits each material point's current volume on
the receiving terrain triangle using its barycentric weights. The sum of vertex
area times height is the total layer volume change. The associated reference mass
stays with the points. Choose a receiving terrain surface and separate supporting
bedrock. The projection represents the volume in each ground column, including
particles above its surface. Use it for a shallow layer. Separating suspended
material and reconstructing overhangs need a different output.

The optional dense dry sand profile uses an implicit μ(I) friction return.
This requires material-specific grain properties and a stress-ratio curve.
The manufactured test verifies the friction relation and unchanged compressed
volume in both memory modes. At 12 mm grid spacing, the untuned Lajeunesse et al.
Figure 3(a) pilot reached a central sample height of 0.464 initial radii at 0.65 s.
Their deposit retains the initial central height near 0.56 radii. The unresolved
height difference and the lack of a steady-incline comparison keep independent
validation open. Dilute collisional granular flow needs a separate constitutive law.

The BB-7 reference fixture drives the live bed with the actual pectoral wake.
At 45 frames the fin-on case cuts about 49.6 μm and raises an adjacent region by
about 73.0 μm relative to the still-fin case. This is a reduced one-way bed-shear
model. It tracks the received horizontal impulse and preserves each grain's mass.
The field does not return unresolved water momentum or pore pressure. Explicit
pore-water transport and reciprocal dynamic contact remain open.

The voxel handoff samples complete solid cubes into a newly loaded solver at a
world step boundary. The sum of reference volumes equals the original selected
volume, and the mass follows the destination material density. Plan sufficient
grid resolution and the solver clock for the expected speed. The handoff starts
new material at rest, with no pre-existing stress. It does not convert liquids,
partial cells, or particles back to voxels. The voxel and physics checkpoints
need to be restored together when rewinding across the transfer.

### Physical strand guides (SOFT-03)

The base native solver covers cylindrical elastic guides at 240 Hz by default. The follow tier
keeps segment lengths and resolves a local bed plane. The rod tier resolves finite compliance
and endpoint-sphere self contact using a sparse grid. Guide shear and twist use artist-supplied
effective moduli where those have been measured. Optional per-link sections support different
mass, axial and shear area, bending stiffness and torsion along the centreline. The two
transverse components share a mean transverse second moment. Contact still uses round radii
and there is no shell ovalization or explicit vane surface.
Sampled bodies are kinematic capsules and
spheres with point contact. Separation between contacts depends on guide spacing and substep
rate. Use enough points to resolve thin obstacles.

Optional dynamic capsule contacts publish an equal reaction to the real RigidSolver in SI.
Moving-capsule tests measure linear and angular impulses including the in-flight registry
reaction. Off-centre contacts include the inverse inertia of the rigid body. At a weighted
edge witness, the clamp carries its share of the reaction. Geometry correction does not
become a velocity impulse. Use the same coupling rate for both solvers. The staggered
registry applies the rigid impulse on its next step and does not rewind the rigid pose.
Optional segment geometry resolves capsule and self intersections along each guide edge
at substep boundaries. The swept profile tests linear endpoint trajectories for both.
Increase the dyadic rate when a fast rotating capsule needs a closer approximation of its
arc. Adjacent links sharing an endpoint are excluded from self contact. The
26-guide sparse test finds fewer than 26 pairs out of 325 possible link pairs.

The direct solve eliminates one six-by-six block per strand edge in forward and backward
passes. The work and memory grow linearly along each open guide. It reserves 1,104 bytes
per authored point for solver scratch. The optional local profile uses less scratch, with
reduced stiffness accuracy as its link count rises.

A 0.28 m inextensible lantern handle matches the finite-amplitude pendulum period within
one 60 Hz observation interval and lags a moving root under a timed reach. The 120 mm
leaf test reverses a 0.6 m/s cross-flow, with approximately 0.944 mm deflection to each
side and exact replay after reversal. This is a beam-and-drag test for narrow
leaves. Lift-driven leaf flutter and canopy wind shielding need a separate model.

The 720-point tapered and swept fixture moved its selected tip 0.7516 m relative to the
still-air control. The workstation rerun changed 2,907 pixels on WebGPU and WebGL2.
The earlier audit recorded 3,022 pixels. Area of change is renderer evidence and depends on the capture.
Plain, shared and restored native state all hash to `9245de2188de6730` in the fixture. The optional entry
is 9,181 B gzip with a 9,457 B ceiling. Both lazy Wasm variants are 48,706 B raw and
18,771 B gzip. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

Native inertial and drag prediction divides disjoint point pairs across one, two or four participants.
Constraint projection, rigid reactions and neighbour sweeps retain their serial order. A candidate
adds a 104 B centreline record per point and 80 B of step settings. The reciprocal path adds 192 B
per dynamic capsule for the trial history and 48 B per rigid body row for candidate impulses.
Prediction adds a 28 B job, 16 B of work per participant, helper stacks and pool control.

The optional horse adapter drives eight tail joints and ten five-point mane and forelock
guides on the existing gait clock. It represents the rest of the strands through hair cards
weighted to those guides. The 1.5 s trotting fixture in a 24 m/s reference-height wind
moved tail, mane and forelock tips by 0.2896, 0.0250 and 0.0579 m relative to the still-air
run. Both backends produced 1,478 changed pixels and replay hash `f1550b4d0b329005`. The
body capsules follow the skin pose on each tick. The parameters represent effective hair
bundles, and bundle-scale stiffness and drag calibration remain open. The horses root and model
entries measure 17,283 B and 12,180 B gzip. The optional strand horse measures 18,244 B gzip.

The weighted avatar binding accepts positive uniform transforms. Its offline replay uses the
same time-sampled anchor and wind functions. On the Seed-san reference avatar the fixed
camera test measured 0.0942 m of ponytail-tip movement and 436 changed pixels on both
backends. Its restored simulation hash is `0bf6500c22b9e929`. The manual rig uses a 240 Hz
world clock. The automatic adapter advances that clock after the Animator pose. The optional
rigging entry measures 1,991 B gzip with a 2,247 B ceiling.

#### SOFT-03 measured single-hair bending

With the existing 3 GPa default and a 96-link direct rod, the predicted deflections at four measured
force points are 21.54, 28.00, 40.76 and 15.58 µm. Akanda et al. report 23.4, 31.0, 46.5 and
17.8 µm for those specimens and loads. Each remains low after a ±0.5 µm plot readout and ±2.5 µN
force sensitivity. Doubling 48 links to 96 shifts predictions by at most 0.64 µm. Halving the
time step at 48 links changes them by at most 0.002 µm. A fourfold reduction in numerical
settling mass changes the longest specimen by less than 0.001 µm. The authors' fitted modulus
does not enter the prediction. The plotted points describe quasistatic bending of individual
fibres. Measured clump motion and calibration of larger horse bundles remain open. [Akanda, Tohmyoh, and Saka 2010](https://doi.org/10.1299/jmmp.4.545)

## Typed events (scene/emitter)

`Emitter` keeps listeners in subscription order and calls them synchronously; the unread buffer of an `events()` iterator holds `capacity` events (default 64, at least 1) and drops the oldest on overflow, counted in `dropped`. Ending an iterator (return, signal, dispose) discards its unread events. A throwing listener goes to `onError`; without one it is rethrown in a microtask. There is no wildcard type, no listener priority and no event bubbling. Size: see `npm run quality -- --gate=sizes` (`@margoengine/scene/emitter`).

## Asset references and templates (scene/asset-pools)

A key has one reference count: `acquire`, preload groups and templates add one each, `release` removes one, and at 0 the value is disposed and unloaded. A plain `load` takes no reference, so a key used with both is unloaded when the references reach 0. Disposal is the `dispose` option or the value's `Symbol.dispose`; a prototype tree is disposed whole (core detaches children on dispose, it does not dispose them). A template build shares one loading signal between concurrent first callers. Instances copy the prototype with `cloneSubtree` (structured-cloneable `userData`, geometry and materials shared); the `AssetPool` entry loads `clone` and the scene index on first use, so a pool without templates imports no engine code, and `scene/assets` (queue and plain registry) never imports the pool.

### Natural granular runout (EARTH-02)

The optional granular-flow entry evolves one vertically integrated layer on a finite rectangular grid with closed walls, constant material density, downward gravity and hydrostatic pressure. It reads exact cell-area averages of the live TerrainBed triangles. Coulomb stress can hold a stopped layer and prescribed basal pore support reduces the dry friction load. Voellmy drag dissipates moving discharge without reversal. This first-order finite-volume tier treats vertical depth and horizontal discharge in the shallow-bed approximation. The roughness tier adds glass-bead start/stop hysteresis, normal-depth Froude scaling and independently tested rational and exponential stopping curves. The documented 1999 front-speed bounds cover bead systems 1 and 3. The same scaling has larger errors for the other two published bead systems. Opt-in bed deposition freezes an arrested plug in one step and conserves transferred mass under density change using the exact vertex support areas. Deposited material changes the geometry read on the next step. Grain segregation, steep-surface curvature forces, effective stress evolution and remobilization have separate evidence requirements. A snapshot for an accumulating world currently needs one completed frame so the framework has allocated the sum region. The optional SEA-06 edge uses a fixed nearshore datum and signed occupied-volume differences. Configure the receiving water solver with the reference bathymetry when the granular source already includes compaction into the bed. Water drag, dynamic buoyancy and near-field amplitude calibration remain separate. The X/depth seismic cross-section is extended along Z, with the nearest field sample used beyond its X span. Ground shaking changes horizontal drive and the vertical support load. Pressure propagation retains the shallow reference gravity. The vertically averaged layer omits the detached vertical trajectory if the normal support vanishes, and liquefaction still needs live pore state. The optional loader gets one plain and one shared Rust SIMD asset and adds nothing to the Physics root, World, Core or Stage.

The granular-flow entry is 5,965 B gzip under a 6,221 B ceiling. The plain SIMD asset is 9,620 B raw and 4,255 B gzip. The shared asset is 9,620 B raw and 4,255 B gzip. Core and Stage remain 24,846 B gzip.

### Ship seakeeping forward course

`Hull.course` adds 16 B per radiation lag and an 8 B count per configured solver hull. Change speed or heading slowly compared with the radiation window (20 s by default). The ordinary-strip model represents small vertical motion about a mean trim with a stern region where the section forces tend to zero. Use slender hulls. A runtime guard rejects speeds at which the finite-kernel static longitudinal stiffness reaches zero. A change to the incident wave diffraction, near-zero encounter qualification in following seas, nonlinear planing, forward corrections to roll, and physical tank validation are separate from these vertical radiation terms.

The optional seakeeping entry is 24,518 B gzip with a 25,254 B ceiling. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Matched hull wake work (SEA-12)

`SurgeWakeCoupling` adds the projected wake reaction to a free hull with only one horizontal translation
  unlocked. Run it at 60 Hz in calm, constant-depth water on an upright fixed-draft mesh with no other
  surge loads. Use an ambient-only sea for other hull hydrodynamics. The receiving wake is periodic and
  reads only this source, with no sponge. The entire source footprint must stay inside the grid. The
  impulse pairs with the same submerged volume operator in the wake. A stationary hull can take energy
  from existing waves. A freely turning, heaving or rolling hull requires its own matched modes.

### Prescribed hull wake work (SEA-12)

`PrescribedWakeWork` accounts for one submerged volume field and an optional zero-pressure surface-volume field
  for a single receiving wake at 60 Hz. Grid size, depth, density and pose cell match WakeSolver. Add the sources
  before the meter and the receiving wake after it. Separate pressure forcing and additional height sources,
  downstream sponge loss and other rigid or actuator work remain outside this ledger.
  Set `mirrored` only on a symmetric straight-quay grid with mirrored state and forcing. The ledger uses one
  forward transform per occupied depth band and one inverse transform on an active tick.

### Free heave and angular wake work (SEA-12)

`FreeHullWakeCoupling` advances one free horizontal translation and heave with native anisotropic rigid
rotation. Wave work includes surge, heave, roll and pitch. The wet waterplane must be a single convex contour.
The submerged source uses the reference draft and the other columns use the current waterplane about the live
centre of mass. Use one undamped rigid substep at 60 Hz with gyroscopic forces enabled and the unused horizontal
translation locked. The periodic wake uses uniform depth and zero sponge. The finite wake keeps fixed open-face
geometry and includes optional perimeter absorption in its balance. Both use exclusively the exchange's two
source ports. The wave model supplies zero yaw torque. Contact, sway and nonlinear wetted geometry evolution
within a time step are outside this work bound. The three waterplane modes and one advancing mode use the
same source projection as the selected receiver.

### Straight quay reflection and spray (SEA-12)

`QuayWakeBoundary` mirrors both hull source layouts about a vertical wall parallel to X. The +Z half is wet.
The grid has an even number of Z rows and shares a 60 Hz staggered group and world cell with the source.
The reflected boundary is fixed and perfectly reflecting in constant depth. Keep the hull and source rows on
the wet side and use the model away from wall ends and corners. WaterWake clips the image in its fragment
draw while retaining the resolved grid for the seam slopes and queries. The visual spray uses a rising crest
crossing and its local velocity. Finite-quay diffraction, nonlinear breaking, discharged volume and droplet
statistics remain outside this binding. The optional compiled entries measure 44,592 B gzip for Physics
loads and 2,172 B for Water wake.

### Finite quay wake and under-apron flow (SEA-12)

The finite quay receiver uses a still-water, cell-centred Cartesian volume with uniform horizontal spacing,
arbitrary vertical layer thicknesses, static solids and optional horizontal face fractions. Closed faces
carry zero normal flow. Adjacent wet cells exchange a shared conductance times the potential difference.
The base and outside faces are closed. The optional perimeter sponge damps elevation and books the absorbed
energy and signed volume. Size its width and run a domain comparison before treating it as an open sea.

`horizontalOrder: 4` and `8` use wider horizontal stencils along open faces and each stores one
additional f64 coefficient per layer. The default uses the two-point flux. The wider stencils reduce
open-water phase error on the fixed grid. The eighth-order option reads up to four neighbours
per side and axis. The stated orders apply to the uniform horizontal interior.
The vertical grid, time step and sharp-corner geometry have their own accuracy bounds.

The default 60 Hz midpoint solves a Robin surface condition with preconditioned conjugate gradients.
`temporalOrder: 4` composes three signed midpoint solves per tick for a better phase in the conservative
wave evolution under held pressure. The source kick and forward sponge remain outside the stages. The
option adds one f64 per surface cell in scratch and reuses the source buffers to publish the full step
atomically. It retains pressure as the full-tick potential difference. The optional loads entry measures
63,109 B gzip. Grids with
at least 2,048 volume cells can use a Galerkin coarse correction. The aggregates follow connected faces in
each horizontal layer. Protected curtain faces remain distinct on both sides so their lower openings keep
the original sum of conductances. Smaller grids use the same block-column solve directly.
Eighth-order grids with at least 32,768 volume slots add the column and coarse corrections
independently. This skips two fine matrix products per iteration and one f64 scratch word
per volume slot. The geometry, linear residual target and iteration limit stay the same.
When at least half the volume is solid, the hot projection and fine-grid interpolation passes visit
an ordered list of wet cells. The list adds four bytes per wet cell. Published depth and source
arrays retain the rectangular layout.

The potential's constant mode is recovered separately for each connected wet basin. The mean
Robin flux equals the integrated signed source in that basin to floating-point precision. The
iterative solve supplies the relative potential and interior gradients.
Each unforced step uses one harmonic volume solve. A tick with submerged displacement uses one extra solve
to transfer those signed volumes to the surface. The accepted normal flux and depth potential come from the
same midpoint and previous state. The solver uses f64 for state and arithmetic. It retains the volume
potential in its snapshot. Source work includes the volume kick and the pressure held over the midpoint
step. Wave breaking, moving obstacles, turbulent edge losses and the fine-grid First Wake replay remain open.
See the entry size report for the optional loads entry.

`pressureAtDepth` adds one f64 head value per surface and volume cell. It uses the accepted potential's
midpoint time derivative with linear Bernoulli pressure and one-sided wet interpolation. `seaSurface()`
gives a consumer the retained pressure and velocities. At an enabled aperture the depth state can be wet
even when the surface is solid above it.

The finite `SurgeWakeCoupling` projects a unit station displacement through the same open faces, source
bands and geometry as the receiving wake. Its return impulse includes perimeter decay before the kick.
This accounts for longitudinal rigid and wave energy plus the sponge on one guided axis at a fixed draft.
It requires exclusive use of the submerged source port. The finite `FreeHullWakeCoupling` also uses the
receiver's wet-side surface kernel for heave, roll and pitch. It pairs all four unit profiles jointly before
publishing the rigid impulse and volume. On an active tick either coupling uses one volume projection
to construct its advancing basis and one to apply the scaled source. The three surface unit profiles
do not require volume solves. The waterplane and guided degrees of freedom above also apply near the fixed quay.

`Hull.wakeWaterplane` is an optional fixed-reference source for prescribed surface motion. The quadrature
uses three f64 values per node for local X, Z and area. The copied bake is paired with one five-f64 wake
row per node. The existing advancing source keeps its own resolution. Use a radius supported by the chosen
wake receiver and choose the spacing from the physical wavelengths. Changing the equilibrium mass or
density can require a new bake. Large heel and changes of immersion need a live waterplane.
The optional seakeeping entry measures 42,604 B gzip.

The finite point-depth port stores signed cubic metres per row at a discrete depth coordinate. It
linearly distributes the volume between the nearest wet depth samples, including the free surface.
The shared horizontal scatter uses four bilinear candidates per pass for radii up to one cell.
For a fractional interior position this replaces 16 candidate visits. The wet-side weights and
work ledger match the cosine stencil at that support exactly. The last depth cell and closed neighbours take the whole local share. Inspect the still-water
layer schedule and receiver spacing to resolve short vertical wavelengths. The band-based periodic
receiver and matched guided-hull operators use their existing source ports.

`Hull.wakeAdvancePoints` pairs with `HullSolver`'s optional `pointAdvance` field. The bake stores
four f64 values per centroid. The live port stores five f64 values per row and retains signed area
and first moments within each bin. Choose panel sizes and depth edges from the wavelengths and draft.
The same reference hull contributes heave, roll and pitch through its separate waterplane field.
Large immersion changes require a new reference or a live wetted surface.

Water's optional wake entry draws the rigid wet mask and the finite-domain heights from the same source.
The mask is fixed per attachment and occupies one u32 per cell on the GPU. The surface reconstruction
uses connected bilinear weights and the same wet-side derivative as the finite pressure receiver.
Dry fragments clip in the draw. WaveQuery intersections use the underlying displaced triangles. The
optional Water wake entry measures 3,264 B gzip.

### Dispersive wake options (SEA-04)

A uniform horizontal current advects the local linear modes. Spatial current gradients,
shear and refraction across current fronts need a variable-coefficient solve. Surface tension
adds gravity–capillary dispersion. The supplied viscosity damps both surface height and
potential with the leading-order clean-surface rate. Bottom boundary-layer damping, contamination,
nonlinear capillary interaction and overdamped viscous modes are outside this model.
The Scott tank comparison covers the independently measured 100–200 ms waves. Relative
wavelength RMS is 1.30%, compared with 22.36% for the gravity-only control. The observations'
reported wavelength precision is 0.4%, so the comparison retains a measurable discrepancy.

The optional SIMD FFT asset is 10,832 B gzip. Each native transform copies the real
grid and its half spectrum once. A source-free gravity step uses three forward and two
inverse transforms. Submerged source bands and stored water velocities add the transforms
reported by `fftWork()`. Rain contact locations and times come from the caller. Each pulse
models linear impulse and deposition over one wake tick.

The opt-in crest field publishes a resolved onset estimate. It rejects crests without a
trackable normal direction or displacement, and reports total rows even if the published
region fills. The wave solve stays linear and supplies onset in the interior away from
applied pressure, the absorber and untracked boundaries. Foam and spray use the same
reported area and crest state.

The optional prescribed mean hull closes the solid faces and uses the second-order
midpoint solve for the normal motion and pressure exchange. Its mask stays at the
reference shape. It represents small displacements and rotations about that shape.
`bakeWakeHullMask` samples a closed, consistently wound triangle mesh at the physical center
of each cell, respecting existing dry cells and exact seam copies. The shoreline and submerged
solid are resolved at grid spacing. Refine the grid to resolve narrow features. Give the baker
a non-self-intersecting mesh. Enclosed cavities follow even–odd fill.
The optional sea entry grows from 12,263 to 14,183 B gzip with a 14,609 B ceiling.
Freely advancing geometry and the held-out Wigley stem elevation remain open. The optional loads entry is 65,111 B gzip with a 67,065 B ceiling.

### Wave impact and green-water evidence and limits (SEA-11)

The strip slam uses one symmetric equivalent section per station, vertical penetration, and the existing
Wagner wetting relation and added-mass growth. Its pressure is a net force and pitch moment. It does not
resolve plating pressure, oblique flare entry, spray breakup or structural whipping. The code now retains
valid stations beneath locally lower decks. The optional native profile bake uses the same numerical
scheme and stores the tables in mesh order. Mesh, density and longitudinal resolution must match the
live hull. The workers act only while preparing the tables. Runtime reads the accepted baked tables.
The seakeeping entry is 48,146 B gzip. The optional strip Wasm is 20,492 B raw and 8,775 B gzip. The
lazy worker and its binding are 727 B gzip.

The green-water grid is shallow water in body coordinates. Its hydrostatic weight loads the deck and live
inlet records carry the receiving cell’s height even at interior mask edges. Its accepted depth and deck
height can be copied by the renderer after each tick. No reliable load on local vertical deck structures,
air entrainment or scupper flow is inferred from the grid.

The held-out Tveitnes comparison (`packages/physics/scripts/sea11-wedge-measured.mjs`) matches one of twelve
measured forces inside its repeatability and figure bounds. At z/d near 0.45, the 15°, 30° and 45°
predictions are 1,106, 542 and 519 N versus 648, 341 and 166 N observed. Near 0.85 they are 116, 162
and 248 N versus 638, 243 and 354 N. The 240–960 Hz sensitivity is at most 0.040 N. The recorded motor
speed is used and the wetted face impact speed was not measured. The test does not establish accuracy on
any measured deck structure. The digital case uses only primary inputs and no fitted coefficients.

The technical workboat in `packages/water/test/wave-impact-film.browser.mjs` couples the dynamic hull to
a 0.72 m wave. At the sampled impact the upward load differs by 69.7 kN and vertical speed by 0.929 m/s
from the matched slam-off control. The copied deck water spreads 1.04 m inboard, grows from 5.6 to
101.3 L, and drains when inflow stops. WebGPU and WebGL2 each reproduce full camera frames and accepted
world bytes through restore and replay. The original EF-6, CY-2 and CY-6 cuts remain open.

### Ship seakeeping evidence and limits (SEA-08)

The optional three-dimensional panel bake evaluates independently sampled reference-frequency systems,
with ordered f64x2 complex elimination and a scalar tail. Set `threads` to 1, 2 or 4. The serial path
is the default. Parallel baking uses independent Wasm memories and completes or rejects the entire response.
The threads do work during the bake. Runtime history integration uses the baked coefficient table.
The linearized panels preserve one reference draft and depth and are intended for small-amplitude motion.
The default strip solver uses deep-water sections. Lewis-form edge bounds and the roll-pivot bound still apply.
The seakeeping entry is 45,195 B gzip. The lazy panel Wasm is 52,774 B raw and 23,275 B gzip. The lazy
worker entry and its private binding are 630 B gzip.

The independent Park, Lee and Kim (2014) short and long KVLCC2 comparisons pass at λ/L = 0.5, 1.1 and 2.
The new physically matched Jung hinged-box regression gives 0.35051 vs 0.33271 observed and 0.89340 s vs
0.930 s using the published geometry and inertia. The unchanged 12% and 5% intervals are regression
tolerances. Kajitani’s Wigley surface elevations at 2x/L = −0.95 remain low on the 25 mm grid.
The solver gives 31.49 mm and 33.05 mm at Froude 0.267 and 0.316 versus 63.80 mm and 77.89 mm measured.
The procedure uses printed precision and does not infer a tank uncertainty band. The exact stem is also low.
[Park, Lee and Kim](https://doi.org/10.3744/SNAK.2014.51.5.396) · [Kajitani et al.](https://archive.org/details/DTIC_ADP003037)

The fixed-camera lake test derives the render mesh and the closed simulation mesh from the same procedural
16.8 m hull. It shows +0.345/−0.399 m heave, +1.16/−1.51° pitch, and 6.70° roll against 0.02° in the
calm control. The rendered wake follows the signed sources from the accepted hull. Snapshots and full
same-backend frames replay exactly on WebGPU and WebGL2. Original EF-1 and EF-2 remain open.

### Ship motion on the wake grid

`HullSolver` with the wake option publishes two five-word f64 records per reference waterplane station. The stamp uses one longitudinal midpoint and two transverse Gauss samples for a centreline-symmetric waterplane. Volume comes from small heave, pitch and roll about the reference draft. A wholly dry or submerged hull emits no waterplane flux. The model uses a signed surface-volume source. Its finite-depth wave propagation is handled by `WakeSolver`, and the hull's reaction still comes from its seakeeping solver. The projection has no three-dimensional radiation calibration or matched energy exchange with the wake grid.

With `submergedAdvance`, each depth band uses an equivalent contiguous lateral interval preserving the section area and first lateral moment. This covers eccentric and asymmetric sections. Disconnected spans are represented by one interval. Two Gauss points on each signed span difference give at most four nodes per station face and band. The bands use the reference upright draft and move with the hull’s horizontal pose. The option supports at most eight bands, 16,384 fixed rows per port and 1,048,576 grid cells. Each active band adds one forward FFT and no extra inverse transform. A nonzero source must reach the wake grid. With full stencil support, each radial tap is distributed to the four adjacent grid centres by bilinear area weights. This preserves the signed volume and its horizontal first moments through subcell motion. A patch clipped by the grid edge retains its volume if it reaches a grid centre. Include the hull’s trajectory and source footprint in the grid to preserve its moments.

The submerged patch radius is the greater of the caller's minimum radius and half a longitudinal station interval.
The transverse points already describe the span. An unchanging full-beam radius attenuated an exact longitudinal
box mode as the grid tightened. The controlled mode now matches the integrated end-face flux, finite-depth transfer
and bilinear grid weights. A second live test compares a closed workboat generated in code and imported from GLB.
Matching body-local geometry and rigid mass properties give identical sampled wake, rigid motion and seek.

The finite-depth transfer is the band average of cosh(k(y+D))/cosh(kD) for y measured up from still water. At k=0 it transmits the full volume. This is the no-flux-bed harmonic Green transfer underlying the Havelock source’s deep-water exponential factor in Eq. 4 of Tuck, Scullen and Lazauskas, *Ship-wave patterns in the spirit of Michell* (2000). WakeSolver advances the resulting surface with the linear potential equations in Tessendorf, *Simulating Ocean Water* (1999–2004), Eqs. 20–21 and 51–52. Tests check depth transfer at fixed wavelengths on three grids, net flux and first moments of an eccentric hull, and frame-zero replay on both arena layouts. The projected source describes linear waves. A straight quay can impose a separate reflecting boundary. The body–wake work ledger remains open. Resolve the desired waveform and independent measured amplitudes before use as a physical reference. [Tuck, Scullen and Lazauskas](https://www.scullen.com.au/DSc/Publications/tuck_scullen_lazauskas_00e.pdf) · [Tessendorf](https://jtessen.people.clemson.edu/reports/papers_files/coursenotes2004.pdf)

The original First Wake course with a closed solver hull proxy at 46d930c1a5 ran continuously for 4,005 steps on the 240 × 64 grid at 1.2 m per cell. At film time 67 s the signed elevation extrema were +0.5362 and −0.4332 m. At 71 s they were +0.3340 and −0.5219 m. The legacy transfer on the same grid gave +3.1298 and −2.7170 m at 67 s, and +2.4895 and −3.1574 m at 71 s. At 71 s the projection used 560 nonzero rows and seven forward transforms. The grid cannot resolve the roughly 1.44 m transverse wavelength at 1.50 m/s. The render mesh is unsuitable for a closed solver volume and no hull-line uncertainty is available for the proxy. These CPU results describe the signed response on that grid. The film physics comparison still needs a fixed-domain refinement with at least 9 cells per target wavelength, a qualified hull geometry and its reflective boundary.

The independent fixed bare KRISO container-ship (KCS) signed wave cut at 1.09864 m cross-track gave 15.55 and 15.10 mm RMS error after five and eight approach lengths across 469 measured stations, with 0.4695 mm reported experimental uncertainty. At eight lengths the predicted elevation RMS was 25.70 mm against 15.32 mm measured and the signed correlation was 0.847. No amplitude scaling, clock shift or use of measured elevations in solver inputs was permitted. The forecast used 0.25 m physical cells on a 200 × 16 m domain at depth 7 m, 96 stations and a closed section loft sampled every 0.025 m vertically from the published hull offsets. The 3.09 m transverse wavelength has about 12 cells. This was one spatial resolution with absorbing edges and an assumed startup history. The original ramp, shape-loft error, grid convergence, reflected waves and three-dimensional near-hull interaction remain unresolved. The comparison falls outside the measured uncertainty. [NMRI KCS case and raw measurements](https://www.nmri.go.jp/study/research_organization/fluid_performance/cfd/cfdws05/Detail/a1-1/index.html) · [Kim, Van and Kim, *Measurement of flows around modern commercial ship models*, 2001](https://doi.org/10.1007/s003480100332)

At 0.25 m per cell the original stencil gave 14.88 and 14.85 mm of profile RMS error at 14 approach lengths and 60 or 120 Hz. Refining the mesh from 0.025 to 0.0125 m vertically and 96 to 192 stations changed the reconstructed displacement from 1.6412 to 1.6449 m³, closer to the published 1.6490 m³. At eight approach lengths and 60 Hz, this mesh, eight instead of four transfer bands, and a 4 m instead of 2 m numerical sponge gave 15.34, 15.38, and 15.11 mm respectively. The subcell stencil reduced the 60 Hz error from 15.10 to 13.86 mm at eight lengths and from 14.88 to 13.60 mm at 14 lengths. Aft of x/L = 0.75 the corrected signed profile reaches 34.60 mm RMS where the measured profile gives 17.90 mm, with correlation 0.987. This residual persists with fixed physical inputs and no fitting. The linear source does not enforce impermeability of the disturbed flow at the hull. The experiment reports an unsteady wet transom flow that is outside this source model. [NMRI model particulars](https://www.nmri.go.jp/archives/institutes/fluid_performance_evaluation/cfd_rd/cfdws15/kcs_gc.html) · [Kim, Van and Kim, 2001](https://doi.org/10.1007/s003480100332)

The optional sea entry is 12,263 B gzip with a 12,631 B ceiling. The seakeeping entry grows from 37,788 to 39,440 B gzip with a 40,624 B ceiling.

## Node versions for test and tool scripts (scripts/support/node-compat.mjs, 2026-11-26)

Tests and repository scripts read Node's newer APIs through `scripts/support/node-compat.mjs`, so they run on Node 22.12. `registerHooks` falls back to `module.register`, `zstdDecompressSync` to `packages/shared/zstd.js`, and `zstdCompressSync` to a store-only zstd writer (`scripts/support/zstd-store.mjs`, raw blocks, so its output is not smaller than its input). The streaming `createZstdDecompress` has no fallback: below Node 22.22 it throws when called. Its one user, the sciviz data preparation script (`examples/assets/sciviz/geo-time/prepare.mjs`), needs Node 22.22 or newer.

### Bare-hull roll damping at forward speed

The `Hull.course` option includes the ITTC lift, skin friction and eddy damping terms when the water-relative longitudinal speed is positive. The three terms use the roll frequency estimated from the hull's hydrostatic stiffness and its high-frequency roll inertia. The formula uses the length at the reference waterline, maximum beam and draft, the midship area coefficient, and the vertical offset from the waterline to the centre of mass. Astern motion uses the still-water coefficients. This increment covers viscous bare-hull roll. Forward changes in wave radiation, bilge keels and a calibrated large-angle decay remain separate.

The forward-roll seakeeping entry is 25,505 B gzip with a 26,271 B ceiling. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

## React local lights and shading materials (react/clustered, react/textures, 2026-11-26)

`<PointLight>`, `<SpotLight>` and `<RectAreaLight>` (`@margoengine/react/clustered`) share one `Clustered` lighting per Canvas or `<Scene>`, so they take its limits: up to 1,024 point and spot lights and 64 rect area lights (the `Clustered` and `AreaLights` defaults), WebGPU only (the WebGL2 compatibility layer draws without them). One invalid light (a negative intensity, say) makes the whole list fail and reaches the `onError` of every light component in that Canvas, because the engine validates the list as one. A named `<Scene>`'s lights light that scene's core meshes; the Canvas's glTF and material meshes take only the Canvas's lights, as with `<Environment>`. `<ClusteredLighting>` (2026-11-26) exposes the shared lighting's `ClusteredOptions` with the engine's defaults: `grid` [16, 9, 24], `maxLights` 1,024 (up to 65,536) and `shadows` (off; `true` or `resolution` 512 and `maxLights` 4, at most 32 shadowed lights), and `<PointLight>` and `<SpotLight>` take a `shadow` (`true` or `near`, `far`, `bias`, `normalBias`, `resolution`) for an integrated map. The engine fixes those options at construction, so a changed `<ClusteredLighting>` prop, or mounting or unmounting it, disposes the shared `Clustered` (its shadow maps, cluster buffers and `AreaLights`) and makes it again with the same lights: one frame's worth of pipeline and buffer creation, not something to animate. Of several `<ClusteredLighting>` in one Canvas or Scene the last one committed sets the options. A light with a `shadow` and no `<ClusteredLighting shadows>`, more shadowed lights than `shadows.maxLights`, or a shadowed light with `range` 0 and no `shadow.far` fails the whole list as any invalid light does. With `shadows`, every `castShadow` mesh and model of the Canvas casts into the maps, found by a per-frame pass over the Canvas's caster registry; a named `<Scene>`'s lighting takes no casters, so its lights' maps stay empty. Not exposed: the `castShadow` lights of `LocalShadows` (`@margoengine/clustered/shadows`: PCSS from `shadow.radius`, directional and area-light shadows), the `bounce` flag, `intensityScale`, the 64 area light cap, and the IES, projector, layers, contact, shapes, stochastic and directional entries. The shading material components (`<UnlitMaterial>`, `<LambertMaterial>`, `<PhongMaterial>`, `<ToonMaterial>`, `<NormalMaterial>`, `<MatcapMaterial>`, `<DepthMaterial>`) are `TextureMaterial` with the class's `shading`: any option change rebuilds the material mesh, and the mesh needs UV geometry.

### Incident waves on a forward course

The ordinary-strip vertical excitation correction on `Hull.course` uses a `SpectralSea` wavelength, phase and amplitude for each wave. The world-space ship velocity gives the encounter frequency. The water-relative course controls the longitudinal added-mass term. The heave and pitch correction is added to the existing velocity-field convolution, including wake and current. Under very small encounter frequencies the finite-history static mass and continuous odd damping ratio replace the unresolved deep-water singularity. Two 56-value f64 arrays and one static mass value are retained per distinct section at the defaults. The section masses come from deep-water Lewis forms. The orbital wave input follows the specified depth. A free three-dimensional hull and a tank require additional measured qualification.

The incident-wave seakeeping entry is 27,343 B gzip with a 28,164 B ceiling. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Bilge keel plate damping

`Hull.bilgeKeels` normal drag and lift apply only when viscous roll damping is enabled. The rectangular-plate integration samples the local surface at two longitudinal stations, with a linear crossing from root to tip. It estimates roll excursion from the current pose and rate at the natural roll frequency, or at the frequency explicitly prescribed for a forced oscillator. The wet normal-force and lift terms cover small roll, a slender hull, and the configured water-relative forward speed. Skegs and large-angle decay measurements remain open.

The bilge-keel seakeeping entry is 28,329 B gzip with a 29,179 B ceiling. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Very small bilge keel excursions

The Wassermann force coefficient is used up to KC 3, with its lower endpoint held at KC 0.3 for smaller excursions. KC 3–4 blends continuously into the Ikeda force. This corrects the divergence of the drag coefficient in near-calm roll. The original Ikeda fit is retained past KC 4, including its pre-existing extrapolation beyond KC 20.

The small-excursion seakeeping entry is 28,388 B gzip with a 29,179 B ceiling. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Attached bilge keel hull pressure

Attach the authored plate midpoint to the closed hull mesh within `1e-8 × max(1 m, plate length)`. A detached plate retains its usual normal drag and lift. The attached pressure closure follows connected transverse mesh strips from the keel to the first waterline or half-section boundary, with two longitudinal samples. It targets a single connected hull contour. It adds a roll moment only. Other force and torque axes from the pressure footprint, phase lag, and physical measurements of hull-pressure amplitudes remain open.

The bilge hull-pressure seakeeping entry is 29,592 B gzip with a 30,480 B ceiling. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Bilge keel added inertia

The `addedMass` path applies the plate’s normal virtual mass through the existing six-axis solve. A dry plate adds zero. The model uses the oscillatory long-plate wall calibration and the current harmonic roll-amplitude estimate. Finite-section and mount-gap corrections, wave excitation of the plates and higher time harmonics remain open. The estimate is a local virtual mass, with no separate time derivative of the plate’s mass matrix during a fast wetting transition.

The bilge virtual-inertia seakeeping entry is 30,177 B gzip with a 30,480 B ceiling. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Holdout roll damping and period with bilge keels

The IIT Madras BK10 flume case gives a damping ratio within its measured repeat variation at two time steps. For the same test the computed period is about 6% short. The bare control also over-predicts damping. This constrained-roll result covers the specified geometry and input only. Period, whole-hull added inertia and nonlinear wake pressure remain separate limitations.

### Three-dimensional surge added mass

The per-hull `surgeAddedMass` flag defaults to false. It uses at most 512 wetted triangular panels at the reference draft and requires the hull to stay clear of the reference bed. The matrix is filled and factored when the optional feature first encounters a wet hull. Assembly uses quadratic storage and the factorization takes cubic work in the panel count. The deep-water branch uses an odd free-surface reflection. The finite-depth branch uses twelve alternating image shells. The cached scalar affects surge acceleration under the existing `addedMass` option. Fully dry hulls carry zero surge inertia. A manoeuvring solver that claims the added mass continues to own its surge row. The option covers the high-frequency limit, with depth and draft held at their reference values. Finite-frequency 3D damping, diffraction and off-diagonal panel forces remain open.

The 3D axial seakeeping entry is 31,553 B gzip with a 32,500 B ceiling. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Seakeeping speed through a current

A configured `Hull.course` uses the surface sample’s mean current when speed is omitted. This is a surface reference velocity at the hull centre, with no depth average over strong shear. An explicit water-relative speed is supported. The incident phase follows the hull’s actual motion relative to the coordinates in which the wave spectrum is defined.

The current-relative seakeeping entry is 31,633 B gzip with a 32,500 B ceiling. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Seakeeping bow and stern displacement

The optional `HullWake.advance` flag starts off. It adds one source row per station face plus the two end faces, for `stations + 1` additional rows per hull. It uses the signed rigid-body speed along the horizontal hull axis relative to the mean surface flow and the untrimmed section areas at the hull’s still-water draft. Only freely moving, surface-piercing hulls emit this source. The depth-integrated approximation sends its volume to the same linear dispersive grid as heave, pitch and roll. Grid propagation keeps the wakes in the grid’s frame, and accuracy near broad bows, breaking waves and strong spatial currents remains unqualified. A vessel’s advance pressure wake and displacement wake are alternative inputs for the same effect.

The advancing-hull seakeeping entry is 31,849 B gzip with a 32,500 B ceiling. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

Using the same wake as a `SpectralSea` patch returns pressure to the advancing hull. The prism test accounts for its rigid impulse and work from the two face pressures. This pressure law treats the wake height as a near-surface head, and the full dispersive grid energy ledger remains open. [Coupling and bounds](./clean-room.md#sea-08-pa-13-wake-pressure-returned-to-the-moving-hull)

The independent Wigley tank comparison at 25 mm grid spacing gives 31.5 and 33.0 mm near the bow, versus 63.8 and 77.9 mm measured at the two fixed-sinkage towing speeds. The crest arrives farther aft in the numerical case. [Measured conditions and reproduction](./clean-room.md#sea-08-independently-measured-wigley-waterline)

### Seakeeping short-wave resistance

`Hull.shortWaveResistance` defaults to false. It uses the mean reference waterline, a projected bow or stern incidence, the absolute forward Froude number and a linear spectral energy sum. It supplies a horizontal axial force through the body centre. Its wall-sided reflection approximation leaves motion-induced head-wave drag, nonlinear breaking and pressure distribution along the hull outside its scope. The conventional speed curve was measured at `λ/L = 0.3`, and finite-depth, large-Froude and strongly following sea extensions are unqualified. The hull must be surface-piercing and the supplied sea must expose spectral wave components.

The short-wave seakeeping entry is 32,715 B gzip with a 33,698 B ceiling. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Developing fin-jet wall layer (SEA-15)

`turbulentTransition` defaults to false. When enabled, a round jet between two and four nozzle diameters from a flat bed develops a turbulent layer past the constant-pressure plateau if its predicted shear exceeds the laminar shear there. The stationary approximation omits adverse pressure gradients, turbulence history, jet travel time and sub-diameter clearances. The paired render carries suspended sediment 15.9 px downstream. The scoped tracer entry grows from 15,007 B to 15,323 B gzip within its 16,702 B ceiling.

Fin-wake and hull-opening coordinates use the common cell length (4,096 m by default). Translating hull openings replaces the same-cell check and reduces the current entry from 15,368 B to 15,322 B gzip.
Fin jets use the tangent plane of the terrain triangle under the source. This preserves normal clearance, normal momentum and pickup area over planar slopes. Curved or stepped beds can depart from that local plane, and the annular stress omits the directional shear of an oblique jet. The scoped entry with the plane projection is 15,449 B gzip.

### Bow tunnel discharge for bed wash (SEA-15)

The optional `Ship.thrusterOutlet` samples a straight submerged round jet. It omits quay and bed reflection, crossflow bending, and travel time after a change in command. The configured diameter and outlet position determine a Gaussian profile whose centreline was 12.7% high against the independent laboratory fit at 20 diameters. Configuring any outlet adds 64 bytes of live state per ship slot. The scoped ship entry grows from 13,770 B to 14,217 B gzip within its 14,951 B ceiling.

## Point and sprite pixel sizes are CSS pixels (2026-11-27)

`size`, `minPixelSize`, `maxPixelSize` and pixel sprite sizes of `@margoengine/points` (`PointsPlugin`, `SurfelPlugin`, and so `PointPicking` and `PointRaycaster`) and a pixel `size` of `DeformedPoints` are CSS pixels, as `@margoengine/lines` widths and the glTF `pointSize` extras are: each covers the drawn target's width over the canvas's CSS width, in target pixels. A canvas without a CSS width (offscreen, or hidden during a `@margoengine/exporters` capture) counts 1. Until 2026-11-27 these were target pixels, so on a canvas backed above 1 pixel per CSS pixel marks now draw larger by that ratio, the default 1 and 256 clamps included. A view drawn into a texture takes the texture's width over the canvas's CSS width, as lines do. `edlRadius` and `OctreeCloud`'s `minNodePixels` stay pixels of the drawn target. Proof: `packages/points/tests/pixel-density-browser.mjs` (20 CSS pixel marks at 1 and 2 pixels per CSS pixel, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer).

## Points on a deforming mesh (animation/deformed-points, 2026-11-26)

`DeformedPoints` (`@margoengine/animation/deformed-points`) draws one camera-facing quad per vertex of a `gltf/pbr` model, instanced from the 80-byte vertices its deformer wrote (`PBRPrimitive.deformed`), on WebGPU and on the WebGL2 compatibility layer. Defaults: `size` 4, `sizeUnits` 'pixels', `color` white, `opacity` 1, `shape` 'square', `vertexColors` true, `visible` true. One draw and one 256-byte uniform slot per primitive; a primitive with no deformer costs a second copy of its vertices (80 bytes each), uploaded once and again only when its vertex array is replaced. Sizes are not clamped: a world-sized point close to the camera can fill the view, and a size of 0 draws nothing. A point is cut by the near plane as a whole at its centre's depth. Round points are a disc cut from the square with no antialiasing beyond the target's MSAA. Opacity below 1 blends over the frame so far in draw order (pass order 1, after the model) and still writes depth, so points do not sort among themselves. Unlit; no shadows, fog, picking, clipping planes, per-point sizes or textures (`@margoengine/points` has those for clouds it owns). `EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing` primitives show one set of points at their node, not one per instance. Render layers do not filter the points; `visible` does. The small WebGL2 preview tier throws `unsupported`.

A hidden model deforms only while a `DeformedPoints` reads it (a count per model in `packages/animation/src/deform-readers.ts`); with `visible` false the points still count as a reader until disposed.

New entry @margoengine/animation/deformed-points: 4,286 B gzip, ceiling 4,542 B. The animation root gains the reader check and stays inside its recorded 26,165 B ceiling. Core and stage gain zero bytes (24,846 B).

## Morph weights per crowd member (animation/instanced-morph, 2026-11-26)

`MorphedCrowd` (`@margoengine/animation/instanced-morph`) gives each member of a bone-texture crowd its own morph weights, on WebGPU and on the WebGL2 compatibility layer. Limit: 64 live targets per bake (`MORPH_TARGET_LIMIT`); `bakeMorphBones` throws RangeError past it, and its `morphs` option names the targets that stay live (the rest are baked in at the model's current weights). A member row is 28 + 4 * ceil(targets / 4) floats (128 to 368 bytes), in the crowd's one instance buffer; a change to any member uploads all rows with the next frame (as every `VATCrowd` instance change does), so setting weights on 10,000 members with 8 targets writes 1.44 MB that frame. Weights are any finite float32; they are not clamped. Target offsets are position and normal only (no tangents), two rgba32float texels per vertex of each primitive that has the target, stored after the bone rows of the bake's 2,048-texel-wide texture: bone rows, one entry texel per (primitive, live target) block and the offsets together must fit 8,192 rows (16,777,216 texels), else RangeError. Texel indices are held as float32, exact over that whole range. The vertex stage reads one entry texel per block of the vertex's own primitive and two more per non-zero weight. New members start at the weights the model had when baked. Targets are joined by name across primitives; two different targets with one name share a weight. Everything else is `SkinnedCrowd`'s (opaque, no CPU culling, WebGPU device needed; the small WebGL2 preview tier throws `unsupported`).
