New entry @margoengine/animation/instanced-morph: 11,416 B gzip, ceiling 11,759 B, of which the skinned crowd it extends is about 10 KB (an app that loads both entries loads that part once). `@margoengine/animation/instanced-skin` gains the layout parameter and stays inside its recorded 10,303 B ceiling. Core and stage gain zero bytes (24,892 B on this base).

### Hull-launch cavity and splash

EntryBody.effectsOnly follows the hull for cavity and splash and leaves its fluid force and displacement in HullSolver. The optional cavityPressure field applies zero gauge pressure behind the transverse contact plane through the hull center while the cavity is open. HullSolver clips pressure and form drag against the plane. The model treats the cavity as vented and uses the existing entry contact-plane approximation. The other hydrostatic, slamming and wake models retain their existing geometry. Observed entry events still carry the source body's speed, direction and height on the live surface. Entry moved from 9,053 to 9,429 B gzip. Seakeeping moved from 33,986 to 34,437 B gzip. Both are within their recorded ceilings and Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Seakeeping full KVLCC2 head-wave benchmark

The measured mean resistance intervals are met at `λ/L = 1.1` and 2.0 on the freely pitching and heaving hull at fixed tow speed with `shortWaveResistance` enabled. The draft-qualified 41 by 13 hull meets the heave and pitch intervals at both wavelengths. At 1.1 it yields 0.75550 and 0.58761 within upper limits of 0.7671 and 0.59368. The volume-matched reference draft is 0.977 mm from nominal. The free-surge case and distributed measured pressure remain open. [Geometry and experiment](clean-room.md#sea-08-measured-resistance-and-motion-on-the-full-kvlcc2-hull)

### SEA-12 rigid member vibration

The opt-in acceleration-coupled wake represents one coherent cross-flow mode on a slender circular member
in a nearly uniform steady current. The shedding frequency must be below half the world rate. Force and
torque act through the wetted interval centre. The independent Carberry case gives lift-frequency ratios
1.15000048 and 1.15000026 at the two tested rates, within 0.007875 of 1.15. The held-out evidence covers
frequency entrainment. Quantitative force phase, free-vibration amplitude and switching between wake branches
require separate models and proof.

### SEA-12 reciprocal shallow-water obstruction

The guided cut-cell mode accepts one upright full-depth convex footprint in a flat, wet periodic grid. The
two footprint extents fit within one cell. When the smallest cell approaches closure, the pressure stages
use its conserved state together with a wet neighbour across the greatest open face. A fully covered
cell publishes zero water and rejoins its neighbour's fluid when it reopens. The circular constructor uses
a 64-sided inscribed footprint with area error below 0.17%. A rectangle uses its supplied edges. The footprint translates linearly during
each step. Rigid coupling locks vertical translation and rotation and requires passive settlement of each
pressure impulse in the published f32 body state. A separate prescribed-path option reports the pressure
reaction without moving a rigid body. The method covers periodic interior translation. Multiple moving
solids, wet/dry cut cells and unrestricted 3D motion need a resolved fluid model.

The supported guided rectangle stays exactly at rest at depths of 0.9 m and 1.0625 μm near 78.49% occupancy.
A 4×4 unit grid with 0.75 m clear depth uses two substeps per tick at rest, both at 99% solid occupancy and
with one completely covered cell. A moving guided rectangle closes and reopens that cell, then travels
across a periodic seam with reciprocal pressure impulse, decreasing coupled energy and exact replay.
A fully closing footprint in co-moving water repeats 50 seams over 1,200 ticks and 7,200 pressure
stages. The 0.125 m³ volume and 234.375 N·s water momentum stay within 256 machine epsilons of
their exact values, and a capped seek restores the same bits.
A binary-exact co-motion stress completed 2,400 ticks and 75 periodic seam crossings with 9,600 substeps,
water volume drift of (1.0×10^{-14}) m³ and momentum drift of (1.82×10^{-11}) N·s. The cycle replays with
the same hash. At each substep the 3×3 periodic grid evaluates 36 HLL face terms. The cut-cell checkpoint
put the hydro entry at 14,291 B gzip, up from 13,617 B. Projected hull and compact-body drag, paddle and wading drag,
and the passive and actuated swimmer reactions exchange horizontal momentum with the existing water grid. The
exchange stencil must remain wet during the step. Rigid axis locks and joints carry external support
reactions. The coupled conservation tests close the free horizontal degrees of freedom. Install the
coupled water and bodies at their intended origin cells. An origin shift after the group starts requires
rebuilding the exchange. This group needs shallow water without the separate guided cut-cell mode.
The depth-averaged grid carries hydrostatic vertical pressure. The Life entry measures 6,884 B gzip, up from 6,645 B. Its optional plain and shared Wasm
assets are 6,890 and 6,981 B raw. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

`ShallowWaterSolver.withFloodLoads` settles paddle and wading profiles after finite-volume transport.
The same-rate body recipients consume the settled loads in the same tick. It uses the final f64 depth,
bed and periodic cell images. Each exchange changes only horizontal water momentum and leaves depth
unchanged. Waders receive buoyancy from the final immersed profile. The water applies paddle exchanges
first and then wading exchanges in input order. Use the fixed bed origin and unit water time scale.
The standalone pre-transport adapters require a persistently wet exchange stencil. The Hydro entry
grows from 18,846 to 22,061 B gzip. The Loads entry grows from 42,251 to 42,369 B gzip. Water field
declarations live outside the settlement code, so surge and surf keep their existing size budgets.
[Labbé et al., Physics of rowing oars (2019), Eq. 3a](https://doi.org/10.1088/1367-2630/ab4226),
[Orselli and Duarte, Joint forces and torques when walking in shallow water (2011), section 2.4](https://ebm.ufabc.edu.br/publications/md/JB11b.pdf)

The optional projected rigid drag settlement supports wetting and drying on standard shallow water.
This raises the Hydro entry from 14,291 to 18,841 B gzip, including periodic stencil handling.
It resolves the final f64 wetted profile, applies one horizontal impulse exchange per body per tick,
and orders overlapping four-cell stencils by rigid row. It respects the resolved periodic axes, using
nearest-image moment arms and one mobility per actual fluid cell. A dry profile produces a zero receipt.
The same-tick relay forwards its horizontal impulse and moment. The first-order transport/exchange
split carries these impulses in the next water step. Volume and shoreline motion follow HYDRO.
The conservation and passivity proof uses free body mobility in the fixed common origin at unit
time scale. Rigid supports, hydrostatic forcing and external flows keep their separate momentum effects.

The optional six-axis radiation profile represents small motions at its zero-speed reference draft. The
fit retains a symmetric positive semidefinite instantaneous inertia and passive modal residues. Away
from that draft it scales them with immersed volume and preserves the modal storage balance. This
scaling approximates changing displacement. It has no variable-mass impulse or convective correction.
Its coupled coefficients are valid about the rigid centre of mass recorded in the body port. The native
solver holds 32 words per ordinary row and 41 per coupled row. It uses at most one native call per
active layout with one arena scratch region. Its plain and shared assets each measure 7,668 B raw,
from 2,884 B. Shared memory uses the same synchronous dispatch.

The optional `water/shallow-surface` renderer mirrors the current Hydro grid with one CPU sample and two
RGBA32F texel writes per cell each frame. The terrain dimensions and centre must match the Hydro grid.
The depth and bed drive Water’s existing shoreline, elevation and depth effects. Visual velocity uses
its coastal reconstruction. The adapter inherits the same shoreline threshold and supplies no breaker
or foam source. The standalone GPU Flood continues to own its separate simulation. The optional
entry is 1,706 B gzip under a 1,962 B ceiling. Water, Core and Stage roots gain zero bytes.

`Flood.coupleRigidDrag` pairs a standalone GPU Flood with one dynamic body with free horizontal
translation. Both advance at 120 Hz with fixed terrain and inputs. The split drag uses one
centre-of-mass cell and a vertical profile, with area 10⁻¹² to 10⁸ m², half-height 10⁻⁹ to 10⁵ m,
drag coefficient 0 to 100 (default 1) and density 10⁻⁶ to 10⁶ kg/m³ (default 1,025). The applied
impulse follows the actual f32 momentum difference. One full-grid copy pass and one 512-byte
asynchronous readback per tick are paid only by paired sessions with the body on the grid. The
exchange stays within the Flood speed bound. Pressure blockage, vertical force, torque, multiple
bodies and live input edits use other paths or remain outside this GPU tier. After abort, the pair
seeks by restoring its start state and replaying. Device or terrain replacement needs a fresh pair.
Supported on both renderers. Real-time readback throughput is unmeasured. The optional Flood entry
grew from 14,457 to 17,057 B gzip. Water, Core and Stage roots gain zero bytes.

Capsule buoyancy uses the local Y axis and a water plane at the body's horizontal centre. A
positive radius and nonnegative cylindrical half-height define the submerged solid. The solver
integrates whole disks analytically and uses tangent-split Gauss–Legendre quadrature for partial
disks. It applies the result at the volume centroid. Drag uses the circular and stadium projections.
The added-inertia model uses a second-moment-equivalent ellipsoid. Spatially varying incident
pressure requires a closed mesh. The Loads entry grew from 40,318 to 41,548 B gzip. Physics,
core and stage roots gain zero bytes.

### Seakeeping encounter-scaled taper loads

The incident-wave velocity and the longitudinal added-mass gradient use the same encounter scaling. The finite-memory continuation applies inside the first tabulated band. Tank qualification of the forward-motion amplitudes and near-stationary three-dimensional flow remain open. The seakeeping entry moved from 33,399 to 33,432 B gzip under its 33,698 B ceiling. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Finite-frequency three-dimensional hull panels

The optional panel bake fits linear potential flow at one reference draft, centre, density and flat-bed depth. It cuts the wetted hull into at most 768 constant triangles and requires their edges to stay under one eighth of the shortest baked wavelength. It takes 2 to 64 angular frequencies. Directional diffraction uses 4 to 64 regularly spaced headings (16 by default, 0 for radiation alone). It applies heading and frequency interpolation. The high end tapers to zero over an additional interval, so the sea still exerts incident pressure at unsampled frequencies. At short encounter wavelengths a mesh can require more than 768 triangles. The solve is intended for small motion. Existing forward strip corrections still have their independent range, and the 3D panel free-surface condition has zero forward speed. It covers flat finite depth and deep water. It does not solve flow separation or wave breaking.

For N panels, the bake assembles N² complex panel influences and uses one partial-pivot factorization per frequency, shared by all radiation motions and incident headings. As N rises from 144 to 480, the influence count rises from 20,736 to 230,400 and trailing factor updates from 984,984 to 36,748,880. The cost is paid during the optional bake rather than the world step. The native response is independent of world-shared memory. Seakeeping measures 37,493 B gzip at a 38,618 B ceiling. The lazy Wasm is 50,232 B raw and 22,012 B gzip. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.
## Physics worlds in netcode (`@margoengine/netcode/physics`)

`physicsGame` keeps a world's whole snapshot as the rollback state, so each simulated frame copies the world's memory twice (a load and a save): 1,661,504 bytes for the test's world of nine bodies, most of it room the world keeps to grow. Its cost follows the world's memory, not what moves, and the session keeps `maxRollback + 2` of them. The world must hold the same bodies, colliders and joints for the whole session, and a world that grows its memory is refused with the sizes. `snapshotDiff` compares 32-bit words, so a change anywhere in a word sends the whole word; a step of one rolling ball in that world is 221 bytes. `BodyInterpolator` moves proxies through `setNextPosition` and `setNextRotation`, so they reach the sampled pose at the end of their next step.

## Motor joint and extra substeps per island (own solver)

A motor joint's six motors solve one axis at a time, each capped alone, and the sliding three and the turning three are then cut back together to their caps as vectors, as Box2D cuts its motor joint's impulse; within a pass the axes do not see each other's cut until the next. Its spring is per kilogram along each row (the `acceleration` motor model), so a body hangs `g / (2 pi frequency)^2` below its target under gravity, and a pull capped far below what the spring asks cannot brake in time: the body overshoots and swings in. `body.additionalSubsteps` holds from 0 to 1024; an island takes the most its bodies ask, so one fine body makes its whole island fine. Stepped phase by phase (`islandMajor: false`, deprecated) there is one count for the world, so every island takes the most any asks.

## Phase vocoder (audio/vocoder, 2026-11-27)

`@margoengine/audio/vocoder` closes the earlier "phase vocoder is not built" gap (time stretch and pitch shift).

- Offline only: whole decoded signals in memory, with no streaming or live form (the mixer's pitch shift is the live
  one). Besides the input it holds the percussive part (input size), the stretched signal (input size times
  `factor * 2 ** (semitones / 12)`) and, with a pitch shift, the result, all as `Float32Array`s.
- Partials closer than about three window bins (35 Hz at the default 85 ms) are not separated: they are heard as one
  beating partial whose beat is stretched with it. In a C major seventh chord with notes 15 Hz apart one partial came
  out at 5 % of its level at the default window; all eight stay within 5 % at `frameMs: 170` with `transients: false`.
- Attacks: the split works only when lengthening. Overlap-add repeats a hit every few milliseconds, so an isolated
  click's peak is 0.85 to 0.98 of the input's at factors 1.5 to 3 (over a sustained tone at 1.5 it is still about twice
  what `transients: false` gives), and noise bursts carry about 1.3 dB less energy than their stretched length would.
  With nothing else sounding, the vocoder alone can keep a single click's peak higher.
- Formants: the envelope is a cepstral fit to the spectral peaks, with the correction held within 60 dB. On a test
  vowel (150 Hz harmonics, one resonance at 900 Hz) shifted by 5 semitones each way, harmonics from 300 to 1800 Hz stay
  within 4 dB of the original envelope. The percussive part is not corrected.
- Pitch shifts resample with the `/resample` defaults: shifting down leaves the top of the band empty, and shifting up
  removes what would pass 0.92 of the Nyquist frequency.
- Quality is measured on generated signals only (README); no listening test and no rival comparison has been run.
- TypeScript on one thread. 30 s of stereo at 48 kHz stretched by 1.25 took 5.0 s in Node on a busy workstation (7.5 s
  with a 3 semitone shift, 8.9 s with formants kept too). A Rust/Wasm version waits for the speed phase's paired runs.
  The event loop gets a turn, and the signal is checked, every 16 vocoder frames.

## Snapshot rendering (2026-11-27)

- `@margoengine/culling/snapshot` records only core's main draw; packages that draw their own batches draw as before,
  and a draw with extra colour attachments never records (a render bundle must name every attachment format, and a
  `GPUTextureView` does not expose its format).
- With `indirect: false` every count change records again; with the default `indirect: true` every core draw of the
  frame goes through drawIndexedIndirect, one 20-byte argument buffer per geometry.
- Core + stage 24,989 to 25,099 B gzip (+110 B) for `DrawOptions.snapshot`; the limit is now 25,100 B
  (`scripts/core-budget.js`).

## Multi-draw (2026-11-27)

- `@margoengine/culling/multidraw` draws ranges of one merged core geometry; every mesh of the geometry draws the same
  shown ranges. Picking draws the whole geometry, hidden ranges included. One package redirects a batch at a time, so a
  MultiDraw geometry is not also given to `CulledMeshes`.
- One call per frame needs the multi-draw-indirect feature (`chromium-experimental-multi-draw-indirect`, a Chromium
  experiment of the WebGPU proposal). No browser on the dev PC exposes it (Edge 158, the WebGL2 layer), so the one-call
  path is checked with a shim of the call; elsewhere, and always inside a snapshot's render bundle, the ranges draw one
  `drawIndexedIndirect` each.
- Core + stage 25,099 to 25,149 B gzip (+50 B) for `Batch.draws` and `Batch.multi`; the limit is now 25,150 B.

## Dual-source transmission blending (2026-11-27)

- One dual-source draw replaces the tint draw and the lit draw only where transmission takes the tinted blend: the
  beauty pass on a linear target (under Tonemap or Bloom, for example) or without native glass, with no transmission
  hook, no OIT pass, no capture and no `renderState.blend`. Native glass on display-encoded targets is unchanged.
- A shading hook that rewrites the lit or tint entry point, or a surface reading sample coverage (alpha to coverage),
  keeps its two draws under 'auto'; 'dual-source' then throws MargoError `unsupported`.
- The WebGL2 layer needs `WEBGL_blend_func_extended` for the feature; without it the device does not offer it and
  'auto' draws twice.
- Core + stage stayed at 25,149 B gzip: the feature is requested through `EngineOptions.features`.

## JPEG 2000 decoding

`@margoengine/decoders/jpeg2000` (2026-11-27) reads JPEG 2000 Part 1 (JP2 and raw codestreams) to RGBA8 or RGBA16, in
module workers or, through `loadJPEG2000`, on the calling thread. Compute's ONNX ImageDecoder uses it.

Limits: output up to `maxPixels` (default 2^26, maximum 2^28) and four times as many samples over all components;
input up to 1 GiB; 65,535 tiles and 2^20 tile-components (tiles times components); 2^22 code-blocks a tile, each band of
a precinct counting as four; a work budget of 2^28 plus 64 per input byte for precinct, code-block and progression
visits (headers can ask for far more of them than their bytes carry); 31 coded bit-planes a code-block (so component
precisions near the standard's 38 bits are refused); 1,024 palette entries. Over a limit throws `RangeError`. Wasm
memory is 32-bit, so a picture near the largest limits can fail to allocate (`MargoError` `failed`). `decodeImage` of
`/image` reads JPEG 2000 to RGBA8 and refuses a file that stops early.

Not read: the HT block coder of Rec. ITU-T T.814 | ISO/IEC 15444-15 and the Part 2 extensions (`unsupported`); JPX
files beyond their JP2 boxes. A restricted ICC profile (matrix and curve RGB, or curve grey) is applied, giving sRGB;
a profile built on lookup tables alone is not, and its samples come out as coded. Subsampled components are resampled
to the largest component by nearest sample.

Checked against another implementation (2026-11-27): 16 streams written by OpenJPEG 2.5.4 through Pillow 13.0.0
(`tests/generate-jpeg2000-openjpeg.py`: the five progression orders, tiles, offsets, precincts, quality layers, PLT,
both wavelets and component counts 1 to 4) decode exactly when lossless and within one 8-bit level when lossy. They
use no code-block style option, packed packet headers, region of interest or subsampling. Malformed input is fuzzed
(`tests/jpeg2000-fuzz.test.js`: 10,086 cases a run, and three runs of 154,086 on 2026-11-27 with no trap or hang).

Conformance (2026-11-27, `tests/jpeg2000-conformance.mjs`): the decoder tests of Rec. ITU-T T.803 (11/2002) |
ISO/IEC 15444-4 pass, all 78 reference components of Classes 0 and 1 for Profiles 0 and 1 within their peak and mean
squared error (Tables C.1, C.4, C.6, C.7), run by the crate's native `t803` example, and all nine JP2 files within a
peak of 2 against their sRGB references (Table G.1 allows 4), run through the shipped Wasm. The set is downloaded by
hand and never in the repository. Not covered: the test sets of the later editions of T.803 (2021 and 2024), which ITU
serves separately; no certification and no speed claim is made.

Size (Vite library min+gzip, with its lazy asset references): `/jpeg2000` 77,274 B, ceiling 79,593 B; `/image` (which
reaches it for a JPEG 2000 file) 1,115,762 B, ceiling 1,149,041 B; `jpeg2000.wasm` 132,372 B raw. Nothing loads unless a file needs the
decoder. Core plus stage is unchanged.

Transparent canvas through TAA, DOF and SceneFade (2026-11-27): by method, on a `TransparentCanvas` TAA's history depth
is `rg32float` (8 bytes a pixel per history instead of 4) and its resolve reads alpha for the 3x3 neighbourhood and
history taps; DOF adds an `r32float` plane at a quarter of the gather's pixels and, with `temporal`, one at the gather's
size. `TAAUpscale` adds no memory. An opaque canvas keeps its shaders and memory. No speed figure.

Raw shaders in SSR, SSGI and GTAO (2026-11-28): by method, `ssr.add(raw)` and `ssgi.add(raw)` add one capture draw per
opaque raw mesh a frame (the meshes with `captureEntry` through it, the rest depth only, their colour fragment with every
target's write mask 0), and one pipeline per material and effect; GTAO takes `gbufferEntry` as SSAO does. Checked on an
RTX A6000, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (`packages/shader/test/raw-check.mjs`: a raw mirror floor reflects a red wall,
241 against 33 of 255 red without the entry; a raw white floor takes the wall's red bounce, 248 against 111; GTAO darkens
the crease 216 against 240). three.js's screen-space passes draw a custom `ShaderMaterial` through an override material,
so they see its geometry's normals, not the ones the shader computes; a raw mesh here gives its own. Scene targets, the
node `ScenePass` and Clustered's bounce take it through `captureEntry` too (2026-11-27; `raw-check.mjs` `mrtOwn`, `passOwn`:
base colour 51, 153, 229 and the normal up in the targets, nothing without the entry). No speed figure.

WebGL2 layer, colour targets without a fragment output (2026-11-28): a WebGPU pipeline whose target has write mask 0
and no shader output draws with that draw buffer off (`packages/webgl2-compat/test/silent-targets-browser.mjs`, before:
GL_INVALID_OPERATION "Active draw buffers with missing fragment shader outputs" on ANGLE, KB-COMPAT-SILENTTARGET1); such
a pipeline sets its draw buffers before and after each draw, two `drawBuffers` calls. No speed figure.

## Stepping: animator/stepping (2026-11-27, KB-STEP-CROUCH1)

`createStepper({legs, start, routes, footfall?, foot?, settle = 0.58 s, kneeFlexion = 8 deg, liftRate = 0.64 m/s})` walks two legs over planned footfalls, left first, and `upperBodyMotion(motion)` returns pelvis, chest, head and arm angles. Kinematic only: no ground forces, no balance recovery, no running. The pelvis plan is sampled every 18 ms over every route given, rate limited to `liftRate`, smoothed by a 21-tap raised cosine and lowered by the filtered window maximum of its excess; between samples the live ceiling clamps it, so a planted leg is never asked past its length. Measured on a 0.88 m leg: level 0.62 m strides give standing knees 8 to 14 degrees, a single-support median of 17, a swing peak of 66 and 4.7 cm of pelvis travel (Perry and Burnfield 2010: about 5, 15 to 20 and 60 degrees; Gard, Miff and Kuo 2004: 4 to 5 cm). The stepping-stones route gives a single-support median of 19 and a peak of 79 (stair ascent swings near 90, Riener, Rabuffetti and Frigo 2002). Standing pelvic list is capped at 0.12 rad, so feet more than about 3 cm apart in height still bend the higher knee. Routes must all have the first route's length. No core or stage bytes.

KB-USDZ-FACTORS1 measured gzip/ceiling changes (2026-11-28): usdz 13,740 to 14,738 B (ceiling 15,156), usdz/worker 14,792 to 15,783 B (16,231), usdz/compose 24,714 to 25,725 B (26,473), usdz/preview-surface 5,479 to 6,278 B (6,509), usdz/clips 28,402 to 29,384 B (30,240), dist/workers/usdz.js 162,958 to 163,956 B (168,844). The bytes read texture scale and bias, emission, occlusion and normal scale in both importers; a split entry would leave the plain import with wrong materials. Core + stage is unchanged.

KB-SHRUB-TUNDRA1 measured gzip/ceiling change (2026-11-28): procedural/tree to 6,418 B (ceiling 6,674, was 6,363), for the leaf blade and stem builders both shrubs use. Core + stage is unchanged.

## Terrain bump near the camera (KB-TUNDRA-GROUNDNOISE1, 2026-11-28)

With `TerrainLayer.bump`, where a pixel covers less than 1/128 of a repeat (3 cm at `scale` 0.25) the relief holds no
detail finer than that, and each showing layer costs 16 texel loads per triplanar axis there (one axis on most ground).
Core and stage are unchanged.

### People obey anatomy by default (`@margoengine/humans`, `./body`, 2026-11-28)

`addPerson` fits the human table to any rig a naming of `fitHuman` knows and holds every clip at the `structural` tier;
`addBody` builds a person from bones and skinned meshes made in code the same way. Limits and accepted differences:

- Calibration reads the roll of the shoulders and hips only from the clips (`hingeRolls`), and trusts a roll only up to
  30 degrees: a clip that bends an elbow the wrong way would otherwise teach a roll that flips the hinge. Elbow, knee
  and finger rolls come from the fit alone.
- Calibration also reads how far the collarbones drop from the rest where the clips hang the arms (`rhythmDrops`, the
  median over the frames within 30 degrees of the side) and takes their zero back by it, never past Ludewig et al.
  2009's rhythm for the rest arm's lift. A model with no clip that hangs the arms keeps the rest as the collarbone's
  zero unless its rest bone already reads raised (KB-RIG-CLAVICLE1).
- A rig with no naming `fitHuman` knows (the UAL mannequins' Unreal names among them) gets no body unless
  `anatomy: {map}` names its joints (KB-HUM-UALNAMES1).
- Measured on the Fauld cast's Character Creator old man, three clips: hands and forearms no longer change; the ring
  fingers rest 12.8 degrees past their supination stop (KB-RIG-RINGROLL1), the thumbs are held up to 22 degrees off
  the walk (KB-RIG-THUMB1), the calf 4.7 and the toes 2. The walk's left collarbone reads 4.2 past its depression stop
  raw: the clip drops it about 34 degrees below its rest while the right rises 3.
- `person.check('structural')` reads the Animator's 32-bit pose, so a joint held at its stop can read a hair past it;
  the pose frames count only what passes by 0.01 degrees.
- `addBody` writes each bone's rest as translation, rotation and scale; a bind matrix with shear loses the shear. A
  person built with no clips gets one, `rest`, of two keys a second apart.
- Proof: `packages/humans/test/anatomy-defaults.test.js`, `body.test.js` and the pose frames
  `packages/humans/test/pose-frames.browser.mjs` (walk, IK reach and seat, front, three-quarter and side, with and
  without limits, on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`).

### Anatomy core and the human table (`@margoengine/rigging/anatomy`, 2026-11-28)

The optional rigging/anatomy entry fits a species table to a rig and rigging/anatomy/human holds the human table.
Defaults: limits on; `clampPose` and `addAnatomyLimits` hold the `structural` tier; the human table is adults of 20
to 44 years, the larger mean of the two sexes; naming is the convention that matches the most bones. Limits and
accepted differences:

- Angles are a swing vector and a twist. A swing of exactly 180 degrees has no defined twist, which then reads 0. Swing
  ranges are capped at 180 degrees and `poseFromAngles` caps a swing it is given at 180.
- The stop of a motion is its largest source value rounded up to 5 degrees plus an allowance (15 for ball, saddle and
  condyloid joints and spine regions, 10 for a hinge's flexion, 0 for the straight side of a hinge, 5 or 10 for a
  direction a joint's kind does not allow). The allowances are engine policy, not measurements.
- An elbow and a knee stop 5 degrees past straight (CDC adult means 4.7 and 1.6, rounded up). The table for men of 45
  to 69 years has no hyperextension at all (mean -0.7).
- 90 of the table's 324 distinct source numbers are from recall and marked `recalled`; none is checked in print. The
  recalled ones are spine levels (61), toe joints, the collarbone's split, knee rotation, wrist twist, the thumb's
  base, the palm's small joints and the weight-bearing ankle (45 degrees, which sets the ankle's stop).
- AAOS and AMA values are read from pages that reproduce them, named in each row; where pages disagree the
  best-labelled AAOS table is used (hip extension 20, abduction 40, adduction 20; knee flexion 135).
- A rig bone that stands for several joints of a region carries their summed range. In a spine region every bone's
  stop is the whole region's, and the region's far end is held to the region's range by easing every bone by one
  share (at most 8 passes).
- A joint whose zero is a direction in the body is left unlimited when the joint at the far end of its segment is not
  mapped. A hip with no knee, a shoulder with no elbow and a thumb base with no thumb joint are such joints.
- A rest bend under 5 degrees is read as straight; from 5 to 20 degrees it sets the hinge side only within 60 degrees
  of the anatomical side. A straight limb with no knuckle bones is taken as unrolled unless `roll` says otherwise;
  `hingeRolls` reads the roll from motion once a hinge has swung 30 degrees.
- The weight-bearing, forefoot and toe-row motions of a foot are lumped: inversion and eversion sit on the subtalar
  joint, a single toe bone is fitted as the great toe joint, and the small joints of the midfoot and palm have 5
  degrees of give and no measured range.
- `poseLimits`, `ikLimits`, `ragdollJoints` and `kinematicsLimits` express a reach that differs by direction as one
  cone (about the middle of the reach for the first two, about the rest direction for a ragdoll, about neutral for
  kinematics). Hinges are exact.
- The face joints of the standard (eyelids, eyeballs, eyebrows, jaw) are not in the table.
- The body must stand upright in its rest pose for the human frame (up is read from the hips to the head); a species
  table may give a fixed up direction instead.


### Progressive flooding evidence and limits (SEA-10)

- The free surface within each compartment is normal to gravity. The model uses lumped inventories and hydrostatic opening strips. It lacks aligned-jet momentum, transient slosh and vent-pipe losses over evolving flow regimes. Damage opening, compartment mass and sea-port coupling are covered. GZ curves, certification criteria, measured sinking speed, PA-58 fire damage, bed settlement and the original EF-11 production cut are open.
- Standalone `Flooding` rejects invalid or non-finite input before publishing accepted data. `convergenceWarning` reports a coded diagnostic when the water or air solve exhausts its 200 sweeps. A known small-scale pressure network repeatedly hits the air limit and publishes a measurable balance residual. That bound is specific to each case; it is not an accuracy guarantee. [Reproduction](known-bugs.md#sea-10-stiff-air-pressure-network)
- Optional Rust SIMD clips the 47 nonzero volume levels on a new attitude. The zero level is stored directly. Identical attitude reuses the table when the body rises or falls. This kernel accelerates volume samples; water and air flow, point-of-action moments, and cargo remain in TypeScript. Node compares all volumes, state and port words at 1, 2 and 4 participants. Packaged Chromium exercises three nested helpers plus the caller.
- A code-built 9 m barge took in 2.695 m³ by 5 s versus 0.247 m³ with early isolation. The late case listed 6.34°, trimmed 1.61° and sank 7.79 cm farther. Closing the outside breach and vent retained 2.759 m³, including 0.274 m³ transferred between tanks afterwards. Both renderers independently replay the complete image and physics state exactly.
- Ruponen 2007 Case A Test 06 is an independent model-basin diagnostic. After the dry-room fix, zero of eight early gauge readings both overlap the measured interval and resolve at the observed scale in the 5, 10 and 20 Hz test. At 5 s the port gauge read 55.2 mm versus the 20 Hz model's 5.87 mm, and the damaged-side gauge read 76.0 mm versus 145.51 mm. The maximum recorded step-size spread was 35.99 mm. In a separate 5 Hz run the upper room R22 remains dry at 120 s, where the source measured 81.3 mm. The measured outcomes were held out from geometry, inputs and discharge coefficients. [Reproduction and comparison](whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-10-progressive-flooding)
- Both optional native variants are 4,930 B raw, 2,471 B gzip and 2,210 B Brotli each. Core and stage receive zero bytes.


### Accepted parcels and independent jet scour (SEA-15)

- Native parcel diffusion moves Philox counter rounds and the subsequent Box–Muller pinned transforms into optional Rust Wasm. The rest of the solver samples its normal water, bed and wind callbacks in order. TracerSolver submits no more than 4,096 active slots per batch. The packaged test drives three real helpers plus the caller, with 21,495 moving slot updates, 107,450 paired Philox rounds and 64,485 normal values. Native and TypeScript output compare bit for bit through signed-origin replay.
- Signed cells for explicitly supplied water and wind are independent of the tracer cell. A callback returning an invalid velocity raises a code and fix link. A failed step leaves accepted particles, budgets and owned ports byte-identical. The rollback journal stores only occupied ordinary rows, the reserved slick and droplet rows, and ledgers and bed stock. Restoring a partially filled run keeps the unused rows empty. Both Wasm variants cost 6,901 B raw and 2,651 B gzip. Brotli is 2,405 B plain and 2,403 B shared. Core and stage receive zero bytes.
- The separate taconite cutaway starts with a live cargo hold and a sealed control. The live hull released 131.09 kg through its breach field. At 4.2 s the scene draws 25.85 kg of suspended fines and 104.50 kg of settled pellets from their accepted locations. The fines move 2.43 m downstream. Each renderer replays its complete accepted state and pixels exactly. The existing swimming cutaway represents a ray's local bed response. The original BB-7 and EF-11 shots and direct measurements of lifting by a ray remain open.
- The held-out final crater deficits at H/D 10 and 20 are 57.49 cm³ and 116.47 cm³. At 5 mm grid spacing the model gives 1.29 cm³ and 1.00 cm³. At 10 mm it gives 2.68 cm³ and a numerically zero deficit. Both misses exceed the radius integration, vertical resolution and observed grid sensitivity allowances. The cumulative released sediment can count repeated lifting and the source measures static post-settling geometry. Absolute mass suspended by a ray, evolving jet recirculation, the short-gap closure and multiple accepting sediment writers are open. [Reproduce the comparison](whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-15-parcel-diffusion-and-scour)


### Accepted film motion and independent incline drops (FLUID-07)

- The optional native participants split the implicit film face matrix over disjoint ranges. The capillary, gravity, wetting and contact terms keep their existing model. The global reductions, convergence decisions, pressure-only correction and coupling sequence remain ordered on the caller. The packaged 35 by 29 case reports 2,137 matrix products, 2,169,055 pressure rows, 4,338,110 gradient faces, 991,568 pressure SIMD pairs and 2,169,055 gradient SIMD pairs in its final accepted step. `workCounts()` stays outside the physical snapshot. Plain and shared assets are each 32,746 B raw and 12,619 B gzip. The threaded lead is 32,933 B raw and 12,726 B gzip. Core and stage receive zero bytes.
- Loaded films report standard `MargoError` codes, with `unsupported` for invalid configured inputs and `failed` for numerical rejection. A failed step preserves accepted depth, drainage, cumulative volume, drop events, loads and wave ports. Pre-publication checks include the pressure output and the volume ledger. Independent exact replay covers a corrected retry.
- The directed technical scene uses oblique rain on a rolling 6 mm pane. The simulation records 18.47 mL intercepted, 9.86 mL resident at cutoff, 4.11 mL resident after drainage and 1.16 mL caught in a second film by actual detached drops. Both renderers replay accepted snapshot bytes and complete resolved RGBA from inside and outside. The original EF-4 production shots remain open.
- Two independent fluoropolymer-coated incline observations hold out measured 47V10 terminal speed from the simulation. The low inclination has a measured terminal band of 2.21–2.83 mm/s. At 0.50 s and 0.333 mm spacing, the cap moves 0.959 mm with an 80 µm precursor and 0.256 mm with 40 µm. These are pre-terminal results. The high inclination has a band of 10.24–11.22 mm/s. At 0.333 mm spacing and 80 µm precursor the model's 2–4 and 4–6 mm interval speeds are 13.92 and 13.73 mm/s. The grid difference at fixed precursor leaves both intervals above the published band. At the same grid spacing a 40 µm precursor gives 2.09 mm of travel in 0.50 s and reaches neither terminal scoring interval. Shallow lubrication remains a small-slope approximation. Macroscopic steep contact slopes, a resolved contact-line slip layer, free pinch-off, splash and wet-surface rebound remain open. [Method and tests](whitepaper/reproduce.md#fluid-07-implicit-film-and-directed-rain)


### Civilian shell contact and independent tube compression (BREAK-03)

- Native workers evaluate independent membrane, plastic-return and loaded pressure faces. They pair explicit deformation and strain calculations and preserve face-order assembly, bending, cohesive, contact and friction behavior. `readNativeWork()` reports accepted work by participant and stays outside the physical snapshot. Threaded operation requires a shared world in Node or a cross-origin-isolated browser worker.
- The 211-face pressure fixture records 183 force evaluations, 38,613 face evaluations, 38,430 SIMD face evaluations, 1,093 plastic returns and 12,993 pressure faces in its final accepted tick. Its result matches the previous scalar kernel and the current one-, two- and four-participant kernels byte for byte. Plain and shared kernel assets each use 24,979 B raw, 11,416 B gzip and 9,916 B Brotli. The lazy threaded lead uses 25,644 B raw, 11,683 B gzip and 10,109 B Brotli. The optional crush entry goes from 21,351 to 24,368 B gzip with a 25,100 B ceiling. The directly coupled seakeeping entry goes from 53,151 to 53,191 B gzip.
- An invalid rigid contact input preserves the last accepted deformation, damage and body impulse outputs. A shell instance belongs to a single world. A second attachment is rejected with the help link, leaving the first instance usable. In the directly coupled carried-water case, zero acceleration retains the previously stored liquid and its contact inertia while eliminating hydrostatic weight.
- The technical dock-fender control uses an authored 55 kg carriage at 0.85 m/s. Its accepted impulse is 87.33 N·s. The clamped sheet deflects 23.00 mm, retains 2.24 mm after unloading and dissipates 3.944 J. The carriage rebounds at 0.7379 m/s. Both renderers replay complete resolved frames and accepted snapshots. The original EF-11 shot, unrestricted shell contact and automatic tearing remain open.
- Across six untouched Jung steel specimens, the reduced law underpredicts mean force by 13.09–27.01% and loading work by 13.87–26.59%. It resolves a single folding plateau. It misses the initial peak and alternating folds. Compaction stroke overlaps one of six measured bands. Input rounding, figure resolution and step refinement leave the force and work misses outside the reported allowances. Trial repeatability and general grounding accuracy remain open. [Methods and tests](whitepaper/reproduce.md#break-03-accepted-shell-and-civilian-fender)

### Placed second-order waves and flume crest counts (SEA-03)

- The optional Rust/Wasm evaluator reproduces the scalar elevation and normals exactly with one, two or four participants. It copies the coefficient tables and uses at most 6 MiB of temporary contribution storage. It sums tiles in the original row order, including linear terms. The 725-component case has 263,175 pairs in two tiles, 263,174 of them evaluated in f64x2 lanes. Two and four participants require Node or an isolated browser worker. Both lazy files use 4,672 B raw and 2,019 B gzip. The optional rogue entry goes from 7,386 to 12,255 B gzip, with a 12,623 B ceiling. Core and stage receive zero bytes.
- The fixed-camera proof is a code-built 5.8 m civilian launch and a prescribed crest. It reaches 1.350 m versus 0.06239 m in the same seeded sea without a placed event. The accepted hull heaves 0.4222 m versus 0.02062 m and rolls 19.73° versus 0.045°. Both renderers repeat accepted state and complete resolved frames through hold, restore, re-advance and rewind. The proof covers the drawn surface and a real load on the launch. The original EF-11 shot and feedback from the hull into the nonlinear sea remain open.
- The independent MARINTEK gauge has 78, 99 and 88 extreme maxima for the three published regimes. At 96 components and 40 Hz the second-order model returns 19, 1 and 3, under both published normalizations. The favorable end of the tabulated height-rounding sensitivity reaches at most 24, 7 and 6. Record-level phases, counts and event-window details are unpublished, so the comparison quantifies a miss without a formal uncertainty bar. Phase-resolved focusing and breaking, finite-depth extreme statistics and stronger kinematics remain open. [Reproduce](whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-03-second-order-waves-and-independent-flume-counts)

### Accepted wave transport and independent Lake George gauges (SEA-01)

- Spatial transport has an optional Rust/Wasm implementation for the two conservative axis sweeps. Its face fluxes and adjacent cell updates use f64x2 SIMD. The 19-by-11 mixed-coast case records six accepted sweeps, 82,971 active fluxes including 81,654 in SIMD lanes, 68,796 full limiter stencils and 76,356 wet updates including 75,144 in SIMD lanes. Its exact scalar bits survive a signed-origin shift and rewind. The native path copies fixed geometry and uses two full-spectrum buffers. Refraction and ST4/WAM source terms still run on the caller. Two and four native participants require Node or an isolated browser worker. Both lazy assets use 4,150 B raw, 1,971 B gzip and 1,821 B Brotli. The optional wave entry grows from 7,548 to 12,962 B gzip with a 13,351 B ceiling. Core and stage receive zero bytes.
- The fixed-camera test uses an upwind gust that stops after 160 s. Across stations separated by 80 m the arriving wave packet lags 36 s. Downstream significant height grows from 0.234 to 0.319 m after the source friction drops to zero. The live buoy rises 0.130 m and falls 0.144 m. Both renderers repeat their complete frame pixels and the complete accepted physics state. The original open-ocean and lake storm shots remain open.
- Two independent Lake George runs score four downstream gauges, each with either the measured upstream boundary or a calm coast. Six of 16 height comparisons intersect the published 95% measurement intervals after digitization and the observed numerical sensitivity. At the farthest gauge both boundary treatments overpredict significant height by about 0.073 m in the 10.81 m/s case and 0.112–0.113 m in the 15.22 m/s case. The stronger-wind peak ends at 0.277 Hz versus 0.326 Hz measured. Per-gauge peak-frequency uncertainty was unavailable. Interpolated depth and a strip approximation limit the comparison, and 6–9 h integration and grid/time-step sensitivity give a numerical range. Active two-way atmospheric or coastal exchange, frequency shifts by currents, and broader measured swell accuracy remain open. [Reproduction](whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-01-accepted-wave-transport-and-lake-george)

### Native surf forcing, accepted swash and measured setup (SEA-05)

- Optional native workers compute directional radiation-stress moments in spectral order, then centered divergence after the phase barrier. The periodic 25-by-9 coast performs 186 accepted moment evaluations, 178 in SIMD lanes, and 4,278 directional contributions. It computes 195 divergence cells, 186 in SIMD lanes. The waves and f64 forcing match scalar output for one, two and four participants, including signed rewind. The host owns wave action, breaking and shoreline history. It computes the fixed direction and refraction-face sines and cosines once per grid initialization. Two and four participants require Node or an isolated browser worker. Both lazy kernels use 4,696 B raw and 2,362 B gzip. The optional surf entry grows from 7,413 to 12,495 B gzip with a 12,870 B ceiling. Core and stage receive zero bytes.
- The published height, angle, wet marks and shoreline read from accepted state. The raw forcing and Stokes-drift queries describe the most recent advanced tick. After restoring, advance the coupled solver before reading the individual forcing contribution. In the fixed-camera test, the grouped shoreline runs from 25.5 to 33.5 m and then retreats to 30.5 m, with a 0.788 m/s backwash. The marked sand cell has 15.56 mm of accepted water at 46 s and 2.11 mm at 52 s, below the renderer's 3 mm dry-point cutoff. Its stored wet mark still darkens the sand. Both renderers repeat full frame and accepted snapshot bytes.
- At the independent Boers gauge at 27 m, calculated setup overpredicts the three measured cases by 5.35, 8.19 and 2.56 mm. The respective local readout and numerical allowances are 1.86, 1.85 and 2.30 mm. Across five gauges in three regimes, 7 of 15 height and 6 of 15 mean-level readings fall within the computed allowances. Gauge calibration and repeatability remain unknown. Phase-resolved wave breaking, the fixed breaker closure, the existing wet-sand uprush estimate, coastal feedback and the original film shots remain open. [Reproduce](whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-05-accepted-surf-and-boers-flume-gauges)

### Native tide and pressure forcing (SEA-07)

The optional native evaluator takes the Sun and Moon's Earth-fixed positions and stages pressure and tidal terms before forming the accepted head. Wet-cell sums stay in their original order. In the 153-cell test, 126 cells are wet and 152 cells use f64x2 lanes in both native phases. The 1-, 2- and 4-participant paths match scalar accepted bytes, including pressure-only and all-dry controls. Two and four participants require Node or an isolated browser worker. Both lazy kernels use 3,899 B raw, 1,808 B gzip and 1,635 B Brotli. The surge entry grows from 4,428 to 9,078 B gzip with a 9,351 B ceiling. Core and stage receive zero bytes.

In the idealized closed basin, the west and east stages are +29.74 and −25.26 mm at 7 hours, then −66.05 and +62.46 mm at 14 hours. The corresponding sill floods on each side. Both stay dry in the tide-off control. The observed channel current changes from −1.635 to +3.092 mm/s by 13 hours. The cutaway uses 1:25,000 horizontal scale and 45 model metres per metre of physical elevation for visibility. The solver, observations and displayed readings use unscaled SI units.

Against 209 independent NOAA observations from 9–11 November 1975, the 8 km Lake Superior run underestimates the Point Iroquois peak by 0.300 m and reaches it an hour early. The station RMSE is 0.102 m and the maximum spread between numerical configurations is 0.047 m. The lake-connected model point is 11 km from the sensor. Duluth and Ontonagon RMSEs are 0.045 and 0.057 m, with peak times five and nine hours early. Historical instrument calibration uncertainty is unavailable. The 2D grid also limits shoreline, wind shelter and vertical circulation. Measured accuracy, marine tide-gauge checks, constituent-dependent tidal effects and self-attraction and loading, wave feedback, and direct synoptic-pressure connection remain open. [Reproduce](whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-07-tide-replay-and-lake-superior)

Entry sizes are in scripts/quality/baselines/sizes.json.

## Ground contact and relief in BiomeView (2026-11-28)

- `TerrainGroundContact` footprints are circles baked on the CPU into a 1024 x 1024 mask of 0.2 m texels (205 m around
  the camera, 2 MB), re-baked whole when footprints inside it change. Only stored stones and tree trunks are fed by
  `BiomeView`; meshes placed by hand need `view.groundContact.set`.
- `BiomeObjects` opens its own grass and ferns in the soil rings (`groundCover`, `scatter/clearing-map`: `thin` 1.4,
  `shorten` 0.6, `reach` 0.25 m, five texel reads a candidate). Grass scattered by a scene itself is not thinned unless
  it takes `thinning` too, and still hides the ring. Chosen on rendered frames, with no measurement: those three values,
  a trunk footprint of 0.3 of its crown's reach and the crown depth 1.2.
- The crown shade (`skyOcclusion.crown`) is a cone about the up axis, not the mesh's outline, and dims sky light only.
  On the treeline stills it deepens crowns a little (crown luma down 3 to 9 percent); it does not separate near and far
  stands, which needs haze (the scene's fog).
- The relief shadows' toothed edges on the treeline summit cliff are the cast outline of a serrated crest: raising the
  bake's march from 48 to 256 steps moved 0.3 percent of those pixels by more than 20 of 255.
- Relief bake work: one compute pass over the height texture, each texel marching `rays + 1` rays of up to `steps`
  samples of 4 reads (defaults 12 and 48): 2,496 texture reads a texel, 10.5 billion for a 2049 x 2049 texture, once
  per rebake. Wall-clock time is not measured (speed is deferred).
- The stone ring's width and strength, a trunk's 0.6 of the sphere form factor, the foot bands' heights and the
  canopy's optical depth (0.5 x stand cover over the lower half) are chosen on rendered frames, with no measurement behind them.
- `relief` shades the terrain only (not the objects on it), from the height texture at `textureResolution`, and
  multiplies with `shadows` where both reach: the same in umbra and light, darker only in soft edges.

Grass leaf colour, clumps and clearings (2026-11-28, plants round 1). GrassShape gains hue (0 to 0.5, default 0.02), yellow (0 to 1, default 0.15), yellowColor (linear RGB 0 to 1, default ANGERS 2003 yellowing leaves [0.1432, 0.1794, 0.0382]), tipBrown (0 to 1, default 0.25) and transmittance (three numbers 0 to 4, default [1.0909, 1.1726, 0]); the colour terms apply in the lit (PBR) stage only, and transmittance only tints `blades.translucency` above 0. Scatter gains clumps ({ size above 0 up to 100000, cover 0 to 1, edge 0.001 to 1, default 0.2 }), clearings (up to 100,000 circles, each one exclusions-buffer row after the rectangles and path segments) and reach (0 to 100000 mesh units). Clumps and clearings are compiled into the distribute shader, so they are fixed for the scatter's life; `cover` is a threshold of the patch noise, not an exact share (0.5 kept 553 of 936 instances in grass.browser.mjs). Sizes: scatter 29,682 to 30,432 B gzip, scatter/grass 3,047 to 3,432 B (scripts/quality/baselines/sizes.json).

Alpine wildflowers (2026-11-28, plants round 1). `@margoengine/procedural/forbs` builds five species (arnica, gentian, aster, bistort, campion); `scale` 0.2 to 5, `heads` 0 to 12 (campion 0 to 400), integer seed. Each part ring is at most a few hundred triangles; there are no petal textures, so petals are flat measured colour with PBR shading. Parts must be drawn with equal `reach`, seed and placement to share instances. Scatter `reach` is now an exact override that must hold every vertex, and a clearing with `inside: true` keeps instances only within the circle and its falloff.

### ATMO-04 size-resolved precipitation and falling drops

The field uses 64 quadrature sizes for bulk moments and 192 for advecting each active species from a moving source. It uses source reference size weights across the shaft. A ray obtains its terminal speed in the column's midpoint air and uses the wind along its approximate midpoint path. A descending ray contributes no arrival when the sampled vertical wind equals or exceeds its terminal speed. The field reconstructs an exponential from each arrived rate. General size-spectrum evolution, along-column changing drag, and heat and phase history remain open. Boundary-layer air, liquid or ice partition and inputs must stay inside their documented finite ranges.

The optional K23 path uses quadratic transient slip drag matched at each drop's ambient terminal equilibrium. Its sphere area and volume stay fixed through the trajectory. Cold fixture snow uses a compact equivalent body, with no crystal orientation, aggregation or breakup. Static contact uses the interpolated first crossing at 240 Hz. The technical flume proves the deposit and linear capillary pulse. Crown spray, melting, evaporation, ocean short-wave rain damping, variable cloud microphysics, and the original EF-7 and EF-12 production shots remain open.

The independent Paris checks compare 17 warm light and 10 stronger five-minute windows. In light rain 2 of 4 diameter groups overlap the observed envelope. In the stronger sample none of 4 do. The predicted 1.5–2.0 mm concentration is 25.13 m⁻³ against 15.82 and 15.46 m⁻³ measured, with a 14.37–17.13 m⁻³ replicate and bin envelope. Seven populated speed comparisons reach the broad observed percentile ranges, while their model centres are faster than both observed medians. All 94 separate Kiruna D-ICI aggregate speeds fall below the prediction outside the approximate instrument allowance of ±10 µm and ±9% speed. Mean measured-to-model speeds for the 0.5–1, 1–2 and 2–4 mm groups are 0.467 to 0.985, 0.525 to 1.188 and 0.432 to 1.295 m/s. The instrument allowance combines the published dimension error, tumbling, point selection and timing. Riming and site-air uncertainty remain unquantified. The shared-lineage Locatelli and Hobbs comparison also misses the observed 4–8 mm and 8–15 mm bands. Measured fidelity remains open.

Weather precipitation grows from 3,852 to 5,702 B gzip, with a 5,958 B ceiling. Physics falling grows from 5,907 to 8,015 B gzip, with an 8,271 B ceiling. Each existing optional Wasm asset grows by 392 B raw and 225 B gzip to 10,501 B raw, 4,498 B gzip and 4,044 B Brotli. Core and stage receive zero bytes. [Evidence and commands](whitepaper/reproduce.md#atmo-04-size-resolved-rain-flight-and-field-measurements)

### ICE-04 shared native drift and independent tow resistance

Each native substep splits independent planar drag and translation into contiguous rows. It joins before ordered grid insertion, floe contacts and vessel impulses. On the 391-floe sample, the four-participant path checks 391 initial velocities and takes 16 mini-steps, with 6,256 f64x2 drift rows and 29,141 existing ordered pair candidates. The one-, two- and four-participant paths repeat the same accepted state at signed origins. Registered foreign rows use their own memory and invalid inputs preserve the accepted step. The optional entry grows from 4,715 to 7,523 B gzip with a 7,779 B ceiling. The plain and shared assets use 6,549 B raw and 3,094 and 3,095 B gzip, respectively. Both use 2,815 B Brotli. Core and stage receive zero bytes.

The tow comparison uses the increase from 60 to 80 percent ice concentration at two speeds. At 0.5 and 0.8 m/s, the measured increases are 0.774 and 1.231 N and the model predicts 0.542 and 1.590 N. Both lie inside the repeat-only envelopes of 0.321–1.227 and 0.566–1.896 N. Using the separately measured floe–floe friction for all contacts gives 0.667 and 2.033 N. The higher-speed result exceeds the repeat-only envelope and remains inside the additional full-scale instrument allowance. The model uses one friction for every contact, equal-area disks for the square floes and a waterline capsule for the vessel. Pitch, under-hull transport, concentration-dependent water flow and absolute resistance remain open. [Evidence and commands](whitepaper/reproduce.md#ice-04-native-floe-drift-and-towing-tank-comparison)

### ICE-01 snowpack acceptance and independent field measurements

The solver stages cross-memory forcing, column state, cover and runoff before publication. Nonfinite candidates leave all accepted outputs intact. Positive infinity still represents a column with no downslope load in the stability field. Native workers process independent columns after the usual ordered snowfall and surface drift, with the same state and output format.

At Col de Porte, independent six-day dry-window depth RMSE is 0.011 and 0.018 m for the cold and warm cases. At the end of the cold case, the model reports 0.290 m against 0.301 m measured. The warm case reports 0.428 against 0.400 m. Its trailing daily mean SWE is 232.89 against 189 kg/m², and its instantaneous lower bound still misses by 31.70 kg/m² against the published 25 kg/m² RMS spatial variability scale. Halving the step changes SWE by at most 0.00084 kg/m². Moving the forcing time by an hour changes it by up to 0.98 kg/m². The model retains too much water in the warm run. Layer creation, microstructure, sublimation, changing albedo, basal-flux uncertainty and full warm-season accuracy remain open. [Reproduction](whitepaper/reproduce.md#ice-01-native-snow-columns-and-col-de-porte)

The four-participant browser case checks 221 columns and 714 conduction interfaces. 694 interfaces use paired f64x2 lanes, with 38,556 bisection iterations in total. The optional entry grows from 4,916 to 8,220 B gzip, with an 8,476 B ceiling. Each binary uses 11,383 B raw and 4,552 B gzip. The plain and shared assets use 4,107 and 4,109 B Brotli. Core and stage receive zero bytes.

### ICE-03 accepted calving and independent capsize measurements

Workers advance independent bodies including vacant release rows. Admission and ordered publication of signed source and freshwater rows remain on the caller. The 259-row Chromium run has 234 active bodies, 887 substeps, 2,008 wrench evaluations and 40,160 paired face dot products. Its four participants complete 240, 253, 244 and 150 substeps. The two grid populations replay exactly and match the previous scalar kernel. When small releases enter vacant slots immediately, the shortest cuboids can dominate adaptive work in one partition. A configured reusable slot retains the remaining event volume in the queue. A physically guided parcel aggregation model remains open.

Measured Burton Figure 5 intervals for 10° to 45°, 45° to 80°, and 10° to 90° are 0.620, 0.278 and 0.998 s. The model takes 0.431, 0.167 and 0.636 s. Each interval misses its conservative readout and release bound. The model reaches 114.28° against 96.07° observed. Halving the integration interval changes the 10° to 90° duration by 0.00010 s. In the separate Heller comparison the measured marker peaks at 0.214 m/s versus 0.403 m/s in the free-body model. The guide assembly restrains surge and contributes rod inertia, so that comparison leaves the effect of those differences unresolved. Added inertia, water feedback and radiation damping, heat-driven melt, irregular shapes, grounding, ship contact and quantitative capsize accuracy remain open.

The optional entry grows from 4,339 to 6,937 B gzip with a 7,193 B ceiling. Both Wasm assets use 9,776 B raw and 4,693 B gzip, with plain and shared Brotli sizes 4,114 and 4,107 B. Core and stage receive zero bytes. [Tests and measured record](whitepaper/reproduce.md#ice-03-native-iceberg-rows-and-capsize-measurements)

### ATMO-05 accepted storm forcing and observations

The prescribed vertical profile misses Hurricane Isabel's observed eyewall jet by about 28.2 m/s.
At a 42 km radius and 1 km height it gives 47.8 m/s, against 76 ± 6 m/s observed. The separate observed
radial component at 1.5 km is weakly outward (+1.7 m/s), while the model remains inward (−18.2 m/s).
Changing the archived pressure, radius and latitude within the observed window retains the jet deficit.
[Montgomery et al. (2006)](https://doi.org/10.1175/BAMS-87-10-1335).

For 27.31, 32.97, 40.92 and 50.80 m/s 10 m wind, the revised closure gives drag coefficients
2.580, 2.600, 2.600 and 2.600 × 10⁻³. The independent field estimates are 1.960, 2.145, 1.860 and
1.499 × 10⁻³. Each predicted value exceeds the plotted upper 95% limit plus the figure readout allowance.
A prescribed drag plateau cannot resolve the observed high-wind decline or wave-age dependence.
[Powell et al. (2003)](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature01481).

### EARTH-08 elastic site response at Mashiki

The KMMH16 test at Mashiki initializes its production elastic section from NIED's original
borehole P–S velocity log as reproduced by NILIM and PWRI. Densities come from Fukutake et al.'s
independent velocity-based estimate. A generic 0.001 m/s horizontal initial packet propagates
upward and downward in the modeled bedrock. Both the surface and 252 m borehole signals are
model outputs. The observations are held out from the section, excitation and damping.

Across 0.75 and 1.5 m depth grids and two packet widths, the modeled surface-to-borehole transit
is 0.33187–0.33609 s. The reference weak-motion impulse-response time from 107 observations is
0.377 s. The model arrives 40.9–45.1 ms early. The logged shear travel integral is 0.33125 s.
The paper's 6% background variability is descriptive and does not give a confidence interval.
For the same logged section, the independent continuum layer calculation has a local
spectral-ratio maximum at 4.025 Hz with and without the illustrative damping. The observed
weak-motion feature is at 3.4 Hz. The comparison does not use the absolute gains from the
recorded borehole, and the model keeps strain-independent elastic properties.
[Esfahani, Cotton and Bonilla](https://doi.org/10.1093/gji/ggae222).
[Reproducible comparison](../packages/physics/scripts/earth08-mashiki-measured.mjs).

#### AERO-02 measured cambered sail polar

Arredondo-Galeana, Babinsky and Viola measured lift and drag on the rigid, zero-twist S3 downwind sail at 0.14 m/s in a water flume. At the camera-derived 30° chord incidence, the solver produces lift coefficient 0.488 and drag coefficient 0.355. The observed values are 1.309 and 0.601. Across the five held-out trims, the 9 × 25 grid produces lift coefficients 0.295–0.488 and drag coefficients 0.202–0.489. The measured ranges are 0.405–1.309 and 0.188–0.888. Four of five comparisons miss for each coefficient after the paper’s measurement allowance, 5 × 13 to 9 × 25 refinement and ±2° incidence sensitivity. The model uses the archived geometry and the independently imaged angles. The force values only enter comparison. The isolated midsurface omits the flume, mount, thickness, turbulent return flow and shed vortices. [Primary experiment](https://doi.org/10.1017/flo.2023.1) [Shape archive](https://doi.org/10.7488/ds/2857)
